Only in Elihu - warning dreams and the interceding angel: The healed man sings before men, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not requited to me'; God does all these things two or three times with a man, to bring him back from the Pit to the light of life; God speaks once, even twice, but people do not perceive it; An angel, an intercessor (malakh melits), one among a thousand, declares a man's uprightness and pleads for him; The sick man's soul draws near the Pit and his life to the 'destroyers' (memitim, angels of death); 'Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom (kofer)'; 'The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of Shaddai gives me life'; In dreams during deep sleep God opens people's ears and seals their warning, to turn them from pride and spare them from the Pit; The angel of death (malak al-mawt), put in charge of humans, takes their souls; Angels glorify God and ask forgiveness for those on earth; The restored man's flesh becomes fresher than a child's and he returns to the days of his youth; Humans created from sticky clay (tin lazib); and 4 more.

matches.label: The deity sets a sign for when the flood hero must board
matches.note: Both signs come from the bakery: Šamaš's deadline is the 'rain of bread-cakes (kukkū) and wheat', then 'go into the boat and seal your hatch'; in 11:40 (and 23:27) it is that 'the oven (al-tannūr) boils', then 'load it'. tannūr is the Akkadian tinūru (bread oven), though Gilgameš does not use the word here.

Only in Namburbi against an ominous sacrifice (STT 2 231): when the slaughtered sheep does not bleed and its entrails are faulty: Wish that the evil cross the river, cross the mountain and be thousands of double-hours from the body, rise like smoke and like an uprooted tamarisk never return; Circling his house, the client declares 'I change my house: my evils are your evils' and tears out the evil the gods placed; Instead of prostrating, the supplicant goes straight to the god's house and kisses its door frame; The client of a ritual is dressed in a strange costume of debasement: grain and silver on the head, jaw bound, rings on fingers and toes, a lead belt, one sandal, wall plaster on the head; Part of the ritual beer or grain is handed to a strange (outsider) woman, carrying the evil out of the house; The bewitched man calls on the gods of the night (the stars), Night personified and the night watches to hear his case against the witch; The god resolves (releases) evil, frightening dreams and bad portents and makes evil and sin pass by; Divination by inspecting the liver (hepatoscopy); The enemies of God vanish like the glory of the pastures, like smoke; A ritual action is performed seven times; A pursued victim raises his hands to the sun god: 'You are a just judge, do not fail me'.

Only in Nergal and Ereškigal, Uruk copy (SpTU 1 1): the chair for Ereškigal, the seven gates, the refused food, and the queen's grief when Erra slips away: The underworld queen orders the god who slighted her envoy brought before her (to die); The forsaken goddess falls from her throne weeping that her lover has gone before she was sated, she who as a girl never knew the play of maidens; The underworld queen begs for her life and offers herself as wife, with kingship over the wide earth and the tablet of wisdom; The wise god gives the descending god a chair (throne) to carry as a gift for the underworld queen; A god going down to the underworld is warned not to sit on the chair offered, eat its bread or meat, drink its beer, have his feet washed, or desire its queen when she bathes; God and goddess lie together for six days; on the seventh the god slips away back up to heaven; A messenger prostrates himself and kisses the ground before the deity he addresses; A message is dictated to a messenger and repeated word for word on delivery, framed by fixed dialogue formulas.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; A hostile spirit is commanded 'go out' of the dwelling; Heavenly beings do obeisance when the first human has been made: to the maker or to the man [divergence between the texts]; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; The underworld or hell has seven doors or gates; The underworld has seven gates, bolted and opened one at a time [divergence between the texts]; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; and 7 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The petitioner asks the deity to set truth on his tongue so that he is well spoken of (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Šuʾila to Marduk (SpTU 2 11): 'Mighty, resplendent, lord', with dates for the rite against the alû demon: Petition: set truth in my mouth and goodness in my heart, so that courtiers and attendants speak well of me; The deity's name fills the mouth like cakes, butter and cream (or honey); A rite is tied to specific favourable days of the month (e.g. day 7, day 20, day 21) with rules for diet and conduct; Cluster of divine epithets in sequence (e.g. the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, doer of what he wills; or Lord, King, God of mankind); Vow of praise: 'save me, so that I may declare your greatness and sing your praises'; Petition that the angry personal god and personal goddess turn back and be reconciled with the sufferer.

Only in Abraham's argument against idols and his prayer: Abraham prays for 'a tongue of truthfulness' (good repute) among later generations; Abraham's creed: the God who created and guides me, feeds and gives drink, heals me when sick, causes me to die and revives me, and will forgive me; In hell the damned dispute with the gods they equated with God and wish for another chance; The deluded and all the hosts of Iblis are hurled headlong into hell; The god who made humans also teaches or guides them and gives them food and drink; Petition that the petitioner's good name (praise, 'a tongue of truth') be set in the mouths of people, or of later generations; On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart; Who sends sickness and who heals [divergence between the texts]; Whether a man's sons (and wealth) help him after death [divergence between the texts]; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; Abraham prayed for his father's forgiveness only by a promise, and disowned him when he proved God's enemy; God wounds and binds up, strikes and his hands heal; and 7 more.

Only in Bīt rimki varia (SpTU 2 12 obv.): the prince washes off guilt and curses, 'may my tablet of guilt be broken', the bound sheep released before Šamaš: Purification: may the curse and complaint from the mouth of many people be removed and poured away; Wish that the king's life be (as constant) in people's mouths as silver or beer; The sun god is asked to guard the petitioner's life daily, renew his reign and grant long days; A bound sheep is untied before the sun god: 'as I untie this sheep, may my guilt and sin be untied'; Petition: may the tablet (record) of my guilt be broken, my sins cut off and scattered; The god transposes evil destinies, releases guilt (mupaṭṭir arni) and keeps sins and transgressions at bay; The washing water from the speaker's body and hands carries the evil onto a substitute figurine (ṣalam nigsagilê) which bears his sin in his place; street and way undo his sins; The speaker washes his hands and body in pure Eridu spring water, removing every evil: bad dreams, signs, portents, bad entrails, demons, illness, curses and witchcraft.

Only in The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger: Whoever is given his book in his left hand wishes he had never been given it and that death had been final; his wealth and power are gone; Whoever is given his book in his right hand says 'Here, read my book!' and lives a pleasing life in a lofty garden with fruit clusters near; He did not believe in God the Great and did not urge the feeding of the poor; The damned have no friend and no food except ghislin (foul washings/pus); Had he fabricated sayings against God, God would have seized him by the right hand and cut his aorta (watin); 'I swear by what you see and what you do not see'; 'Seize him, fetter him, roast him in hellfire, then thread him on a chain seventy cubits long'; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Reclining on couches lined with brocade, with the fruit of the gardens hanging near; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; An offence concerning food is repaid with foul food and drink [divergence between the texts]; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A ritual recites a long catalogue of possible offences (social, verbal, cultic, against kin) that may have brought the curse (māmītu), so that it can be released (weight 7.1); The sufferer asks his god to show him his sins so that he may confess them openly at the city gate (weight 6.4). Only in Šurpu II (SpTU 2 13 obv.): the catalogue of sins - good for evil, bribed judges, the widow wronged, father set against son, captives kept in darkness, false measures: Catalogue sin: he did not release the captive or loosen the bound man, and did not show light to the prisoner; Catalogue sin: he despised father and mother, was hostile to his elder brother and sinned against his elder sister; Catalogue sin: he knew but did not say, said but exaggerated, said 'there is' for 'there is not'; Catalogue sin: he separated son from father, father from son, daughter from mother, daughter-in-law from mother-in-law, brother from brother, friend from friend; The wicked kill the widow, the stranger and the orphan; Whether a bound captive is released or killed; Knowing the matter and not speaking: withholding testimony as a sin; Making the judge take a bribe to win a case; Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, darkness light and bitter sweet; The wicked takes a bribe from the bosom to pervert the ways of justice; Giving with the small measure and taking with the large: short weight to others, full weight for oneself; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

Only in Kummanni prayer, further cases, unknown offences and colophon of Lūrma (CTH 382 §8-13): The storm god filled the mother's breasts for our good, and as people are sated with cold water so may he grant satiety; Since humans know only the words that came out of their mouth, the underworld gods are asked to search out in the dark earth the offences they do not know; If the gods grant the plea, the king will be his god's glory: gods and men will say 'truly the god recognised this man', and his descendants will revere the god; Petition not to be held for offences committed unknowingly, forgotten or by mistake; Plea that the deity not destroy the whole community for what one or a few have done; Intercessor asks: shall one man sin and you rage at the whole community?; A text ends with a note on its source or on where it was written.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/16-ane-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The evil plot or sorcery turns back upon its own author (weight 7.3); The evil plan devised against others returns upon the plotter's own head (weight 5.5). Pair score 12.9.

Only in Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ obv. ii): incantations to Ea, Asalluhi, Šamaš and Sîn as creators; to Gula against the adversary's sorcery; to Marduk for bright days: A man has an adversary and slanderer; hatred, injustice, 'cutting of life' and 'seizing of the mouth' surround him; Petition that bright days shine on me and god, king, noble and prince be reconciled with me and rejoice to see me; The healing goddess (Gula) is hailed as creator of mankind and giver of share, ration and offerings, and asked to stand by the petitioner in court; Humans are those whose clay the birth goddess (Aruru) pinched off to form them; The sun god is shepherd of the land and father of the black-headed; Vow of praise: 'save me, so that I may declare your greatness and sing your praises'.

Only in The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned: God made humans successors (khala'if) on the earth; Heirs of the Book are of three kinds: one who wrongs himself, one who is moderate, and one foremost in good deeds; The guilty, heads bowed before their Lord, beg to be returned to do good; God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; if they ceased, no one else could hold them; If God took people to task for what they earned he would not leave a creature on the earth's back, but he defers them to a set term; Paradise is the abode of permanence where no toil or weariness touches the blessed and grief is removed; The evil plot or sorcery turns back upon its own author [divergence between the texts]; The evil plot encompasses only its own authors; In paradise the righteous are adorned with gold bracelets and pearls and wear silk; The god (alone) holds the heavens (and earth) in place: the bond or rope of heaven, holding back the sky; In hell the damned neither die nor live; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; and 2 more.

matches.note: Šuʾila to Ištar: tayyārāti u rēmēnâti ennenêti u muppašrāti (you are relenting and merciful, compassionate and forgiving); 2:37: fa-tāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa t-tawwābu r-raḥīm. Only in Ludlul bēl nēmeqi I: the sufferer abandoned by his gods, omens confused, seven courtiers plot, friends turn, property divided, tears day and night (CTN 4, 201, obverse 41-reverse 54): Each morning the sufferer hopes for good; a month passes, the sun shines; a whole year passes to its term; The sufferer's heart burns like fire as he prays, his prayers are a squabble, his lips stiff as in gloom; The sufferer's office is given to another and a stranger installed in his cultic duties; The sufferer's property is shared out among the riffraff, his canal silted up, the harvest song silenced, his city made silent like an enemy's; From constant crying the sufferer's eyes are strained and his cheeks burn with tears; In his affliction the sufferer's friend speaks lies to him and his companion repays his truthful words with falsehood; The king's heart hardens against his loyal official; courtiers conspire, each vowing to seize his life, post, office or household; The sufferer has no one to walk at his side and sees no champion or helper; The man who walked proudly learns to slink; his proud head bends to the ground, his broad chest is pushed aside by a youth; A clique of seven courtiers, one after another, swears to destroy the official and share out his position; The sufferer's omens are contradictory every day, diviner and dream interpreter cannot resolve his case, street talk and dreams portend evil; The sufferer's own god and goddess abandon him; his protective spirits (shedu, lamassu) veer off and seek someone else; and 2 more.

Only in Uruk nocturnal ritual: offerings on the ziggurat roof to Anu and Antu of heaven and to the seven planets; the great torch; fire carried to every temple and house; gates open till dawn (TCL 6, 41): On the festival night the city watch lights fires in the streets and squares and the city gates stay open until dawn; At nightfall on the temple tower a purification priest lights a great aromatic torch with sulphur fire and recites the hymn 'Star of Anu, lord of heaven'; A large ḫarû jar is broken before the god during the festival rite; On the festival night the gods sit in the temple court in a vigil (bayyātu) until dawn; the gate is not shut; Fire from the temple's great torch is carried down and kindled in every temple of the city, and the people light brushwood fires in their houses; The ritual torch is extinguished in holy water mixed with beer, milk, wine and oil; The king sets out offerings to the planets and stars of heaven and prays to them for long life and a firm throne; The god enters his newly built house in procession and takes possession of it; Water for washing the hands is presented to the gods (mê qātī našû), and the king and the people touch it.

Only in Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah: Men thickened on their lees who say in their hearts 'YHWH will do neither good nor evil'; The Day of YHWH is a sacrifice he has prepared, with invited guests consecrated; Litany of the Day: day of wrath, distress, ruin, darkness, cloud and thick darkness, shofar and alarm; God will search Jerusalem with lamps to find the complacent; Named districts of Jerusalem (Fish Gate, Mishneh/Second Quarter, Maktesh/Mortar) wail; A prophet's genealogy is traced several generations back to a king (Hezekiah); God will punish officials and princes who wear foreign garments; People bow and swear both by YHWH and by Malkam (their king or Milcom); God will sweep away humans, beasts, birds of the air and fish of the sea from the face of the ground (creation reversed); Idolatrous priests (kemarim) who burned incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations are put down; 'The imminent (al-azifa) has drawn near'; none but God can remove it; Priests do not tread on a temple threshold, explained by an event; and 6 more.

Anzu, set by Enlil to guard the door of the sanctuary (ne₂-reb ki-iṣ-ṣi ... i-qip-šu {d}EN.LIL₂), says lul-qe₂-e-ma DUB NAM-MEŠ DINGIR-MEŠ a-na-ku 'I will take the Tablet of Destinies of the gods' and seizes it while Enlil bathes. Shared motifs, rarest first: Men build great structures to endure, but the builders and their buildings pass [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Harper's Song of Inherkhau (TT 359): Build yourself a house (tomb) in the necropolis so that your name endures in it; Give your heart drunkenness every day until the day of landing (death) comes; Do not remember evil, what the god abhors; The dead is praised as upright, just, calm, patient, content, cheerful and one who speaks no evil; The Nile flows north and the north wind blows south: each man goes at his hour; At the feast of life the beloved wife sits at your side; put singer and harper before you; A man's (or nation's) term is fixed to the hour: nothing is added or advanced; The day of death is called the day of 'landing' (mnj), mooring in the land that loves silence; Generations pass away and others take their place, since the time of the ancestors (or of the god); Refrain 'Make holiday (a beautiful day)! Do not weary of it!'; Follow your heart (desire) while you live: put myrrh on your head, dress in fine linen, do your things on earth.

Only in Hud and the monument-building people of Ad: The people of ʿĀd build a monument on every height and take fortresses (maṣāniʿ) hoping to live forever; Their graves (qirbam = qivram) are their houses forever, though they named lands after themselves; The prophet Hūd is sent to the people of ʿĀd; Monuments built so that their builders may live for ever [neutral]; Nimrod, first mighty man, a mighty hunter before the LORD; Building with baked bricks and bitumen instead of stone and mortar; Woe to the one who builds a city (Zion) with bloodshed and injustice; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness; Builders seek to make a name for themselves and avoid dispersal; and 2 more.

Only in The aged Re, the plot of mankind, the council of the gods and the Eye sent as Hathor (Heavenly Cow, Seti I): The aged god's body is described as precious materials: bones of silver, flesh of gold, hair of lapis lazuli; The destroying goddess wades in the blood of the slain humans; The sun god sends out his Eye in the form of a goddess (Hathor/Sakhmet) to slay rebellious humankind; Humankind came into being from the creator's eye (his tears); When the sun god has grown old, humankind plots against him (kꜣi̯ md,t r ...); The aged creator wishes to return to the primeval waters (Nun) from which he came into being; Recurring etiological formula 'so came about X' (ḫpr X pw) deriving a name, place, rite or custom from a word or act of the god.

Only in Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206): The divine warning commands: abandon riches, spurn property and save life; After the flood all humankind has returned to clay; the plain is flat as a roof; Instead of the flood, a lion, a wolf, famine or plague should have diminished the people; The mother goddess bars the god who caused the flood from the offering, for he acted without counsel; Huge measured quantities of bitumen, pitch and oil are poured into the kiln and the hull; The hero slaughters oxen and sheep and gives the workers beer, oil and wine like river water, so they feast as at the New Year festival; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer; The chief god sees the boat and is enraged that a living being escaped: 'no man should survive!'; What the ark contains; Besides kin and animals, craftsmen of every skill are taken aboard; The god gives the hero a cover story: Enlil hates me, I am going down to the Apsû, and he will rain abundance on you (bread-cakes in the morning, a torrent of wheat in the evening) - an ambiguous promise of the coming flood; How the ark is described; and 79 more.

matches.note: Pabil's messengers: 'take, Kirta, peace-gifts (šlmm) ... silver and yellow gold'; Kirta: 'why should I (want) silver and yellow gold? give what is lacking in my house'. Bilqīs: 'I will send them a gift and see what the envoys bring back'; Sulaymān: 'do you supply me with wealth? What God gave me is better'. In both the threatened ruler buys off the king with wealth, the king spurns it, and the story ends with the woman brought to him.

matches.note: Yarikh: 'give Nikkal ... I will give her bride-price (mhr) to her father: a thousand of silver, ten thousand of gold'; the father first proposes another daughter (Pidray). Only in Baal Cycle 1.5 I: Mot's message: though you smote Lotan the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads, you shall go down into my throat; my appetite is the lion's of the steppe, the whale's in the sea; you did not invite me to the feast: The heavens wither and droop (when the storm god is defeated); The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations; Death's appetite is that of the lion of the steppe and the whale in the sea, a pool that wild bulls seek; his cup is mixed with a whole river; Death complains that the storm god did not invite him to eat bread and drink wine with his brothers; Leviathan, the great sea monster, named; YHWH with his hard, great, strong sword will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and slay the dragon (tannin) in the sea; A seven-headed serpent is among the monsters slain by the warrior god; God crushed the heads (plural) of Leviathan, the many-headed sea serpent; The storm god's mountain Ṣapān is 'my holy place, the mountain of my inheritance, the pleasant place, the hill of victory'.

Only in Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness: On the day the caller calls from a place near at hand, and they hear the Cry (al-sayha): the day of coming forth; The damned man's companion (qarin) disputes before God: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress'; The earth splits open from them and they hasten forth to the gathering; 'Enter it in peace': the day of eternity; they have what they wish and more (mazid) with God; The Garden is brought near to the God-fearing, not far off; God created the heavens and earth in six days and no weariness (lughub) touched him; Every soul comes with a driver (sa'iq) and a witness (shahid); The stupor (sakra) of death comes with the truth: 'this is what you tried to avoid'; Two receivers sit on the right and the left recording every word a person utters; At judgment the covering is removed from a person and his sight that day is sharp as iron; Whether the work of creation brings toil and weariness on the divine [divergence between the texts]; Whether the work of creation brings toil and weariness on the divine [response between the texts]; and 24 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/22-ane-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Wadis or rivers that run with honey (nḫlm tlk nbtm / anhār min ʿasal) (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Baal Cycle 1.6 III-IV: in El's dream the heavens rain oil and the wadis run with honey; El laughs: 'Baal lives, the prince, lord of the earth, exists'; 'the furrows of the fields are parched, O Shapsh: where is mighty Baal?'; Shapsh will seek him: In the high god's dream the heavens rain oil and the wadis run with honey, a sign that the storm god lives; Joy that the dead god lives again: 'I will sit and rest, for mighty Baal is alive, the prince, lord of the earth, exists'; A libation of wine is poured before a deity sets out to search for the lost god; A revelation comes to a god or man 'in a dream, in a vision' (ḥlm // ḏhrt); Seeing the visitor, the high god unfurrows his brow and laughs, puts his feet on the footstool and twiddles his fingers; The furrows of the fields are parched; 'where is mighty Baal, where is the prince, lord of the earth?'; The Sun deity is called 'the Lamp of the gods' (nrt ilm špš); In that day the mountains drip sweet wine and the hills flow with milk; Letter greeting: 'may the gods (the thousand gods, the gods of Ugarit) guard you in well-being' (ilānū ana šulmāni liṣṣurūka; Ugaritic ilm tġrk tšlmk).

Only in Muhammad: deeds nullified, striking necks and freeing captives, and the four rivers of the Garden: The damned are given boiling water to drink which tears their bowels apart; The Garden has rivers of unstaling water, of milk unchanged in taste, of wine delightful to drinkers, and of purified honey; Some listen to the prophet and on leaving ask the learned 'What did he say just now?'; God has sealed their hearts; Those killed in God's way: their deeds are not lost; he guides them and admits them to a Garden he has made known to them; The signs/portents (ashrat) of the Hour have already come; The prophet is told to ask forgiveness for his own sin and for the believing men and women; In battle, strike the necks of unbelievers; when they are subdued bind them, then free them as favor or for ransom until war lays down its burdens; People eat as sheep or cattle eat; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; If you help God he will help you and make your feet firm; The Hour will come upon them suddenly while they are unaware; Whether a bound captive is released or killed [contrast between the texts]; and 14 more.

Only in Kuntillet ʿAjrud plaster inscriptions - may he lengthen days; when El shone forth the mountains melted; blessing Baal on the day of war (Meshel 4.1.1, 4.2): A god (Baal, El) is blessed or his name invoked on the day of battle; A broken line speaks of holiness over the land; When God shines forth or appears, the mountains are crushed (d-k-k); YHWH is named by a place: YHWH of Samaria, YHWH of Teman; Blessing 'by YHWH ... and by his asherah' (lyhwh ... wlʾšrth); Prayer that the king's days be prolonged for generations and he be enthroned forever before God.

Only in Psalm 68, let God arise; the rider of the clouds marches from Sinai to his mountain: God rebukes the beast of the reeds (Egypt as hippopotamus or crocodile) and the herd of bulls; Envoys come from Egypt and Cush (Ethiopia) stretches out its hands to God; God ascends on high leading captives and receiving gifts among men; God's chariots are myriads, thousands upon thousands; the Lord among them as at Sinai; God says he will bring back (enemies or people) from Bashan and from the depths of the sea; God rides in the heaven of heavens of old and utters his mighty voice; Many-peaked mountains (Bashan) look with envy at the mountain God chose for his dwelling; A dove's wings covered with silver and its pinions with yellow-green gold; When Shaddai scattered kings, it snowed on Zalmon; A great host of women heralds (mevasserot) announces the victory and women divide the spoil; Dogs lick the blood of the slain enemies (or of the wicked king); The guilty are known by their marks and seized by the forelocks and the feet; and 10 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: 'Had it not been that the lord released me, I would have gone down to the netherworld' as a refrain of thanksgiving (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in 'My lord granted me relief': taken by the hand, the lion muzzled, the gravedigger's shovel wrested, pulled back from the river of death; 'had it not been for the lord' (Ludlul V 1-36): The god makes the attacker drop his weapon, muzzles the lion, takes the sling from the stalker, the shovel from the gravedigger, the knife from the mourner; God sends his angel and shuts the lions' mouths so they do not harm the innocent; God lifts the speaker out of the roaring pit and miry clay and sets his feet on a rock; The god rescued the sufferer from the pit and pulled him back from Hubur, the river of the netherworld; God turned the speaker's mourning into dancing, loosed his sackcloth and girded him with joy; God brought the speaker up from Sheol and kept him alive from going down to the pit (healing as resurrection); God wounds and binds up, strikes and his hands heal; God is 'the lifter of my head'; In adversity the god takes the sufferer's hand, slaps him awake with the right hand and raises his head with the left.

Only in The damned questioned; the blessed on facing couches; the tree of Zaqqum: Beside them are wide-eyed maidens of restrained glance, as if they were sheltered eggs; The blessed sit on couches facing one another; Gather the wrongdoers, their mates and what they worshipped and lead them to the path of hell; stop them, they will be questioned; One of the blessed recalls a companion who denied the resurrection, looks down and sees him in the midst of hell; The effects of wine on the drinker [contrast between the texts]; In the punishment the misled and their misleaders turn on each other in recrimination and share the punishment; Paradise drink from which they suffer no headache nor intoxication; Idolaters ask 'shall we abandon our gods for a mad poet?'; Reclining on couches and drinking wine, and how it is judged [contrast between the texts]; The blessed will not die except their first death and will not be punished; Opponents call the revelation jumbled dreams, a forgery, or the work of a poet; Rejecters reply 'we follow what we found our fathers upon'; and 4 more.

Only in The king turns against him; seven courtiers conspire; friends, kin and slaves become enemies; goods and offices given to others (Ludlul I 55-104): Whoever spoke well of the sufferer fell into a pit and whoever said 'Mercy on him' died quickly, while his slanderer prospered with a god's help; The sufferer's own slave curses him in the assembly and his slave girl slanders him before the crowd; Brothers, kin, guests, maidservants and servants all estrange themselves from the sufferer; his breath is strange to his wife; The king's heart hardens against his loyal official; courtiers conspire, each vowing to seize his life, post, office or household; The sufferer has no one to walk at his side and sees no champion or helper; The sufferer is pointed at in the street, eyed askance in the palace; his own city glowers at him like an enemy; The man who walked proudly learns to slink; his proud head bends to the ground, his broad chest is pushed aside by a youth; A clique of seven courtiers, one after another, swears to destroy the official and share out his position; The once eloquent sufferer is muzzled as with a snaffle; his lips fall silent, he becomes like a deaf-mute; The fallen man's possessions are shared out among the riffraff, his fields and canals ruined and his offices given to a stranger.

Only in Psalm 38 - the sick penitent abandoned by friends: God's arrows have sunk into the sufferer and his hand pressed down on him; Superscription 'to bring to remembrance' (lehazkir), linked to the memorial offering; Because of his sin the sufferer's wounds stink and fester; no soundness in his flesh; The speaker fasted in sackcloth for his enemies when they were sick; they repay evil for good; Plea: 'Do not rebuke me in your anger nor chasten me in your wrath'; The sinner must confess the sin he committed; Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in Demons from the netherworld attack; the body broken limb by limb; wallowing in dung; wasting; exorcist baffled; the tomb readied; enemies rejoice (Ludlul II 49-120): A demon has clothed himself in the sufferer's body as in a garment; The sufferer's diseases come as demons from the ends of heaven, the breast of the netherworld, the Apsu, the mountain: evil vapour, migraine, ghost, Lamashtu, ague; When the sufferer's ill-wisher hears of his plight, his face lights up; the woman who wished him ill is glad; In his illness the sufferer's eyes look but do not see, his ears are open but do not hear; The sick man's bed is his confinement, his house his jail, his own flesh his manacle and fetter; The sick man spends the night in his own dung like an ox and wallows in his excrement like a sheep; The sufferer's tomb is opened and his grave goods set out; lamentation for him is complete before he has died; From lack of food the sufferer's flesh wastes, his blood dries, his bones stick out covered only with skin, his features are unrecognisable; For the bereaved the bright daylight turns to darkness; 'I have escaped by the skin of my teeth'; bones cleave to skin; The exorcist recoils from the symptoms and cannot diagnose them; the diviner gives no time limit to the illness; At night his bones are pierced and his gnawing pains take no rest; and 7 more.

Only in Maqlû IV 115-122: 'Six are their bindings, seven are my undoings': Foreign women (Gutean, Elamite, Hanigalbatean) and native women tie magical bindings (knots) against the speaker; Whatever the witches bind by night the speaker releases by day, and what they bind by day he releases at night; Female sorcerers work their magic with knots and spittle; refuge or release is sought from it; The great gods (Ea and Marduk) hand the witch over to the fire god Girra; Refuge from the evil of those (women) who blow on knots (al-naffathat fi al-'uqad), i.e. knot-tying sorcery.

Only in Eliphaz continues - seek God, accept discipline: 'To which of the holy ones will you turn?': appeal to heavenly intercessors; The righteous will have a covenant with the stones of the field and peace with wild beasts; God catches the wise in their own craftiness; Suffering as divine discipline: happy the man whom God reproves; 'Man is born to trouble' (as sparks fly upward); The righteous come to the grave in ripe age like a sheaf gathered in its season; The 'sons of Resheph' (sparks, or the plague god's brood) fly upward; God wounds and binds up, strikes and his hands heal; Friend's doctrine: no innocent man ever perished; those who plow iniquity reap it.

matches.label: Female sorcerers work their magic with knots and spittle; refuge or release is sought from it
matches.note: IV:116-117 gutêti elamâtu habigalbatâtu / mārāt māti irakkasāni riksī, 'the Gutean, Elamite, Hanigalbatean women, the daughters of the land are tying knots (riksī) against me'; Q 113:4 wa-min sharri n-naffāthāti fī l-ʿuqad, 'from the evil of the women who blow on knots'. Only in Maqlû Ritual Tablet 1-31': the night rite begins — mouth-washing, the tallow figurine on the torch, prostration, Nuska on the roof: A tallow figurine with salt in its mouth is set on a burning torch so that it drips away over a bowl; The speaker raises a reed torch and kindles (sets alight) the fire god himself; May the witch's mouth be tallow and her tongue salt: her evil word drips away like tallow, her witchcraft dissolves like salt; A protective circle (zisurrû) is drawn with flour or gypsum around the burning vessel, the bed or the gates; Incense and offerings are made to the heavenly goddess on the roofs of the houses; A ritual tablet lists the incantations of a series by their opening words, each with the ritual act or material prescribed for it; The victim makes figurines of his witch and warlock and sets them before the gods (or hands them to the fire god) as the accused in his lawsuit.

Only in Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple I - iron tongues, slanders taken, the Ḫantašepa deities (CTH 416 §1-19): Wooden Ḫantašepa deities with blood-stained eyes and blood-red garments hold human heads and spears; Clay cups filled with a liquid (tarlipa-) are carried in and called 'blood'; A basin holds a 'heaven' of iron and one of copper with nine nails; Tongues of iron are put in the mouths of king and queen and the 'tongues' (slanders) of the population are taken from them; King and queen spit three times on a clay figurine, an ox, or a clay army that carries off their evil; After removing the royal couple's evil the expert sacrifices and asks the gods for mercy and protection; A clay army set on a bread, with a bronze dagger on it, is waved over or spat on by the royal couple and then buried; The participants eat and drink at the end of the rite; The carrier figurines and cups are buried in the earth and nailed down so that the evil may not come back up.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/12-ane-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Human deeds are nothing but wind, or are blown away by the wind (weight 6.8); The wicked are like chaff driven by the wind (weight 5.9). Pair score 12.7.

Only in Maqlû V 48-56: 'Whoever you are, O witch ... three months, ten days' — cord of the qadištu; blown away like chaff: The spell acts by command of Ištar, Dumuzi, Nanaya mistress of love, and Kanisurra mistress of witches; The witch has worked sorcery against the victim for a set span: three months, ten days and half a day; A roadside harlot referred to as a qedeshah ('consecrated woman'); Aromatic plants (thyme, sesame, kukru, a cone) are sent or raised against the witch to scatter her witchcraft and break her bond; The speaker sends sorcery and the evil word away on the wind; The witch's spells, bonds and knots are loosed and undone (pašāru, puṭṭuru) and her deeds nullified.

Only in Raging hell, the disowning of false gods, the split sky and the regretful wrongdoer: Thrown chained into a narrow place of hell, the damned cry for annihilation (thubūr); God turns the unbelievers' deeds into scattered dust (habāʾ manthūr); Unbelievers demand that angels be sent down or that they see their Lord; The damned are gathered on their faces to hell; God appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the guilty; Unbelievers ask why the Quran was not sent down all at once; it is sent in stages to strengthen the prophet's heart; On that day the wrongdoer bites his hands, wishing he had not taken so-and-so as a friend; The sky torn open for a descent from heaven [divergence between the texts]; When the damned are cast in they hear hell gasping/roaring as it boils, nearly bursting with rage; A request to see God, by the prophet or by the people [contrast between the texts]; The sky splits and is frail that day, and the angels are on its borders; Earlier messengers were only men who ate food and were not immortal; and 2 more.

matches.note: V:57 zīru ša tēpušāni tušēpišāni ana muhhīkunu ēpuša, 'the hate(-magic) you performed against me I perform against you' (paired with love-magic, râmu, in VII:75); Q 2:102 fa-yataʿallamūna minhumā mā yufarriqūna bihi bayna l-marʾi wa-zawjihi, 'they learn from the two what separates a man from his wife'. Only in Maqlû V 57-75: 'Hate-magic that you performed against me I perform against you' — smoke an abomination to heaven: The smoke of the burning witch is 'an abomination to heaven' (ikkib šamê); Talionic litany: the demon (utukku, ghost, Lamaštu, lilû) you caused to seize me, may it seize you; the anger and terror you inflicted on me, may it be inflicted on you; The figurines are burned with pure sulphur (kibrītu) before the god; The lilû, lilītu and ardat-lilî (Lilith-type wind demons) are named among the evil spirits to be driven off; A thing or conduct is declared an abomination (Sumerian niĝ2-gig, Akkadian ikkibu, Hebrew to'evah) to a god or king; Talionic formula: bewitch the witch with the witchcraft with which she bewitched me; A list of named kinds of witchcraft: love-magic and hate-magic, perversion of justice, Zikurrudû (cutting of life), muteness, pacification, madness; Named demons (udug, lamma, Dimme, Namtar, Asag) beset mankind, entering by night and not leaving a man alone; The evil plan devised against others returns upon the plotter's own head.

Only in Maqlû VIII 28-45: 'When the witch crossed the river' — Ea darkens her face; hands washed over her figurines: When the witch crossed the river and sat in the ferry, the sages of the apsû saw her, Ea darkened her face and struck her with epilepsy and trembling, and River cast her own fear upon her; The speaker washes his hands and body in pure Eridu spring water, removing every evil: bad dreams, signs, portents, bad entrails, demons, illness, curses and witchcraft; A list of named kinds of witchcraft: love-magic and hate-magic, perversion of justice, Zikurrudû (cutting of life), muteness, pacification, madness; Seven wisdoms (or seven sages/spirits of wisdom) attend the king or deity; The speaker sends sorcery and the evil word away on the wind; The divine River of the Ordeal (Id-lurugu) clears the just man and catches the evil.

Only in Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden: The angels are seen surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord; The blessed praise God who gave them the land (ard) as inheritance to settle in the Garden where they will; The Book (record) is laid down, the prophets and witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed with truth; Unbelievers are driven to hell in throngs (zumar) and the godfearing to the Garden in throngs; the gates open and the keepers address each; The keepers of the Garden greet the righteous 'Peace be upon you, you have been good; enter'; Lest a soul say 'Alas for my neglect of God' or 'If only I had another chance (karra)'; If you associate partners with God your deeds will come to nothing; At the first trumpet blast all in heaven and earth swoon (sa'iqa) except whom God wills; at the second they stand looking; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; The earth shines (lit up) with God's glory; The earth shines (lit up) with God's glory [divergence between the texts]; At the gate of the netherworld the gatekeepers question those who arrive [divergence between the texts]; and 14 more.

Only in Marduk's Address to the Demons 100'-128': 'May Asalluḫi extirpate you' — handed to the gatekeepers of the netherworld; exorcised by heaven and earth: The demons are handed to the gate of the Land of No Return, to the seven gatekeepers of Ereškigal, to Namtar and to the chief gatekeeper, who shuts the gate on them; A speaker adjures or swears 'by the life of heaven'; The evil powers are adjured 'by the life (nīš)' of named gods (Šamaš, Ea, Asalluḫi, Girra) to separate from the speaker; Death himself is driven away, netted and led down to the queen of the netherworld and her gatekeeper; The demons are exorcised by heaven and earth and by the primeval divine pairs (Anu and Antu, Enlil and Ninlil, Duri and Dari, Laḫmu and Laḫamu) and by everyday things (incense, shadow, daylight, path, seat); Exorcistic litany: be off, begone, depart, flee from my body; do not turn back, approach or draw near to my body.

Only in Telipinu myth, the gods under the hawthorn and the anger shut in bronze vessels below (CTH 324.1 §31-37): A magic goddess (Kamrušepa) halts the god's fury and takes from his body his anger, wrath, sin and sullenness; What goes into the place below cannot come out again [divergence between the texts]; The underworld or hell has seven doors or gates; The god's anger, wrath, sin and sullenness are to burn like brushwood, dry like malt, go out like fire, not flow back like water in a pipe; The gods hold assembly under the hatalkešna-tree (hawthorn), where long years lie and all the gods sit; The evil is shut in below under a closed cover; The god's anger must not go into the fruitful field, the garden or the forest, but take the road of the dark earth; The god's anger, wrath, sin and sullenness are sent down to the dark earth into cauldrons of bronze or iron with lids of lead; what goes in does not come up but perishes there.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The underworld has seven gates, bolted and opened one at a time (weight 5.8); The underworld is the land of no return, the road whose traveller never comes back (weight 5.4). Pair score 11.2.

Only in Nergal goes down, passes the seven gates and refuses all she offers (Nergal and Ereškigal, SB): The underworld queen orders the god who slighted her envoy brought before her (to die); One god alone does not stand or kneel before the underworld queen's envoy, an insult for which she demands him to be sent down to die; A god going down to the underworld is warned not to sit on the chair offered, eat its bread or meat, drink its beer, have his feet washed, or desire its queen when she bathes; The underworld as a land of darkness and deep shadow, without order, where light is like darkness; In the House of Dust the dead eat dust and clay, are clothed in feathers like birds and see no light; A messenger prostrates himself and kisses the ground before the deity he addresses.

Only in Telipinu myth, the gods under the hawthorn and the anger shut in bronze vessels below (CTH 324.1 §31-37): A magic goddess (Kamrušepa) halts the god's fury and takes from his body his anger, wrath, sin and sullenness; What goes into the place below cannot come out again [divergence between the texts]; The underworld or hell has seven doors or gates; The god's anger, wrath, sin and sullenness are to burn like brushwood, dry like malt, go out like fire, not flow back like water in a pipe; The gods hold assembly under the hatalkešna-tree (hawthorn), where long years lie and all the gods sit; The evil is shut in below under a closed cover; The god's anger must not go into the fruitful field, the garden or the forest, but take the road of the dark earth; The god's anger, wrath, sin and sullenness are sent down to the dark earth into cauldrons of bronze or iron with lids of lead; what goes in does not come up but perishes there.

Only in Ninurta's weapons and bow (Macranthropic Hymn to Ninurta): The divine bow's upper limb shakes heaven and its lower limb rouses the netherworld; its arrow is a star; The god's weapon swallows the sea like gruel, melts mountains like tallow, and turns stone mountains to ashes; The god's weapon is merciless: it accepts no supplication and hears no prayer; The warrior god deploys the south, north, east and west winds as his battle line against the enemy; The warrior god angrily piles up the skulls of the rebel land and scatters its chaff to the sky; A catalogue of monsters the warrior god has already slain (dragon, six-headed ram, Anzu bird, seven-headed snake...); A divine warrior lists his personified, named weapons (Mows-down-a-myriad, Crushes-a-myriad, the fifty-headed mace ...).

Only in Psalm 68, let God arise; the rider of the clouds marches from Sinai to his mountain: God rebukes the beast of the reeds (Egypt as hippopotamus or crocodile) and the herd of bulls; Envoys come from Egypt and Cush (Ethiopia) stretches out its hands to God; God ascends on high leading captives and receiving gifts among men; God's chariots are myriads, thousands upon thousands; the Lord among them as at Sinai; God says he will bring back (enemies or people) from Bashan and from the depths of the sea; God rides in the heaven of heavens of old and utters his mighty voice; Many-peaked mountains (Bashan) look with envy at the mountain God chose for his dwelling; A dove's wings covered with silver and its pinions with yellow-green gold; When Shaddai scattered kings, it snowed on Zalmon; A great host of women heralds (mevasserot) announces the victory and women divide the spoil; Dogs lick the blood of the slain enemies (or of the wicked king); The guilty are known by their marks and seized by the forelocks and the feet; and 10 more.

matches.note: The same gesture for breaking a sworn bond: Akkadian warkika tattasuk 'you have thrown (it) behind you' (nasāku 'throw'), Arabic nabadhūhu warāʾa ẓuhūrihim 'they threw it behind their backs' (nabadha 'throw'). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: An oath sworn before God's altar in the temple, judged by God (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Muarihu to the prefect: you bought back my slaves for 400 silver from Hehea the Egyptian; you swore in the house of the gods; give me their ransom silver and the rest, let there be no debt between us, we are one man (RS 15.0011): A creditor asks that the account be settled so that there be no debt between the two, 'for we are one man'; A slave redeemed (released for silver) from foreigners is sent back to his master, with a plea that no bad word come between the two rulers.

Only in Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform: The king kneels on a bronze platform in the court and spreads his hands to heaven; People away from Jerusalem or in exile pray in the direction of the land, city and temple; Captives confess in exile 'We have sinned, done wrong and acted wickedly'; 'Arise, YHWH, to your resting place, you and the ark of your might'; Prayer lists famine, pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, siege and sickness as occasions for prayer; A foreigner from a far land who hears of God's name comes to pray at the temple and is heard; 'There is no man who does not sin'; Temple called a 'house of zebul' (exalted dwelling), a place for God to dwell forever; 'O my servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy; God forgives all sins'; God has said he will dwell in thick darkness ('arafel); The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness; The direction faced in prayer [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

matches.label: Who fixes the shares of a man's children in his estate
matches.note: Opposite rulings on who decides the sons' shares (šīmtu). At Ugarit the father, before the king, 'decided the share of his sons', cleared one son 'as the sun is clear' of his father and brothers and gave houses, fields, cattle and slaves to two others. 4:11 takes the decision away from the father: 'God charges you concerning your children ... your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit: an ordinance from God'.

Only in Shalmaneser I of Assyria to Ibiranu of Ugarit: Tudhaliya of Hatti sent tablets of war and of peace, refused to return fugitives or to touch the oath-tablet before the Sun; at Nihriya I entered the Hittite army and made a great slaughter (RSO 07, 046): A king asks why we, who are brothers, are enemies to one another; An enemy king's messenger carries two tablets of hostility and one of peace, showing whichever suits the situation; A herald cries to the camp: put on your coats of mail and mount your chariots, the enemy king is drawn up and coming; Challenged to touch a tablet of oath before the sun god to prove his peaceful intent, a king refuses; The king boasts in the first person of how he crushes the enemy: foot on their neck, blood, nets, weapons; The treaty is sworn before a list of gods (including the vassal's own gods) or before the planets and stars, who guarantee it; Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back.

Only in Ḫatiya's ritual for the demoness Wišuriyant at the river (CTH 396.1.1 §1-6): The demoness Wišuriyant (the 'strangler') is brought down to the river, a tent set up, and she is washed with clay of the bank: 'see, I have purified you'; A fish with a cake in its mouth is released into the river to go to the mountain and the river and bring the offering to the demoness; The fish is thrown on the hearth and burned, and there is no smoke; Three pits are dug before the river bank and breads broken for the fate goddesses and the mother goddess, who are asked for life, health, vigour, long years and sight; The deity is asked to give the patient life, health, vigour, long years and the sight of the eyes; The Sun god of heaven is called as witness of the offering: if the demoness hides anything, you shall know it; The ritualist sets food and drink before the angry god and invokes him (mugai-): eat, drink, still your hunger and thirst, come back and be at peace.

Only in SAA 2 1: Treaty of Šamšī-Adad V with Marduk-zākir-šumi of Babylon (clauses and curses): Curse: may the god pour out the oath-breaker's life like water; Curse: may the storm god withhold rain from heaven and flood from the deep, and the wise god dam the rivers at their source; Curse: may the god turn the oath-breaker's land into a flood-ruin mound and his cities into tells; Curse: may the high god decree for the oath-breaker a reign of sighing, few days and years of want; Curse: may the moon god clothe the oath-breaker in skin disease (saharšubbû) like a garment, so that he roams the open country; The sky over you bronze and the earth under you iron; rain turned to dust; Curse: may the gods break the oath-breaker's sceptre and overthrow his kingship; Disobedience punished by scattering among the nations.

Only in Report even father and mother; if a city, a house or one man sins (CTH 133 §§5-12): If a city within the land sins it is killed with its men; if a house within a city sins that house dies with its people; if one man sins, he alone; The vassal people's troop levy is fixed (from 150 to 60 heavy-armed men) and must be of free men, not servants or hirelings; Whether an offender's household and kin share his punishment [contrast between the texts]; Any letter or messenger arriving from the enemy or a foreign land must be seized and sent on to the king; Loyalty to the lord overrides a listed series of kin: father, mother, son, brother, kinsman; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

Über Rasur. Die Lücke am Anfang von Vs. 6' reicht für ca. 8 Zeichen, von denen ein Teil auf das Prädikat des vorausgehenden Kolons entfällt. Lesungsvorschlag von Del Monte 1981, 218 (gegen seine ältere Auffassung als Ortsname in Del Monte-Tischler 1978, 371); so auch Beckman 1999, 26 und CHD P, 5b. Da -wa nicht die Partikel der direkten Rede sein kann, hat man es wohl als irreguläre Stützsilbe zwischen -ŠU und -aš zu betrachten. Für eine weitere ungewöhnliche Graphie in diesem Text s. KUR-e-TAM in Vs. 3'. Man beachte die Abwesenheit der scriptio plena. Die Autographie in KUB 36 bietet vor der Lücke ein AŠ (Del Monte 1981, 215 liest na-aš [ ), aber nach Foto scheint diese Lesung schwierig; das beschädigte Zeichen ist vielleicht besser als -a[m- zu lesen. Das Kolon ist von dem folgenden durch einen schrägen Keil getrennt. Der Paralleltext KBo 19.39 + KUB 8.81 (CTH 41.II.1) trennt die entsprechenden Kola in Vs. II 4'-5' durch einen Abschnittsstrich. Dies könnte auf eine nachträgliche Einfügung hinweisen. Für die Emendation <Ú-UL> nach der Parallele KUB 8.81+ Rs. III 3 s. schon Petschow 1963, 244 Anm. 40. Petschow 1963, 245, Anm. 49: „Es liegt wohl eine (bedingte) Selbstverfluchung vor“. *...* über Rasur.

Only in SAA 2 5: Esarhaddon's treaty with Baal, king of Tyre: deputy, shipwreck, ports, and curses by the gods of the West: Curse: may the storm gods (the Baals) raise an evil wind against the oath-breaker's ships, loosen their moorings, tear out their masts and sink them in the sea; The overlord entrusts named ports and trade routes along the coast (Akko, Dor, Philistia, Byblos, Lebanon) to the vassal; An Assyrian royal deputy (qēpu) is set over the vassal: the vassal must heed him and may not open the king's letters without him; Curse: may a foreign enemy divide the oath-breaker's possessions; Curse: may the gods hand the land to destruction and the people to deportation, and take away food from the mouth, clothing from the body and oil for anointing; If a vassal's ship is wrecked on the overlord's coast, its cargo belongs to the overlord but the people aboard are not harmed and are sent home; Curse: may the gods (Bethel and Anat-Bethel) hand the oath-breaker over to a man-eating lion; Curse: may the healing goddess put unhealing illness and a lasting wound in the oath-breaker's body; may he bathe in blood and pus as in water; Curse: may the war goddess make the oath-breaker kneel or sit bound at the feet of his enemy; Curse: may the war goddess break the oath-breaker's bow in fierce battle; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; Curse: may the gods break the oath-breaker's sceptre and overthrow his kingship; and 2 more.

Only in Messengers in their people's tongue; Moses and the days of God; the threatened messengers (Surah 14:1-17): In hell death comes from every side, yet the damned does not die; If you and all on earth disbelieve, God is free of need and praiseworthy; God proclaims: if you are grateful I will give you more; if ungrateful, my punishment is severe; The rejecting peoples thrust their hands into their mouths at the messengers; Every messenger is sent speaking the language of his own people to make things clear; The people reject their messengers: 'you are only humans like us'; Formula on trust: let whoever trusts, trust; we trust in our god / on God let the trusters trust; Every messenger is sent speaking the language of his own people to make things clear [divergence between the texts]; The elite threaten the prophet and believers: expulsion unless they return to the old religion; Moses is told to remind his people of 'the days of God'; In hell they taste no coolness nor drink except boiling water (hamim) and dark, foul fluid (ghassaq), or drink from a boiling spring; God brings believers out of darknesses into light; false gods lead others from light into darkness; and 4 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed (weight 6.1); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 11.0.

Only in SAA 2 8: Zakūtu (Naqiʾa), queen mother, imposes a loyalty oath for her grandson Ashurbanipal: The queen mother herself imposes a loyalty oath on the royal family and the whole land in favour of her grandson the king; If the sworn party hears of a plot to kill the king, or of men inciting revolt among courtiers, kin or the people, he must report it and seize and kill the plotters; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; The treaty is sworn before a list of gods (including the vassal's own gods) or before the planets and stars, who guarantee it.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 21.6.

Only in SAA 2 9: Loyalty oath of Babylonian allies to Ashurbanipal after Šamaš-šuma-ukīn's revolt: Curse: may the god uproot the oath-breaker above among the living and deprive his ghost of water below in the earth; Curse: may the high god decree for the oath-breaker a reign of sighing, few days and years of want; Any letter or messenger arriving from the enemy or a foreign land must be seized and sent on to the king; Curse: may the war goddess make the oath-breaker kneel or sit bound at the feet of his enemy; Madness, blindness and confusion; groping at noon like the blind in darkness; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The servant declares: 'Whatever my lord says, I will do'.

Only in Slander, the great kings, Ahhiyawa erased, embargo on Assyria (CTH 105 §§10-14): The king of Ahhiyawa is written among the great kings of equal rank and then erased from the tablet; The vassal's merchants may not go to the enemy land (Assyria), nor may its merchants enter or cross the vassal's land; one who comes is to be seized and sent to the king; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord.

Only in The case against Mita, the neighbours' oath and duties (CTH 146 §15-19): The king threatens that whoever does not fight the rebels he will kill first, before attacking the rebel city; The loyal subjects must at once 'bathe their hands in blood' against the rebels before the king's army arrives; Everything must be handed over: not even (as much as) a woollen thread may be held back; The rebel must be handed over together with his wife, sons, grandsons, servants, cattle, sheep and all property; The vassal is said to have sinned again and again and to have utterly broken the sworn word; The vassal must not send his messenger to the enemy nor admit the enemy's messenger into his presence or his city gate; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help.

Only in SAA 2 13: Treaty with an Arab ruler: no peace with the enemy, no secret messages, report every hostile word: The sworn party must not send messages secretly, 'whether by the hand of a fish of the sea or a bird of the sky'; The vassal is bound to fear the overlord and do what is good for him; Forbidden: sending secret messages to the overlord's (God's) enemy.

Only in Šunaššura treaty, Hittite version (CTH 41.II.2): Mittani, help 'if it suits him', fugitives, wife and children as compensation: Whoever hides a fugitive in his house must give twelve persons in compensation, or himself be killed; a hiding slave's master may forfeit him; An oath by YHWH settles a dispute without witnesses; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Forbidden: sending secret messages to the overlord's (God's) enemy (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in SAA 2 13: Treaty with an Arab ruler: no peace with the enemy, no secret messages, report every hostile word: The sworn party must not send messages secretly, 'whether by the hand of a fish of the sea or a bird of the sky'; The vassal is bound to fear the overlord and do what is good for him; The vassal must not make peace or come to terms ('put his mouth') with the overlord's enemy; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

Only in Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge: Abraham and those with him are an excellent example: they declared themselves quit of their people and their gods, with enmity until they believe; Except Abraham's saying to his father 'I will ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power for you before God'; They despair of the hereafter as the unbelievers despair of those in the graves; Believers must not take God's enemies, who expelled the prophet, as allies (awliya') or secretly show them affection; Prohibition of killing one's children; Do not hold on to marriage ties with unbelieving women; dowries are reckoned between the communities; Believing women who emigrate are to be examined; if believers, they are not returned to the unbelievers, whose dowries are repaid; The women's pledge (bay'at al-nisa'): not to associate anything with God, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, bring a fabricated slander, or disobey in what is right; Abraham declares to his father and people that he is free of what they worship, except the one who created him; Dissolving marriages with women outside the community [divergence between the texts]; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Neither your blood-ties nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; and 10 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.5.

Only in SAA 2 15 i-iii: no other king, no oath to another lord, report evil words even from the prince's kin: Relative or friend who secretly entices to other gods must be stoned, your hand first; Loyalty to the sovereign overrides kin: brothers, fathers, sons, clan are named and not exempted [divergence between the texts]; Command not to add to or subtract from the divine words; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

Only in Al-Mujadila: the woman who disputed, the zihar formula and its expiation; God the fourth of three; the party of God: Before a private consultation with the prophet give charity (sadaqa); the rule is then relaxed; God has written: 'I will surely prevail, I and my messengers'; They greet the prophet with a greeting with which God did not greet him (al-sam for al-salam); When told to make room in assemblies, make room, and God will make room for you; rise when told to rise; The party of Satan (hizb al-shaytan) are the losers; the party of God (hizb Allah) are the successful; Secret counsels (najwa) for sin, aggression and disobedience are of Satan; confer rather in piety; God has heard the woman who argued with the prophet about her husband and complained to God (Khawla, 'she who disputes'); Expiation for zihar before touching again: free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor; There is no secret conversation of three but God is the fourth, nor of five but he is the sixth, wherever they are; God is well pleased with them and they with him (radiya llahu 'anhum wa-radu 'anhu); Expiation in steps according to what one can afford [divergence between the texts]; God will put his law within the people and write it on their hearts; and 14 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet: Formula: in future days the national god is 'your god' and the crown prince 'your lord'; your sons and grandsons shall fear him; The sworn must not perform a rite to undo the oath (anointing with tallow from the gods, binding something on the thigh, 'turning back' or 'releasing' the oath); An oath or profession spoken with the lips (tongues) only, not with the whole heart; The sworn must take the oath with their whole heart, not with the lips only, and teach it to their sons who come after; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them; The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; Command not to add to or subtract from the divine words.

Only in Protect the king's line; do not act like Mašturi; be ready to die (CTH 105 §§5-9): A vassal betrays his benefactor's son, asking 'shall I protect a bastard?', and is held up in a later treaty as a warning; The great king takes the vassal by the hand, gives him his sister in marriage, makes him his brother-in-law and king of his land; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it (weight 6.8); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet: Formula: in future days the national god is 'your god' and the crown prince 'your lord'; your sons and grandsons shall fear him; The sworn must not perform a rite to undo the oath (anointing with tallow from the gods, binding something on the thigh, 'turning back' or 'releasing' the oath); An oath or profession spoken with the lips (tongues) only, not with the whole heart; The sworn must take the oath with their whole heart, not with the lips only, and teach it to their sons who come after; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; Command not to add to or subtract from the divine words; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

Only in Alakšandu's chosen son, mutual protection, the fugitive conspirator (CTH 76 §§6-9): If the vassal's brother or kin rebels and seeks the throne, the overlord will recognise only the vassal, not accept the rebel, and destroy the rebel's land; The overlord promises that the son the vassal will beget shall be king after him and shall be protected as his father is; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy.

Shared motifs, rarest first: An oath or profession spoken with the lips (tongues) only, not with the whole heart (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet: Formula: in future days the national god is 'your god' and the crown prince 'your lord'; your sons and grandsons shall fear him; The sworn must not perform a rite to undo the oath (anointing with tallow from the gods, binding something on the thigh, 'turning back' or 'releasing' the oath); The sworn must take the oath with their whole heart, not with the lips only, and teach it to their sons who come after; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them; The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; Command not to add to or subtract from the divine words; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

Only in Al-Fath: the clear opening, the sakina, the hand of God over their hands and the bedouin who stayed behind: The bedouin who stayed behind plead that wealth and families kept them busy and ask for forgiveness insincerely; No blame on the blind, the lame or the sick (for not going out to fight); Those who pledge allegiance to the prophet pledge to God; 'the hand of God is over their hands'; To God belong the hosts (junud) of the heavens and the earth; Those who stayed behind ask to follow when spoils are in prospect and are refused; God forgives the prophet his past and future sins; 'We have opened for you a clear opening/victory (fath mubin)' (the Hudaybiya treaty); The divine presence (root sh-k-n / s-k-n) dwelling on the sanctuary or sent down into hearts [divergence between the texts]; Prophet stakes his authority: 'If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me'; Oath sworn by raising the hand to God; Whether those who stayed behind share in the spoil [contrast between the texts]; Who is exempted from going out to war [contrast between the texts]; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Only in SAA 2 15 vi: the sworn speak: 'if we rebel, make terms with his enemy, or conceal sedition': If the sworn party hears of a plot to kill the king, or of men inciting revolt among courtiers, kin or the people, he must report it and seize and kill the plotters; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; The vassal must not make peace or come to terms ('put his mouth') with the overlord's enemy.
