Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly.

Pair score 102.6.

Only in SAA 2 15 vii: further curses and simile curses (bronze sky, mule's seed, iron plough, ewe and lambs, oath entering the body): Treaty enactment: an animal brought not for sacrifice but for the oath is dismembered with the words 'this head is not the lamb's head, it is the head of X'; as it is cut, so may the oath-breaker be; Curse: in famine the mother bars her door against her own daughter; you eat the flesh of your sons, grind their bones instead of grain; man eats man and wears his skin; Curse: may the scribe god who bears the tablet of fates erase your name and destroy your seed from the land; Curse: may the sun god cast his bronze bird-snare and inescapable net over you and not let you out; Curse: may your corpses find no burial; may dogs and pigs (or eagle and jackal) eat your flesh, their bellies your grave; The evil diseases of Egypt removed from the obedient or brought on the disobedient; Simile curse: 'just as this (object, animal, wax figure, ewe, water-skin) is treated, so may it be done to you'.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: analogical and simile curses I: iron earth and bronze sky to the stinking bug (SAA 2 6:526-611): Curse: as honey is sweet, may the blood of your wives and children be sweet in your mouth; Simile curse: as these lambs are slit and their entrails rolled round their feet, so may yours and your children's be; Simile curse: may your flesh and your family's be consumed like the flesh of a chameleon; Simile curse: as a honeycomb is pierced with holes, may holes be bored in your flesh while you live; Curse: may you be like a fly in the hand of your enemy, who crushes you; Simile curse: as snake and mongoose do not share a hole but plot each other's death, may husband and wife not share house or bed; Curse: instead of rain may burning coals rain on your land; Simile curse enacted with an object or animal: 'just as this X is ..., so may you be ...'; Simile curse: as a wax figure burns in fire and a clay figure dissolves in water, so may your form be burned and sink; Simile curse: as malt in the mash does not sprout, may your seed vanish from the land; The king catches fleeing enemies like gazelles, wild asses, fish or birds in nets and traps; Curse: you will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6). Pair score 11.3.

Only in Slander, the great kings, Ahhiyawa erased, embargo on Assyria (CTH 105 §§10-14): The king of Ahhiyawa is written among the great kings of equal rank and then erased from the tablet; The vassal's merchants may not go to the enemy land (Assyria), nor may its merchants enter or cross the vassal's land; one who comes is to be seized and sent to the king; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord; The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The sworn speak in the first person ('if we ...') and call on the named gods to seek out their seed if they rebel (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: the vassals' first-person oath and further curses by Aššur, Palil, Ea, Girra (SAA 2 6:494-525): Curse: may water and oil become taboo to you; Curse: may the god of the deep give you water of death to drink and fill you with dropsy; Curse: may the oath-breakers' seed and images be burned in fire and their torch extinguished in water; Your corpse food for birds and beasts with no one to frighten them away; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

Only in CTH 52.I §11-12: the gods of Mittani; Šattiwazza and the Hurrians curse themselves - tamarisk, water of the gutter, smoke, salt; their blessing in the lord's shade: Self-curse: as salt has no seed, so may we have no seed; like a dissolved lump of salt may we not be restored; Self-curse: as a felled tree (tamarisk/acacia) puts out no shoot, so may we have no seed; Self-curse: may we rise like smoke to heaven; The vassal asks that the great king love him and his land as he loves his own lands, sons and his own tablet; The sworn people pray to eat a rich harvest in their lord's shade (ṣillu) while he goes before them; Mitra, Varuna, Indra and the Nāsatyas are invoked as witnesses of a Mittani treaty; Mortality likened to water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up; Treaty blessing: may the land be restored as of old, grow rich and lie down (rabāṣu) in peace; Treaty curse: may the gods overturn your throne; The vassal may keep concubines but may take no wife above or equal to the overlord's sister or daughter, who must be chief wife; The people and lands relax under the king's broad protection (an-dul3, 'shade'); Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed (weight 6.1); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 16.6.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: fight a usurper; resist incitement to set the prince against his father and brothers (SAA 2 6:302-372): The treaty quotes the envious instigators' persuasive speech ('where is what the gods said about him? ... guard your lives') to forbid it; Jealous brothers spread slander and falsehood against the chosen heir and turn the father's heart against him; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

Only in The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39): A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content; Do not say even 'uff' to aged parents nor rebuke them; speak to them gently; Do not walk the earth exultantly: you cannot split the earth nor reach the mountains in height; Do not keep your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it out fully: moderation in spending; Lower the wing of humility to parents and pray 'Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when small'; Squanderers are brothers of the devils; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content [divergence between the texts]; Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and heart will be questioned; Do not kill your children for fear of poverty; God provides for them and you; Do not speak harshly or arrogantly to your parent; A decreed order includes reverence and humility toward father and mother [divergence between the texts]; and 21 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God's righteousness will be told to a people yet unborn (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Assurbanipal's hymn to Aššur (SAA 3 1): The god is creator of those of heaven and earth, fashioner of the mountains and creator of the gods; A hymn opens with the singer's resolve: 'let me magnify the god, make his greatness manifest, extol his name'; A deity is 'wide of ear' and knows everything; All the Igigi kneel before the god and the Anunnaki praise his name from their sanctuaries; The warrior god (Ninurta, or Nabû in commentary) defeats and kills the Anzu bird; The god's ingenuity is like tangled threads no eye can follow; he is his own counsellor and no one comprehends his deeds; 'Who can change the word that An, the king, has spoken?': the high god's decree cannot be altered; 'Who can change the word that has gone out?' / 'none can change his words'.

Only in Epic fragment of Assurbanipal's Elamite war: Madaktu broken, graves violated, Nabû-bēl-šumāti (SAA 3 22): The graves of the enemy (Elamite kings) are violated; In his anger the king breaks the enemy's royal city; The gods dwelling in a conquered city are carried off with its property; A hymn closes by asking the deity to bless the king who reveres her: firm throne, long life, offspring, abundance.

Only in Three vassals under one oath; disputes before the king (CTH 67 §§8-11): A dispute between fellow vassals is not to be pursued by rash hostility but brought before the great king, who judges it and sets them back on the road; Fellow vassals bound by one oath must be of one mind: not harm, kill or seize one another, not shelter one another's runaways, and fight a common enemy together; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself.

Only in El takes two women at the shore; they bear Shahar and Shalim and the gracious gods, who are sent to the holy desert for seven years (KTU 1.23 30-76): The high god's wives give birth to Shahar and Shalim, Dawn and Dusk; The high god shoots a bird from the sky, plucks it and roasts it on the coals as a sign of his potency; The high god sees two women at a basin, takes them into his house and, according to their cry, makes them his wives (not daughters) for ever; The high god walks along the shore of the sea, the shore of the deep; The newborn gods put one lip to the earth and one to the heavens; birds of the sky and fish of the sea enter their mouths, yet they are not sated; Gifts are lifted up to the Sun, the Lady, and to the fixed stars; The newborn gods are sent to dwell as strangers among stones and trees in the holy desert for seven full years, eight cycles; The wanderers from the desert ask the watchman of the sown land to open and give them bread and wine; Good news of a birth brought to the father: 'a son (a bull) is born to you'; The high god asks the arriving goddess if she is hungry or thirsty, offers bread and wine, or asks if 'the hand of El the king' (his love) stirs her; Newborn gods suck at the nipples of the mother goddess's breast; The gracious gods are 'those who split day from day'; and 1 more.

Only in Mock incantation against Bēl-ēṭir son of Ibâ (SAA 3 30): An invective quotes an obscene oath of its target; An invective is framed as a mock incantation (beginning with the incantation rubric); A satirical text mocks a named official as low-born, filthy, sexually degraded and boastful.

Only in Nun: by the pen; the prophet's great character; the swearer, slanderer and base-born man branded on the snout: God threatens: 'We shall brand him on the snout (khurtum)'; The deniers wish the prophet would compromise (tudhin) so they would compromise; The prophet is not mad; he has an unfailing reward and is of a great moral character (khuluq 'azim); Mamzer excluded from the assembly to the tenth generation; Oath 'Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe'; The ruler is told not to listen to, or obey, the slanderer; The man who goes about (comes and goes) with words, setting brothers / people against each other; A go-between who carries slander between men; A mark (tav) is put on the foreheads of those who sigh over the city's abominations so the destroyers spare them; Do not obey every contemptible swearer, backbiter going about with slander, hinderer of good, coarse and moreover 'zanim' (base-born, ignoble); The prophet is no soothsayer (kahin), no madman, no poet awaiting the accident of fate; God will put his hook in the enemy king's nose and his bit in his lips and lead him back; and 4 more.

Only in Underworld Vision: the dead king, Nergal's warning, the prince's terror and the scribe's report (SAA 3 32 rev. 22-35): In the netherworld vision the seer is shown the corpse (pagru) of a great king, his own father, conqueror from sunrise to sunset; A scribe who hears the vision takes it to heart and reports it to the palace as a warning (namburbû) for himself; After the vision the seer runs into the street like a man who has shed blood, crying 'woe, my heart!' and putting dust of the street into his mouth; The god releases the visionary from the netherworld with a commission: may this word lodge like a thorn in your heart, go up and proclaim it; He awoke, and it was a dream; One is guilty even for a sin committed without knowing; The king is to rule from the rising to the setting of the sun, from the upper to the lower sea.

Only in Al-Sajda: creation, the angel of death, and the two fates: Whenever the damned try to get out of the fire they are driven back into it; On the Day of the Opening/Victory (al-fath) the unbelievers' faith will not benefit them; A divine day whose measure is a thousand (or fifty thousand) years of human reckoning; God makes people taste the nearer punishment before the greater one, that they may return; The angel of death (malak al-mawt), put in charge of humans, takes their souls; The guilty, heads bowed before their Lord, beg to be returned to do good; God's word: 'I will fill hell with jinn and humans all together'; No soul knows what delight of the eyes is hidden in store for the righteous; Whether Moses wrote the book or was given it [divergence between the texts]; Man described by the lowly bodily substance he is made of [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; What goes into the place below cannot come out again [divergence between the texts]; What God did when the six days of creation were done [divergence between the texts]; and 14 more.

Only in Underworld Vision: before Nergal's throne; Išum intercedes; the prince is sent back (SAA 3 32 rev. 11-21): A divine adviser (Išum) intercedes with the angry god who wants to kill the seer: 'Do not let the young man die'; The angry god's voice roars over the seer like a raging storm; The netherworld king (Nergal) sits on a royal throne with a crown, holding two fierce maces, lightning flashing from his arms, the Anunnaki kneeling right and left; Overwhelmed by the god's radiance, the seer trembles, kisses the god's feet and kneels; The seer is seized by the forelock (abūsātu) and dragged before the enthroned god; The vision seizes the prophet with labor pains; he is bowed down, terrified and his twilight pleasure turns to trembling; The god releases the visionary from the netherworld with a commission: may this word lodge like a thorn in your heart, go up and proclaim it; A man is seized by the forelock and brought before the judging deity [divergence between the texts]; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates.

Only in Vision of abominations in the temple - image of jealousy, animal chamber, Tammuz, sun worship: Idolaters 'put the branch (zemorah) to their nose', an obscure cultic gesture; Seventy elders stand with censers in hand offering incense in the dark, each in his chamber of images; A human-like figure of fire from the waist down and gleaming like hashmal (amber/electrum) from the waist up; Though they cry in God's ears with a loud voice, he will not listen; An idol called 'the image (semel) of jealousy that provokes jealousy' stands at the north gate of the temple; Prophet is told to dig through a wall and enters through the opening; Hidden temple chamber whose walls are engraved all around with creeping things, loathsome beasts and idols; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; About twenty-five men with their backs to the temple bow eastward to the sun between the porch and the altar; Prophet in exile is brought 'in visions of God' to the Jerusalem temple; Elders of the people come and sit before the prophet in his house to inquire; The glory of YHWH appears in the cloud; and 5 more.

matches.label: Whether a man can die on a day other than his fixed one, and by whose command [neutral]
matches.note: ina qibīt Aššur bēliya ... 3 arhī ul umallīma ina ūme lā šīmtišu urruhiš imtūt 'at the command of Aššur my lord ... he did not complete three months; on a day not his fate he died suddenly' ~ wa-mā kāna li-nafsin an tamūta illā bi-idhni llāhi kitāban muʾajjalā 'no soul may die except by God's leave, at a term written' (3:145). Only in Lifted-hand prayers to Adad after lightning strikes a temple (šuʾila Adad 3 incipit and 4): Lightning, thunderbolts or hail sent from heaven at the god's command strike what he wills [divergence between the texts]; When the storm god's thunder or lightning has struck a city's temple, palace or wall, or burned a god's statue, a prayer and ritual are performed; The storm god gathers the clouds, waters the scorching land and rains down plenty, so the mountains and fields rejoice; The sky god speaks: 'I am the only one among the gods with the great divine powers; my utterance shall never be altered'; Formula: his call was heard, and the god accepted his prayer and supplication; The petitioner closes: grant my plea, that I may proclaim your greatness and sing your praises to the widespread peoples; A prayer is labelled a lifted-hand prayer (šuʾila) and followed by its ritual: roof swept, pure water sprinkled, portable altar, censer of juniper, libation, recitation three times, prostration.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds in flight, wings spread, praise the deity; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The god titled 'light of heaven(s) and earth' (nūr šamāmī u qaqqari / nūru l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ), and those deprived of light walk in darkness; and 11 more.

Only in Lifted-hand prayer to Ea, with Banītu-tēreš's insertion against portents and witchcraft (šuʾila Ea 1a): The god is addressed as creator of humans and of the womb; By the wise god's 'incantation of life' the moribund recover and the bonds of witches are released; The wise god (Enki) is praised as great farmer, carpenter, sage (abgal) and master of purification rites; Closing blessing: may heaven rejoice over the deity, the deep be glad, and all the gods bless and magnify her; God is 'the lifter of my head'; The god brings the river flood and abundance, makes plenty sprout in seas and reed-beds, and creates grain, the life of the people; The god turns evil signs and portents (eclipse, broken chariot part, ants in the house, bad dreams) to good: may their evil not draw near the petitioner or his house; The witch's spells, bonds and knots are loosed and undone (pašāru, puṭṭuru) and her deeds nullified; A prayer is labelled a lifted-hand prayer (šuʾila) and followed by its ritual: roof swept, pure water sprinkled, portable altar, censer of juniper, libation, recitation three times, prostration.

Only in Sincerity, daybreak and mankind: God's unity and the two refuges: Refuge from the evil of darkness (or the moon) when it settles (ghasiq idha waqab); Refuge from the evil of an envier when he envies (evil eye); God is al-Samad (the Eternal Refuge, the solid one who needs nothing); Triple title: Lord of mankind, King of mankind, God of mankind; Refuge from the evil of the slinking whisperer (al-waswas al-khannas) who whispers in people's breasts, from jinn and humans; Calling on a divine name or seeking refuge with God protects a person in the dark of night; God does not beget and was not begotten [contrast between the texts]; A deity is called king of (all) mankind; Protection against beings or evil of the night, invoked with the coming of dawn; Protective formula 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of...' (qul a'udhu bi-rabbi) against named evils; Sorcery is done by binding or knotting; Psalm used as protection against demons and harm (later amulet and 'song of plagues'); and 10 more.

Only in Lifted-hand prayers to Ea, creator of everything (šuʾila Ea 1b and 2): The god is said to have created the great gods and to render their verdicts; All the Igigi kneel before the god and the Anunnaki praise his name from their sanctuaries; Prayer that whoever sees the petitioner speak his praise and that his praise be placed in people's mouths; The god is creator of everything, without whom nothing whatsoever was formed and no lord could exist.

Only in Šuʾila to Ištar 1: 'O valiant Ištar, cherished among the goddesses': Hymnic confidence: how sweet it is to pray to the god, how near is the god's hearing; The love-and-war goddess is the twin sister of the sun god and shares his office of judging the world; Personified Justice stands at the deity's right hand and Favour at the left, protective spirits going before and behind; The prayer or incantation is to be recited three times; Incense and juniper are burned as an offering before a deity; The deity reverses fortunes: makes the weak strong, the unfortunate fortunate, raises the fallen; The deity is hailed as the torch, light or luminary of heaven and earth; Vow of praise: 'save me, so that I may declare your greatness and sing your praises'; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'; A prayer is labelled a lifted-hand prayer (šuʾila) and followed by its ritual: roof swept, pure water sprinkled, portable altar, censer of juniper, libation, recitation three times, prostration.

Only in The fast of Ramadan: Fasting prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you; Eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn; Those able only with hardship may ransom fast days by feeding a poor person (fidya); Spouses not approached while in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques; Marital relations permitted on fast nights; spouses are garments for one another; Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down; The sick and the traveler may make up missed fast days later; A gift (bribe) from or to the powerful in court, to deprive another of his right; Making the judge take a bribe to win a case [divergence between the texts]; Marital relations during a fast [contrast between the texts]; What the annual fast is tied to [divergence between the texts]; Money or a gift passes to the judge of a case to pervert the verdict; and 6 more.

matches.note: Parched in the desert, Sinuhe hears the lowing of cattle; 'the chief among them, who had been in Egypt, recognised me; he gave me water and boiled milk for me', and Sinuhe goes with him to his tribe (W2:46/2-51/2). The fugitive from Egypt is received at the water by an elder of the herding people; the giving of water is reversed, to the fugitive in Sinuhe, by the fugitive in the Quran.

matches.label: What drives a man of the Egyptian court to flee Egypt in fear [neutral]
matches.note: Sinuhe hears the messenger speaking of the king's death, 'my heart was distraught, my arms spread, trembling fell on all my limbs', and runs, 'I did not expect to live after this' (W2:24-31); to his host he insists 'I was not spat upon, I was not reproached' (W2:64). Mūsā, after the killing of 28:15, is warned by a running man: 'the chiefs are conspiring to kill you, so leave'; 'he left it fearful, watchful (khāʾifan yataraqqab)' (28:20-21). The panicked flight from Egypt of a man of the court in fear for his life; the cause differs: no crime at all, against a killing.

sides.note: Ammunenshi: 'you will be well with me (nfr tw ḥnꜥ =j), you will hear the speech of Egypt'; 'why have you come here? has something happened at the Residence?'; Sinuhe answers with a half-truth, said 'as if' (m jwms) (W2:54-63). In 28:25 Mūsā 'told him the story', and the chief answers 'do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people'. The host's question, the fugitive's account and the assurance of safety; the honesty of the account differs.

sides.note: Bata as a bull to his wife: 'See, I am still alive.' 'Who are you?' 'I am Bata. I know that when you had the cedar felled it was to keep me from living' (15_8/2-15_10). matches.label: The grounds the young man gives for refusing his master's wife [neutral]
matches.note: Bata: 'you are like a mother to me, your husband like a father; he who is older than I raised me (sḫpr wj). What is this great crime (btꜣ,w ꜥꜣ)?' (3_9/2-3_10/3). Yūsuf: 'God's refuge! He is my lord (rabbī), he made my lodging good (aḥsana mathwāya); wrongdoers do not prosper' (12:23). Both refusals rest on the husband's past kindness to the youth; the Quran adds the refuge in God, the Egyptian adds the mother-and-father kinship and names no god.

Only in Two Brothers: sent home for seed, Bata is propositioned by his elder brother's wife and refuses: Refusing, the hero tells the woman she is like a mother to him and her husband like a father, and calls her proposal a great crime; The hero promises to tell no one of the woman's proposal and orders her never to speak of it again; The temptress promises the young man fine clothes as reward for lying with her; A man in fury becomes 'like a leopard (of the south)'.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 140 more.

matches.label: How God made the human mate, and for what purpose
matches.note: Re-Harakhti to Khnum: 'fashion a woman for Bata so that he does not dwell (ḥmsi̯) alone' (9_6/2); Khnum makes her more beautiful than any woman. Q 7:189: God 'made from it its mate that he might dwell (li-yaskuna) with her'. A god makes a wife for a lone man for the purpose of companionship. Here she is made from nothing named, for one hero; in the Quran from the first soul itself, for all humankind. Both couples then go wrong: the wife betrays Bata's heart, and the couple of 7:190 'ascribe partners'.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/25-ane-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: How God made the human mate, and for what purpose (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Two Brothers: Bata alone in the Valley of the Cedar; the Ennead has Khnum fashion him a wife; the Seven Hathors: A god (the potter Khnum) is told to fashion a wife for a man 'so that he does not live alone'; she is more beautiful than any woman, the seed of every god in her; The hero opens his whole heart to his wife, telling her the secret (his heart in the tree) on which his life depends; The Seven Hathors come to see a newborn (or newly made) being and decree its fate 'with one mouth'; The exiled hero lives alone in the Valley of the Cedar (Pine), hunting desert game and sleeping under the tree that holds his heart; he builds himself a house there.

Only in The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols: A couple vow thanks for a sound child, then ascribe partners to God in what he gave; Those you call on besides God are servants like yourselves; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Parents' words to God about the child he gave them [divergence between the texts]; Taunt: do the idols have feet to walk, hands to grasp, eyes to see, ears to hear?; Likeness between the idols and those who call on them [divergence between the texts]; Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; Having eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, said of idols or of people; First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps; Humankind is created from a single soul, from which its mate was made to dwell with it; The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 21.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 5 more.

Only in Slander, the great kings, Ahhiyawa erased, embargo on Assyria (CTH 105 §§10-14): The king of Ahhiyawa is written among the great kings of equal rank and then erased from the tablet; The vassal's merchants may not go to the enemy land (Assyria), nor may its merchants enter or cross the vassal's land; one who comes is to be seized and sent to the king; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 7 more.

Only in Ships, fortifying, fragmentary clauses (CTH 105 §§15-20 and §22''''): The vassal's merchants may not go to the enemy land (Assyria), nor may its merchants enter or cross the vassal's land; one who comes is to be seized and sent to the king.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 15.9.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 6 more.

Only in Protect the king's line; do not act like Mašturi; be ready to die (CTH 105 §§5-9): A vassal betrays his benefactor's son, asking 'shall I protect a bastard?', and is held up in a later treaty as a warning; The great king takes the vassal by the hand, gives him his sister in marriage, makes him his brother-in-law and king of his land; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 15.2.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 6 more.

Only in Report even father and mother; if a city, a house or one man sins (CTH 133 §§5-12): If a city within the land sins it is killed with its men; if a house within a city sins that house dies with its people; if one man sins, he alone; The vassal people's troop levy is fixed (from 150 to 60 heavy-armed men) and must be of free men, not servants or hirelings; Whether an offender's household and kin share his punishment [contrast between the texts]; Any letter or messenger arriving from the enemy or a foreign land must be seized and sent on to the king; Loyalty to the lord overrides a listed series of kin: father, mother, son, brother, kinsman.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0). Pair score 10.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 7 more.

Only in Arnuwanda's oath imposed on the elders of Ura (CTH 144): The sworn must always listen to whatever the king will say in future; The king sends a silver rhyton to a local god, from which the god is to be given drink regularly; The overlord summons the elders and heads of towns to a place and puts them under oath; Treaty: on the battlefield the vassal must not spare an enemy even if he is his brother, son, friend or kinsman; Conqueror carries off hostages (bene ta'aruvot) along with treasure; Loyalty to the lord overrides a listed series of kin: father, mother, son, brother, kinsman.

Pair score 9.9.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 7 more.

Only in Treaty with Paddatiššu of Kizzuwatna (CTH 26): fugitives, envoys, plotters and migrating settlements: If the population of a settlement migrates with its people, goods and herds to the other kingdom, it is seized and returned; A fugitive accused of plotting against his lord is returned unless he denies it, in which case notables of the land swear an oath and he is then returned; A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; Whether one who crosses over from the other party is examined and returned [neutral] [contrast between the texts]; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same').

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0). Pair score 10.9.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 7 more.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §48-60: war on Hurri, refusing Hurrian gifts, a new tablet, trusting messengers: The vassal is to trust a messenger only if his spoken words agree with the words written on the tablet he brings; The tablet of a vassal's former oath to a rival overlord is erased, the rival's word rejected and a new tablet made; A foreign king grants the fugitive hero a town to live in; The vassal must not make peace or come to terms ('put his mouth') with the overlord's enemy.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 27.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 4 more.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3). Pair score 10.8.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 7 more.

Only in CTH 51.I §6-8: Tušratta killed by his son, the storm god's verdict, not a straw taken, Šattiwazza set on his father's throne and given a daughter: The death of a king is read as the god's verdict in a lawsuit between rival claimants ('the storm god decided Artatama's case'); A king is murdered by his own son, who takes the throne; A king insists he took not so much as a straw or a splinter of wood from a land or a person; The overlord gives his sister or daughter in marriage to the vassal king; The great king says he will bring a dead (ruined) land back to life and restore it to its place; The great king takes an exiled prince by the hand and seats him on his father's throne; The vassal may keep concubines but may take no wife above or equal to the overlord's sister or daughter, who must be chief wife.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land (weight 6.0); Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions (weight 6.0); Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people (weight 5.7); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 28.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting; and 4 more.

Only in CTH 52.I §8-10: deposit and reading, tampering, the Hittite gods as witnesses, curses and blessings (duplicate of CTH 51.I §16-18): Treaty blessing: may your sons and grandsons rule as kings for ever and your father's throne grow old; Treaty curse: may the oath crush you with your land like a reed; Treaty curse: may the ground be ice so that you slip, and your land a pond in which you sink; Treaty curse: may the oath gods give you poverty and nakedness; Treaty curse: you shall be enemies of the thousand gods and they shall hunt you down; Treaty blessing: may the land be restored as of old, grow rich and lie down (rabāṣu) in peace; The god's word or covenant is read or proclaimed aloud before the king and assembly; Simile curse: as malt in the mash does not sprout, may your seed vanish from the land; Treaty curse: may the gods overturn your throne; A copy of the treaty tablet is deposited before the chief god of each party; Treaty curse: may the gods destroy the oath-breaker's name and seed from the earth; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods (weight 6.8); The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting (weight 5.5); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 17.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in The gods of Hatti, Kizzuwatna and Nuḫašše as witnesses (CTH 53 §§17-20): Among the treaty witnesses the moon god is called 'lord of the oath' and Išḫara 'queen of the oath'; A mountain is written with the divine determinative and receives cult as a god; The storm god of Mount Hazzi (Ṣapon, Jebel Aqra) is invoked as a witness god; The gods of the lulaḫḫi mountain-folk and the gods of the Habiru (ḫapiri) are named among the treaty witnesses; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9). Pair score 11.8.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 7 more.

Only in Help against enemies and the feeding of Hittite troops (CTH 53 §§8-9): When the overlord's troops march into the vassal's towns he must give them food and drink; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath (weight 7.3); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 29.0.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; and 4 more.

Only in Aid in revolt, feeding troops, captives, evil words and secret orders (CTH 62 §§12-16): If the king secretly orders something that cannot be done, the vassal must protest on the spot 'I cannot do this and I will not do it'; failing to do a feasible order breaks the oath; A secret word confided by the ruler must be kept; divulging it is a breach; When the overlord's troops march into the vassal's towns he must give them food and drink; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting (weight 5.5); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0). Pair score 15.8.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 6 more.

Only in Refugees set on the road, booty by request, the gods to see and hear (CTH 62 §§17-20): A people or fugitive passing through the vassal's land must be set safely on the road to the overlord's land with good words, not turned toward the mountains or to another land; Whatever the vassal desires (people, captives, booty) he must ask of the great king; what the king gives he may take, what he does not give he may not take; Of captives or spoil, what the lord gives you, take; what he does not give (or forbids), leave; The gods summoned to the oath are to stand as witnesses, to see it and to hear it.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Diese ungewöhnliche Form statt NI-IŠ DINGIR-LIM findet sich auch in A₃ II 9' und außerhalb dieses Manuskripts nur in KUB 14.1 Vs. 51 (CTH 146). Fehler für -ta; s. Friedrich 1926, 35. Nachträglich eingefügt. So Friedrich 1926, 18 mit Anm. „Ergänzung unsicher“. Auf dem Kolumnentrenner. Versehentliche Wiederholung von III 1. Mit Friedrich 1926, 45 handelt es sich bei kūš memiyaš kuiš um eine partitive Apposition. Friedrich 1926, 20, 45 interpoliert den Imperativ DÙ-ia; der hier gebotene Text folgt CHD CHD L-N, 272a. evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0). Pair score 17.3.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Only in Calling for troops, runaway soldiers, Arzawa captives (CTH 67 §§12-14): The vassal must look after the overlord's garrison troops as after his own person and house, support them and do them no harm.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7). Pair score 11.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 7 more.

Only in Three vassals under one oath; disputes before the king (CTH 67 §§8-11): A dispute between fellow vassals is not to be pursued by rash hostility but brought before the great king, who judges it and sets them back on the road; Fellow vassals bound by one oath must be of one mind: not harm, kill or seize one another, not shelter one another's runaways, and fight a common enemy together; A fugitive rebel is demanded from or handed over by the foreign king who sheltered him; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting (weight 5.5); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 16.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in The thousand gods called to assembly; heaven, earth and the Šeḫa River's waters (CTH 69 §§19-25): The underground watercourses (KASKAL.KUR, sinkholes) of a land are invoked among the treaty witnesses; Among the treaty witnesses the moon god is called 'lord of the oath' and Išḫara 'queen of the oath'; The gods summoned to the oath are to stand as witnesses, to see it and to hear it; The gods of the lulaḫḫi mountain-folk and the gods of the Habiru (ḫapiri) are named among the treaty witnesses; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses.
