evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 16.3.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in Rumours of revolt, 'come alone', no bird oracle, campaigns and the great kings (CTH 76 §§10-14): When summoned to help the king, the vassal must not first take a bird oracle; Taking or reading an omen from birds is set aside; The oath is broken if the vassal hears of sedition and overlooks it, saying 'let that evil happen'; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 16.2.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in Mankind is corrupt; the four kings of Arzawa; borders; fugitives (CTH 76 §§15-18): 'Because mankind is unreliable, rumours go round': if someone whispers that the king plans evil against the vassal, he must write to the king and wait, not act rashly; A free fugitive from the vassal's land who reaches Hatti is not returned ('it is not right'), but a farmer or craftsman who fled without doing his work is seized and sent back; Fellow vassals bound by one oath must be of one mind: not harm, kill or seize one another, not shelter one another's runaways, and fight a common enemy together; A rumour or report must be checked before anyone acts on it: referred to the ruler, or verified; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting (weight 5.5); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 16.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in The witness gods, with the gods of Wiluša and Appaliuna (CTH 76 §§20-23): A god [A]ppaliuna (possibly Apollo) is named among the gods of Wiluša (perhaps Troy) invoked as treaty witnesses; The underground watercourses (KASKAL.KUR, sinkholes) of a land are invoked among the treaty witnesses; Among the treaty witnesses the moon god is called 'lord of the oath' and Išḫara 'queen of the oath'; The storm god of Mount Hazzi (Ṣapon, Jebel Aqra) is invoked as a witness god; The gods of the lulaḫḫi mountain-folk and the gods of the Habiru (ḫapiri) are named among the treaty witnesses; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses; The sun god is shepherd of the land and father of the black-headed.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5). Pair score 29.3.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting; and 4 more.

Only in Friend and enemy, half-hearted war, mutual aid (CTH 92 §§10-16): If the vassal writes to the enemy 'the troops of Hatti are coming to attack you; be on your guard', he has broken the oath; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

matches.label: Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back
matches.note: Opposite rulings on the same clause of a pact between two sides: the treaty orders 'let Niqmepa seize him and return him (litēršu) to the king of Hatti', and keeping a fugitive 'transgresses the oath' (ištu māmīti ītetiq); 60:10 orders, for women who come over as believers after examination, 'do not return them (lā tarjiʿūhunna) to the unbelievers', with what the husbands spent paid back instead.

matches.label: The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend
matches.note: The treaty formula in the sovereign's first person, 'with my friend be friendly, with my enemy (nakrīya) be hostile', against God's first person in 60:1, 'do not take my enemy and your enemy (ʿaduwwī wa-ʿaduwwakum) as friends (awliyāʾ)'. In both the superior party names his enemy as the partner's enemy; 60:1 adds the secret passing of affection to them (tusirrūna ilayhim bi-l-mawadda).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend (weight 7.7); Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 7 more.

Only in Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge: Abraham and those with him are an excellent example: they declared themselves quit of their people and their gods, with enmity until they believe; Except Abraham's saying to his father 'I will ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power for you before God'; They despair of the hereafter as the unbelievers despair of those in the graves; Believers must not take God's enemies, who expelled the prophet, as allies (awliya') or secretly show them affection; Prohibition of killing one's children; Do not hold on to marriage ties with unbelieving women; dowries are reckoned between the communities; Believing women who emigrate are to be examined; if believers, they are not returned to the unbelievers, whose dowries are repaid; The women's pledge (bay'at al-nisa'): not to associate anything with God, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, bring a fabricated slander, or disobey in what is right; Abraham declares to his father and people that he is free of what they worship, except the one who created him; Dissolving marriages with women outside the community [divergence between the texts]; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Neither your blood-ties nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; and 9 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Šuppiluliuma I to Niqmaddu of Ugarit: do not fear Nuhašše and Mukiš; keep the treaty, and the booty and fugitives you take are yours (RS 17.0132): The overlord promises the vassal that, once victorious, he will give him a sealed tablet of treaty; The overlord tells the vassal 'do not fear' the hostile neighbouring kings and promises to deal with them; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal serves the king as his father and his father's father served him; The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy; A letter opens with the formula 'Say to my lord (X): thus says Y, your servant' (or, from the king, 'thus says your lord').

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

passages.text: (§21:181) [ … -]el tup-pí-aš INIM{MEŠ} wa-aḫ-nu-š[i] (§21:182) [ … ] Nach der Textzusammenstellung von Kühne – Otten 1971, 80 ist B Vs. 8-9 folgendermaßen zu lesen: (8) [ ca. 16-17 Zeichen AŠ-ŠU]M EN-UT-TIM [ _ (_) -t]a nu IT-TI ⌈KUR⌉ [{U]RU}⌈Ḫa⌉-at-ti-[a _ _ -]x (9) [ ca. 12-13 Zeichen KUR {URU}Ḫa-at-t]i-a pa-aḫ-ḫa[- _ _ ] wa-aš-ta-aš. Der Schreiber in Exemplar B scheint die beiden Sätze B Vs. 8 [ … AŠ-Š]UM EN-UT-TIM [PAP-aš-t]a und B Vs. 9 [ … KUR {URU}Ḫa-at-t]i-a pa-aḫ-ḫa-a[š-ta] direkt untereinander gesetzt zu haben. Nach der Textedition steht waštaš (Vs. 9) ohne eine Satzeinleitung nach paḫḫa[šta], obwohl ein freier Raum zwischen den beiden Worten vorhanden ist. Mit Kühne – Otten 1971, 31 ist deshalb wahrscheinlich nu ITTI KUR {URU}Ḫatti=a (B Vs. 8) waštaš (B Vs. 9) zu nu ITTI ⌈KUR {URU}Ḫatti=a⌉ [Ú-UL ku-it-k]i waštaš zusammenzufassen. Diesen Satz hat der Schreiber zuerst (wahrscheinlich) vergessen und erst später eingefügt. Weil der linke Rand bereits durch das Ende von B Vs. 7 beansprucht war, standen dem Schreiber nur die - bis dahin leeren - Zeilenenden von B Vs. 8-9 für diesen Zusatz zur Verfügung. Da der vorhandene Raum B Vs. 8-9 nicht ausreicht, um den Text A I 22-25 aufzunehmen, dürfte B eine Variante – nach Kühne – Otten 1971, 31 (I 22 f.) die einzige nachweisbare Textvariante – enthalten. Vermutlich hat der Schreiber entweder den Text von A I 22-23 oder den Text A I 24-25 (versehentlich?) weggelassen. Das Exemplar B ist somit wahrscheinlich als Abschrift zu betrachten.

matches.note: The same case, a killer who is caught: in Ini-Tešub's agreement 'he pays the man threefold' (awīla 3-šu umalla) and the goods threefold, with no word of death for the killer; 2:178 prescribes retaliation 'free for free', with payment only where the dead man's 'brother' pardons. Only in Ini-Tešub's agreement with the men of Ugarit: a man of Carchemish killed in Ugarit is compensated threefold, and his lost goods threefold (RS 17.0230): When the killers of a man are not caught, the people of the town where he died swear an oath before his kinsmen that they do not know the killers, and pay compensation; When a king's merchants are murdered in another land, the people of that land must pay compensation (three minas of silver per man) and restore the goods.

Only in Retaliation and bequests: Kin of the slain may pardon and accept compensation (diya) instead of retaliation, a lightening from God; 'In retaliation there is life for you'; Retaliation (qisas) for the slain: free for free, slave for slave, female for female; What person is matched to a man who was killed [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Clause on whoever alters a sealed grant or a bequest [divergence between the texts]; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; Whoever alters the wording of a fixed text (tablet, bequest) after it is set bears the penalty; A negligent owner may pay a ransom for his life; Retaliation (talion) for killing or injury [divergence between the texts]; In a homicide, the 'lord of the blood' decides: if he says 'let him die' the killer dies, if 'let him pay' he pays; the king has no part; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis).

matches.label: Vines or palms of a hostile neighbour are cut down
matches.note: Cutting the other side's trees is the act in both. In the Hittite verdict it is an offence to be cleared by oath: Ugarit charges that the men of Siyannu cut its vines, and both sides must swear 'we did not cut their vines' (nakkis). In 59:5 the believers' cutting of the Banu Nadir's palms during the siege is declared lawful: 'whatever palms you cut or left standing on their roots, it was by God's leave'.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Vines or palms of a hostile neighbour are cut down [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Hittite verdict between Ugarit and Siyannu: oaths about Habiru of the tower, cut vines, provisions to raiders from Beirut, and the return of slaves (RS 17.0341): The people of a town must swear that they did not strike, rob or harbour raiders, or else pay threefold compensation; Whoever, after the tablet, is found to have sold a fugitive slave of the other kingdom must pay compensation like a thief; One people accuses its neighbours of cutting down their vineyards, and the accused must swear they did not; A king's verdict assigns one party an oath; by swearing (or by being released from the oath through settlement) the case is decided; Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back; Bandits or brigands called sa-gaz (Akkadian ḫabbātu, the Ḫabiru/ʿapiru).

Only in Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay': The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world; God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr); Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave; Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; How spoil taken from the enemy is distributed [divergence between the texts]; Fay' (booty gained without cavalry or camels) goes to God, the messenger, kin, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, so wealth does not circulate only among the rich; They thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; The wealth of a ruined or expelled people passes to others who did not have it [divergence between the texts]; The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; What becomes of the spoil taken from the enemy: brought to the god or assigned to God [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

matches.label: A king receives a gift and scorns it in a speech to the sender's side
matches.note: A gift reaches a king and he answers it with scorn. The Ugarit king's 'lapis' is a stone 'just lifted from the ground', and the king says 'is this not a mockery of me?'. The Queen of Sheba's gift is real wealth, and Sulaymān rejects it because 'what God has given me is better than what he has given you; rather you exult in your gift'. The first king is angry that the gift is worthless; the second refuses a gift of value.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 42 more.

Only in Deed before the mayor of Ugarit and elders: Rapʾanu takes ʾAbi-malku into brotherhood with 100 shekels; whoever hates the other leaves; the childless one's goods pass to the other; seven witnesses (RS 25.0134): Two men make a contract of brotherhood (aḫḫūtu) before the mayor and elders, with a deposit of silver; whoever 'hates' the other forfeits and leaves, and the childless one's estate passes to his adopted brother; Legal formula: 'if X hates (zêru) Y' marks the unilateral dissolution of a marriage, adoption or brotherhood, with a fixed penalty; If a man dies without a son, all his property goes to the man he adopted as brother or son; Who inherits the estate of a man who dies without a son [divergence between the texts]; A legal deed closes with a list of named witnesses (IGI ...) and the scribe.

Only in Wealth by consent, major sins, and discord in marriage: Command: do not kill yourselves (or one another); In marital discord an arbiter is sent from his family and one from hers; If the major sins (kabāʾir) are avoided, God expiates lesser misdeeds; Men are maintainers (qawwāmūn) of women by God's preference and their spending; A wife whose rebellion (nushūz) is feared is admonished, left alone in bed, then struck; Those bound to you by oath-alliance receive their share; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; The ground of a husband's authority over his wife [divergence between the texts]; How a man and woman who have become estranged are brought together again [divergence between the texts]; Do not consume one another's wealth wrongfully (bil-bāṭil), only by trade with mutual consent; Do not covet; each has his own share (in the division among kin); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property; and 1 more.

Only in Westcar: Khafre's tale: Ubaoner's wife and the commoner; the wax crocodile; the adulteress burned: The magician commands the crocodile to bring up the man from the depths and later the king tells it to take away 'what is yours'; no one knows where it took him; A priest's wife takes a commoner as lover; they spend the day drinking in the pavilion of his garden lake and the caretaker reports it to the husband; A magician makes a crocodile of wax; thrown into the water after the adulterer it becomes a real crocodile of seven cubits and seizes him; picked up again it is wax; Portrait of the man who slept with another man's wife: no one walks with him, life passes him by, no just man holds him dear, he is thrown away like a worthless coin and clothed as if under heavy punishment; An object thrown down becomes a live beast and, taken in the hand, returns to what it was [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; After each wonder tale the king orders offerings (a thousand loaves, a hundred jars of beer, an ox, incense) for the dead king and his magician: 'I have seen his deed of knowledge'; Adulterer and adulteress both put to death; The king's sons rise one after another to tell the king a wonder (bjꜣ,yt) worked by a magician-priest in the days of a former king.

Only in Judah and Tamar: Man spills his seed on the ground to avoid raising offspring for his dead brother and is struck dead; God kills a man for unspecified wickedness; A kid of the goats promised as a harlot's hire; Seal, cord and staff left as a pledge, later used as proof of paternity; Midwife ties a scarlet thread on the hand of the twin who emerges first; Man acknowledges the wronged woman: 'She is more righteous than I'; Twins contend at birth over who emerges first; A widow veils herself, sits by the road and is taken for a harlot by her father-in-law; Father-in-law withholds his youngest son from the widow, fearing he too will die; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; What a woman's veil or cloak signals to men who see her [contrast between the texts]; Sheep-shearing as an occasion for travel and festivity; and 2 more.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 139 more.

leads.title: David's thanksgiving psalm (composite of Pss 105, 96, 106) ↔ Hypocrites and the call to judgment; 'we hear and obey'; the promise of succession
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Hymn recalls God's covenant with Abraham, oath to Isaac and statute to Jacob for a thousand generations (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in David's thanksgiving psalm (composite of Pss 105, 96, 106): A psalm sung in the narrative is stitched from passages found in the Psalter; Prayer: 'save us, gather us and deliver us from the nations'; The patriarchs few in number wander from nation to nation, protected by God; All the people say 'Amen' and praise YHWH; 'Touch not my anointed ones, do my prophets no harm'; The world is firmly established and cannot be moved; Heavens, earth, sea, fields and trees rejoice and sing before the coming God; God comes to judge the earth with righteousness, and all creation rejoices; Proclamation among the nations: 'YHWH is king' (YHWH malakh); Idols called 'elilim' ('nothings'); YHWH is great and to be feared above all gods; Refrain 'Give thanks to YHWH for he is good, for his steadfast love is forever'.

Only in Hypocrites and the call to judgment; 'we hear and obey'; the promise of succession: God promises the believers succession (istikhlāf) in the land as he gave it to those before them, exchanging fear for security; 'You are my witnesses,' says YHWH: before me no god was formed and after me there shall be none; Blessing: God removes harmful wild beasts from the land; This people honors God with lips while its heart is far; its fear of him is a commandment of men learned by rote; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do.

leads.title: Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer ↔ The hypocrites' false promises, Satan's disowning, the Quran on a mountain, and the litany of beautiful names
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'There is none like you and no God beside you' (weight 6.6). Pair score 6.6.

Only in Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer: Pun on 'house': the king would build God a house; God will build the king a house (dynasty); Revelation described as God 'uncovering the ear' of his servant; The king lives in a cedar house while the ark of God remains under curtains; God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent; God promises to make the chosen one's name great; Israel is the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for himself; A prophet approves a plan, then is corrected by a revelation that night; God took the ruler from following the sheep; Prayer of humility: 'Who am I and what is my house?'; The king's son, not the king, will build the house for God's name; God declares the king his son: 'I will be his father and he my son'; God promises David's house and throne will endure forever; and 1 more.

Only in The hypocrites' false promises, Satan's disowning, the Quran on a mountain, and the litany of beautiful names: They fight only from fortified towns or behind walls; you think them united but their hearts are divided; Those who forgot God, so he made them forget themselves; Hypocrites promise their unbelieving allies to leave or fight with them, but will not; Let every soul look to what it has sent ahead for tomorrow; Had this Quran been sent down on a mountain you would see it humbled and split asunder for fear of God; Like Satan who says to man 'Disbelieve!' and when he disbelieves says 'I am quit of you, I fear God'; A mountain shaken by God's descent or by his revelation [divergence between the texts]; The mountain smokes like a furnace and quakes as God descends in fire; A mountain bows, or fails to bow, before the divine, and is broken [divergence between the texts]; Litany of divine names: King, Holy, Peace, Faithful, Guardian, Mighty, Compeller, Proud, Creator, Maker, Fashioner; to him belong the most beautiful names; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; Opening formula: whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God (sabbaha / yusabbihu lillah).

Only in David's assembly speech and the written pattern of the temple: The cherubim over the ark are called 'the chariot' (merkavah); God's election narrows from tribe to family to man to the chosen son; Eunuchs (sarisim) serve among the royal officials; Multiple gold and silver lampstands and tables in the temple; The Davidic king sits on 'the throne of YHWH'; The king may not build the temple because he is a man of war who shed much blood; The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness; God looks on the heart, not on appearance or height; God declares the king his son: 'I will be his father and he my son'; Formula: be strong and courageous, do not fear, God will not leave or forsake you; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

leads.title: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What the queen of Sheba says of Solomon's God [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); A foreign queen tests the king with riddles and he answers them all (weight 7.3). Pair score 14.7.

Only in The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon: Visitor confesses that reports did not tell even half of the king's wisdom and wealth; Rare almug wood from Ophir used for temple supports and lyres for singers; never seen again; A visitor seeing the king's court is left breathless ('no more spirit in her'); A royal visitor arrives with camels carrying spices, gold and precious stones; A foreigner declares that YHWH is greater than all gods; Fleets with Phoenician sailors sail from the Red Sea to Ophir and bring back gold; Kings of all the earth send to hear the wise king's wisdom.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 41 more.

leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: King keeps tens of thousands of chariot horses and horsemen (weight 7.3); King must not multiply horses, wives or silver and gold, nor return the people to Egypt (weight 6.4). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Solomon's gold, ivory throne, fleet and horse trade: Gold coming to the king each year weighs 666 talents; King makes hundreds of shields of beaten gold and hangs them in the palace; King's merchants import horses from Egypt and Kue and export chariots to Hittite and Aramean kings at fixed prices; Great ivory throne overlaid with gold, with six steps and twelve lions on the steps and two beside the arms; The king makes silver and gold as common as stones and cedar as sycamores; Kings of all the earth send to hear the wise king's wisdom; Tarshish ships every three years bring gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks (or baboons).

Only in Solomon's steeds, the body on his throne, and the unmatched kingdom: God tested Solomon by placing a body (jasad) on his throne; then he repented; Devils serve Solomon as builders and divers, and others are bound together in fetters; Solomon asks for a kingdom such as no one after him should have; Fine steeds shown to Solomon in the evening distract him from remembrance of God until the sun hides; he has them brought back and strokes (or slashes) their legs and necks; No king after the speaker will equal (or be given) what he has [divergence between the texts]; Solomon's horses [divergence between the texts]; What Solomon asks of God and the gift none after him will match [divergence between the texts]; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; The enemy's horses are hamstrung and their chariots burned by divine command; Devils (shayāṭīn) and jinn labor for Solomon, diving and building.

Shared motifs, rarest first: King calls the prophet 'troubler of Israel' (okher Yisra'el); prophet returns the charge (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Contest on Mount Carmel: Prophet repairs the ruined altar with twelve stones for the tribes of Jacob; Contest of gods: the god who answers by fire on an unlit sacrifice is God; The prophets of Baal are seized and slaughtered at the brook Kishon; Prophet mocks the silent god: perhaps he is musing, relieving himself, travelling, or asleep and must be woken; Sacrifice and altar drenched with four jars of water three times, filling a trench, before the miracle; The people fall on their faces crying 'YHWH, he is God! leads.title: Contest on Mount Carmel ↔ Ha-Mim: the idols created nothing; a witness from Israel; the Book of Moses
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped' (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Contest on Mount Carmel: Prophet repairs the ruined altar with twelve stones for the tribes of Jacob; Contest of gods: the god who answers by fire on an unlit sacrifice is God; The prophets of Baal are seized and slaughtered at the brook Kishon; Prophet mocks the silent god: perhaps he is musing, relieving himself, travelling, or asleep and must be woken; Sacrifice and altar drenched with four jars of water three times, filling a trench, before the miracle; The people fall on their faces crying 'YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!'; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; An offering consumed by fire as proof of the true God or messenger [response between the texts]; Fire from heaven falls and consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust and water; 'How long will you hop between two branches? If YHWH is God, follow him; if Baal, follow him'; A single prophet of YHWH stands against 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah; How the people respond to the prophet's challenge over Baal [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the idols created nothing; a witness from Israel; the Book of Moses: Before it was the Book of Moses as a guide (imam) and mercy; this Arabic book confirms it; A witness from the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it and believes; 'I am no novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you'; What Moses' written book is for: witness against the people, or guide and mercy [divergence between the texts]; Formula: the sending down of the Book (tanzil al-kitab) is from God, the Mighty, the Wise/Knowing; Opponents accuse the prophet of forging lies against God; Formula 'no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve'; The revelation is sent down as an Arabic Quran; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; Opponents call the prophet or his message 'manifest sorcery'; Challenge to idolaters: show me what those besides God have created; God will raise up a prophet like Moses from among the brothers and put his words in his mouth; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in The wounded prophet's parable against Ahab: Wounded prophet, disguised with a bandage over his eyes, tells the king a case and the king condemns himself; Man who refuses a prophet's command to strike him is killed by a lion; 'Your life for his life': a guard who loses a prisoner forfeits his life or a talent of silver; King goes home 'sullen and angry' (sar ve-za'ef) after a prophet's rebuke; Band of prophets with harp, drum, flute and lyre prophesying in ecstasy; Ban (herem): total destruction of a conquered population.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Offender stoned to death by the community (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

Only in Naboth's vineyard: Commoner refuses to sell or trade his ancestral vineyard to the king: 'God forbid I give you my fathers' inheritance'; Queen writes letters in the king's name, sealed with his seal, ordering a judicial murder; A fast is proclaimed and two worthless men falsely testify that the victim 'blessed (cursed) God and king'; Innocent victim is taken outside the city and stoned to death; King goes home 'sullen and angry' (sar ve-za'ef) after a prophet's rebuke; Thwarted king lies on his bed, turns his face to the wall and refuses to eat; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property; Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness.

Only in The people of the town, the three messengers and the man who came running: A man comes running from the farthest part of the city urging his people to follow the messengers; The believer is told 'enter the Garden' and says 'Would that my people knew how my Lord forgave me'; Two messengers sent to a town are rejected, so God reinforces them with a third; The townsfolk say 'we augur ill of you' and threaten to stone the messengers; they reply 'your omen is with you'; No host from heaven was needed: a single Shout (sayha) and they were extinguished; Augury: a bird's flight or alighting is an omen bound to a person [divergence between the texts]; The dead cannot go back to the life they left; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied; Intercession avails only for whom God permits; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

leads.title: Micaiah son of Imlah and the lying spirit ↔ Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A false prophet strikes the true prophet on the cheek (weight 7.7); Court prophet makes iron horns: 'with these you will gore Aram' (weight 7.7); Four hundred court prophets unanimously promise victory (weight 7.7); Prophet first sarcastically repeats the favorable oracle, then under oath tells the true one (weight 7.7); A single true prophet, hated by the king because he never prophesies good for him (weight 7.7); A spirit volunteers in the divine council to be a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths (weight 7.3); Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd' (weight 6.5). Pair score 52.6.

Only in Micaiah son of Imlah and the lying spirit: Prophet imprisoned on short rations of bread and water until the king returns in peace; God asks the heavenly council 'who will entice the king?'; a spirit volunteers; Prophet stakes his authority: 'If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me'; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [divergence between the texts]; Prophet sees God seated on his throne with all the host of heaven standing to his right and left; Whether the adversary, devils or deceiving spirits have access to God's council [contrast between the texts]; God uses a false prophet to test whether Israel loves him.

Only in Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death: The enemy commander orders his chariots to fight no one but the king; When the threatened king cries out, God turns the attackers away from him; 'Hear, all you peoples' (quotation linking the prophet to Micah); One king entices (hesit) another into a disastrous war; Two kings sit in royal robes on thrones at the threshing floor by the city gate; A righteous king allies by marriage with a wicked king's house; Prophet imprisoned on 'bread of affliction and water of affliction'; The prophet swears to speak only what his God tells him; The wounded king props himself in his chariot all day and dies at sunset; An arrow shot at random strikes the king between the joints of his armor; A king disguises himself in battle while his ally wears royal robes; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates.

matches.note: Both say falsehood can be put into prophets' speech and that it serves as a test or snare. 1Kgs: a spirit of the heavenly court volunteers, wə-hāyîtî rûaḥ šeqer bə-fî kol nəvîʾāyw, and YHWH approves (təfatteh wə-gam tûkāl ... nātan YHWH rûaḥ šeqer); Q 22:52-53: the source is Satan (alqā sh-shayṭān), God abrogates it and makes it a trial (fitna) for those whose hearts are sick. Only in Solomon's dominion, provisions and wisdom: King rules all kingdoms from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt, who bring him tribute; King speaks three thousand proverbs and a thousand and five songs; King's wisdom surpasses that of the people of the East, of Egypt and of named sages; The quantities of flour, cattle, sheep and game consumed daily at the royal table are listed; God gives the king wisdom and 'breadth of heart' like the sand on the seashore; Solomon's wisdom concerning animals [divergence between the texts]; Wise king discourses on trees from cedar to hyssop, and on beasts, birds, creeping things and fish; Everyone dwells safely under his own vine and fig tree; Kings of all the earth send to hear the wise king's wisdom.

Only in Solomon's steeds, the body on his throne, and the unmatched kingdom: God tested Solomon by placing a body (jasad) on his throne; then he repented; Devils serve Solomon as builders and divers, and others are bound together in fetters; Solomon asks for a kingdom such as no one after him should have; Fine steeds shown to Solomon in the evening distract him from remembrance of God until the sun hides; he has them brought back and strokes (or slashes) their legs and necks; No king after the speaker will equal (or be given) what he has [divergence between the texts]; What Solomon asks of God and the gift none after him will match [divergence between the texts]; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; The enemy's horses are hamstrung and their chariots burned by divine command; Devils (shayāṭīn) and jinn labor for Solomon, diving and building.

The horses become a moral episode, a love of wealth that distracted him from remembering God until sunset, followed by his turning back (innahu awwāb).

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Solomon's great bronze works were produced [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.6.

Only in The bronze sea, wheeled stands and temple vessels: Ten golden lampstands stand before the inner sanctuary, five on each side; Ten wheeled bronze stands decorated with lions, oxen, cherubim and palms carry basins; The bronze used for the sanctuary is so abundant its weight was not determined; Bronze vessels cast in the clay ground of the Jordan plain between Succoth and Zarethan; A round vessel ten cubits across measures thirty around (pi taken as three); Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil; An accounting of the gold, silver and bronze used for the sanctuary; A bronze laver where priests wash hands and feet before service, lest they die; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God.

Only in David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff: God made a spring of molten copper (or brass) flow for Solomon; The jinn did not know the unseen, else they would not have stayed in humiliating labor; Solomon dies leaning on his staff; only a creature of the earth gnawing the staff reveals his death when he falls; A superhuman craftsman casts metal vessels and furniture for a lord [divergence between the texts]; David and the coat of mail [contrast between the texts]; A king covers a journey of many stages in a single day [divergence between the texts]; How Solomon died and how his death became known [divergence between the texts]; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail; Rivers clap their hands and mountains sing together before YHWH; Who did Solomon's building and craft work [divergence between the texts]; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; and 2 more.

matches.note: Solomon's cast bronze. 1 Kgs: wa-yyaʿaś ʾeṯ-ha-yyām mûṣāq ... ʿōmēḏ ʿal-šənê ʿāśār bāqār; bə-kikkar ha-yyardēn yəṣāqām ha-mmeleḵ bə-maʿăḇēh hā-ʾăḏāmâ (cast in clay moulds in the Jordan plain). Q: wa-asalnā lahu ʿayna l-qiṭr (God makes a spring of molten copper flow for him) ... wa-jifānin ka-l-jawābi wa-qudūrin rāsiyāt. The metal comes from a miraculous spring instead of the foundry, and the 'sea' and its stands are matched by basins like reservoirs and fixed cauldrons. Lead: identification of the jifān/qudūr with the yām and mekonot is a proposal.

leads.title: Hiram the bronze-smith and the pillars Jachin and Boaz ↔ David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Who did Solomon's building and craft work [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Hiram the bronze-smith and the pillars Jachin and Boaz: Master bronze-smith is son of an Israelite widow and a Tyrian father, filled with wisdom and skill; Pillar capitals with lily work, chain-network and rows of pomegranates; A key figure is identified as the son of a widow; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

Only in David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff: God made a spring of molten copper (or brass) flow for Solomon; The jinn did not know the unseen, else they would not have stayed in humiliating labor; Solomon dies leaning on his staff; only a creature of the earth gnawing the staff reveals his death when he falls; A superhuman craftsman casts metal vessels and furniture for a lord [divergence between the texts]; David and the coat of mail [contrast between the texts]; A king covers a journey of many stages in a single day [divergence between the texts]; How Solomon died and how his death became known [divergence between the texts]; How Solomon's great bronze works were produced [divergence between the texts]; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail; Rivers clap their hands and mountains sing together before YHWH; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; and 3 more.

leads.title: The ark brought into the temple; the cloud fills the house ↔ Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: What the ark contains [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The ark brought into the temple; the cloud fills the house: Ends of the ark's poles visible from the holy place but not outside, 'to this day'; Ark brought in procession into the temple at the autumn feast in the seventh month; Sheep and cattle sacrificed so many that they could not be counted; Temple called a 'house of zebul' (exalted dwelling), a place for God to dwell forever; God has said he will dwell in thick darkness ('arafel); Archaic (Canaanite/Phoenician) month names Ziv, Bul and Ethanim are used; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; The cloud and glory fill the sanctuary so that even the leader cannot enter; Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; A candidate for kingship is judged by his bodily size or strength (too small for the throne; given increase of body) [divergence between the texts]; A claimant's body is weighed as fitness for kingship [divergence between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A champion whom everyone fears is killed by one unlikely man; and 17 more.

leads.title: Solomon's prayer of dedication ↔ Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A foreigner from a far land who hears of God's name comes to pray at the temple and is heard (weight 7.7); 'There is no man who does not sin' (weight 7.7); Heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, much less a temple (weight 7.1); The direction faced in prayer [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Prayers made toward the temple (or toward the land, city and house when in exile) are heard in heaven (weight 7.1); Prophet spreads out his palms to God in prayer (weight 6.5); Heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to God (weight 6.5). Pair score 49.6.

Only in Solomon's prayer of dedication: Exiles in an enemy land turn back with all their heart and pray toward their land, and God grants them mercy before captors; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; Egypt called an iron furnace (smelting furnace); Heaven is shut and no rain falls because of the people's sin; repentance brings rain; Long catalogue of curses for covenant violation (disease, defeat, famine, exile); God alone knows the hearts of all humans.

Only in Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform: The king kneels on a bronze platform in the court and spreads his hands to heaven; People away from Jerusalem or in exile pray in the direction of the land, city and temple; Captives confess in exile 'We have sinned, done wrong and acted wickedly'; 'Arise, YHWH, to your resting place, you and the ark of your might'; Prayer lists famine, pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, siege and sickness as occasions for prayer; An oath sworn before God's altar in the temple, judged by God; Temple called a 'house of zebul' (exalted dwelling), a place for God to dwell forever; 'O my servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy; God forgives all sins'; God has said he will dwell in thick darkness ('arafel); The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness; God looks on the heart, not on appearance or height; Sacrifice only at the place God will choose to make his name dwell; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Mother vows her (unborn) child to God's service [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Mother names her child with a speech explaining the name (weight 6.8); Mother vows her (unborn) child to God's service (weight 6.8). Pair score 21.4.

Only in Hannah's vow and Samuel's birth: Barren favored wife provoked by a fertile rival co-wife; Child brought to the sanctuary once weaned, with sacrifices; Child's name explained as 'asked of God'; A woman's silent prayer, lips moving without voice, is mistaken for drunkenness; Mothers nurse their children two full years; weaning by mutual consultation; wet-nursing permitted; A petitioner calls to God in a hidden, secret voice [divergence between the texts]; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between [contrast between the texts]; Mother keeps a vow of silence [divergence between the texts]; Child consecrated as a nazirite from the womb, his hair never to be cut; Remember God within yourself, humbly, without loud speech, morning and evening.

Only in Saul anointed, prophesies, and is chosen by lot at Mizpah: The chosen king hides among the baggage and is found by oracle; King chosen by lot, narrowing from tribe to clan to man; Rules of the kingship written in a book and laid up before YHWH; Prophet foretells a series of chance encounters as signs confirming the anointing; Spirit transforms a man into 'another man', giving him a new heart; Proverb 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'; Asking for a human king is a rejection of God's kingship; Prophet anoints a future king privately with oil from a flask; Band of prophets with harp, drum, flute and lyre prophesying in ecstasy; People acclaim 'Long live the king!'; Spirit of God rushes upon a man, giving him strength or ecstasy.

leads.title: David spares Saul in the cave at En-gedi ↔ The call to go forth; the second of two in the cave
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet is 'the second of two' hiding in the cave, telling his companion 'do not grieve, God is with us' (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in David spares Saul in the cave at En-gedi: Hero secretly cuts the corner of the king's robe as proof he could have killed him; King enters a cave 'to cover his feet' where the hero is hiding; Hero swears not to cut off the king's descendants or name; Persecuting king weeps and admits 'You are more righteous than I'; Hero finds the hostile king defenseless and spares him as the LORD's anointed; A proverb of the ancients is quoted; Self-abasement: 'after a dead dog, after a single flea'.

Only in The call to go forth; the second of two in the cave: God's own Presence (face) will go with the people; God threatens to destroy a people and put another in its place [divergence between the texts]; Reproaching followers who hang back, the leader recalls how he escaped a crisis without them; The deity is the one more of a company: third of two, fourth of three; Sign: the young woman ('almah) is pregnant and will bear a son and call his name Immanuel ('God with us'); A poem lists the tribes, praising those who fought and shaming those who stayed home; God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; The oppressed people hide in caves, dens and mountain strongholds; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers; If God wills he takes you away and brings another people in your place.

leads.title: Nabal the fool, Abigail the wise and David's averted vengeance ↔ The disbelievers, the help, and the flame
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A person's name declared to match his character: 'as his name is, so is he' (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Nabal the fool, Abigail the wise and David's averted vengeance: The soul bound in 'the bundle of the living' with God; A rich man insultingly refuses food to the hero's men at a feast; On hearing the news a man's heart dies within him and he becomes like stone, then dies; The hero marries the widow of a man who wronged him; An outlaw band claims a gift for having protected a rich man's shepherds; The king gives the hero's wife (his own daughter) to another man; God will make for the chosen one a 'sure house' (enduring dynasty); The hero adds wives to his household; Sheep-shearing as an occasion for travel and festivity; A wise woman intercepts an avenging warrior with gifts and speech and averts bloodshed; Every male cut off, idiom 'one who pisses against the wall', 'bond and free'; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them.

Only in The disbelievers, the help, and the flame: Curse on Abu Lahab ('father of flame'): his hands perish, he will burn in a fire of flame, and his wife carries firewood with a rope of palm fiber (masad) on her neck; Repeated mutual disavowal: 'I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship'; 'to you your religion and to me mine'; Foreign daughter-in-law swears to follow her mother-in-law: your people my people, your God my God [contrast between the texts]; When God's help and the opening (al-fath) come, people enter God's religion in crowds; the prophet is to glorify and seek forgiveness; Wealth does not profit on the day of wrath.

leads.title: Amalekites burn Ziklag; David recovers all and makes the spoil law ↔ Al-Fath: the clear opening, the sakina, the hand of God over their hands and the bedouin who stayed behind
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether those who stayed behind share in the spoil [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Amalekites burn Ziklag; David recovers all and makes the spoil law: A sick slave abandoned by the raiders is revived with food and guides the hero to them; The hero recovers every captive and all the spoil, nothing missing; The enemy is caught off guard while eating, drinking and celebrating their spoil; Part of the army is too exhausted to cross a stream and stays behind; Only four hundred young men escape on camels; Leader sends portions of spoil as gifts to the elders of many towns; People weep until they have no strength left to weep; Amalek attacks Israel on the way; Hero consults God through the ephod with yes/no questions about future events; Returning warriors divide the spoil with their brothers at home; The people are about to stone their leader.

Only in Al-Fath: the clear opening, the sakina, the hand of God over their hands and the bedouin who stayed behind: The bedouin who stayed behind plead that wealth and families kept them busy and ask for forgiveness insincerely; No blame on the blind, the lame or the sick (for not going out to fight); Those who pledge allegiance to the prophet pledge to God; 'the hand of God is over their hands'; To God belong the hosts (junud) of the heavens and the earth; Those who stayed behind ask to follow when spoils are in prospect and are refused; God forgives the prophet his past and future sins; 'We have opened for you a clear opening/victory (fath mubin)' (the Hudaybiya treaty); The divine presence (root sh-k-n / s-k-n) dwelling on the sanctuary or sent down into hearts [divergence between the texts]; Prophet stakes his authority: 'If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me'; Oath sworn by raising the hand to God; Who is exempted from going out to war [contrast between the texts]; Household, wife or family as a ground for staying behind from a campaign [contrast between the texts]; and 7 more.

matches.note: 1Sam 8:5, 20 śîmâ llānû melek lĕ-šopṭēnû kĕ-kol ha-ggôyim ... wĕ-nilḥam ʾet milḥămōtênû: a king 'like all the nations', to judge and fight our wars, which God reads as rejecting him (8:7 kî ʾōtî māʾăsû mi-mmĕlōk ʿălêhem); Q 2:246 qālū li-nabiyyin lahumu bʿath lanā malikan nuqātil fī sabīli llāh: a king so that 'we may fight in God's way'. The motive changes from imitating the nations to holy war, God's displeasure is left out, and the prophet (Samuel) is unnamed. The Quran adds the prophet's doubt that they will fight, and their turning away (tawallaw illā qalīlan).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The chosen king is taller than all the people from the shoulders up [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The chosen king is taller than all the people from the shoulders up (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.8.

Only in Saul seeks his father's donkeys and meets Samuel: Girls going out to draw water direct the stranger; God tells the prophet a day in advance that the chosen man will come; Youth searching for his father's lost donkeys is led to the prophet and made king; Honored guest given a reserved portion (the thigh) at a sacrificial meal; Gloss: 'the prophet of today was formerly called a seer'; Seer consulted for lost property with a small payment; Prophet anoints a future king privately with oil from a flask.

leads.title: Solomon at Gibeon asks for wisdom; his chariots, wealth and horse trade ↔ Solomon's steeds, the body on his throne, and the unmatched kingdom
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What Solomon asks of God and the gift none after him will match [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); King must not multiply horses, wives or silver and gold, nor return the people to Egypt (weight 6.4). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Solomon at Gibeon asks for wisdom; his chariots, wealth and horse trade: A people as numerous as the dust of the earth; Offered any gift, the king asks for wisdom to judge rather than long life, riches or victory; God tells a person: 'Ask what I shall give you'; King's merchants import horses from Egypt and Kue and export chariots to Hittite and Aramean kings at fixed prices; A king offers a thousand burnt offerings; The king makes silver and gold as common as stones and cedar as sycamores; The ark stands in Jerusalem while the Mosaic tabernacle and altar remain at Gibeon; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

Only in Solomon's steeds, the body on his throne, and the unmatched kingdom: God tested Solomon by placing a body (jasad) on his throne; then he repented; Devils serve Solomon as builders and divers, and others are bound together in fetters; Solomon asks for a kingdom such as no one after him should have; Fine steeds shown to Solomon in the evening distract him from remembrance of God until the sun hides; he has them brought back and strokes (or slashes) their legs and necks; No king after the speaker will equal (or be given) what he has [divergence between the texts]; Solomon's horses [divergence between the texts]; King keeps tens of thousands of chariot horses and horsemen; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; The enemy's horses are hamstrung and their chariots burned by divine command; Devils (shayāṭīn) and jinn labor for Solomon, diving and building.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates (weight 6.2). Pair score 6.2.

Only in Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death: The enemy commander orders his chariots to fight no one but the king; When the threatened king cries out, God turns the attackers away from him; 'Hear, all you peoples' (quotation linking the prophet to Micah); One king entices (hesit) another into a disastrous war; Two kings sit in royal robes on thrones at the threshing floor by the city gate; A righteous king allies by marriage with a wicked king's house; Prophet imprisoned on 'bread of affliction and water of affliction'; The prophet swears to speak only what his God tells him; The wounded king props himself in his chariot all day and dies at sunset; Four hundred court prophets unanimously promise victory; Court prophet makes iron horns: 'with these you will gore Aram'; A single true prophet, hated by the king because he never prophesies good for him; and 6 more.

Only in The chosen patriarchs; the Gardens of Eden and the quarrel of the damned: The damned ask 'Why do we not see men we counted among the wicked, whom we mocked?'; The prophet had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed (over Adam); Elisha (al-Yasa') is named among the excellent; Ishmael is named among the chosen prophets; The provision of paradise never runs out; Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are 'possessors of hands and sight' (power and insight); God's choice of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and what it passes on [divergence between the texts]; Entering hell, a crowd is greeted by those already there with 'No welcome to them!' and they retort in kind; A prophet called Dhū l-Kifl is listed among the patient; The Gardens of Eden have their gates opened for the righteous; Paradise has full-breasted companions of equal age (kawa'ib atrab); Whether a prophet has first-hand knowledge of the heavenly council [contrast between the texts]; and 3 more.

leads.title: Jehoshaphat's fast and prayer; the Levite oracle; enemies destroy one another as the choir sings ↔ Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Abraham is called God's friend (ohev, 'lover') (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Jehoshaphat's fast and prayer; the Levite oracle; enemies destroy one another as the choir sings: Prophetic assurance: 'the battle is not yours but God's'; The army arrives to find the enemy host all corpses on the ground, none escaped; 'Believe in YHWH and you will be established' (wordplay ha'aminu/te'amenu); A coalition of Moab, Ammon and their allies invades Judah from beyond the Dead Sea; Nations Israel was forbidden to attack during the exodus now repay this by attacking; The king stands in the temple court before the assembly and prays in a national crisis; 'We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you'; The king proclaims a fast throughout the land in a crisis; Ships built in alliance with a wicked king are wrecked, as a prophet foretold; Singers praising God march ahead of the army into battle; The spoil is so great that gathering it takes three days; All Judah stands before God with their little ones, wives and children; and 9 more.

Only in Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend: Satan commands people to alter God's creation; Idolaters invoke only female beings besides God, and only a rebellious Satan; Salvation is not by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book: whoever does evil is requited; Cursed Satan vows to take an appointed share (naṣīb mafrūḍ) of God's servants; Satan commands people to slit the ears of cattle (a pagan dedication rite); The faithless wife credits her lovers (the Baals) with her bread, water, wool, flax, oil and drink, not knowing God gave them; A rebel against the high god vows, in a string of first-person 'I will' clauses, to take and to command [divergence between the texts]; Whoever does good, male or female, and believes, enters paradise; God does not forgive associating partners with him (shirk) but forgives anything less; Not wronged by a date-stone's thread (fatīl) or groove (naqīr): proverbial minimal measures; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater; Offerings, incense and libations to the 'Queen of Heaven'.

leads.title: Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed ↔ Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed: After the usurper's execution the people rejoice and the city is quiet; A priestly coup is timed to the Sabbath change of temple guards, keeping both shifts; The newly crowned king stands by his pillar at the entrance; The usurper is led out so that she is not killed in the house of YHWH; The usurping queen tears her clothes and cries 'Treason, treason!'; The temple of Baal is torn down and its priest slain before the altars; Coronation in which the king receives the crown (nezer) and the 'testimony' (edut); King David's spears and shields kept in the temple are issued to the guards; A priest organizes the guards to overthrow a ruler and enthrone the hidden heir; King and people enter a covenant to seek or serve YHWH in a public ceremony; People acclaim 'Long live the king!'; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers.
