evidence.text: No longer produced by the current pipeline (2026-10-31): its statistics or cognate checks no longer meet the thresholds after a method change. Kept for review.
Shared motifs, rarest first: A small enemy force defeats a very great army because the people forsook God (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Joash repairs the temple with the collection chest; after Jehoiada's death he stones Zechariah: A king who was righteous under a mentor turns to idolatry after the mentor's death; A child king does right as long as his priestly guardian lives; A chest is set at the temple gate for donations, emptied daily by royal and priestly officials; A murdered prophet's dying words call on God to see and avenge; A king kills the son of the man who saved and raised him, forgetting his loyalty; The Levites are slow to carry out the king's command and are rebuked; A priest is buried among the kings because of the good he did; The priestly guardian takes two wives for the king; The priest dies old and full of days at 130; A prophet is stoned in the temple court at the king's command; God sends prophets to warn the people but they will not listen; Surplus donations are made into gold and silver temple vessels; and 9 more.

Only in Badr and Uhud: God helped you at Badr when you were weak; The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter; Such days God alternates among people; Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils); Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection; After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters; Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds; Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken; The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them; Those who restrain anger and pardon people; It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me; Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled; and 17 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Who tests whom between Solomon and the queen of Sheba [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The queen of Sheba visits Solomon (weight 7.7); The queen of Sheba's gifts and Solomon's response [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The great throne in the Sheba story, and whose it is [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The queen of Sheba overwhelmed by Solomon's buildings [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); What the queen of Sheba says of Solomon's God [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); A foreign queen tests the king with riddles and he answers them all (weight 7.3). Only in The Queen of Sheba tests Solomon; his gold, ivory throne, ships and death: A foreign ruler blesses Israel's God for setting the king on his throne; The king exceeds all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom; An annual income of 666 talents of gold; A visitor says she did not believe the report until she saw: not half was told her; Rare almug wood from Ophir used for temple supports and lyres for singers; never seen again; Promised land stretches from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates; A visitor seeing the king's court is left breathless ('no more spirit in her'); A royal visitor arrives with camels carrying spices, gold and precious stones; All the kings of Arabia and governors bring gold and silver; Shields of beaten gold made or captured and displayed; Great ivory throne overlaid with gold, with six steps and twelve lions on the steps and two beside the arms; The king reigns forty years; and 6 more.

matches.note: Who tests whom: in Chronicles the queen comes to test Solomon with riddles (lənassôt ʾet Šəlōmōh bə-ḥîdôt) and he answers all (wə-lōʾ neʿlam dāvār miš-Šəlōmōh); in the Quran Solomon tests the queen: nakkirū lahā ʿarshahā nanẓur a-tahtadī, and she answers ka-annahu huwa.

passages.text: וּמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א שָֽׁמְעָה֮ אֶת שֵׁ֣מַע שְׁלֹמֹה֒ וַתָּב֣וֹא לְנַסּוֹת֩ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְחִיד֜וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בְּחַ֣יִל כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֡ד וּ֠גְמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב לָרֹ֖ב וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם לְבָבָֽהּ
וַיַּגֶּד לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת כָּל דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ וְלֹֽא נֶעְלַ֤ם דָּבָר֙ מִשְּׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ
قَالَ نَكِّرُوا۟ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا نَنظُرْ أَتَهْتَدِىٓ أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ قِيلَ أَهَٰكَذَا عَرْشُكِ قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ وَأُوتِينَا ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ

matches.label: The queen of Sheba's gifts and Solomon's response
matches.note: The gifts: Chronicles has the queen bring 120 talents of gold, spices and gems, which Solomon accepts, and he gives her all she desires (nātan ... ʾet kol ḥefṣāh). In the Quran she sends a gift (hadiyya) to test him, and Solomon refuses it, a-tumiddūnani bi-mālin fa-mā ātāniya llāhu khayrun mimmā ātākum, and threatens to invade with armies they cannot resist.

passages.text: וּמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א שָֽׁמְעָה֮ אֶת שֵׁ֣מַע שְׁלֹמֹה֒ וַתָּב֣וֹא לְנַסּוֹת֩ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְחִיד֜וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בְּחַ֣יִל כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֡ד וּ֠גְמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב לָרֹ֖ב וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם לְבָבָֽהּ
וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֗ב וּבְשָׂמִ֛ים לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ כַּבֹּ֣שֶׂם הַה֔וּא אֲשֶׁר נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה
וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א אֶת כָּל חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר הֵבִ֣יאָה אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַֽתַּהֲפֹ֛ךְ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ
وَإِنِّى مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِم بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌۢ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ قَالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍ فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم بَلْ أَنتُم بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ
ٱرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُم بِجُنُودٍ لَّا قِبَلَ لَهُم بِهَا وَلَنُخْرِجَنَّهُم مِّنْهَآ أَذِلَّةً وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ

matches.label: The queen of Sheba overwhelmed by Solomon's buildings
matches.note: The queen overwhelmed by Solomon's building: Chronicles has her see the house he built (wə-hab-bayit ʾăšer bānâ) until wə-lōʾ hāyâ ʿôd bāh rûaḥ; the Quran has the palace of smooth glass (ṣarḥun mumarradun min qawārīr) that she takes for deep water (ḥasibathu lujjatan) and uncovers her legs. Awe becomes a test she fails and then learns from. cf. Targum Sheni Esther 1:2 (glass floor), outside the HB.

passages.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה
וּמַאֲכַ֣ל שֻׁלְחָנ֡וֹ וּמוֹשַׁ֣ב עֲבָדָיו֩ וּמַעֲמַ֨ד מְשָׁרְתָ֜יו וּמַלְבּֽוּשֵׁיהֶ֗ם וּמַשְׁקָיו֙ וּמַלְבּ֣וּשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וַעֲלִיָּת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה ע֛וֹד בָּ֖הּ רֽוּחַ

قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدْخُلِى ٱلصَّرْحَ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ صَرْحٌ مُّمَرَّدٌ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

matches.label: What the queen of Sheba says of Solomon's God
matches.note: The queen's last word: Chronicles has a blessing of Solomon's God, yəhî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkā bārûkh ʾăšer ḥāfēṣ bəkhā lə-tittəkhā ʿal kisʾô, 'your God', praised for Israel's king. The Quran has a conversion: rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī wa-aslamtu maʿa Sulaymāna lillāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn, after the hoopoe reported that she and her people worshipped the sun (27:24). Chronicles never calls her an idolater.

matches.label: The great throne in the Sheba story, and whose it is
matches.note: The great throne: Chronicles praises Solomon's own (wa-yyaʿaś ham-melekh kissēʾ šēn gādôl wa-yṣappēhû zāhāv ṭāhôr); in the Quran the great throne is the queen's (wa-lahā ʿarshun ʿaẓīmun), and Solomon has it carried to him in the blink of an eye by one with knowledge of the Book.

matches.label: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon
matches.note: jiʾtuka min Sabaʾin bi-nabaʾin yaqīnin innī wajadtu mraʾatan tamlikuhum ~ û-malkat Šəvāʾ šāməʿâ ʾet šēmaʿ Šəlōmōh wat-tāvôʾ: a woman ruling Sheba (Sabaʾ / Šəvāʾ), a report (nabaʾ / šēmaʿ), and her coming to Solomon. The direction of the report is reversed: in Chronicles she hears of Solomon, in the Quran Solomon hears of her through the hoopoe.

leads.title: Athaliah's usurpation and the hidden prince Joash ↔ Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Coronation in which the king receives the crown (nezer) and the 'testimony' (edut) (weight 7.7); King David's spears and shields kept in the temple are issued to the guards (weight 7.7); The temple of Baal is torn down and its priest slain before the altars (weight 7.7); A priest organizes the guards to overthrow a ruler and enthrone the hidden heir (weight 7.7); People acclaim 'Long live the king!' (weight 6.6). Pair score 37.6.

Only in Athaliah's usurpation and the hidden prince Joash: Deposed ruler tears her/his garments crying 'Conspiracy, conspiracy!' or 'Treason!'; A condemned person is taken out so as not to be killed inside the sanctuary; A covenant is made between God, the king and the people; The king stands by (or on) the pillar in the temple according to custom; A queen mother seizes power by killing all the royal offspring; Sole surviving royal infant is stolen away with his nurse and hidden in the temple for years; Men tear their garments in grief or dismay.

Only in Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed: After the usurper's execution the people rejoice and the city is quiet; A priestly coup is timed to the Sabbath change of temple guards, keeping both shifts; The newly crowned king stands by his pillar at the entrance; The usurper is led out so that she is not killed in the house of YHWH; The usurping queen tears her clothes and cries 'Treason, treason!'; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; King and people enter a covenant to seek or serve YHWH in a public ceremony; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: After crossing the sea the people see idol-worshipers and ask the prophet for a god like theirs (weight 7.3); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 5.8). Pair score 13.1.

Only in Fall of Samaria and the sermon on Israel's exile: God warned the people by all his prophets and seers, 'Turn from your evil ways', but they would not listen; Vassal king withholds tribute and seeks help from Egypt, and is imprisoned; A capital city is besieged for three years before it falls; Kings or people practice divination (qesem) and augury (nihush); Theological sermon explaining the fall and exile of a nation as punishment for idolatry; Formula: he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat who made Israel sin; God calls Israel a stiff-necked people; King makes his son 'pass through the fire' after the abominations of the nations; Idols called 'elilim' ('nothings'); An Assyrian king named in the narrative (Pul, Tiglath-pileser, Shalmaneser, Sennacherib, Esarhaddon); People bow down to all the host of heaven; Pagan worship on high mountains, hills and under every green tree; and 1 more.

Only in Israel asks for a god like the idol-worshipers: Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; People demand a king 'like all the nations'; Israel chosen as God's treasured people (am segullah) out of all peoples; Ruler orders the killing of male infants.

leads.title: The resettled peoples, the lions and the syncretistic cult of Samaria ↔ Pagan portions and taboos; eight pairs; what is forbidden to all and to the Jews
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Settlers fear YHWH yet serve their own gods (syncretism) (weight 7.7); Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods (weight 6.2). Pair score 14.0.

Only in The resettled peoples, the lions and the syncretistic cult of Samaria: Catalogue of foreign gods brought by settler peoples (Succoth-benoth, Nergal, Ashima, Nibhaz, Tartak, Adrammelech, Anammelech); Each land has a god whose 'manner' (mishpat) newcomers must learn; God sends lions to kill settlers who do not know the 'law of the god of the land'; Empire settles foreign peoples in the cities of a deported population; A deported priest is sent back to teach the settlers how to fear the local god; Mutual declaration: Israel avows YHWH as God, YHWH avows Israel as his treasured people.

Only in Pagan portions and taboos; eight pairs; what is forbidden to all and to the Jews: Pagans set apart cattle whose backs may not be ridden or burdened; Eight in pairs: sheep, goats, camels and cattle, male and female; which did God forbid?; Idolaters say 'had God willed we would not have associated partners nor forbidden anything'; Give its due on the day of harvest; For the Jews God forbade every animal with claws/undivided hoof and the fat of cattle and sheep except on backs, entrails or bone; Do not be wasteful; God does not love the wasteful (musrifīn); Pagans assign a portion of crops and cattle to God and a portion to their partners; Pagans declare certain cattle and crops taboo (ḥijr), to be eaten only by whom they will; Pagans reserve what is in the wombs of cattle for males, forbidden to wives unless stillborn; The camel is unclean because it does not have a split hoof [contrast between the texts]; List of clean and unclean animals: split hoof and chewing cud [response between the texts]; The due from crops and young animals is given at once, at harvest time [divergence between the texts]; and 14 more.

leads.title: Hezekiah's reform; Sennacherib's invasion and the Rabshakeh's speech ↔ Sennacherib's invasion; the Rabshakeh's speech at the conduit
leads.summary: 12 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Invader promises deportees a land like their own, of grain, wine, oil and honey (weight 7.7); Officials ask the envoy to speak Aramaic, not Judean, so the people on the wall will not understand (weight 7.7); Invader claims the defenders' own god sent him to destroy the land (weight 7.7); Each man under his own vine and fig tree, drinking from his own cistern (weight 7.7); Enemy envoy addresses the besieged at the city wall to break their morale (weight 7.7); The people keep silent and do not answer the enemy at the king's command (weight 7.7); Threat that the besieged will eat their own dung and drink their urine (weight 7.3); Egypt likened to a broken reed staff that pierces the hand of whoever leans on it (weight 7.3); Taunt: Where are the gods of the conquered nations? Could they save their lands from my hand? (weight 6.8); An Assyrian king named in the narrative (Pul, Tiglath-pileser, Shalmaneser, Sennacherib, Esarhaddon) (weight 6.6); Command to smash altars, standing stones and Asherah poles and burn idols (weight 6.4); Men tear their garments in grief or dismay (weight 5.7). Pair score 86.7.

Only in Hezekiah's reform; Sennacherib's invasion and the Rabshakeh's speech: King smashes the bronze serpent made by Moses, called Nehushtan, because people burned incense to it; Image of a serpent on a pole heals those who look at it; A capital city is besieged for three years before it falls; King strips the temple and palace treasuries to buy off an invader; Conquered population deported to Assyria or another distant land; Formula: there was none like him among all the kings before or after.

Only in Sennacherib's invasion; the Rabshakeh's speech at the conduit: Prophet meets the king at the conduit of the upper pool on the highway of the Fuller's Field; Judah (or allies) put trust in Egypt and Cush for help against Assyria and are put to shame.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The king tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and goes into the temple in crisis (weight 7.7); Proverb of crisis: children have come to the birth-stool and there is no strength to deliver (weight 7.7); Royal parricides flee to the land of Ararat (weight 7.7); God puts a spirit in the invader so that he hears a rumor and returns home (weight 7.7); The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses (weight 7.7); The arrogant king boasts of climbing the heights of Lebanon and cutting its cedars, drying up rivers with his feet (weight 7.7); The 'virgin daughter of Zion' laughs at and wags her head after the enemy (weight 7.7); Sign: this year eat aftergrowth, next year what springs of itself, the third year sow and reap (weight 7.7); God says the conqueror's victories were planned by him long ago; the conqueror is only his instrument (weight 7.7); The escaped remnant shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward; a remnant goes out from Zion (weight 7.7); King spreads the enemy's threatening letter before God in the temple (weight 7.7); God's angels strike the enemy army [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); The enemy is said to reproach (harref) 'the living God' (weight 7.3); Enemy king is murdered by his own sons while worshipping in his god's temple (weight 7.1); God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant (weight 7.1); God will put his hook in the enemy king's nose and his bit in his lips and lead him back (weight 6.8); Conquered nations' gods were burned because they were no gods, only wood and stone made by hands (weight 6.8); Taunt: Where are the gods of the conquered nations? Could they save their lands from my hand? (weight 6.8); God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim (weight 6.5). Pair score 141.0.

Only in Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter: God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant [divergence between the texts]; When the punishment descends in their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings.

matches.label: The sage lets the prophet accompany him on condition he asks nothing until told
matches.note: A disciple insists on staying with a master who has hidden power, and the master's repeated warning sets a hard condition: šēb-nāʾ pōh ... ḥay-YHWH ... ʾim-ʾeʿezbekkā (three times), hiqšîtā lišʾôl ʾim-tirʾeh ʾōtî ... yəhî-ləkā kēn; hal attabiʿuka ʿalā an tuʿallimani ... innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabrā (three times) ... fa-lā tasʾalnī ʿan shayʾ. The roles are reversed: Elisha meets his condition and inherits the spirit, while Moses, the great prophet, fails three times and is sent away (hādhā firāqu baynī wa-baynik).

leads.title: Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God's power to make water sweet or bitter [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3); Bitter water made drinkable by throwing in a piece of wood God shows the leader (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.4.

Only in Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel: Small boys jeer 'Go up, baldhead!'; the prophet curses them and two she-bears maul forty-two of them; Prophet throws salt from a new bowl into the spring and heals the deadly, miscarriage-causing water 'to this day'.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 9 more.

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys ↔ Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm
leads.summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward) (weight 7.7); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die' (weight 7.7); A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king (weight 7.7); Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping (weight 7.7); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 7.3); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz (weight 7.3); At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won (weight 7.1). Pair score 60.1.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts]; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm: Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years; A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered; My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom; God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction; The dead cannot praise God: no wonders for the dead, no hesed in the grave, no faithfulness in Abaddon; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; In distress the sufferer chirps like a swift or crane and moans like a dove; Death or Sheol has gates (sha'arei mavet).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts]; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant; and 1 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 42 more.

וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע עֲלֵיהֶם֮ חִזְקִיָּהוּ֒ וַיַּרְאֵ֣ם אֶת כָּל בֵּ֣ית נְכֹתֹ֡ה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף֩ וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֨ב וְאֶת הַבְּשָׂמִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת שֶׁ֣מֶן הַטּ֗וֹב וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִמְצָ֖א בְּאֽוֹצְרֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא הֶרְאָ֧ם חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ וּבְכָל מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ
وَإِنِّى مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِم بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌۢ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ قَالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍ فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم بَلْ أَنتُم بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ

Shared motifs, rarest first: In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 7.3). Pair score 14.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts]; Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant; At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won.

Only in Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay: Spend before death comes and one says 'My Lord, if only you would delay me a little, I would give charity'; God delays no soul when its term comes; It is the same whether the prophet asks forgiveness for the hypocrites or not; God will not forgive them; The hypocrites testify 'You are God's messenger'; God knows he is, and testifies that the hypocrites are liars; The hypocrites say 'When we return to Medina the mightier will expel the meaner from it'; but might belongs to God, his messenger and the believers; Let not your wealth and children divert you from God's remembrance; The hypocrites' bodies impress and their speech is heard, but they are like propped-up timbers, thinking every cry is against them; The hypocrites take their oaths as a shield (junna) and will swear falsely even to God at the resurrection; When you eat and are full, beware lest you forget God; God forbids the prophet to pray or intercede for the people, for he will not hear; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain.

leads.title: Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot) (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo: Idolatrous cult objects are burned and their dust carried away or thrown on graves; Despite the righteous king's reform, God does not turn from his anger over a predecessor's sins; Horses dedicated to the sun at the temple entrance and chariots of the sun burned; The high places Solomon built on the 'mount of destruction' (Mount of Olives) for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom; The righteous king is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho; Priests of the high places are slaughtered on their own altars; The bones of a prophet are left undisturbed when other graves are desecrated; Priests of the high places may not serve at the altar but eat unleavened bread among their brothers; The Tophet in the valley of Ben-hinnom is defiled so no one may burn children to Molech; A Passover such as had not been kept since the days of the judges; Women weave 'houses' (garments, hangings) for Asherah in the temple precinct; A covenant is made between God, the king and the people; and 11 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; Night covers the sleepers as a garment, the land as in death; the day is a rising (waking); Two waters, the sweet and the salt sea, meet or mingle [divergence between the texts]; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; What sets the daily sleeping and rising of people [divergence between the texts]; God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; A god's act sets fresh (sweet) water against salt (bitter) water [divergence between the texts]; God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; The wind carries good news (Akk. bussurtu, Ar. bushr, mubashshirāt) [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah (weight 7.7); The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon (weight 7.7); The captive king's sons are slaughtered before his eyes, then his eyes are put out (weight 7.3); Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken (weight 7.3); Famine becomes severe in the besieged city; there is no bread (weight 6.6); A Babylonian king named in the narrative (Merodach-baladan, Nebuchadnezzar, Evil-merodach) (weight 6.6). Pair score 43.5.

Only in The siege and destruction of Jerusalem; Gedaliah; Jehoiachin released: Exiled king's head is 'lifted up' from prison; he changes his prison garments and eats at the conqueror's table; Temple pillars eighteen cubits high with bronze capitals, network and pomegranates; Only the poorest of the land are left behind as vinedressers and farmers; The temple, palace and great houses are burned by the conqueror's chief of guards (rav tabbahim); The bronze pillars, stands and sea are broken up and their bronze carried away; A governor appointed by the conqueror is assassinated by a member of the royal seed; The remnant flees to Egypt for fear of the conquerors (reverse exodus); Siege of Jerusalem begun on the tenth day of the tenth month (later a fast day); Captive's eyes are gouged out by his captors.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians; The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho; The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; Seven princes or counselors who 'see the king's face' advise the king; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; The temple treasures and gold vessels of Solomon are carried off to Babylon; and 1 more.

leads.title: Jehoram's campaign against Mesha of Moab ↔ Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay'
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not cut down fruit trees during a siege: is the tree of the field a man? (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Jehoram's campaign against Mesha of Moab: Besieged king offers his firstborn heir as a burnt offering on the city wall, and 'great wrath' falls on Israel, who withdraw; Prophet calls for a musician; as he plays, the hand of YHWH comes upon him; Prophet says he would not even look at the wicked king were it not for the righteous ally; Allied kings on a seven-day detour run out of water for army and beasts and despair; A sheep-breeding vassal king pays tribute of a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams; At sunrise the water looks red as blood; the enemy thinks the kings have slain each other and rushes to plunder; Dry wadi fills with water though no wind or rain is seen; Invaders fell every good tree, stop every spring and ruin every good field with stones; Standard regnal formula: age at accession, length of reign, mother's name, evaluation, burial, successor; Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods.

Only in Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay': The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world; God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr); Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave; Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts; Vines or palms of a hostile neighbour are cut down [divergence between the texts]; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; How spoil taken from the enemy is distributed [divergence between the texts]; Fay' (booty gained without cavalry or camels) goes to God, the messenger, kin, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, so wealth does not circulate only among the rich; They thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; The wealth of a ruined or expelled people passes to others who did not have it [divergence between the texts]; The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; and 8 more.

leads.title: The Shunammite woman and her son ↔ Zechariah's secret prayer and the birth of John (Surah 19:1-15)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The Shunammite woman and her son: Child in the harvest field cries 'My head, my head!' and dies at noon on his mother's knees; Woman protests the promise of a son: 'Do not lie to your maidservant'; Prophet admits 'YHWH has hidden it from me and not told me'; A wealthy woman has a small roof-chamber built for the holy man with bed, table, chair and lamp; Offered a favor with king or general, the hostess replies 'I dwell among my own people'; Mother lays her dead son on the prophet's bed, shuts the door and rides to fetch him; Husband asks why she visits the prophet when it is neither new moon nor sabbath; Prophet lies on the child, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands, until the body warms; Servant lays the prophet's staff on the dead child's face but there is no voice or response; Revived child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes; Servant sent in haste must greet no one and answer no greeting on the road; Bereaved woman grasps the prophet's feet; the servant tries to push her away; and 7 more.

Only in Zechariah's secret prayer and the birth of John (Surah 19:1-15): The child is given judgment and wisdom while still a boy; The aged father asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is very old; As a sign of the promised son the father cannot speak to people for three days or nights; The announced son receives a name never given to anyone before; A petitioner calls to God in a hidden, secret voice; The mute priest comes out of the sanctuary and signals to the people to glorify God; The childless priest fears for his kinsmen after him and asks for an heir to the family of Jacob; A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name [divergence between the texts]; Formula: 'from when you did not exist' / 'when you were nothing'; Old man's prayer: 'my bones have weakened and my head is aflame with gray'; A childless man pleads with the deity for a son to inherit from him and stand in his house, and is granted one; A childless man prays to his god for an heir, recalling his past devotion; and 16 more.

leads.title: Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb and David's punishment ↔ David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A man with many sheep takes another's only ewe [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The king confesses 'I have sinned' and the prophet announces forgiveness with a remaining penalty (weight 7.7); David's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A case about a ewe is brought to David for judgment [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A prophet tells a case as if real; the king condemns the offender and is told 'You are the man' (weight 7.1). Pair score 38.0.

Only in Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb and David's punishment: A child born of the sin dies as punishment for the father; A child is given a second name by a prophet at God's word; Father fasts and lies on the ground praying for a dying child; God reminds the king he gave him his predecessor's house and wives; 'I shall go to him, but he will not return to me'; After the death the mourner unexpectedly rises, washes, anoints himself and eats; A poor man's only ewe lamb, raised like a daughter, taken by a rich man for a guest; Punishment: the sword will never depart from the king's house; Punishment: the king's wives will be lain with publicly 'before the sun'; Five oxen for a stolen ox and four sheep for a stolen sheep.

Only in David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes: Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him; A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument; A case is put to a judge as real, and his verdict on it turns on himself [divergence between the texts]; 'O David, we made you a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; judge between people with truth and do not follow desire'; David realizes he was being tested, asks forgiveness, falls down bowing and turns in repentance; God strengthened David's kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive judgment (fasl al-khitab); A named 'day of reckoning' on which accounts are settled; Shall God treat believers like those who spread corruption, the godfearing like the wicked?; Sheep are divided so that one party takes nine (ninety-nine) and the other one [divergence between the texts]; A man of means covets and seizes a poorer man's animal, and the case goes before a judge [divergence between the texts]; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth.

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה אֶת נָתָ֖ן אֶל דָּוִ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ שְׁנֵ֣י אֲנָשִׁ֗ים הָיוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר אֶחָ֔ת אֶחָ֥ד עָשִׁ֖יר וְאֶחָ֥ד רָֽאשׁ
وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا۟ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ

matches.label: A man with many sheep takes another's only ewe
matches.note: The case itself. Sam: lə-ʿāšîr hāyâ ṣōʾn û-ḇāqār harbēh məʾōḏ wə-lā-rāš ʾên-kōl kî ʾim-kiḇśâ ʾaḥaṯ qəṭannâ ... wa-ttəhî-lô kə-ḇaṯ. The rich man takes the lamb to feed a traveller. Q: inna hādhā akhī lahu tisʿun wa-tisʿūna naʿjatan wa-liya naʿjatun wāḥidatun fa-qāla akfilnīhā wa-ʿazzanī fī l-khiṭāb. The exact number 99 against Samuel's 'very many', 'my brother' against 'two men in one city', and the claim made by force of speech, not by theft for a guest. The pathos of the lamb 'like a daughter' is gone.

passages.text: לְעָשִׁ֗יר הָיָ֛ה צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד

וְלָרָ֣שׁ אֵֽין כֹּ֗ל כִּי֩ אִם כִּבְשָׂ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָ֔ה וַיְחַיֶּ֕הָ וַתִּגְדַּ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ וְעִם בָּנָ֖יו יַחְדָּ֑ו מִפִּתּ֨וֹ תֹאכַ֜ל וּמִכֹּס֤וֹ תִשְׁתֶּה֙ וּבְחֵיק֣וֹ תִשְׁכָּ֔ב וַתְּהִי ל֖וֹ כְּבַֽת

וַיָּ֣בֹא הֵלֶךְ֮ לְאִ֣ישׁ הֶֽעָשִׁיר֒ וַיַּחְמֹ֗ל לָקַ֤חַת מִצֹּאנוֹ֙ וּמִבְּקָר֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת לָאֹרֵ֖חַ הַבָּא ל֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֗ח אֶת כִּבְשַׂת֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָרָ֔אשׁ וַֽיַּעֲשֶׂ֔הָ לָאִ֖ישׁ הַבָּ֥א אֵלָֽיו
إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِى لَهُۥ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِىَ نَعْجَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلْخِطَابِ

matches.label: David's repentance and what follows it
matches.note: Verdict, recognition and outcome. Sam: David burns with anger, ben-māweṯ hā-ʾîš, fourfold restitution; Nathan: ʾattâ hā-ʾîš; David: ḥāṭāʾṯî la-YHWH; pardon with a penalty, gam ha-bbēn ha-yyillôḏ ləḵā môṯ yāmûṯ, and the sword never leaves his house (12:10). Q: a calm verdict, la-qad ẓalamaka bi-suʾāli naʿjatika ilā niʿājihi; no 'you are the man'. David himself perceives (ẓanna Dāwūdu annamā fatannāhu) that it was a test, fa-staghfara rabbahu wa-kharra rākiʿan wa-anāb, and then fa-ghafarnā lahu dhālika wa-inna lahu ʿindanā la-zulfā wa-ḥusna maʾāb. Full forgiveness and honour, with no dead child and no curse on the house. The sin (Uriah, Bathsheba, 2 Sam 12:9) is never named.

passages.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֥ף דָּוִ֛ד בָּאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל נָתָ֔ן חַי יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֣י בֶן מָ֔וֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה זֹֽאת
וַיֹּ֧אמֶר נָתָ֛ן אֶל דָּוִ֖ד אַתָּ֣ה הָאִ֑ישׁ כֹּה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָנֹכִ֞י מְשַׁחְתִּ֤יךָֽ לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָנֹכִ֥י הִצַּלְתִּ֖יךָ מִיַּ֥ד שָׁאֽוּל
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל נָתָ֔ן חָטָ֖אתִי לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר נָתָ֜ן אֶל דָּוִ֗ד גַּם יְהוָ֛ה הֶעֱבִ֥יר חַטָּאתְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תָמֽוּת

قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِى بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًا وَأَنَابَ

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God strengthened David's kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive judgment (fasl al-khitab) (weight 7.7); A prophet tells a case as if real; the king condemns the offender and is told 'You are the man' (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.8.

Only in The wise woman of Tekoa wins Absalom's return: A returned exile may not see the king's face; The king guesses who is behind a petitioner's speech; An only heir called 'my remaining ember' that kinsmen would quench; A woman disguised as a long-mourning widow petitions the king with an invented case; Oath that not one hair of the person shall fall to the ground; Mortality likened to water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up; A brother kills his brother in the first murder; A person praised as 'good (or wise) as an angel of God'; A wise woman intercepts an avenging warrior with gifts and speech and averts bloodshed; The 'redeemer of blood' (go'el ha-dam) kills the murderer.

Only in David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes: Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him; A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument; A case about a ewe is brought to David for judgment [divergence between the texts]; A case is put to a judge as real, and his verdict on it turns on himself [divergence between the texts]; 'O David, we made you a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; judge between people with truth and do not follow desire'; David realizes he was being tested, asks forgiveness, falls down bowing and turns in repentance; David's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts]; A named 'day of reckoning' on which accounts are settled; A man with many sheep takes another's only ewe [divergence between the texts]; Shall God treat believers like those who spread corruption, the godfearing like the wicked?; The king confesses 'I have sinned' and the prophet announces forgiveness with a remaining penalty; Sheep are divided so that one party takes nine (ninety-nine) and the other one [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God gave David the Psalms (Zabur) (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in The last words of David: A just ruler is like the morning sun on a cloudless day; Poem opening with 'Oracle (ne'um) of the man...' formula; The spirit of God speaks through the king's tongue; The wicked are thorns that cannot be handled and are burned; God has made an everlasting covenant with the king's house.

Only in The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three': The angels brought near (al-muqarrabūn) to God; God spoke to Moses directly (kallama taklīman); Jesus is God's word cast to Mary and a spirit from him; Catalogue of prophets who received revelation, from Noah to Jesus; People of the Book, do not go to excess (lā taghlū) in your religion; The Messiah does not disdain to be a servant of God, nor do the angels brought near; Do not say 'three'; God is only one god (rejection of a triad); First servant song: God's chosen servant with his spirit brings justice to the nations without crying out; a bruised reed he will not break; Of the messengers before you, some we have related to you and some we have not; God speaks to the prophet face to face, as a man speaks to his friend; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; Denial that God has taken a son (walad); and 2 more.

leads.title: David's census, the plague, and Araunah's threshing floor ↔ Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn) (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in David's census, the plague, and Araunah's threshing floor: Itinerary of census-takers around the land's borders; The king's heart strikes him after a sin; The commander objects to the king's census; Counting the people requires a ransom for each life to avert plague; A prophet offers the king a choice among three punishments; God halts the destroying angel at a specific spot: 'Enough, stay your hand'; God himself incites a person to an evil act; The king refuses a free gift of land for an altar and pays its price; King asks that punishment fall on him and his house rather than on the innocent 'sheep'; Census totals given tribe by tribe; Exact number of dead in a divine plague is given; A threshing floor where the plague was stopped becomes the site of the altar and temple; and 1 more.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Executed men's hands and feet cut off and their bodies hung up publicly (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Ishbosheth murdered in his bed; Mephibosheth's lameness: A severed head is buried in another man's tomb; A king is murdered on his bed during the noonday rest; A royal child is lamed when his nurse drops him while fleeing; A man who brings 'good news' of the enemy king's death and claims credit is executed; Assassins bring the severed head of a king to his rival hoping for reward.

Only in Penalty for waging war on God; the ransom of the earth; the thief's hand: Cut off the hands of the male and female thief as recompense; Those who repent before they are overpowered are pardoned; Seek a means of approach (al-wasīla) to God; Those who wage war on God and spread corruption: killed, crucified, hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or exiled; Cutting off hands and feet as the punishment of those who sin against (wage war on) the god [divergence between the texts]; Neither their silver nor their gold can save them on the day of YHWH's wrath; Each wrongdoer would ransom himself with all that is on earth, if he could; The penalty for theft [neutral] [contrast between the texts]; No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly.

matches.note: Q: an yuqattalū aw yuṣallabū aw tuqaṭṭaʿa aydīhim wa-arjuluhum min khilāfin. 2Sam: wa-yyahargûm wa-yqaṣṣəṣû ʾet-yədêhem wə-ʾet-raglêhem wa-yyitlû ʿal-hab-bərēkhāh. Hands and feet cut off and the body exposed. In 2Sam it is the king's one-off sentence on assassins; in Q a standing law for those who wage war on God and his Messenger, with 'opposite sides' and an alternative of exile (yunfaw).

leads.title: David king over all Israel; capture of Jebusite Zion ↔ Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether the blind and the lame may enter the house or share its table [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in David king over all Israel; capture of Jebusite Zion: Defenders boast that even the blind and lame could repel the attacker; A city is entered through its water shaft or conduit; A conquered fortress is renamed after the conquering king; A foreign king sends cedar wood and craftsmen to build the king's house or temple; The hero adds wives to his household; The people (or tribe) themselves anoint a king; A claimant appeals: remember that I am your bone and your flesh; A king's age at accession and length of reign are given; List of the king's sons, daughters, wife and commander; The king is called to 'shepherd' God's people.

Only in Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger: Do not address the messenger as you address one another, nor slip away without his leave; Elderly women past hope of marriage may lay aside their outer garments without displaying adornment; No blame on the blind, lame, sick or anyone eating in the houses of listed relatives or friends, together or apart; Slaves and children must ask permission at three times of undress: before dawn prayer, at noon and after the night prayer; You may eat your fill in a neighbor's vineyard or pluck ears by hand, but not carry away or use a sickle; On entering houses greet one another with a blessed greeting from God; Creditor must wait outside for the pledge and return a poor man's cloak by sunset; Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind.

matches.note: laysa ʿalā l-aʿmā ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā l-aʿraji ḥarajun ... an taʾkulū min buyūtikum ~ ʿal kēn yōʾmərû ʿiwwēr û-fissēaḥ lōʾ yāvôʾ ʾel hab-bāyit: the same pair, blind and lame (aʿmā, aʿraj ~ ʿiwwēr, pissēaḥ). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark is carried on a new cart drawn by oxen (weight 7.7); The ark stays three months in a foreigner's house and God blesses his household (weight 7.7); A man who reaches out to steady the ark when the oxen stumble is struck dead (weight 7.7); The ark is brought up in procession with singing, lyres, harps, drums, cymbals and trumpets (weight 7.3); Kiriath-jearim also called Baalah or Kiriath-baal (weight 7.1); God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim (weight 6.5). Pair score 44.1.

Only in The ark brought to Jerusalem; Uzzah struck; David dances; Michal despises him: The ark is set in a tent the king pitched for it; The king blesses the people and gives each person bread and cakes; The king dances with all his might, girded in a linen ephod; A sacrifice offered after the first six steps of the bearers; A wife mocks her husband for exposing himself while dancing; Offenders punished by dying childless; A woman looks out through the window lattice; A place is named after an event that happened there, 'to this day'.

Only in The first attempt to bring up the ark; Uzza struck down: A place is named for God's 'breaking out' (perets) against someone (Perez-uzza, Baal-perazim); Witness fears he will die because he has seen God or an angel.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A prophet approves a plan, then is corrected by a revelation that night (weight 7.7); Israel is the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for himself (weight 7.7); God promises to make the chosen one's name great (weight 7.7); God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent (weight 7.7); God took the ruler from following the sheep (weight 7.7); Prayer of humility: 'Who am I and what is my house?' (weight 7.7); The king's son, not the king, will build the house for God's name (weight 7.3); God declares the king his son: 'I will be his father and he my son' (weight 7.1); God promises David's house and throne will endure forever (weight 6.6). Pair score 67.5.

Only in Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer: God's steadfast love will not be withdrawn from the heir as it was from the previous king; Obscure phrase 'this is the torah of man (adam)'; Wordplay on 'house' as temple and as dynasty; Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts]; God disciplines Israel as a man disciplines his son; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; The king, living in a cedar palace, proposes to build a house for God; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer: Pun on 'house': the king would build God a house; God will build the king a house (dynasty); Revelation described as God 'uncovering the ear' of his servant; The king lives in a cedar house while the ark of God remains under curtains; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

Only in Visions of locusts, fire and plumb line; Amos and Amaziah: The high places of Isaac (yishaq, spelled with sin) will be desolate; 'I am no prophet nor a prophet's son; I am a herdsman, and YHWH took me from following the flock'; Prophet's curse on the opposing priest: his wife will be a harlot, his children fall by sword, he will die in an unclean land; The priest of the royal sanctuary at Bethel reports the prophet to the king and orders him back to Judah: 'Go, seer, flee'; Vision of a cosmic fire that devours the great deep (tehom rabbah); the prophet intercedes and God relents; Vision of locusts after the king's mowing; the prophet intercedes 'Forgive! leads.title: The golden image and the fiery furnace ↔ Abraham, the stars, the smashed idols and the fire
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people (weight 6.2). Pair score 6.2.

Only in The golden image and the fiery furnace: God sends his angel to rescue his servants from death; All are commanded to bow to the king's image on pain of being thrown into a blazing furnace; The flames kill the men who throw the heroes into the furnace; A fourth figure appears walking in the fire, looking like a son of the gods (bar elahin); The furnace is heated seven times more than usual; The king sets up a golden image sixty cubits high and six wide on the plain of Dura; Envious courtiers 'eat the pieces' (slander) of the Jews and denounce their non-compliance to the king; The pagan king decrees that anyone who blasphemes or fails to fear the Jewish God will be punished; The rescued have not a hair singed, their garments unchanged, and no smell of fire on them; Long repeated list of imperial officials (satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates); A listed orchestra of instruments (horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, symphonia) signals the moment to bow to the idol; The faithful declare that God can save them, but even if he does not, they will not serve the king's gods; and 7 more.

Only in Abraham, the stars, the smashed idols and the fire: Abraham glances at the stars and says 'I am sick', so his people leave him behind; Abraham asks the idols 'Will you not eat? Why do you not speak?' and strikes them with his right hand; The people build a structure (bunyan) and cast Abraham into the blaze, but God makes them the lowest; Abraham looks at the stars, and why [divergence between the texts]; 'Do you worship what you carve, when God created you and what you make?'; Hero reasons from the stars, moon and sun to the one God; Hero smashes or burns idols; Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols.

leads.title: The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man ↔ The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man: Thrones are set and the Ancient of Days sits, his garment white as snow and his hair like pure wool; The seer asks one of the attendants or an angel, who explains the vision to him; A bear raised on one side with three ribs in its mouth is told 'Arise, devour much flesh'; The arch-enemy beast is slain and its body given over to burning fire; A heavenly figure or the holy ones are given everlasting dominion, glory and kingdom which all peoples serve; God's throne is flames of fire with wheels of burning fire; Four great beasts rise from the sea, each different, symbolizing successive kingdoms; A leopard with four wings and four heads is given dominion; The holy ones of the Most High (qaddishe 'elyonin) receive and possess the kingdom forever; The horn makes war against the holy ones and prevails until the Ancient of Days comes; A little horn with human eyes and a mouth speaking great things uproots three horns; Thousands of thousands serve God and myriads of myriads stand before him; and 15 more.

Only in The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger: Whoever is given his book in his left hand wishes he had never been given it and that death had been final; his wealth and power are gone; Whoever is given his book in his right hand says 'Here, read my book!' and lives a pleasing life in a lofty garden with fruit clusters near; He did not believe in God the Great and did not urge the feeding of the poor; The damned have no friend and no food except ghislin (foul washings/pus); Had he fabricated sayings against God, God would have seized him by the right hand and cut his aorta (watin); 'I swear by what you see and what you do not see'; 'Seize him, fetter him, roast him in hellfire, then thread him on a chain seventy cubits long'; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Reclining on couches lined with brocade, with the fruit of the gardens hanging near; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; An offence concerning food is repaid with foul food and drink [divergence between the texts]; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

leads.title: The ram, the he-goat and the little horn; Gabriel explains ↔ Dhul-Qarnayn, the setting and rising sun, and the barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-101)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Dhu l-Qarnayn ('the two-horned') is given power on earth and a way to everything (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The ram, the he-goat and the little horn; Gabriel explains: A king 'fierce of face' and understanding riddles arises, destroys the holy people, and is broken without human hand; Desolation reckoned as 2,300 evenings and mornings before the sanctuary is restored; A small horn grows up to the host of heaven, casts down some of the stars and tramples them; The tyrant magnifies himself against the Prince of the host / Prince of princes; A two-horned ram (Media-Persia) is trampled by a he-goat with one great horn (Greece) coming from the west without touching the ground; The seer is exhausted and sick for days after the vision; The seer finds himself in a vision at Susa the citadel by the river Ulai; The vision concerns the time of the end (et qets); The great horn breaks at its height and four horns arise toward the four winds (the successor kingdoms); A heavenly being or the seer asks 'Until when (ad matai)?' the desolation will last; The seer falls into a deep sleep on his face; the angel touches him and sets him on his feet; The seer is told to shut up and seal the vision/book until the end; and 3 more.

matches.label: Dhu l-Qarnayn ('the two-horned') is given power on earth and a way to everything
matches.note: hāʾayil ʾăšer-rāʾîtā baʿal haqqərānāyim malkê māday ûpārās, a two-horned ram pushing west, north and south, wəʾên maṣṣîl miyyādô; Dhū l-Qarnayn ('the possessor of the two horns') given power on earth and a way to everything, who travels west and east. The epithet is the same, baʿal haqqərānāyim / dhū l-qarnayn. In Dan it is the Persian empire, broken by the goat-king of Yāwān (Greece); in Q a just, God-guided ruler (usually identified with Alexander).

passages.text: וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ וָאֶרְאֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֣ה אַ֣יִל אֶחָ֗ד עֹמֵ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֻבָ֖ל וְל֣וֹ קְרָנָ֑יִם וְהַקְּרָנַ֣יִם גְּבֹה֗וֹת וְהָאַחַת֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה מִן הַשֵּׁנִ֔ית וְהַ֨גְּבֹהָ֔ה עֹלָ֖ה בָּאַחֲרֹנָֽה
רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת הָאַ֡יִל מְנַגֵּחַ֩ יָ֨מָּה וְצָפ֜וֹנָה וָנֶ֗גְבָּה וְכָל חַיּוֹת֙ לֹֽא יַֽעַמְד֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל מִיָּד֑וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה כִרְצֹנ֖וֹ וְהִגְדִּֽיל

وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَن ذِى ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ قُلْ سَأَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْهُ ذِكْرًا

قُلْ إِن كَانَ ءَابَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَآؤُكُمْ وَإِخْوَٰنُكُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُكُمْ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمْ وَأَمْوَٰلٌ ٱقْتَرَفْتُمُوهَا وَتِجَٰرَةٌ تَخْشَوْنَ كَسَادَهَا وَمَسَٰكِنُ تَرْضَوْنَهَآ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَجِهَادٍ فِى سَبِيلِهِۦ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِىَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِۦ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

leads.title: Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy (weight 7.7); Who must make pilgrimage to the sanctuary, and how often [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 6.4). Pair score 21.4.

Only in Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah: Unleavened bread, bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste; Justice, justice shall you pursue; No Asherah tree planted beside God's altar and no standing stone; Passover in the month of Aviv, at evening, at the chosen place; Feast of Weeks counted seven weeks from the first sickle in the standing grain; Seven full weeks (fifty days) counted from the sheaf offering to the new grain offering; Appoint judges and officers in every town to judge righteously; Passover offering boiled (bishalta) and eaten, flock or herd; Rejoice before God with sons, daughters, slaves and the Levite; Feast of Booths seven days after gathering threshing floor and winepress; you shall be only joyful; What is slaughtered on stone altars (nuṣub/anṣāb) is forbidden; the stones are abomination; Seven-day festival of dwelling in booths recalling the wilderness; and 3 more.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; Whether the deity eats (receives) the food and drink of the offerings [divergence between the texts]; The deity shows or assigns to the builder the site (old foundation) of the deity's house; and 13 more.

sides.note: Deut 19:15 lōʾ yāqûm ʿēd ʾeḥād bĕ-ʾîš ... ʿal pî šĕnê ʿēdîm ʾô ʿal pî šĕlōšâ ʿēdîm yāqûm dābār: two or three witnesses, sex not specified, for any charge; Q 2:282 wa-stashhidū shahīdayni min rijālikum fa-in lam yakūnā rajulayni fa-rajulun wa-mraʾatāni ... an taḍilla iḥdāhumā fa-tudhakkira iḥdāhumā l-ukhrā: two men, or one man and two women so that one can remind the other. The two-witness rule kept, applied to contracts, with women admitted at two for one.

matches.label: Limits on how many wives the leader may take
matches.note: A limit on the leader's wives. Deut: wə-lōʾ yarbeh-lô nāšîm wə-lōʾ yāsûr ləḇāḇô, a general cap on number, for fear his heart turns. Q: first an enumerated permission (innā aḥlalnā laka azwājaka ... khāliṣatan laka min dūni l-muʾminīn), then a freeze: lā yaḥillu laka n-nisāʾu min baʿdu wa-lā an tabaddala bihinna min azwājin wa-law aʿjabaka ḥusnuhunna. matches.note: How the word reaches the prophet: Deut 18:18 wə-nātattî dəvāray bə-fîw wə-dibber ʾălêhem, God puts his words in the prophet's mouth; Q 26:193-195 nazala bihi r-rūḥu l-amīnu ʿalā qalbika ... bi-lisānin ʿarabiyyin mubīnin, a spirit brings it down onto his heart, in Arabic. matches.label: Opponents accuse the prophet of forging lies against God
matches.note: The prophet who forges a message falls under God's sanction: ʾaḵ han-nāḇîʾ ʾăšer yāzîḏ lə-ḏabbēr dāḇār bi-šmî ʾēṯ ʾăšer lōʾ ṣiwwîṯîw ... û-mēṯ han-nāḇîʾ hahûʾ vs. am yaqūlūna ftarāhu qul ini ftaraytuhu fa-lā tamlikūna lī mina llāhi shayʾan. Deuteronomy gives the community a rule to judge the prophet; the Prophet turns the rule round as his own defence: if he forged it, God would deal with him, and no one could save him.

وَقَٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ
فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
وَقَٰتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ لِلَّهِ فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوْا۟ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: Men leave the battle line to go home, and how that is judged
matches.note: Going home from the battle line. Deut grants it as a right: mî-hā-ʾîš ʾăšer bānâ ḇayiṯ-ḥāḏāš ... yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô ... mî-hā-ʾîš ha-yyārēʾ wə-raḵ ha-llēḇāḇ yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô. The Quran condemns the same plea: yastaʾdhinu farīqun minhumu n-nabiyya yaqūlūna inna buyūtanā ʿawratun wa-mā hiya bi-ʿawratin in yurīdūna illā firārā. The exempted house and the fainthearted of Deut are the hypocrites of the Quran.

passages.text: וְדִבְּר֣וּ הַשֹּֽׁטְרִים֮ אֶל הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ מִֽי הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֤ה בַֽיִת חָדָשׁ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֲנָכ֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יַחְנְכֶֽנּוּ
וְיָסְפ֣וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים֮ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל הָעָם֒ וְאָמְר֗וּ מִי הָאִ֤ישׁ הַיָּרֵא֙ וְרַ֣ךְ הַלֵּבָ֔ב יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֛ס אֶת לְבַ֥ב אֶחָ֖יו כִּלְבָבֽוֹ

وَإِذْ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ يَثْرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمْ فَٱرْجِعُوا۟ وَيَسْتَـْٔذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوْرَةٌ وَمَا هِىَ بِعَوْرَةٍ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارًا
وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُوا۟ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ لَءَاتَوْهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُوا۟ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرًا

matches.label: Book-people who aided the enemy are brought down from their fortresses, terror cast in their hearts; some killed, some captured, their land inherited
matches.note: Treatment of a defeated walled enemy: wə-hikkîṯā ʾeṯ-kol-zəḵûrāh ... raq ha-nnāšîm wə-ha-ṭṭap̄ ... kol-šəlālāh tāḇōz lāḵ vs. farīqan taqtulūna wa-taʾsirūna farīqan wa-awrathakum arḍahum wa-diyārahum wa-amwālahum. matches.label: Messengers offer peace terms before battle
matches.note: The roles are reversed. Deut: Israel makes the offer (wə-qārāʾtā ʾēlêhā lə-šālôm), and a city that answers šālôm becomes forced labour (yihyû ləkā lāmas waʿăbādûkā). matches.label: Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness

matches.note: The fate of male enemies after the battle. Deuteronomy: first wə-qārāʾṯā ʾēlêhā lə-šālôm; if refused, wə-hikkîṯā ʾeṯ kol zəḵûrāh lə-p̄î ḥāreḇ, and women, children and cattle are spoil (šālāl). Quran: fa-ḍarba r-riqābi ḥattā idhā athkhantumūhum fa-shuddū l-wathāqa fa-immā mannan baʿdu wa-immā fidāʾan ḥattā taḍaʿa l-ḥarbu awzārahā: kill in the fight, but captives taken are freed as a favor or for ransom. matches.label: Who is exempted from going out to war
matches.note: Who may stay home from the campaign. Deuteronomy exempts by circumstance of property and family: mî hā-ʾîš ʾăšer bānâ ḇayiṯ ḥāḏāš ... nāṭaʿ kerem ... ʾēraś ʾiššâ wə-lōʾ ləqāḥāh yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô. The Quran rejects exactly that excuse: sa-yaqūlu laka l-mukhallafūna mina l-aʿrābi shaghalatnā amwālunā wa-ahlūnā (our property and families kept us busy), and exempts by disability only: laysa ʿalā l-aʿmā ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā l-aʿraji ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā l-marīḍi ḥaraj.

وَلَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا مَآ أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَآ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوا۟ وَّأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ ٱلدَّمْعِ حَزَنًا أَلَّا يَجِدُوا۟ مَا يُنفِقُونَ
إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَـْٔذِنُونَكَ وَهُمْ أَغْنِيَآءُ رَضُوا۟ بِأَن يَكُونُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلْخَوَالِفِ وَطَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

matches.note: Both remove a rebellious son for his parents' sake. Deut: after the fact and in public, bēn sôrēr ûmôreh ... ûrgāmuhû kol-ʾanšê ʿîrô, at the parents' own complaint. Q: a hidden pre-emptive killing by God's servant of a boy who has done nothing yet, fa-khashīnā an yurhiqahumā ṭughyānan wa-kufrā, which Moses protests as nafsan zakiyyatan bi-ghayri nafs. God then gives the parents a better child.

passages.text: כִּֽי יִהְיֶ֣ה לְאִ֗ישׁ בֵּ֚ן סוֹרֵ֣ר וּמוֹרֶ֔ה אֵינֶ֣נּוּ שֹׁמֵ֔עַ בְּק֥וֹל אָבִ֖יו וּבְק֣וֹל אִמּ֑וֹ וְיסְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵיהֶֽם
וְאָמְר֞וּ אֶל זִקְנֵ֣י עִיר֗וֹ בְּנֵ֤נוּ זֶה֙ סוֹרֵ֣ר וּמֹרֶ֔ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ שֹׁמֵ֖עַ בְּקֹלֵ֑נוּ זוֹלֵ֖ל וְסֹבֵֽא
וּ֠רְגָמֻהוּ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִיר֤וֹ בָֽאֲבָנִים֙ וָמֵ֔ת וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִשְׁמְע֥וּ וְיִרָֽאוּ
فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَٰمًا فَقَتَلَهُۥ قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَكِيَّةًۢ بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ لَّقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا نُّكْرًا
وَأَمَّا ٱلْغُلَٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَٰنًا وَكُفْرًا
فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهُ زَكَوٰةً وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًا

matches.note: Deut 21:1, 3 kî yimmāṣēʾ ḥālāl ... lōʾ nôdaʿ mî hikkāhû ... ʿeglat bāqār ʾăšer lōʾ ʿubbad bāh ʾăšer lōʾ māšĕkâ bĕ-ʿōl: an unsolved killing and an unworked heifer; Q 2:71-72 lā dhalūlun tuthīru l-arḍa ... wa-idh qataltum nafsan fa-ddāraʾtum fīhā: a heifer not used for ploughing and a killing over which people dispute. The ending is reversed: in Deut the killer stays unknown, the neck is broken (wĕ-ʿārĕpû) and the elders declare yādênû lōʾ šāpĕkû ʾet ha-ddām ha-zzeh, the blood atoned; in the Quran the cow is slaughtered (fa-dhabaḥūhā) and God brings out what was hidden (wa-llāhu mukhrijun mā kuntum taktumūn): the dead man is revived and the killer known.

וְהוֹרִ֡דוּ זִקְנֵי֩ הָעִ֨יר הַהִ֤וא אֶת הָֽעֶגְלָה֙ אֶל נַ֣חַל אֵיתָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא יֵעָבֵ֥ד בּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֣א יִזָּרֵ֑עַ וְעָֽרְפוּ שָׁ֥ם אֶת הָעֶגְלָ֖ה בַּנָּֽחַל

فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْىِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

matches.note: Deut 21:15 kî tihyênā lĕ-ʾîš šĕtê nāšîm hā-ʾaḥat ʾăhûbâ wĕ-hā-ʾaḥat śĕnûʾâ: a man with two wives, one loved and one hated, must still be fair to the hated wife's son; Q 4:3 fa-nkiḥū mā ṭāba lakum mina n-nisāʾi mathnā wa-thulātha wa-rubāʿa fa-in khiftum allā taʿdilū fa-wāḥidatan: marry two, three or four, but only one if you fear you cannot be just. Both take plural wives as given and regulate fairness; the Quran sets a number and makes fairness a condition.

matches.label: Who receives a double share of inheritance
matches.note: Deut 21:17 kî ʾet ha-bbĕkōr ... yakkîr lātet lô pî šĕnayim bĕ-kōl ʾăšer yimmāṣēʾ lô: the firstborn son gets a double portion; Q 4:11 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn: each son gets double a daughter's share. Deuteronomy: bēn sôrēr û-môreh ʾênennû šōmēaʿ bə-qôl ʾāḇîw û-ḇə-qôl ʾimmô ... zôlēl wə-sōḇēʾ; the parents bring him to the elders and kol ʾanšê ʿîrô stone him (ûḇiʿartā hā-rāʿ). Quran: wa-lladhī qāla li-wālidayhi uffin lakumā a-taʿidāninī an ukhraja; the charge is denying the resurrection (asāṭīru l-awwalīn), the parents pray for him (yastaghīthāni llāh), and there is no human penalty, only God's sentence (ḥaqqa ʿalayhimu l-qawl).

וּ֠רְגָמֻהוּ כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִיר֤וֹ בָֽאֲבָנִים֙ וָמֵ֔ת וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִשְׁמְע֥וּ וְיִרָֽאוּ

units.title: Divorce, newlyweds, pledges, wages, gleanings
