matches.label: How a husband divorces his wife
matches.note: Deut 24:1 kî māṣāʾ bāh ʿerwat dābār wĕ-kātab lāh sēper kĕrîtut wĕ-nātan bĕ-yādāh wĕ-šillĕḥāh: divorce for 'some indecency', by a written bill handed to her; Q 2:228-229 wa-l-muṭallaqātu yatarabbaṣna bi-anfusihinna thalāthata qurūʾin ... aṭ-ṭalāqu marratāni fa-imsākun bi-maʿrūfin aw tasrīḥun bi-iḥsān: no grounds and no document named; a waiting period of three menstrual cycles, the husband's right to take her back within it, and a limit of two revocable divorces. šillaḥ / sarraḥa, both 'send away'.

passages.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם לֹ֧א תִמְצָא חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ

وَٱلْمُطَلَّقَٰتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَٰثَةَ قُرُوٓءٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ إِنْ أَرَادُوٓا۟ إِصْلَٰحًا وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإِمْسَاكٌۢ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌۢ بِإِحْسَٰنٍ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُوا۟ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفْتَدَتْ بِهِۦ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

matches.label: Whether a divorced wife may return to her first husband after another marriage
matches.note: Opposite rulings on the same case. Deut 24:4 lōʾ yûkal baʿlāh hā-rīšôn ʾăšer šillĕḥāh lāšûb lĕ-qaḥtāh ... ʾaḥărê ʾăšer huṭṭammāʾâ kî tôʿēbâ hîʾ: after she has been another man's wife the first husband may never take her back, it is an abomination; Q 2:230 fa-in ṭallaqahā fa-lā taḥillu lahu min baʿdu ḥattā tankiḥa zawjan ghayrahu fa-in ṭallaqahā fa-lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā an yatarājaʿā: after the third divorce she may return to the first husband only after marrying another. The intervening marriage that bars return in Deut is the condition for return in the Quran.

passages.text: וְיָצְאָ֖ה מִבֵּית֑וֹ וְהָלְכָ֖ה וְהָיְתָ֥ה לְאִישׁ אַחֵֽר

לֹא יוּכַ֣ל בַּעְלָ֣הּ הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן אֲשֶֽׁר שִׁ֠לְּחָהּ לָשׁ֨וּב לְקַחְתָּ֜הּ לִהְי֧וֹת ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֗ה אַחֲרֵי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֻטַּמָּ֔אָה כִּֽי תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תַחֲטִיא֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה

فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنكِحَ زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُۥ فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ إِن ظَنَّآ أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ يُبَيِّنُهَا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ

matches.label: Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away
matches.note: Grounds and house reversed. Deut 24:1 kî māṣāʾ vāh ʿerwat dāvār we-kātav lāh sēfer kerîtut ... we-šillḥāh mi-bbêtô (he finds 'some indecency', writes a writ, sends her out of HIS house). Q 65:1 lā tukhrijūhunna min buyūtihinna wa-lā yakhrujna illā an yaʾtīna bi-fāḥishatin mubayyinatin: during the ʿidda the wife may not be put out of HER house, and 'flagrant indecency' is the only ground for eviction, not the ground for divorce. No written writ in the Quran; instead a counted waiting period (aḥṣū l-ʿidda).

passages.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם לֹ֧א תִמְצָא חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ

matches.note: Return to the wife: Deut 24:4 lōʾ yûkal baʿlāh hā-riʾšôn ... lāšûv le-qaḥtāh (after she has married another, never; tôʿēvāh hîʾ). sides.note: Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent.

passages.text: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا
وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ ٱلزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا۟ بِٱللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا۟ كِرَامًا

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

sides.note: A short list of apodictic prohibitions, the women's pledge as a small decalogue. Exodus: lōʾ yihyeh ləḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāp̄ lōʾ tiḡnōḇ lōʾ ṯaʿăneh ḇə-rēʿăḵā ʿēḏ šāqer. Quran: ʿalā an lā yushrikna bi-llāhi shayʾan wa-lā yasriqna wa-lā yaznīna wa-lā yaqtulna awlādahunna wa-lā yaʾtīna bi-buhtānin yaftarīnahu bayna aydīhinna wa-arjulihinna wa-lā yaʿṣīnaka fī maʿrūf. The same order of other gods, theft, adultery, killing and false speech, but addressed to women as a pledge (bayʿa) to the Prophet: murder narrowed to infanticide, false witness to a slander 'between their hands and feet' (false paternity, in tafsir), obedience to the Prophet added; no Sabbath, parents or coveting.

leads.title: Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature ↔ Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr) (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature: All things are wearisome; the eye is not sated with seeing nor the ear filled with hearing; Endless cycles: the sun rises and pants back to its place, the wind circles, rivers run to the sea which is never full; There is no remembrance of former people nor will there be of those yet to come; What has been is what will be; there is nothing new under the sun; The speaker Qohelet ('the assembler') is presented as son of David and king over Israel in Jerusalem (royal fiction); A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever; What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience).

Only in Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship: The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness; A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride; God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk; Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?'; God made the flood ship (or its survivors) a sign for all the worlds; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The moon travels across the sky as a vessel floats or swims; The sun ends its daily course at a resting place (the bedchamber where it is told 'Rest!', or its mustaqarr) [divergence between the texts]; God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning; The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); The crescent moon fixes the months and the reckoning of time; and 5 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes: He will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart; When goods increase, those who eat them increase; the owner only sees them with his eyes; The profit of the land is for all; a king is for (served by) the cultivated field; Sweet is the sleep of the laborer whether he eats little or much, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep; He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with income; If you see oppression of the poor in a province, do not be amazed: a high one watches over a high one, and higher ones over them; 'Naked I came from my mother's womb and naked I shall return there'; What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

leads.title: Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled ↔ God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: This life is fleeting; whether anything real follows it [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience) (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.8.

Only in Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled: Whatever has come to be has already been named; man cannot dispute with one stronger than he; All man's toil is for his mouth, yet the appetite (nefesh) is never filled; Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire; A man with a hundred children and long life who is unsatisfied and has no burial: the stillborn (nefel) is better off than he; Even if he lived a thousand years twice and saw no good, do not all go to one place?; God gives a man riches, possessions and honor but not the power to enjoy them; a stranger enjoys them; Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn; Human days on earth are a shadow.

Only in God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary: God made a secure sanctuary (haram amin) while people around are snatched away; Life on earth is slight or unreal set against the true life of the hereafter [divergence between the texts]; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [contrast between the texts]; Was not God's earth wide enough for you to emigrate (hijra) in it?; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; God provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him; Every soul shall taste death; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

leads.title: Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing) ↔ Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Let them laugh a little and weep much (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this; The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride; Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool; In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other; A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth; Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart; Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad; Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?; Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor; Do not be quick to anger, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; and 1 more.

Only in Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin: The Bedouin (al-a'rab) are harder in unbelief and hypocrisy; Shirkers say 'do not go out in the heat'; hell's fire is hotter; Poor volunteers turn away weeping because the prophet has no mounts for them; Who is excused from going out to war [divergence between the texts]; Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief; The prophet must never pray over a dead hypocrite or stand at his grave; The desert nomad does not know the gods' place or God's limits, and does not pray; Catalogue of believers: repenting, worshiping, praising, wandering/fasting (sa'ihun), bowing, prostrating, enjoining right; God uses the unbelievers' wealth and children to punish them in this life; Hypocrites swear excuses and ask permission to stay behind from the campaign; Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

leads.title: Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back! (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution: Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil; There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve; Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?'; I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things; Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine; Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it; No man has power over the wind (ruah) to restrain it, nor power over the day of death; there is no discharge in war; For everything there is a season and a time for every matter under heaven (birth and death, planting and uprooting, etc.); Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Human days on earth are a shadow; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 10 more.

matches.label: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back!
matches.note: No man can hold back the departing spirit: ʾên ʾāḏām šallîṭ bā-rûaḥ li-ḵlôʾ ʾeṯ hā-rûaḥ wə-ʾên šilṭôn bə-yôm ham-māweṯ vs. fa-lawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥulqūm ... fa-lawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīn. Qohelet states it as a limit of human power; the Quran turns it into a challenge: if you are not to be judged, bring the soul back.

leads.title: Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city ↔ Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city: A great king besieges a small city; a poor wise man delivers it by his wisdom, yet no one remembers him; Wisdom is better than might and weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good; A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down its trusted stronghold; The race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; time and chance (pega') happen to all; Man does not know his time; like fish caught in a net and birds in a snare, people are trapped in an evil time; 'Better is X than Y' comparative saying (tov ... min).

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; On the day of the Hour every community is seen kneeling (jathiya), each called to its book of deeds; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The prophet's mission and the hearers' closed ears, eyes and hearts: caused, sealed, or beyond his cure [divergence between the texts]; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 2 more.

leads.title: Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal: Royal decree that every man shall rule in his own house; Merry with wine, the king orders the queen brought in her crown to show her beauty to his guests; A decree written into the laws of Persia and Media cannot be revoked; At the royal banquet drinking is by rule, no one compelled; The disobedient queen is deposed and her royalty given to 'another better than she'; The queen refuses to come at the king's command and the king is enraged; King holds a banquet showing his riches for 180 days; The queen holds a separate banquet for the women; Seven named eunuchs serve the king; Palace garden decorated with fine hangings, marble columns, gold and silver couches and mosaic pavement; Susa the citadel (Shushan ha-birah) as setting; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; and 2 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 42 more.

leads.title: The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot ↔ Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether an adopted or fostered child counts as one's own child [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot: King grants the provinces a remission and gives gifts at the new queen's feast; Virgins gathered from all provinces so the king may choose a new queen; Hero's genealogy runs back to Kish the Benjaminite (Saul's father); Heroine at the foreign court hides her people and kindred on her guardian's orders; A courtier's service is recorded in the royal book of chronicles before the king; Heroine has a Hebrew name (Hadassah) and a foreign one (Esther); Two eunuch doorkeepers plot to kill the king; the hero learns of it and reports it; A royal eunuch keeps the harem and supplies the women's cosmetics; Hero's family was deported from Jerusalem with King Jeconiah; Heroine wins the favor of her guardian official, who gives her special treatment; Heroine asks for nothing beyond what the eunuch advises when she goes to the king; Each maiden goes to the king for one night and passes to the concubines' house; and 5 more.

Only in Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers: God took a solemn covenant (mithaq) from the prophets: Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary; Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God has not put two hearts inside any man; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him; Zihar: a husband declaring his wife 'like my mother's back'; she is not his mother, the saying is false and abhorrent; The ruler (crown prince, prophet) is to be loved as, or to be closer than, one's own self [divergence between the texts].

leads.title: Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman; the lot is cast and the decree of extermination issued ↔ Pharaoh, 'no god but me', Haman's tower of fired brick, and the drowning

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Hāmān appears as Pharaoh's minister and partner (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman; the lot is cast and the decree of extermination issued: Villain called 'the Agagite' opposes a hero descended from Kish the Benjaminite; Villain offers the king ten thousand talents of silver for permission to destroy a people; King promotes a courtier and sets his seat above all the princes; Courtiers press the hero day after day to obey the order, and he refuses; Decree to destroy, kill and annihilate an entire people, young and old, women and children, on a single day; King and his vizier sit down to drink while the city is thrown into confusion by their decree; King takes off his signet ring and gives it to a courtier to seal decrees; Offended by one man, the villain seeks to destroy his whole people; The lot (pur) is cast day by day and month by month to choose the date of destruction; A people 'scattered and dispersed among the peoples' whose laws differ from all others is denounced to the king; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; Royal letters carried by runners throughout the realm; and 2 more.

Only in Pharaoh, 'no god but me', Haman's tower of fired brick, and the drowning: Pharaoh's people are made leaders who call to the Fire and are cursed in this world; A ruler has bricks made for a lofty building that reaches up to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Fire is kindled to make the bricks of a lofty house or tower [divergence between the texts]; The wise counselors of Pharaoh in Zoan and Memphis are fools: 'I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings'; Pharaoh tells his chiefs: 'I know of no god for you other than me'; Pharaoh orders Haman to build him a lofty tower (sarh) to reach the ways of heaven and look at Moses' God; Pharaoh's question about, or claim to know, the god of Moses [divergence between the texts]; Building with baked bricks and bitumen instead of stone and mortar; The king of Egypt is called god (by his vassals, or by himself) [divergence between the texts]; A king is called, or calls himself, the god of his people [divergence between the texts]; Humans build a tower whose top reaches heaven [divergence between the texts]; The king of Egypt is (called) the god or lord of those under him; and 4 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman; the lot is cast and the decree of extermination issued: Villain called 'the Agagite' opposes a hero descended from Kish the Benjaminite; Villain offers the king ten thousand talents of silver for permission to destroy a people; King promotes a courtier and sets his seat above all the princes; Courtiers press the hero day after day to obey the order, and he refuses; Decree to destroy, kill and annihilate an entire people, young and old, women and children, on a single day; King and his vizier sit down to drink while the city is thrown into confusion by their decree; King takes off his signet ring and gives it to a courtier to seal decrees; Offended by one man, the villain seeks to destroy his whole people; The lot (pur) is cast day by day and month by month to choose the date of destruction; A people 'scattered and dispersed among the peoples' whose laws differ from all others is denounced to the king; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; Hāmān appears as Pharaoh's minister and partner; and 2 more.

Only in Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons: Midwives observe the newborn on the birthstool (ovnayim, 'the two stones'); Oppressed people forced to build store-cities with mortar and bricks; God rewards the God-fearing midwives by making them houses (families); Midwives excuse themselves: Hebrew women are vigorous and give birth before the midwife arrives; Two named midwives fear God and disobey the king's order to kill boys; A new king arises who did not know the former benefactor; The more the people are oppressed, the more they multiply; The people 'swarm' (sharats) and fill the land like creatures in creation; Ruler fears the immigrant people will grow numerous and join his enemies; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How Egypt remembers Joseph [divergence between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

leads.finding: Why Pharaoh oppresses Israel

units.title: Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons
Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water

matches.label: Why Pharaoh oppresses Israel
matches.note: Why Pharaoh oppresses: Exodus gives his fear that the people will grow and side with enemies (pen yirbeh ... wə-nôsaf gam hûʾ ʿal śōnʾênû); the Quran gives his arrogance (ʿalā fī l-arḍ) and division of the people into factions. The Quran adds God's counter-purpose: to make the oppressed leaders and heirs and to show Pharaoh, Hāmān and their hosts 'what they feared' (mā kānū yaḥdharūn), so the fear of Exod 1:10 is the very thing God brings about.

matches.label: Pharaoh's order to kill the sons and let the women live
matches.note: Kill the sons, spare the daughters, on the same root: wa-hămittɛn ʾōṯô wə-ʾim-baṯ hîʾ wā-ḥāyâ ... wə-ḵol-ha-bbaṯ təḥayyûn vs. uqtulū abnāʾa lladhīna āmanū maʿahu wa-staḥyū nisāʾahum (ḥ-y-y in both: 'let live'). Q: after Moses arrives with the truth, against the sons of those who believe with him, a religious persecution.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows (weight 7.7); Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites (weight 7.7); What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 5.7); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 5.5). Pair score 34.5.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 16 more.

Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; The defeated enemy's form (image or body) is kept as a sign (Akk. ittu, Ar. āya) for those who come after [divergence between the texts]; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; The defeated foe (its image or its body) is kept as a sign (ittu / aya) for those who come after; How Moses' own people in Egypt respond to his message [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

matches.note: Why Pharaoh pursues: in Exod regret at losing the slave labour (mah-zōʾt ʿāśînû kî-šillaḥnû ʾet-yiśrāʾēl mēʿobdēnû); in Q aggression and enmity (fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu wa-junūduhu baghyan wa-ʿadwan).

passages.text: וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם וַ֠יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָבְדֵֽנוּ

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتْ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓا۟ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

matches.label: What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea
matches.note: The drowned are seen as a sign afterwards: fa-l-yawma nunajjīka bi-badanika li-takūna li-man khalfaka āyatan vs wayyarʾ yiśrāʾēl ʾet-miṣrayim mēt ʿal-śᵉpat hayyām. Exod shows the Egyptian dead on the shore to Israel then; Q singles out Pharaoh's body, saved from the sea as a sign for later generations.

passages.text: וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיַּ֤רְא יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵ֖ת עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם
فَٱلْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ ءَايَةً وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَغَٰفِلُونَ

matches.label: The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives
matches.note: wa-jāwaznā bi-banī isrāʾīla l-baḥra fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu ... ḥattā idhā adrakahu l-gharaq vs wayyāšūbû hammayim wayᵉkassû ʾet-hārekeb ... lᵉkōl ḥêl parʿōh.

passages.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיְכַסּ֤וּ אֶת הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאֶת הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים לְכֹל֙ חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיָּ֑ם לֹֽא נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד אֶחָֽד

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغْيًا وَعَدْوًا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَتْ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓا۟ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

matches.label: Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows
matches.note: At the sea the pursuers recognise Israel's God: wayyōʾmer miṣrayim ʾānûsāh mippᵉnê yiśrāʾēl kî YHWH nilḥām lāhem vs Pharaoh's āmantu annahu lā ilāha illā lladhī āmanat bihi banū isrāʾīl. Exod gives it to the Egyptians as a group, Q to Pharaoh alone. cf. Pirqe de-R. Eliezer 43 and Mekhilta (Pharaoh survives and repents), outside the canon.

passages.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵֽן
וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יֹצְאִ֖ים בְּיָ֥ד רָמָֽה
וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִ֤י מְחַזֵּק֙ אֶת לֵ֣ב מִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָבֹ֖אוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל חֵיל֔וֹ בְּרִכְבּ֖וֹ וּבְפָרָשָֽׁיו

وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ ءَاتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُۥ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَٰلًا فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِكَ رَبَّنَا ٱطْمِسْ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَٱشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Only in The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna: The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); Manna named from the people's question 'What is it?' matches.label: Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites
matches.note: Motive for the pursuit: Exodus gives Pharaoh's regret (mah zōʾt ʿāśînû kî šillaḥnû ʾet Yiśrāʾēl mēʿovdēnû) and God hardening his heart so he will pursue and God be glorified (wə-ḥizzaqtî ʾet lēv Parʿōh wə-rādaf ʾaḥărêhem wə-ʾikkāvədâ bə-Farʿōh); Q 26:52 says only that God warned Moses 'innakum muttabaʿūn', and 26:54-55 gives Pharaoh's contempt (la-shirdhimatun qalīlūna ... la-ghāʾiẓūn). There is no regret over losing slaves and no hardening.

matches.label: Whether those who saw the sea miracle believed
matches.note: Ending of the sea story: Exod 14:31 wa-yyîrəʾû hā-ʿām ʾet YHWH wa-yyaʾămînû ba-YHWH û-və-Mōše ʿavdô, the people believe, and the Song follows (15:1). The Quran's refrain: inna fī dhālika la-āyatan wa-mā kāna aktharuhum muʾminīna, a sign, yet most of them did not believe. matches.label: Twelve springs in the wilderness

'underneath') of the mountain; Q 2:63 wa-idh akhadhnā mīthāqakum wa-rafaʿnā fawqakumu ṭ-ṭūra khudhū mā ātaynākum bi-quwwatin: God raises the mountain above them as he takes the covenant. matches.label: Moses' upbringing in Pharaoh's house
matches.note: a-lam nurabbika fīnā walīdan wa-labithta fīnā min ʿumurika sinīna ~ wat-təviʾēhû lə-vat Parʿōh wa-yhî lāh lə-vēn: Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house. Exodus credits Pharaoh's daughter and never has Pharaoh mention it; in the Quran Pharaoh himself throws the upbringing at Moses as a favor he is owed.

passages.text: וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ
قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ

matches.label: How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged
matches.note: The killing: Exod 2:12 wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš wa-yyakh ʾet ham-Miṣrî wa-yyiṭmənēhû ba-ḥôl, deliberate and hidden, to defend a Hebrew (2:11); Q 26:20 faʿaltuhā idhan wa-ana mina ḍ-ḍāllīna, Moses admits he did it while 'astray', and Pharaoh calls him ungrateful (wa-anta mina l-kāfirīn). Exodus has no confession.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו
וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל

قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

leads.finding: Moses helps the women at the water of Midian

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry
At the water of Midian; the two women, their old father and the marriage contract

matches.label: Moses helps the women at the water of Midian
matches.note: At the water of Midian: Exodus has seven daughters of the priest of Midian (šebaʿ bānôt) who draw water, shepherds who drive them off (wa-ygārəšûm), and Moses who rescues them (wa-yyôšiʿān) and waters their flock. The Quran has two women holding back their flock (imraʾatayni tadhūdāni) until the shepherds finish, explaining abūnā shaykhun kabīrun; Moses waters for them unasked, then withdraws to the shade and prays (rabbi innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr). There is no fight with the shepherds.

passages.text: וּלְכֹהֵ֥ן מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֣בַע בָּנ֑וֹת וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה וַתִּדְלֶ֗נָה וַתְּמַלֶּ֨אנָה֙ אֶת הָ֣רְהָטִ֔ים לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת צֹ֥אן אֲבִיהֶֽן
וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ הָרֹעִ֖ים וַיְגָרְשׁ֑וּם וַיָּ֤קָם מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיּ֣וֹשִׁעָ֔ן וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת צֹאנָֽם

وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

matches.label: Moses' father-in-law in Midian
matches.note: The father: Exodus has a named priest, kōhēn Midyān and Rəʿûʾēl, who scolds his daughters for leaving the stranger and invites him to eat (qirʾen lô wə-yōʾkhal leḥem); the Quran has an unnamed 'very old man' (shaykhun kabīr), no priest, who sends a daughter to pay Moses his wage (li-yajziyaka ajra mā saqayta lanā) and reassures him: lā takhaf najawta mina l-qawmi ẓ-ẓālimīn.

passages.text: וּלְכֹהֵ֥ן מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֣בַע בָּנ֑וֹת וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה וַתִּדְלֶ֗נָה וַתְּמַלֶּ֨אנָה֙ אֶת הָ֣רְהָטִ֔ים לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת צֹ֥אן אֲבִיהֶֽן
וַתָּבֹ֕אנָה אֶל רְעוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִיהֶ֑ן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַדּ֛וּעַ מִהַרְתֶּ֥ן בֹּ֖א הַיּֽוֹם
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל בְּנֹתָ֖יו וְאַיּ֑וֹ לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ן אֶת הָאִ֔ישׁ קִרְאֶ֥ן ל֖וֹ וְיֹ֥אכַל לָֽחֶם

وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ

فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them
matches.note: The daughters' role: in Exodus they report together to their father, ʾîš Miṣrî hiṣṣîlānû mi-yyad hā-rōʿîm, 'an Egyptian man saved us' (Moses taken for an Egyptian); in the Quran one daughter walks shyly (tamshī ʿalā stiḥyāʾ) to invite him and then advises her father, istaʾjirhu inna khayra mani staʾjarta l-qawiyyu l-amīnu, 'hire him, the best one to hire is the strong and trustworthy'.

passages.text: וַתֹּאמַ֕רְןָ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י הִצִּילָ֖נוּ מִיַּ֣ד הָרֹעִ֑ים וְגַם דָּלֹ֤ה דָלָה֙ לָ֔נוּ וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת הַצֹּֽאן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל בְּנֹתָ֖יו וְאַיּ֑וֹ לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ן אֶת הָאִ֔ישׁ קִרְאֶ֥ן ל֖וֹ וְיֹ֥אכַל לָֽחֶם

فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
قَالَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسْتَـْٔجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ

matches.label: The terms of Moses' marriage in Midian
matches.note: The marriage: Exodus has wa-yyôʾel Mōše lāševet ʾet hā-ʾîš wa-yyittēn ʾet Ṣippōrâ vittô lə-Mōše, a named bride and no terms; the Quran has an unnamed daughter given under a contract of service, ʿalā an taʾjuranī thamāniya ḥijajin fa-in atmamta ʿashran fa-min ʿindika, eight years or ten if he wishes, sworn before God (wa-llāhu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīl).

passages.text: וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ הָרֹעִ֖ים וַיְגָרְשׁ֑וּם וַיָּ֤קָם מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיּ֣וֹשִׁעָ֔ן וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת צֹאנָֽם
וַתֹּאמַ֕רְןָ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י הִצִּילָ֖נוּ מִיַּ֣ד הָרֹעִ֑ים וְגַם דָּלֹ֤ה דָלָה֙ לָ֔נוּ וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת הַצֹּֽאן

وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

sides.note: wa-lammā warada māʾa Madyana ... fa-jāʾathu iḥdāhumā ~ hinnēh ʾānōkhî niṣṣāv ʿal ʿên ham-mayim û-vənôt ʾanšê hā-ʿîr yōṣʾōt lišʾōv māyim: a man arriving at a town's water meets the young woman who leads to a marriage. In Genesis the woman waters the stranger's animals as a sign; in the Quran the stranger waters the women's flock.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand (weight 7.7); Kinsman rebuffs the hero: 'Who made you prince and judge over us?' (weight 7.7); How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land (weight 6.8). leads.finding: How Moses killed the Egyptian

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry
Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian

matches.label: How Moses killed the Egyptian
matches.note: The killing: Exodus has Moses see an Egyptian beating a Hebrew 'of his brothers', look this way and that and see no one (wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš), strike him and hide him in the sand. The Quran has him find two men fighting, one of his party (shīʿa) and one of his enemy; at his kinsman's cry for help he strikes one blow and the man dies (fa-wakazahu Mūsā fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi). There is no looking around and no hiding of the body; the act is unpremeditated.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיִּגְדַּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל אֶחָ֔יו וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו
וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged
matches.note: Moral verdict on the killing: Exodus passes none; Moses only fears exposure (wa-yyîrāʾ Mōše wa-yyōʾmar ʾākhēn nôdaʿ had-dāvār). The Quran has Moses judge it at once, hādhā min ʿamali sh-shayṭān ... rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī fa-ghfir lī, and God forgives him (fa-ghafara lahu), so Moses is a repentant penitent before he is a prophet.

passages.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ

matches.label: The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing
matches.note: The second day: in Exodus two Hebrews (šənê ʾănāšîm ʿIvrîm) fight, Moses rebukes the guilty one, and that Hebrew retorts mî śāməkhā lə-ʾîš śar wə-šōfēṭ ʿālênû ha-lə-hārəgēnî ʾattâ ʾōmēr ka-ʾăšer hāragtā ʾet ham-Miṣrî. In the Quran the same kinsman again calls for help against an enemy, Moses calls the kinsman 'clearly misguided' (la-ghawiyyun mubīn), and as he moves to strike the enemy he hears a-turīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bi-l-amsi in turīdu illā an takūna jabbāran fī l-arḍ. 'Prince and judge' becomes 'tyrant' (jabbār).

passages.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנֵֽי אֲנָשִׁ֥ים עִבְרִ֖ים נִצִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע לָ֥מָּה תַכֶּ֖ה רֵעֶֽךָ
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ הַלְהָרְגֵ֨נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת הַמִּצְרִ֑י וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר
فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ

فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ

matches.label: How Moses learns that his life is sought
matches.note: How the danger reaches Moses: Exodus has wa-yyišmaʿ Parʿōh ʾet had-dāvār haz-zeh wa-yvaqqēš lahărōg ʾet Mōše, Pharaoh himself; the Quran has the chiefs plotting (al-malaʾa yaʾtamirūna bika li-yaqtulūka) and an unnamed sympathizer running from the far end of the city to warn him (wa-jāʾa rajulun min aqṣā l-madīnati yasʿā).

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר
وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

matches.label: Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land
matches.note: fa-kharaja minhā khāʾifan yataraqqabu ... wa-lammā tawajjaha tilqāʾa Madyana ~ wa-yyivraḥ Mōše mip-pənê Farʿōh wa-yyēšev bə-ʾereṣ Midyān: flight to Midian (Madyan / Midyān). The Quran adds two prayers (rabbi najjinī ... ʿasā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāʾa s-sabīl).

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ מִדְיָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עַֽל הַבְּאֵֽר
فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ

leads.finding: Who decides that Moses be put on the water

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry
Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water

matches.label: Who decides that Moses be put on the water
matches.note: Who decides to put the child on the water: Exodus has the mother, on her own, hide him three months and, when she can hide him no longer (wə-lōʾ yākhlâ ʿôd haṣṣəfînô), make a papyrus basket sealed with pitch. In the Quran God inspires her (awḥaynā ilā ummi Mūsā): nurse him, cast him into the river when you fear, and 'we will return him to you and make him one of the messengers'. The rescue is announced in advance.

passages.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים
וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

matches.label: Infant placed in a container and set on the water
matches.note: fa-alqīhi fī l-yammi ~ wat-tāśem bas-sûf ʿal śəfat hay-yəʾōr: Exodus places him carefully among the reeds at the edge of the Nile (yəʾōr), in a basket (tēvat gōmeʾ) with bitumen and pitch; the Quran says 'cast him into the yamm', with no vessel in this passage, using the word that elsewhere names the sea where Pharaoh drowns.

passages.text: וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר
وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

matches.label: Infant adopted by a royal woman
matches.note: Who finds and adopts him: Pharaoh's daughter (bat Parʿōh), bathing, sees the basket, has pity on the crying child, recognizes him as Hebrew (mī-yaldê hā-ʿIvrîm zeh) and later names him. In the Quran Pharaoh's household picks him up (iltaqaṭahu ālu Firʿawn), and Pharaoh's wife (imraʾat Firʿawn) pleads with Pharaoh: qurratu ʿaynin lī wa-laka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan. Daughter becomes wife, pity becomes intercession, and the Quran adds the divine irony 'so that he would be an enemy and a grief to them' (28:8).

passages.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ
וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה
וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ
فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

matches.label: Sister offers to find a nurse
matches.note: The sister's offer: Exodus has hăʾēlēkh wə-qārāʾtî lākh ʾiššâ mêneqet min hā-ʿIvriyyōt on her own initiative; the Quran first has God forbid the other wet-nurses to him (wa-ḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu), then the sister offers a household that will rear him. cf. b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts), outside the HB.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד
وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ

matches.label: Infant returned to his own mother to nurse
matches.note: Why the child goes back to his mother: Exodus has a paid arrangement with the princess, hêlîkhî ʾet hay-yeled haz-zeh wə-hênîqihû lî wa-ʾănî ʾettēn ʾet śəkhārēkh; the Quran has God keeping his promise, fa-radadnāhu ilā ummihi kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzana wa-li-taʿlama anna waʿda llāhi ḥaqqun. The Quran omits the naming and its etymology (Exod 2:10).

passages.text: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ
فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

matches.label: Infant's sister watches over him
matches.note: qālat li-ukhtihi quṣṣīhi fa-baṣurat bihi ʿan junubin wa-hum lā yashʿurūna ~ wat-tētaṣṣav ʾăḥōtô mē-rāḥōq lə-dēʿâ mah yyēʿāśeh lô: the sister watches from a distance. In the Quran the mother sends her.

passages.text: וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ
وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

units.title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry

matches.label: Pharaoh seeks to kill Moses, and when and why
matches.note: wa-yyišmaʿ parʿōh ʾeṯ-ha-ddāḇār ha-zze wa-yəḇaqqēš lahărōḡ ʾeṯ-mōšeh vs. wa-qāla Firʿawnu dharūnī aqtul Mūsā wa-l-yadʿu rabbahu innī akhāfu an yubaddila dīnakum. In Exodus Pharaoh wants Moses dead for killing an Egyptian, before his call; in the Quran he wants it after the mission, fearing for 'your religion' (dīn).

matches.note: The righteous woman of Pharaoh's house: Exodus has bat parʿōh, who pities the Hebrew child (wattaḥmōl ʿālāyw) and adopts him (wa-yehî lāh le-vēn). The Quran has imraʾata firʿawna, held up as the model believer who prays rabbi bni lī ʿindaka baytan fī l-janna wa-najjinī min firʿawna wa-ʿamalihi: daughter becomes wife, and she is set against Pharaoh himself. Her rescue of Moses is told in Q 28:9, outside this unit.

Only in Altar law: Altar to be made of earth; God will come and bless in every place where he causes his name to be remembered; God declares that he spoke from heaven; No steps up to the altar, lest nakedness be exposed; Altar of whole stones on which no iron tool is lifted; Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate (weight 7.3); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); No other gods before YHWH (weight 6.8); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.8); Sabbath rest on the seventh day for all, including servants, animals and strangers (weight 6.6); Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship (weight 6.6); God visits the fathers' sin on the third and fourth generation, but keeps steadfast love for thousands (weight 6.5); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 6.5); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property (weight 6.2); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.9); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.7). Pair score 72.1.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them; and 3 more.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

passages.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה דַּבֵּר אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּ֖נוּ וְנִשְׁמָ֑עָה וְאַל יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּ֛נוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים פֶּן נָמֽוּת

sides.note: 'You speak with us... lest we die'

passages.text: אָ֠נֹכִי עֹמֵ֨ד בֵּין יְהוָ֤ה וּבֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לְהַגִּ֥יד לָכֶ֖ם אֶת דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י יְרֵאתֶם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֵ֔שׁ וְלֹֽא עֲלִיתֶ֥ם בָּהָ֖ר לֵאמֹֽר
וַתֹּאמְר֗וּ הֵ֣ן הֶרְאָ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת כְּבֹד֣וֹ וְאֶת גָּדְל֔וֹ וְאֶת קֹל֥וֹ שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָאֵ֑שׁ הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ רָאִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי יְדַבֵּ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָֽאָדָ֖ם וָחָֽי
וְעַתָּה֙ לָ֣מָּה נָמ֔וּת כִּ֣י תֹֽאכְלֵ֔נוּ הָאֵ֥שׁ הַגְּדֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את אִם יֹסְפִ֣ים אֲנַ֗חְנוּ לִ֠שְׁמֹעַ אֶת ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ ע֖וֹד וָמָֽתְנוּ

sides.note: who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God and lived

matches.label: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life

passages.text: כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ

sides.note: kabbēd ʾet-ʾābîkā wəʾet-ʾimmekā ləmaʿan yaʾărikûn yāmêkā; wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara ... fa-lā taqul lahumā uffin ... wa-qul rabbi rḥamhumā ka-mā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. Q drops the promise of long life and puts in its place care for parents in old age and a prayer for them. Duty to parents comes second, right after God, in both.

passages.text: כַּבֵּ֤ד אֶת אָבִ֨יךָ֙ וְאֶת אִמֶּ֔ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲרִיכֻ֣ן יָמֶ֗יךָ וּלְמַ֨עַן֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ

sides.note: Deut: kabbēd ʾet-ʾāvîkhā wə-ʾet-ʾimmekhā ... ləmaʿan yaʾărîkhūn yāmêkhā û-ləmaʿan yîṭav lākh ʿal-hā-ʾădāmāh. Q: wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan. 'Honour' becomes 'kindness', and the promise of long life in the land is dropped.

matches.label: No other gods before YHWH

passages.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
לֹא יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ

sides.note: Q: wa-mā min ilāhin illā ilāhun wāḥidun; man yushrik bi-llāhi fa-qad ḥarrama llāhu ʿalayhi l-janna. Deut: lōʾ yihyeh-ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy. Q has Jesus himself proclaim it (uʿbudū llāha rabbī wa-rabbakum).

matches.label: Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness

passages.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
לֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

passages.text: לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
וְלֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף
וְלֹֽא תַעֲנֶ֥ה בְרֵֽעֲךָ֖ עֵ֥ד שָֽׁוְא

sides.note: Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent.

passages.text: (20:8) זָכ֛וֹר אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ (20:9) שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּֽעֲבֹ֔ד וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ כָּל מְלַאכְתֶּֽךָ (20:10) וְי֨וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽ֣א תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה כָל מְלָאכָ֜ה אַתָּ֣ה וּבִנְךָֽ֣ וּבִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ (20:11) כִּ֣י שֵֽׁשֶׁת יָמִים֩ עָשָׂ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת הַיָּם֙ וְאֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר בָּ֔ם וַיָּ֖נַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י עַל כֵּ֗ן בֵּרַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וַֽיְקַדְּשֵֽׁהוּ
זָכ֛וֹר אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ
וְי֨וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽ֣א תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה כָל מְלָאכָ֜ה אַתָּ֣ה וּבִנְךָֽ֣ וּבִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ

וְי֨וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א תַעֲשֶׂ֣ה כָל מְלָאכָ֡ה אַתָּ֣ה וּבִנְךָֽ וּבִתֶּ֣ךָ וְעַבְדְּךָֽ וַ֠אֲמָתֶךָ וְשׁוֹרְךָ֨ וַחֲמֹֽרְךָ֜ וְכָל בְּהֶמְתֶּ֗ךָ וְגֵֽרְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ לְמַ֗עַן יָנ֛וּחַ עַבְדְּךָ֥ וַאֲמָתְךָ֖ כָּמֽוֹךָ

sides.note: so that your slave may rest like you

passages.text: לֹֽ֣א תַֽעֲשֶׂ֨ה לְךָ֥ פֶ֨סֶל֙ וְכָל תְּמוּנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִמַּ֔עַל וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּ֑חַת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּמַּ֖יִם מִתַּ֥חַת לָאָֽרֶץ
לֹֽא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑ם כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל בָּנִ֛ים עַל שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽי

passages.text: לֹֽא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑ם כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל בָּנִ֛ים עַל שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽי
וְעֹ֥שֶׂה חֶ֖סֶד לַאֲלָפִ֑ים לְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽי

וְעֹ֥שֶׂה חֶ֖סֶד לַֽאֲלָפִ֑ים לְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מצותו מִצְוֺתָֽי

leads.finding: No other gods before YHWH

units.title: The Ten Words and the people's fear
The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39)

matches.label: No other gods before YHWH
matches.note: lōʾ yihyeh-ləkā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy; lā tajʿal maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhar: same first commandment ('other gods' / 'another god'). The frame changes: Exod opens with the exodus, ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkā mēʾereṣ miṣrayim; Q frames the code with the command at both ends (17:22, 17:39) and with no history of Israel, wa-qaḍā rabbuka. Q's code also has no Sabbath, no images clause and no coveting.

passages.text: אָֽנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים
לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
لَّا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَّخْذُولًا

وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
ذَٰلِكَ مِمَّآ أَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ رَبُّكَ مِنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتُلْقَىٰ فِى جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَّدْحُورًا

matches.label: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life
matches.note: kabbēd ʾet-ʾābîkā wəʾet-ʾimmekā ləmaʿan yaʾărikûn yāmêkā; wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara ... fa-lā taqul lahumā uffin ... wa-qul rabbi rḥamhumā ka-mā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. Q drops the promise of long life and puts in its place care for parents in old age and a prayer for them. Duty to parents comes second, right after God, in both.

passages.text: כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ

وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا

matches.label: Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right
matches.note: lōʾ tirṣāḥ, unqualified; wa-lā taqtulu n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqq: Q adds 'except by right' and gives the victim's walī authority, fa-lā yusrif fī l-qatl, folding the blood-avenger law into the commandment.

passages.text: לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِۦ سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يُسْرِف فِّى ٱلْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مَنصُورًا

matches.label: Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden
matches.note: lōʾ tinʾāp; wa-lā taqrabū z-zinā innahu kāna fāḥishatan: Q forbids even approaching it, and its zinā covers any illicit intercourse, not only with a married woman.

passages.text: לֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةً وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا

وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَٰقٍ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْـًٔا كَبِيرًا
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةً وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them; and 13 more.

Only in Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius: The three goddesses al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, 'the third, the other', named and rejected; They follow only conjecture (zann), and conjecture avails nothing against the truth; God created the pairs, male and female, from a drop of sperm (nutfa) when it is emitted; A surah ends with the command to prostrate (sajda verse); God destroyed 'Ad 'the first' (implying a second 'Ad); God knew you when he produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' bellies; do not claim purity; The idols are only names you and your fathers have named, for which God sent down no authority; God is 'the Lord of Sirius' (al-shi'ra), a star worshipped by some Arabs; Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, except minor slips (al-lamam), find God's forgiveness wide; To your Lord is the final end (al-muntaha); 'Is the male for you and the female for him? That is an unfair division'; 'Which of your Lord's bounties (ala') will you dispute/deny?'; and 19 more.

matches.label: The Ten Commandments (Decalogue)
matches.note: A recited list of commandments compared item by item. Kept: no other gods (allā tushrikū bihi shayʾan = lōʾ yihyeh-ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm), parents, killing, sexual sin, false speech. Omitted: the Sabbath (zākhôr ʾet-yôm haš-šabbāt) and coveting; the image ban is folded into 'associate nothing'. Added: allā taqtulū awlādakum min imlāqin, the orphan's property, full measure and weight, keeping God's covenant. The prologue ʾānōkhî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkhā ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkhā mē-ʾereṣ miṣrayim becomes qul taʿālaw atlu mā ḥarrama rabbukum, without the Exodus.

passages.text: אָֽנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים
לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
זָכ֛וֹר אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ

قُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا۟ بِهِۦ شَيْـًٔا وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُم مِّنْ إِمْلَٰقٍ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَٱعْدِلُوا۟ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ وَبِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْفُوا۟ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
وَأَنَّ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطِى مُسْتَقِيمًا فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلسُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

Q drops the promise of long life and puts in its place care for parents in old age and a prayer for them. Duty to parents comes second, right after God, in both.

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَٱعْدِلُوا۟ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ وَبِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْفُوا۟ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ

matches.note: A short list of apodictic prohibitions, the women's pledge as a small decalogue. Exodus: lōʾ yihyeh ləḵā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāp̄ lōʾ tiḡnōḇ lōʾ ṯaʿăneh ḇə-rēʿăḵā ʿēḏ šāqer. Quran: ʿalā an lā yushrikna bi-llāhi shayʾan wa-lā yasriqna wa-lā yaznīna wa-lā yaqtulna awlādahunna wa-lā yaʾtīna bi-buhtānin yaftarīnahu bayna aydīhinna wa-arjulihinna wa-lā yaʿṣīnaka fī maʿrūf. The same order of other gods, theft, adultery, killing and false speech, but addressed to women as a pledge (bayʿa) to the Prophet: murder narrowed to infanticide, false witness to a slander 'between their hands and feet' (false paternity, in tafsir), obedience to the Prophet added; no Sabbath, parents or coveting.

matches.note: Q quotes the talion as written in the Torah (wa-katabnā ʿalayhim fīhā) but changes the list. Q: al-nafsa bi-l-nafsi wa-l-ʿayna bi-l-ʿayni wa-l-anfa bi-l-anfi wa-l-udhuna bi-l-udhuni wa-l-sinna bi-l-sinni wa-l-jurūḥa qiṣāṣun. Exod: nefeš taḥat nāfeš ʿayin taḥat ʿayin šēn taḥat šēn yād ... regel ... kəviyyāh ... peṣaʿ taḥat pāṣaʿ ḥabbûrāh. Q adds nose and ear, drops hand, foot, burn and bruise, and sums up the rest as jurūḥ (= peṣaʿ). Exod's taḥat ('in place of') becomes Q's bi-.

leads.title: Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days ↔ Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

Only in Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days: The cloud covers the mountain six days and God calls on the seventh; God's glory appears as a devouring fire; Joshua serves as Moses' attendant; Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain; Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts]; A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

Only in Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya: People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued; Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; A large army must not claim the victory for itself [divergence between the texts]; City accepting peace becomes forced labor; one resisting has its males killed; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); God supports the prophet with hosts (junud) the believers did not see; God reinforces the believers in battle with a thousand (or more) angels.

matches.note: Root s-k-n / š-k-n for God's presence coming down: thumma anzala llāhu sakīnatahu ʿalā rasūlihi wa-ʿalā l-muʾminīn vs wayyiškōn kᵉbôd-YHWH ʿal-har sînay. The noun šᵉkînāh is rabbinic, not biblical; in Q sakīna is calm sent into the fighters, in Exod the glory settling on the mountain. A lead on the word, to check.

leads.title: Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand ↔ Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold (weight 7.7); A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark (weight 7.7); A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups (weight 7.1); A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God (weight 6.8); The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 6.6); Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark (weight 6.5). Pair score 42.5.

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar: Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil; Recipe of the holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil.
