passages.text: (37:17) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ (37:18) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (37:19) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (37:20) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (37:21) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה (37:22) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:24) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל כֵּלֶֽיהָ

passages.text: (25:23) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:24) וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:25) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (25:26) וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (25:27) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:28) וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא בָ֖ם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:29) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם (25:30) וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד

passages.text: (37:10) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:11) וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:12) וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (37:13) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (37:14) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת בָּתִּים֙ לַבַּדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:15) וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:16) וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת הַכֵּלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֶת קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶת הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר

passages.text: (25:10) וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:11) וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:12) וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (25:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (25:14) וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם (25:15) בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ (25:16) וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

(37:1) וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:2) וַיְצַפֵּ֛הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר מִבַּ֣יִת וּמִח֑וּץ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:3) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּע֔וֹת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (37:4) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (37:5) וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הָאָרֹֽן
וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ

וַ֠עֲשֵׂה כְּר֨וּב אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה מִן הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עַל שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָֽיו
וְהָי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל אָחִ֑יו אֶל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת יִהְי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים
וַיַּ֛עַשׂ שְׁנֵ֥י כְרֻבִ֖ים זָהָ֑ב מִקְשָׁה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת

וַיִּהְי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹֽכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל אָחִ֑יו אֶל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים

Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 6.6). Pair score 14.4.

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; and 2 more.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; A candidate for kingship is judged by his bodily size or strength (too small for the throne; given increase of body) [divergence between the texts]; A claimant's body is weighed as fitness for kingship [divergence between the texts]; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A champion whom everyone fears is killed by one unlikely man; and 16 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A middle bar runs through the frames from end to end (weight 7.7); An embroidered screen at the entrance of the tent or court (weight 7.7); Tabernacle walls of acacia frames set in silver sockets (weight 7.7); Eleven goat-hair curtains form the tent over the tabernacle (weight 7.7); Outer coverings of red-dyed ram skins and tahash skins (weight 7.7); Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps (weight 7.7); A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies (weight 7.3); Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim (weight 7.3). Pair score 61.2.

Only in Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil: The lampstand stands on the south side and the table on the north; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); The innermost room, the holy of holies, holds the ark; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames: God gives the master craftsmen the ability to teach others; The people bring more than enough and must be told to stop giving; God calls a master craftsman by name for the sacred work; A second craftsman from the tribe of Dan assists the master craftsman; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

passages.text: (26:15) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים (26:16) עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:17) שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן (26:18) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (26:19) וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו (26:20) וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ (26:21) וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:22) וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים (26:23) וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם (26:24) וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִים֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ (26:25) וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A perpetual lamp fed with pure beaten olive oil (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Bronze altar, courtyard and lamp oil: Bronze-plated altar of burnt offering with a bronze grating; The altar is hollow, made of boards and carried with poles; The tabernacle court measures 100 by 50 cubits with linen hangings; An altar with horns at its four corners; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds in flight, wings spread, praise the deity; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The god titled 'light of heaven(s) and earth' (nūr šamāmī u qaqqari / nūru l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ), and those deprived of light walk in darkness; and 12 more.

matches.note: miṣbāḥun ... yūqadu min shajaratin mubārakatin zaytūnatin ... yakādu zaytuhā yuḍīʾu ~ šemen zayit zākh kātît la-mmāʾôr ləhaʿălōt nēr tāmîd: a lamp lit with olive oil (zayt / zayit, cognate). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The priest carries Israel's names before God as a memorial (weight 7.7); The robe's neck opening is bound so it will not tear (weight 7.7); The priest's robe has gold bells and pomegranates on its hem so he does not die (weight 7.7); The names of the twelve tribes are engraved like seals on gemstones (weight 7.7); Priests wear linen breeches to cover their nakedness, on pain of death (weight 7.3); The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces (weight 7.3); The breastpiece of judgment set with twelve gems in four rows (weight 7.3); A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead (weight 7.1). Pair score 60.1.

Only in The high priest's vestments: Aaron and his sons are designated as priests; Priestly garments are made for glory and beauty; Priests are installed by anointing and 'filling the hand'; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

Only in The vestments made; the work completed and blessed: Gold is beaten into sheets and cut into threads for weaving; The leader sees the finished work and blesses the workers; Completion of the sanctuary is narrated in the language of the completion of creation; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Ordination of priests lasts seven days (weight 7.7); Blood and anointing oil are sprinkled on the priests and their garments (weight 7.7); Priests are washed with water at the entrance before ordination (weight 7.3); Anointing oil is poured on the head of the priest (weight 7.3); Blood is daubed on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe (weight 7.3); Sacred meat left over until morning is burned (weight 7.3); Portions are waved before God as a wave offering (weight 7.3); The offerer lays his hand on the head of the animal (weight 6.8); The flesh, skin and dung of the sin offering are burned outside the camp (weight 6.8); Blood is put on the horns of the altar with the finger and poured at its base (weight 6.8). Pair score 72.7.

Only in Ordination of the priests: A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered; An outsider may not eat holy food; The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days; The breast and the right thigh are the priests' portion; Whatever touches the most holy altar or holy things becomes holy; Sacrificial animals must be without blemish; The fat, the two kidneys and the lobe of the liver are burned on the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered; An offering by fire is a pleasing odor to God.

Only in Moses ordains Aaron and his sons: Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination; The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite; Anointing makes the tent and its furnishings holy; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead; A ritual action is performed seven times.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy) [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Moses, Ishmael and Idris remembered; the later generation that neglected prayer (Surah 19:51-65): The angels say 'We descend only by your Lord's command'; God has no namesake or equal (samiyy); Ishmael was true to his promise and enjoined prayer and alms on his family; When the Merciful's verses are recited the prophets fall prostrate and weeping; In paradise the blessed receive their provision morning and evening; One of a list of ancient sages or prophets ascends, or is raised, to heaven or a high place; God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds; A prophet named Idrīs is mentioned among the righteous; God raised Idris to a high place; After the prophets came a generation that neglected prayer and followed lusts; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); and 6 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh (weight 7.7); Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); What Moses asks Pharaoh to allow [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The departing slaves ask their neighbors for silver, gold and clothing and so plunder their oppressors (weight 6.8); God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 6.6). Pair score 36.7.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy) [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 46 more.

units.title: The burning bush and the divine name

matches.label: The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh
matches.note: The divine title before Pharaoh: YHWH ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivriyyîm niqrâ ʿālênû (Exod 3:18, also 5:3) ~ innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīna, and when Pharaoh asks 'and what is the Lord of the worlds?', Moses answers rabbu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā ... rabbu l-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi. The god of one people becomes the Lord of the cosmos.

passages.text: וְשָׁמְע֖וּ לְקֹלֶ֑ךָ וּבָאתָ֡ אַתָּה֩ וְזִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֗יִם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽעִבְרִיִּים֙ נִקְרָ֣ה עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה נֵֽלֲכָה נָּ֞א דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְנִזְבְּחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ
فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ

matches.label: Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story
matches.note: 'God of your fathers' changes addressee. Exod 3:15, said to Israel: YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăvōtêkem ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv. Q 26:26, said to Pharaoh and his court: rabbukum wa-rabbu ābāʾikumu l-awwalīna, 'your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers'. The God of Israel's ancestors becomes the Lord of the Egyptians' ancestors too.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ע֨וֹד אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה כֹּֽה תֹאמַר֮ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם זֶה שְּׁמִ֣י לְעֹלָ֔ם וְזֶ֥ה זִכְרִ֖י לְדֹ֥ר דֹּֽר
قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed (weight 7.1). Pair score 22.5.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; and 15 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign; A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff; and 4 more.

matches.label: Why Moses approaches the fire
matches.note: Why Moses goes to the fire: Exodus has him alone with Jethro's flock at Horeb, turning aside to see the great sight (ʾāsurâ nāʾ wə-ʾerʾeh ʾet ham-marʾeh hag-gādōl haz-zeh); the Quran has him traveling with his family (qāla Mūsā li-ahlihi), going to bring back news or a burning brand 'that you may warm yourselves'. The Quran names neither flock, mountain nor Jethro.

passages.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת הַצֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֛א אֶל הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָה
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹא יִבְעַ֥ר הַסְּנֶֽה
إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ

matches.label: How God names himself to Moses from the fire
matches.note: God's self-identification from the fire: Exodus has ʾānōkhî ʾĕlōhê ʾāvîkā ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv, then ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh; the Quran has yā Mūsā innahu ana llāhu l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu, preceded by subḥāna llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīna. The God of the fathers becomes the Lord of the worlds, and the name-riddle becomes 'Allāh'. The Quran also leaves out the sandals and Moses hiding his face (Exod 3:5-6).

فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

matches.label: Where and how Moses comes to the place of his call
matches.note: Place and occasion of the call: Exodus has Moses shepherding Jethro's flock 'behind the wilderness' to Horeb, the mountain of God, a place of holy ground (ʾadmat qōdeš hûʾ), where he must take off his sandals. The Quran has Moses, after completing his term (qaḍā Mūsā l-ajala), traveling with his family, seeing fire on the side of the Mount (jānib aṭ-Ṭūr), and called from the right bank of the valley in 'the blessed spot' (al-buqʿa al-mubāraka). There are no flock and no sandals; the holy ground becomes a blessed spot.

passages.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת הַצֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֛א אֶל הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָה

فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارًا قَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Who revives rotten bones? Fire from the green tree; Be and it is: The skeptic asks 'Who will give life to bones when they have rotted?'; the answer: he who produced them the first time; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; God created livestock and subjected them to people for riding, food, benefits and drink; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation); Deity creates by spoken command (Let there be...); God creates by saying to a thing 'Be' and it is (kun fa-yakun).

matches.note: Who makes the calf. Exod: Aaron, at the people's demand, qûm ʿăśēh-lānû ʾĕlōhîm ... pārəqû nizmê hazzāhāb ... wayyiṣar ʾōtô baḥereṭ wayyaʿăśēhû ʿēgel massēkâ. leads.title: Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer ↔ Messengers, the Mother of the Book and the witness of scripture (Surah 13:30-43)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God erases what he wills and confirms, and with him is the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab) (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer: Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire; The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies; God strikes the people with plague for idolatry; The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven; The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle; The tablets are written on both sides by God; The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; God sends an angel ahead of Israel who bears God's name; and 16 more.

Only in Messengers, the Mother of the Book and the witness of scripture (Surah 13:30-43): For every term there is a book (a written decree); The messenger's duty is only to deliver the message; the reckoning belongs to God; Challenge to the polytheists: 'Name them!' (the partners they ascribe to God); Some to whom the Book was given rejoice at the new revelation while factions deny part of it; Even a recitation that moved mountains, cleft the earth or made the dead speak would not convince the deniers; Messengers were mocked; God gave the deniers respite, then seized them; Those with knowledge of the earlier Book are invoked as witnesses to the prophet's mission; Scripture has decisive verses (muhkamat), the mother of the book, and ambiguous ones (mutashabihat) whose interpretation God knows; God comes to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; Earlier messengers were given wives and offspring; Those with knowledge of the earlier Book are invoked as witnesses to the prophet's mission [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Jesus asks 'Who are my helpers to God?' and the disciples (hawariyyun) answer 'We are God's helpers' (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer: Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire; The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies; God strikes the people with plague for idolatry; The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven; The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle; The tablets are written on both sides by God; The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; God erases what he wills and confirms, and with him is the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab); and 16 more.

Only in Al-Saff: ranks like a solid structure; Moses hurt by his people; Jesus foretells Ahmad; the disciples as God's helpers: A trade (tijara) that saves from punishment: believe and strive in God's way with wealth and selves; Goodly dwellings in the Gardens of Eden ('Adn); Jesus son of Mary confirms the Torah and announces a messenger to come after him named Ahmad; 'We have opened for you a clear opening/victory (fath mubin)' (the Hudaybiya treaty); Opponents wish to put out God's light with their mouths, but God will perfect his light; God loves those who fight in his way in ranks as though they were a solid structure (bunyan marsus); God makes his people's hearts stray or swerve [divergence between the texts]; If you have given your word, deliver and do not revoke it; promising and not delivering is abhorrent to the god; The lamp of God had not yet gone out; Moses asks his people: 'Why do you hurt me when you know I am God's messenger to you?'; when they swerved God made their hearts swerve; Moses ill-treated by his own people [divergence between the texts]; The coming prophet is found written in the Torah and the Gospel; and 7 more.

matches.note: Moses confronts Aaron, who blames the people: qāla bna umma inna l-qawma staḍʿafūnī wa-kādū yaqtulūnanī vs ʾal-yiḥar ʾap ʾădōnî ʾattāh yādaʿtā ʾet-hāʿām kî bᵉraʿ hûʾ. matches.label: What happens after God refuses to be seen by Moses
matches.note: After the refusal God points Moses to the rock or mountain: wa-lākini nẓur ilā l-jabali fa-ini staqarra makānahu fa-sawfa tarānī vs hinnēh māqôm ʾittî wᵉniṣṣabtā ʿal-haṣṣûr. passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה מָק֖וֹם אִתִּ֑י וְנִצַּבְתָּ֖ עַל הַצּֽוּר
וְהָיָה֙ בַּעֲבֹ֣ר כְּבֹדִ֔י וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ בְּנִקְרַ֣ת הַצּ֑וּר וְשַׂכֹּתִ֥י כַפִּ֛י עָלֶ֖יךָ עַד עָבְרִֽי
וַהֲסִרֹתִי֙ אֶת כַּפִּ֔י וְרָאִ֖יתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָ֑י וּפָנַ֖י לֹ֥א יֵרָאֽוּ

وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَٰتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِىٓ أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ قَالَ لَن تَرَىٰنِى وَلَٰكِنِ ٱنظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْجَبَلِ فَإِنِ ٱسْتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُۥ فَسَوْفَ تَرَىٰنِى فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكًّا وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقًا فَلَمَّآ أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَٰتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِىٓ أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ قَالَ لَن تَرَىٰنِى وَلَٰكِنِ ٱنظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْجَبَلِ فَإِنِ ٱسْتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُۥ فَسَوْفَ تَرَىٰنِى فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكًّا وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقًا فَلَمَّآ أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Formula: 'gracious and merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, relenting of evil' (weight 6.4). Pair score 6.4.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; How far God's mercy and his punishment extend [divergence between the texts]; and 21 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers: The damned say 'Lord, you caused us to die twice and gave us life twice; we confess our sins; is there a way out?'; The Day of the Approaching (al-azifa) when hearts reach the throats, choking; God as Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty (string of divine epithets); God casts the Spirit (al-ruh) of his command upon whom he wills of his servants to warn of the Day of Meeting; The beings that carry God's throne, and what they do [divergence between the texts]; God knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal; In terror eyes swerve and hearts reach the throats; The heavenly host speak for a human before the high god and ask his forgiveness; The angels who bear the Throne and those around it glorify God and ask forgiveness for the believers, praying they and their righteous kin enter Eden; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); On the Day God asks 'Whose is the kingdom today?' and answers 'God's, the One, the Overpowering'; Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.6.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; How far God's mercy and his punishment extend [divergence between the texts]; Moses hews a second pair of tablets to replace the broken ones; and 20 more.

Only in Forty nights, the request to see God and the tablets: When God manifests himself to the mountain it is crushed to dust; The prophet falls down unconscious at the theophany and repents on waking; The tablets contain an exhortation and an explanation of all things; The appointed time on the mountain is thirty nights completed with ten more, making forty; Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain; Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts]; Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts]; A mountain is shattered when God passes by or manifests himself [divergence between the texts]; The prophet asks to see God's glory; What happens after God refuses to be seen by Moses [divergence between the texts]; God answers the prophet's request to see him: 'You will not see me'; and 8 more.

leads.title: Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar ↔ Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 6.6). Pair score 6.6.

Only in Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil; Recipe of the holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; A candidate for kingship is judged by his bodily size or strength (too small for the throne; given increase of body) [divergence between the texts]; A claimant's body is weighed as fitness for kingship [divergence between the texts]; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Healing for hearts, the atom's weight, God has no son

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.5). Pair score 6.5.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוָ֖ה מזה מַה זֶּ֣ה בְיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מַטֶּֽה
وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ

matches.label: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign
matches.note: Exod: wəhinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat kaššāleg, a leprous hand, given so that the people will believe (ləmaʿan yaʾămînû). Q: takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾ, white 'without harm', which denies the disease, and given li-nuriyaka min āyātinā l-kubrā, a sign for Moses himself.

passages.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּקֹלִ֑י כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ לֹֽא נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה
לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב
וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג
وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى

matches.label: Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'
matches.note: Exod: speech trouble is an objection to the call, lōʾ ʾîš dəbārîm ʾānōkî ... kî kəbad-peh ûkəbad lāšôn ʾānōkî ... šəlaḥ-nāʾ bəyad-tišlāḥ, and God rebukes him, mî śām peh lāʾādām. Q: it is a prayer, rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī ... wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī, granted at once, qad ūtīta suʾlaka yā Mūsā.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו מִ֣י שָׂ֣ם פֶּה֮ לָֽאָדָם֒ א֚וֹ מִֽי יָשׂ֣וּם אִלֵּ֔ם א֣וֹ חֵרֵ֔שׁ א֥וֹ פִקֵּ֖חַ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָֽה
וְעַתָּ֖ה לֵ֑ךְ וְאָנֹכִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִם פִּ֔יךָ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּֽר
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى

Q: Moses asks for him, wa-jʿal lī wazīran min ahlī Hārūna akhī ushdud bihi azrī wa-ashrikhu fī amrī, so that they may glorify God much (kay nusabbiḥaka kathīrā). No anger, and no 'as God'.

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town: The 'People of the Rass' (aṣḥāb al-rass, the well) named among destroyed peoples; Most unbelievers are like cattle, or even further astray; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; 'Do not go about after your heart and your eyes'; The sign the flood leaves for later generations [divergence between the texts]; The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); The people mock God's messengers, despise his words and scoff at his prophets; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities; and 2 more.

matches.note: wa-jaʿalnā maʿahu akhāhu Hārūna wazīran ~ hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-hāyâ hûʾ yihyeh lləkā lə-feh wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm: Aaron joins his brother. leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 6.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 6.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 6.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 6.5). Pair score 47.9.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; and 44 more.

matches.label: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death
matches.note: Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Salih, the rock-hewn houses of Thamud and the she-camel: The people say the prophet is one of the bewitched and a mere human like them, and demand a sign; The prophet Ṣāliḥ is sent to the people of Thamūd; Thamūd hew houses out of the mountains, among gardens, springs and palms with tender spathes; Edom dwells in the clefts of the rock (sela) and thinks no one can bring it down; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'.

matches.note: As at Q 27:10: wa-yyānās Mōše mip-pānāyw ~ wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib; Exodus' command to seize the snake's tail (wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô) becomes yā Mūsā aqbil wa-lā takhaf innaka mina l-āminīn, 'come forward and do not fear, you are safe'.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַשְׁלִיכֵ֣הוּ אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ אַ֖רְצָה וַיְהִ֣י לְנָחָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֥נָס מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפָּנָֽיו
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ
وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْءَامِنِينَ

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign
matches.note: Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג
וְהָיָה֙ אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וְהֶֽאֱמִ֔ינוּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֥ת הָאַחֲרֽוֹן

וְהָיָ֡ה אִם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֡ינוּ גַּם֩ לִשְׁנֵ֨י הָאֹת֜וֹת הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּן֙ לְקֹלֶ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֙ מִמֵּימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֔ר וְשָׁפַכְתָּ֖ הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְהָי֤וּ הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקַּ֣ח מִן הַיְאֹ֔ר וְהָי֥וּ לְדָ֖ם בַּיַּבָּֽשֶׁת

ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed
matches.note: Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי
וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ
וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִ֑יו וְאָנֹכִ֗י אֶֽהְיֶ֤ה עִם פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְעִם פִּ֔יהוּ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן

قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

matches.label: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death
matches.note: rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 6.6). Pair score 14.4.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts]; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning: Each sign shown to Pharaoh's people was greater than the one before it; Pharaoh scorns Moses as contemptible, barely able to speak, without gold bracelets or attending angels; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh is the great tannin (crocodile/dragon) lying in the midst of his Nile channels; Pharaoh boasts to his people: is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?; The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted [divergence between the texts]; The water of the river of Egypt is said to be at its king's disposal [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; A man brought before Pharaoh is afraid and cannot speak [divergence between the texts]; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves [divergence between the texts]; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives [divergence between the texts]; King invests the hero with ring, linen and chariot; and 3 more.

matches.label: Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him
matches.note: Moses' speech defect, told by a different speaker. Exodus: Moses says it of himself to God: lōʾ ʾîš dəḇārîm ʾānōḵî ... kî ḵəḇaḏ peh û-ḵəḇaḏ lāšôn ʾānōḵî. Quran: Pharaoh says it to mock him: am ana khayrun min hādhā lladhī huwa mahīnun wa-lā yakādu yubīn. A humble excuse becomes the enemy's taunt.

leads.title: Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How the defeated court magicians respond [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 6.5); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 6.0). Pair score 27.2.

Only in Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice: The dead frogs are piled in heaps and the land stinks; Egyptians dig around the Nile for drinkable water; Prophet lets the king choose when the plague should end, to prove God's power; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted [divergence between the texts]; Prophet confronts the king at the river in the morning; The dust of the earth becomes lice on man and beast; Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs; King asks the prophet to intercede with God to remove a plague; Nile water is turned to blood; and 1 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; and 47 more.

sides.note: Pharaoh's response to the sign: Exod 7:13 wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿ ʾălēhem ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart hardened as God foretold (God hardens it himself at 14:4, 14:8); Q 26:49 has no hardening and no divine agency, only Pharaoh's rage: āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu la-kabīrukumu lladhī ʿallamakumu s-siḥra, with a threat of amputation and crucifixion.

וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִ֑וא וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה
فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

leads.title: Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice ↔ Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice: The dead frogs are piled in heaps and the land stinks; Egyptians dig around the Nile for drinkable water; Prophet lets the king choose when the plague should end, to prove God's power; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; How the defeated court magicians respond [divergence between the texts]; Prophet confronts the king at the river in the morning; The dust of the earth becomes lice on man and beast; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs; King asks the prophet to intercede with God to remove a plague; and 3 more.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning: Each sign shown to Pharaoh's people was greater than the one before it; Pharaoh scorns Moses as contemptible, barely able to speak, without gold bracelets or attending angels; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh [divergence between the texts]; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh is the great tannin (crocodile/dragon) lying in the midst of his Nile channels; Pharaoh boasts to his people: is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?; The water of the river of Egypt is said to be at its king's disposal [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; A man brought before Pharaoh is afraid and cannot speak [divergence between the texts]; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves [divergence between the texts]; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives [divergence between the texts]; King invests the hero with ring, linen and chariot; and 3 more.

matches.label: The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted
matches.note: Pharaoh asks Moses to pray and breaks his word once relieved: wa-yiqrāʾ p̄arʿōh ... haʿtîrû ʾel YHWH wə-yāsēr haṣ-ṣəp̄arḏəʿîm ... wa-ʾăšalləḥâ ʾeṯ hā-ʿām; wa-yarʾ parʿōh kî hāyəṯâ hā-rəwāḥâ wə-haḵbēd ʾeṯ libbô vs. wa-qālū yā ayyuha s-sāḥiru dʿu lanā rabbaka bi-mā ʿahida ʿindaka innanā la-muhtadūn; fa-lammā kashafnā ʿanhumu l-ʿadhāba idhā hum yankuthūn. Changes: the speakers are Pharaoh's people, not Pharaoh alone; they address Moses as 'magician' (sāḥir); 'your Lord' (rabbaka) replaces 'YHWH'; the promise is to be guided (muhtadūn), not to release the people; and the relapse is breaking a pledge (nakth), with no heart-hardening (kibbēḏ lēḇ).

وَقَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهْتَدُونَ

matches.label: Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'
matches.note: The magicians' end. Exod: they fail at the lice and say ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hiwʾ, but stay at court (they are struck by boils at 9:11), and Pharaoh's heart is hardened. Q: wa-ulqiya l-saḥaratu sājidīna qālū āmannā bi-rabbi l-ʿālamīna rabbi Mūsā wa-Hārūna. They convert at the first contest, are threatened with mutilation and crucifixion (la-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin thumma la-uṣallibannakum), and pray to die as muslims (wa-tawaffanā muslimīna). Grudging recognition becomes conversion and martyrdom.

וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִ֑וא וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה
وَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ

matches.label: King asks the prophet to intercede with God to remove a plague
matches.note: Exod: haʿtîrû ʾel-YHWH wə-yāsēr haṣ-ṣəfardəʿîm ... wa-ʾăšalləḥāh ʾet-hā-ʿām, then wa-yyarʾ Parʿōh kî hāyətāh hā-rəwāḥāh wə-hakhbēd ʾet-libbô. Q: yā Mūsā dʿu lanā rabbaka ... la-in kashafta ʿannā l-rijza la-nuʾminanna laka wa-la-nursilanna maʿaka banī Isrāʾīla ... idhā hum yankuthūna. The vow made under a plague and broken afterwards. Q adds a promise of faith (la-nuʾminanna) and says 'they break their word', where Exod says the heart was made heavy.

passages.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּזֹ֣את תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַכֶּ֣ה בַּמַּטֶּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר בְּיָדִ֗י עַל הַמַּ֛יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיְאֹ֖ר וְנֶהֶפְכ֥וּ לְדָֽם

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֡ן קַ֣ח מַטְּךָ֣ וּנְטֵֽה יָדְךָ֩ עַל מֵימֵ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם עַֽל נַהֲרֹתָ֣ם עַל יְאֹרֵיהֶ֣ם וְעַל אַגְמֵיהֶ֗ם וְעַ֛ל כָּל מִקְוֵ֥ה מֵימֵיהֶ֖ם וְיִֽהְיוּ דָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה דָם֙ בְּכָל אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבָעֵצִ֖ים וּבָאֲבָנִֽים

וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵן֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֤רֶם בַּמַּטֶּה֙ וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּיְאֹ֔ר לְעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּהָֽפְכ֛וּ כָּל הַמַּ֥יִם אֲשֶׁר בַּיְאֹ֖ר לְדָֽם

וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵ֨ן הַחַרְטֻמִּ֧ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֛ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת הַכִּנִּ֖ים וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה

leads.title: Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes (weight 7.7); Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves (weight 7.3); God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh (weight 7.1); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 6.0); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 5.7). Pair score 33.8.

Only in Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs: Hero is eighty (and his brother eighty-three) when they confront the king; God makes the prophet 'as God' to the king with his brother as his prophet; Wonders done so that Egypt shall know 'I am YHWH'; Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh turned away with his power/pillar (rukn) and called Moses 'a sorcerer or a madman'; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes [divergence between the texts]; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts]; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts]; and 1 more.

Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; The defeated enemy's form (image or body) is kept as a sign (Akk. ittu, Ar. āya) for those who come after [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

וַיִּקְרָא֙ גַּם פַּרְעֹ֔ה לַֽחֲכָמִ֖ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֨וּ גַם הֵ֜ם חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּלַהֲטֵיהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן

matches.note: Exod: Aaron's staff (wayyašlēk ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wayhî lətannîn), and the magicians really do the same, wayyaʿăśû gam-hēm ḥarṭummê miṣrayim bəlahăṭêhem kēn ... wayyihyû lətannînim, before wayyiblaʿ maṭṭēh-ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭōtām. matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest
matches.note: Exod 7:11 wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm, Pharaoh simply summons them and they repeat the sign with their secret arts (bə-lahăṭêhem). leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 6.5); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 6.0); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 5.7). Pair score 25.2.

Only in Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs: Hero is eighty (and his brother eighty-three) when they confront the king; God makes the prophet 'as God' to the king with his brother as his prophet; Wonders done so that Egypt shall know 'I am YHWH'; Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh turned away with his power/pillar (rukn) and called Moses 'a sorcerer or a madman'; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes [divergence between the texts]; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts]; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves; God sends Moses and Aaron together, with his signs, to Pharaoh; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents; and 2 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; and 3 more.

matches.label: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents
matches.note: Who throws the staff, and how. Exod: Aaron throws (wa-yyašlēkh ʾAhărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wa-yhî lə-tannîn); the magicians do the same (bə-lahăṭêhem kēn); and maṭṭēh-ʾAhărōn swallows their staffs (wa-yyivlaʿ). Q: Moses throws (fa-alqā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya thuʿbānun mubīnun); the magicians offer him the first throw (immā an tulqiya); their act is siḥr that 'bewitched the people's eyes' (saḥarū aʿyuna l-nāsi), and Moses' staff talqafu mā yaʾfikūna. Aaron drops out of the act; the magic is illusion.

leads.title: Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory ↔ Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The beings that carry God's throne, and what they do [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The creatures' wings sound like many waters, like the voice of Shaddai; and 13 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers: The damned say 'Lord, you caused us to die twice and gave us life twice; we confess our sins; is there a way out?'; The Day of the Approaching (al-azifa) when hearts reach the throats, choking; God as Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty (string of divine epithets); God casts the Spirit (al-ruh) of his command upon whom he wills of his servants to warn of the Day of Meeting; God knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal; In terror eyes swerve and hearts reach the throats; The heavenly host speak for a human before the high god and ask his forgiveness; The angels who bear the Throne and those around it glorify God and ask forgiveness for the believers, praying they and their righteous kin enter Eden; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); On the Day God asks 'Whose is the kingdom today?' and answers 'God's, the One, the Overpowering'; Formula: 'gracious and merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, relenting of evil'; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied; and 1 more.
