leads.title: Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory ↔ Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The creatures' wings sound like many waters, like the voice of Shaddai; and 14 more.

Only in Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary: The heart did not falsify what it saw; the gaze did not swerve nor transgress; When there covered the Lote-Tree that which covered it (an ineffable phenomenon); Oath 'By the star when it sets/falls (idha hawa)'; He saw him at a second descent by the Lote-Tree of the Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), near the Garden of Refuge; The heavenly figure came within two bow-lengths or nearer (qaba qawsayn aw adna) and revealed to his servant; Leaders see God with a sapphire-like pavement under his feet; One mighty in power (shadid al-quwa) taught him, stood poised on the highest horizon, then drew near and descended; Taken up to heaven, the mortal looks from the horizon (base of heaven) to the heights of heaven and sees its awesomeness; Your companion has not erred; he does not speak from desire; it is only revelation revealed; Whether a prophet speaks from his own heart or desire, or by revelation [contrast between the texts]; A literary work is 'what was revealed to' a named sage or poet and what he then proclaimed; What or whom the visionaries saw: God himself or his messenger [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

matches.label: He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord
matches.note: A prophet's vision of the divine described with deliberate distance. Ezekiel: dəmûṯ kə-marʾēh ʾāḏām ... kə-marʾēh haq-qešeṯ ʾăšer yihyeh ḇe-ʿānān ... hûʾ marʾēh dəmûṯ kəḇôḏ YHWH wā-ʾerʾeh wā-ʾeppōl ʿal pānāy (the likeness of the appearance of the glory, framed by a bow in the cloud). Quran: fa-kāna qāba qawsayni aw adnā ... mā kadhaba l-fuʾādu mā raʾā ... la-qad raʾā min āyāti rabbihi l-kubrā. Bow (qešeṯ / qaws, cognate) and seeing in both; Ezekiel falls on his face, while the Prophet's 'sight did not swerve' (mā zāgha l-baṣaru). The bow link is a lead only: the Quran's 'two bow-lengths' is a measure of distance.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The creatures' wings sound like many waters, like the voice of Shaddai; and 13 more.

Only in Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears; That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them; At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing; Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast); Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?'; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; The count of days and nights a destroying wind or flood-storm blows [divergence between the texts]; A destroying storm rages for seven days and seven (or eight) nights [divergence between the texts]; The overturned city (al-mu'tafika, Sodom) God hurled down and covered with what covered it; A roaring cold wind (sarsar) on a day of continuous ill omen plucks men away like trunks of uprooted palms; A storm wind is paired with a seven/eight count; and 7 more.

leads.title: Coals from between the cherubim; the wheels full of eyes; the glory leaves the temple ↔ The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The form, faces and number of wings of heavenly beings [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Each cherub or living creature has four faces (human, lion, ox/cherub, eagle), four wings and human hands under the wings (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in Coals from between the cherubim; the wheels full of eyes; the glory leaves the temple: Burning coals are taken from between the cherubim / wheels and scattered over the city; Above the firmament over the living creatures appears something like sapphire in the likeness of a throne; The sound of the cherubim's wings is heard like the voice of El Shaddai when he speaks; The wheels are called by the name 'galgal' ('whirl') in the prophet's hearing; The bodies, backs, hands, wings and wheels of the throne-creatures are full of eyes all around; A heavenly man clothed in linen with a scribe's writing kit at his waist; The spirit of the living creature is in the wheels, which move with them; Wheels gleaming like beryl, constructed as a wheel within a wheel, beside each creature; The divine glory leaves the temple in stages: from the cherub to the threshold, to the east gate, to the mountain east of the city; The glory of YHWH appears in the cloud; God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim.

Only in The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas: God made the angels messengers with wings in twos, threes and fours, adding to creation what he wills; To God ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up; Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy; he calls his party to the blaze; The false gods do not own even the thin skin of a date-stone (qitmir); they cannot hear prayer and will disown it at the Resurrection; What God opens no one can shut, and what he withholds no one can release; What happens where fresh and salt water meet [divergence between the texts]; A god's act sets fresh (sweet) water against salt (bitter) water [divergence between the texts]; If God willed he could remove you and bring a new creation; God began man's creation from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of a despised fluid, then shaped him and breathed of his spirit; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; No one is granted long life or has his life shortened except it is in a Book; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; and 6 more.

Only in Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot: The adorned bride trusts in her beauty and plays the harlot with every passer-by; Sons and daughters born to God are slaughtered and offered to idols as food; A newborn girl is cast into the open field unwashed, unsalted and unswaddled, with her navel cord uncut, loathed on the day of her birth; God spreads his garment-wing over the grown foundling, swears a covenant and takes the city as his wife, bathing, anointing, clothing and adorning her; Unlike other harlots, the city pays fees to her lovers instead of receiving them; God passes by the infant wallowing in her blood and says twice 'In your blood, live!'; The unfaithful wife makes male images (tsalmei zakhar) from the gold and silver God gave her and fornicates with them; Political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea pictured as harlotry with lovers ('big of flesh'); An assembly stones the adulteress and hacks her with swords and burns her houses before many women; God gathers the adulteress's lovers, strips her naked before them and hands her over to be judged; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; Man asked to spread his garment-wing over a woman as a sign of marriage; and 3 more.

Only in Six communities judged; all things prostrate; garments of fire and bracelets of gold: Hooked maces of iron (maqāmiʿ) drive back those who try to escape hell; God will judge between believers, Jews, Sabians, Christians, Magians and polytheists on resurrection day; In hell the unbelievers are cut garments of fire and boiling water is poured on their heads, melting their insides and skins; The place of humans in the worship offered by all creation [divergence between the texts]; All in heaven and earth prostrate to God: sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, beasts and many humans; The host of heaven bows down to God; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Catalogue of bridal finery: embroidered cloth, tahash sandals, linen, silk, bracelets, necklace, nose-ring, earrings and a crown (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot: An assembly stones the adulteress and hacks her with swords and burns her houses before many women; God gathers the adulteress's lovers, strips her naked before them and hands her over to be judged; The adorned bride trusts in her beauty and plays the harlot with every passer-by; Bride given a gold nose-ring and bracelets; King makes his son 'pass through the fire' after the abominations of the nations; Sons and daughters born to God are slaughtered and offered to idols as food; A newborn girl is cast into the open field unwashed, unsalted and unswaddled, with her navel cord uncut, loathed on the day of her birth; God spreads his garment-wing over the grown foundling, swears a covenant and takes the city as his wife, bathing, anointing, clothing and adorning her; Unlike other harlots, the city pays fees to her lovers instead of receiving them; Worship of other gods described as 'whoring after' them; God passes by the infant wallowing in her blood and says twice 'In your blood, live!'; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; The unfaithful wife makes male images (tsalmei zakhar) from the gold and silver God gave her and fornicates with them; Political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea pictured as harlotry with lovers ('big of flesh'); Man asked to spread his garment-wing over a woman as a sign of marriage.

Only in Entering houses, lowering the gaze, head-coverings, marriage and manumission: Do not enter others' houses until you have asked leave and greeted the household; if told to go back, go back; A father must not make his daughter a prostitute; Women should not strike their feet to make known their hidden ornaments (anklets); Freed slave must not be sent away empty-handed but furnished from flock, threshing floor and winepress; Believing men and women are told to lower their gaze and guard their private parts; Grant slaves who ask a written manumission contract (kitāba) and give them of God's wealth; Marry off the unmarried among you and your righteous slaves; God will enrich the poor; Believing women draw their head-coverings (khumur) over their bosoms and do not show adornment except to listed kin.

leads.title: Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant ↔ Lot and the destruction of his town
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy (weight 7.3); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 6.2). Pair score 13.6.

Only in Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant: When God atones for her she will remember, be ashamed and never again open her mouth; Proverb 'like mother, like daughter'; God will restore the fortunes of Sodom and Samaria along with Jerusalem; Samaria (elder, on the left/north) and Sodom (younger, on the right/south) are Jerusalem's sisters, and she is worse than both; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; God promises an everlasting covenant (berit olam) with his people; God swears 'As I live'.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts]; God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); The fate of Lot's wife; God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; and 1 more.

leads.title: Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance ↔ The primordial covenant ("Am I not your Lord?")
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest; 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; Intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden; and 4 more.

Only in The primordial covenant ("Am I not your Lord?"): God takes all Adam's descendants from their loins and makes them testify 'Am I not your Lord?' ('Yes'); A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; Covenant made with those present and with those not here today [divergence between the texts]; The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; The people are made witnesses against themselves to their choice; Covenant made with those present and with those not here today; An oath or covenant that binds descendants not yet born [divergence between the texts]; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; Intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden; and 4 more.

leads.title: Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey ↔ Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A spirit enters the prophet and sets him on his feet (weight 7.7); Israel called 'a rebellious house' (beit meri) (weight 7.7); The prophet sees 'the likeness of the glory of YHWH' as radiant fire enthroned (weight 7.3); The prophet must speak 'whether they hear or refuse' (weight 7.3); 'The hand of YHWH was upon' the prophet, bringing a vision or transport (weight 7.3). Pair score 37.5.

Only in Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey: Heavenly voice cries 'Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place'; God makes the prophet's forehead as hard as diamond against a hard-faced people; Foreign peoples of strange speech would heed the prophet, but Israel will not; A hand is stretched out to the prophet holding a scroll; The prophet is made to eat a heavenly scroll; God addresses the prophet as 'son of man' (ben adam); The prophet lives among briers, thorns and scorpions, yet must not fear; The spirit lifts and carries the prophet away; After his vision the prophet sits stunned among the people for seven days; A great rushing sound of the creatures' wings and the wheels behind the prophet; The eaten scroll tastes sweet as honey in the prophet's mouth; A scroll written on front and back with laments, mourning and woe; and 5 more.

Only in Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house: The glory seen by the river appears again to the prophet in a valley/plain; The prophet is told to shut himself in his house; If the watchman fails to warn the wicked, God requires their blood from him; Muteness imposed as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A righteous man who turns to iniquity dies and his former righteousness is not remembered; God appoints the prophet as a watchman (tsofeh) for the house of Israel; God makes the prophet's tongue cleave to his palate so he is mute except when God speaks; The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory; Each person dies for his own sin.

leads.title: Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain ↔ The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings (weight 7.7); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 6.4). Pair score 14.1.

Only in Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain: The being was blameless from the day he was created until iniquity was found in him; God brings out a fire from within the sinner that consumes him and turns him to ashes on the ground; The king of Tyre is called 'the seal of perfection (hotem toknit), full of wisdom and perfect in beauty'; The primal being walked among the 'stones of fire' on God's mountain; 'You were an anointed guardian cherub; I placed you on the holy mountain of God'; A city or king claims or is called 'perfect in beauty' (kelilat yofi); A primal figure was in Eden, the garden of God, covered with every precious stone (sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, emerald) and gold settings prepared on the day of his creation; By wisdom and trade the ruler amasses gold and silver and his heart grows proud because of his wealth; The breastpiece of judgment set with twelve gems in four rows; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; The destroyed one will be sought but never found again; 'I will make you terrors and you shall be no more'; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; and 3 more.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; In the divine realm the human is given a garment to put on [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 23 more.

Only in The valley of dry bones: God will open his people's graves, bring them up from their graves and bring them to the land of Israel; The exiles say 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off'; The prophet summons the breath (ruah) from the four winds to breathe into the slain so they live; The prophet is set down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones and led around among them; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The revived dead stand on their feet, an exceedingly great army; God will put his own spirit within them and cause them to walk in his statutes; A multitude of dead revived [divergence between the texts]; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; A single cry or rebuke (zajra) and the dead stand looking; At the prophet's word there is a rattling; bones come together bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath; and 3 more.

Only in Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships: God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn); Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies; A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters; God's crafting of the human body, and what is said to follow from it [divergence between the texts]; Man is made from compacted (clotted) blood and then bones; God makes the fluid (seed) in women into a human and forms the child in its mother's belly; At creation God fixed the weight of the wind, the measure of the waters, a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; God fashions seven heavens; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay; and 1 more.

וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ גּ֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֥שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָֽל

leads.title: Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds ↔ The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: After the first punishment God restores Israel's turn with wealth and sons (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds: God strikes the bow from the invader's left hand and makes the arrows drop from his right hand; The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own iniquity because God hid his face, not because he was weak; The carrion-eaters are sated at God's table with horses, charioteers, warriors and all men of war; God sends fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands; God will no longer hide his face from Israel, for he has poured out his spirit on the house of Israel; Israel plunders those who plundered them and despoils those who despoiled them; God invites every bird and beast to his great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel to eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of princes, as of rams, lambs, goats and Bashan bulls, till drunk with blood; All Israel buries the dead for seven months to purify the land; appointed men search the land and mark every human bone with a sign (tsiyyun) for the buriers; Gog and his horde are buried in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea, renamed Valley of Hamon-Gog; a city is named Hamonah; Israel's townsfolk burn the enemy weapons (shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears) as fuel for seven years, cutting no wood from the forest; Strong bulls of Bashan encircle the sufferer; The final invader comes from the farthest recesses of the north (yarketei tsafon); and 7 more.

Only in The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8): Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant; Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)'; It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice; God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs; The storm or enemy destroys the city a second time; The enemy sent against the city enters its sanctuary and wrecks what it finds; The god himself rouses a mighty foreign enemy against his own land or people; The god himself sends a fierce foreign people against his own city or people; God sends against Israel servants of his of great might who range through their homes; Because of his people's offence their own god lets a foreign power oppress them for a time, and later gives the land (or the upper hand) back; A swift journey by night ends at a distant sanctuary; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; and 6 more.

leads.title: Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds ↔ Dhul-Qarnayn, the setting and rising sun, and the barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-101)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Gog and Magog are let loose and swarm down from every height before the end [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince (nesi rosh) of Meshech and Tubal, an eschatological invader (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.1.

Only in Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds: God strikes the bow from the invader's left hand and makes the arrows drop from his right hand; The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own iniquity because God hid his face, not because he was weak; The carrion-eaters are sated at God's table with horses, charioteers, warriors and all men of war; God sends fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands; God will no longer hide his face from Israel, for he has poured out his spirit on the house of Israel; Israel plunders those who plundered them and despoils those who despoiled them; God invites every bird and beast to his great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel to eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of princes, as of rams, lambs, goats and Bashan bulls, till drunk with blood; All Israel buries the dead for seven months to purify the land; appointed men search the land and mark every human bone with a sign (tsiyyun) for the buriers; Gog and his horde are buried in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea, renamed Valley of Hamon-Gog; a city is named Hamonah; Israel's townsfolk burn the enemy weapons (shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears) as fuel for seven years, cutting no wood from the forest; Strong bulls of Bashan encircle the sufferer; The final invader comes from the farthest recesses of the north (yarketei tsafon); and 6 more.

Only in Dhul-Qarnayn, the setting and rising sun, and the barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-101): When God's promise comes the barrier is leveled to the ground; The conqueror is given the choice to punish the people at the sunset or treat them kindly; A people complain that Gog and Magog spread corruption in the land; A barrier of iron blocks filling the gap between two cliffs, heated with bellows and sealed with molten copper, shuts out Gog and Magog; At the sun's rising the conqueror finds a people with no shelter from it; Between two mountain barriers the conqueror finds a people who scarcely understand speech; At the end peoples surge into one another like waves; At the place of sunset the conqueror finds the sun setting in a muddy (or hot) spring; The people offer tribute for a barrier; the conqueror declines payment and asks for their labor; A ruler builds a barrier across the gap between two mountains to cut off invading peoples; A ruler builds a barrier across the gap between two mountains to cut off invading peoples [divergence between the texts]; Whether a king's barrier against invaders holds or is breached [divergence between the texts]; and 15 more.

leads.title: The glory of God returns to the temple ↔ Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The earth shines (lit up) with God's glory [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The earth shines (lit up) with God's glory (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in The glory of God returns to the temple: God's voice (or the sound of his coming) is like the sound of many waters; Kings' corpses or memorials (pigre malkehem) beside the temple defile God's holy name; The temple stands on the top of a (very high) mountain whose whole territory is most holy; The prophet is to describe the temple's plan so that Israel will be ashamed of its sins; The divine glory returns to the temple from the east through the east gate; The temple is called the place of God's throne and the soles of his feet, where he will dwell forever; Fear that the spirit of YHWH will carry the prophet off to an unknown place; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory; The cloud and glory fill the sanctuary so that even the leader cannot enter; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden: The angels are seen surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord; The blessed praise God who gave them the land (ard) as inheritance to settle in the Garden where they will; The Book (record) is laid down, the prophets and witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed with truth; Unbelievers are driven to hell in throngs (zumar) and the godfearing to the Garden in throngs; the gates open and the keepers address each; The keepers of the Garden greet the righteous 'Peace be upon you, you have been good; enter'; Lest a soul say 'Alas for my neglect of God' or 'If only I had another chance (karra)'; If you associate partners with God your deeds will come to nothing; At the first trumpet blast all in heaven and earth swoon (sa'iqa) except whom God wills; at the second they stand looking; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; At the gate of the netherworld the gatekeepers question those who arrive [divergence between the texts]; Heaven and earth held in a hand or under the feet [divergence between the texts]; Who holds the keys that open and shut [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in The shut east gate, foreigners excluded, Levites and Zadokite priests: The east gate stays shut forever because YHWH the God of Israel entered by it; The first of the dough (reshit arisot) is given to the priest so that blessing rests on the house; Levites who went astray after idols are demoted to gatekeepers and slaughterers, barred from priestly service; Priests stand as judges in disputes, judging by God's ordinances; Priests may neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long, but must trim it; Priests serve in linen only, with no wool, and must not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat; Only the prince (nasi) may sit in the shut gate to eat bread before YHWH; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Priestly tribe receives no land: 'I am your portion and inheritance'; Priest may defile himself only for close kin; Priests may not marry a harlot or divorcee; the high priest only a virgin of his people; Priests must take off their holy garments in special chambers before going out to the people, lest the garments transmit holiness; and 5 more.

Only in Prayer not while drunk; bathing and dry ablution: Do not approach prayer while intoxicated, until you know what you say; One in major impurity (junub) must bathe before prayer, except a traveller passing through; Purification after seminal emission or intercourse [divergence between the texts]; Emission of semen makes a man (and his partner) unclean until evening; No wine before approaching God [divergence between the texts]; One who has had intercourse must wash before approaching the deity's service or prayer; Without water, purify with clean earth (tayammum), wiping face and hands.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Priests may not eat any bird or beast that died of itself or was torn (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The shut east gate, foreigners excluded, Levites and Zadokite priests: The east gate stays shut forever because YHWH the God of Israel entered by it; The first of the dough (reshit arisot) is given to the priest so that blessing rests on the house; Levites who went astray after idols are demoted to gatekeepers and slaughterers, barred from priestly service; Priests stand as judges in disputes, judging by God's ordinances; Priests may neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long, but must trim it; Priests serve in linen only, with no wool, and must not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat; Only the prince (nasi) may sit in the shut gate to eat bread before YHWH; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Priestly tribe receives no land: 'I am your portion and inheritance'; Priest may defile himself only for close kin; Priests may not marry a harlot or divorcee; the high priest only a virgin of his people; Priests must take off their holy garments in special chambers before going out to the people, lest the garments transmit holiness; and 5 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: What happens where fresh and salt water meet [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

leads.title: The end has come upon the four corners of the land ↔ Pharaoh leads his people into the fire; the towns standing and mown
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The gods of a people judged by God cannot help them (weight 7.3); 'Far be it from God to do wickedness, from Shaddai to do wrong'; he repays a man according to his deeds (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.4.

Only in The end has come upon the four corners of the land: God's 'treasured place' (tsefuni) is profaned by robbers when he turns his face away; Survivors on the mountains moan like doves of the valleys, each for his iniquity; Proclamation 'An end has come, the end has come' upon the land (qets ba); In disaster people seek a vision from the prophet, but instruction perishes from the priest and counsel from the elders; Hoarded gold and silver are heated in hell and used to brand the hoarders' foreheads, sides and backs; In terror all hands go slack and all knees run with water; The people assemble in fasting, sackcloth and earth on their heads; On the day of wrath people fling their silver into the streets; silver and gold cannot save them; God gathers the dispersed from the four corners (kanfot, 'wings') of the earth; Prophecy concerning 'the end of days'; Formula 'and you/they shall know that I am YHWH' closing a judgment or salvation oracle; Judgment by the triad sword, famine and pestilence; and 1 more.

Only in Pharaoh leads his people into the fire; the towns standing and mown: Of the destroyed towns some still stand, some are mown down; On judgment day Pharaoh will lead his people down into the fire, an evil watering place; The deity's seizing (of the guilty) is slow to come but severe and final once it falls; Pharaoh goes at the head of his people to their destruction [divergence between the texts]; Divine punishment falls on a town by night or while its people take the midday rest; At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped'.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Vision of abominations in the temple - image of jealousy, animal chamber, Tammuz, sun worship: Idolaters 'put the branch (zemorah) to their nose', an obscure cultic gesture; Seventy elders stand with censers in hand offering incense in the dark, each in his chamber of images; A human-like figure of fire from the waist down and gleaming like hashmal (amber/electrum) from the waist up; Though they cry in God's ears with a loud voice, he will not listen; An idol called 'the image (semel) of jealousy that provokes jealousy' stands at the north gate of the temple; Prophet is told to dig through a wall and enters through the opening; Hidden temple chamber whose walls are engraved all around with creeping things, loathsome beasts and idols; A hand seizes the prophet by a lock of his hair and the spirit carries him between earth and heaven to a distant place; About twenty-five men with their backs to the temple bow eastward to the sun between the porch and the altar; Prophet in exile is brought 'in visions of God' to the Jerusalem temple; Elders of the people come and sit before the prophet in his house to inquire; The glory of YHWH appears in the cloud; and 5 more.

leads.title: Covenant to send away foreign wives; assembly in the rain; list of offenders ↔ Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Dissolving marriages with women outside the community [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Covenant to send away foreign wives; assembly in the rain; list of offenders: The assembly sits trembling in the open square in the winter rains; Mixed marriages have already produced children, who are included in the dismissal; Community covenants to send away all foreign wives and their children; Named individuals are recorded as opposing the assembly's decision; Leader neither eats bread nor drinks water in mourning for the people's sin; Sons of the high priest are among those who married foreign wives; Named list of men who had married foreign wives; Leader makes the priests, Levites and all Israel swear to carry out the reform; Whoever fails to attend loses his property (herem) and is separated from the congregation; Leader prays and confesses weeping, prostrate before the house of God; 'There is still hope for Israel concerning this'; A tribunal of family heads examines each case at appointed times; and 1 more.

Only in Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge: Abraham and those with him are an excellent example: they declared themselves quit of their people and their gods, with enmity until they believe; Except Abraham's saying to his father 'I will ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power for you before God'; They despair of the hereafter as the unbelievers despair of those in the graves; Believers must not take God's enemies, who expelled the prophet, as allies (awliya') or secretly show them affection; Prohibition of killing one's children; Do not hold on to marriage ties with unbelieving women; dowries are reckoned between the communities; Believing women who emigrate are to be examined; if believers, they are not returned to the unbelievers, whose dowries are repaid; The women's pledge (bay'at al-nisa'): not to associate anything with God, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, bring a fabricated slander, or disobey in what is right; Abraham declares to his father and people that he is free of what they worship, except the one who created him; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Neither your blood-ties nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; and 10 more.

leads.title: Ezra's priestly lineage and journey to Jerusalem ↔ 'Uzayr and the Messiah called sons of God; rabbis and monks as lords
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The standing of Ezra (ʿUzayr): scribe or son of God [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Ezra's priestly lineage and journey to Jerusalem: The journey from Babylon to Jerusalem takes four months, first to fifth month; A priest's genealogy traced back to Aaron the chief priest; The scribe set his heart to seek (study) the Torah, to do it and to teach it; Hero called a skilled scribe (sofer mahir) in the Torah of Moses; Success attributed to 'the good hand of my God upon me'; The king grants the hero everything he asks.

Only in 'Uzayr and the Messiah called sons of God; rabbis and monks as lords: Polemic: the Jews are said to call 'Uzayr (Ezra?) son of God; People of the Book took their rabbis (ahbar) and monks as lords besides God; Religious personnel eat up goods that are not theirs (the god's offerings, people's wealth) [divergence between the texts]; Many rabbis and monks devour people's wealth wrongfully; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [response between the texts]; Opponents wish to put out God's light with their mouths, but God will perfect his light; Hoarded gold and silver are heated in hell and used to brand the hoarders' foreheads, sides and backs; Silver is hidden away: wrapped in rags, sealed in jars and boxes and buried in a hole in the cattle-pen or a dark corner of the house; Polemic against calling the Messiah son of God; God sent his messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion; A bribe blinds the clear-sighted and perverts the words of the righteous.

leads.title: The Flood in Genesis ↔ Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 6.5); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain (weight 6.4); Hero blessed on leaving the vessel (weight 6.2); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 6.2); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 6.1); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 5.5). Pair score 5.5.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; and 27 more.

Only in New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites: When you pour down from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram); Take provision, but the best provision is God-consciousness (taqwa); Remember God on the counted days; no sin whether one hastens in two days or delays; Piety is not entering houses from their backs but from their doors; Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress; Prayer 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next, and guard us from the fire'; Complete the pilgrimage (hajj) and visitation (umra) for God; Do not fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there; No sexual talk, wickedness or quarreling during the pilgrimage; Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more; The sacred month for the sacred month; violations are subject to retaliation; Do not shave heads until the sacrificial offering (hady) reaches its place; and 12 more.

matches.label: The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq)
matches.note: Creation by splitting a unity. Gen: the rāqîaʿ divides waters from waters, wîhî mabdîl bên mayim lāmāyim. Q: heaven and earth themselves were one closed mass, kānatā ratqan fa-fataqnāhumā. What is divided differs: the waters in Gen, heaven from earth in Q.

Shared motifs, rarest first: What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them (weight 6.8); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters (weight 6.4); Creation is completed in six days (weight 6.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 5.5). Pair score 32.7.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; and 23 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; Night covers the sleepers as a garment, the land as in death; the day is a rising (waking); Two waters, the sweet and the salt sea, meet or mingle [divergence between the texts]; What sets the daily sleeping and rising of people [divergence between the texts]; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; A god's act sets fresh (sweet) water against salt (bitter) water [divergence between the texts]; God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; The wind carries good news (Akk. bussurtu, Ar. bushr, mubashshirāt) [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

matches.note: After the six days: Gen 2:2 wa-yəkhal ʾĕlōhîm ba-yyôm haš-šəvîʿî məlaʾktô ... wa-yyišbōt ba-yyôm haš-šəvîʿî, God ceases or rests on the seventh day; Q 25:59 khalaqa s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa wa-mā baynahumā fī sittati ayyāmin thumma stawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi r-raḥmānu, God takes his seat on the Throne. Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; and 26 more.

Only in Who revives rotten bones? Fire from the green tree; Be and it is: The skeptic asks 'Who will give life to bones when they have rotted?'; the answer: he who produced them the first time; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; God created livestock and subjected them to people for riding, food, benefits and drink; God made fire for you from the green tree, from which you kindle; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 5.5). Pair score 5.5.

matches.label: The form God gave humans at creation
matches.note: Human form at creation. Gen: wa-yyiḇrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-hā-ʾāḏām bə-ṣalmô ... wə-hinnēh-ṭôḇ məʾōḏ. Q: wa-ṣawwarakum fa-aḥsana ṣuwarakum. leads.finding: The order of creating heaven and earth and the days allotted to each

units.title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest
Ha-Mim Fussilat: the veil between; creation in days; heaven as smoke

matches.label: The order of creating heaven and earth and the days allotted to each
matches.note: The order and the counting of the days. Gen: the firmament called šāmāyim on day 2 (yôm šēnî), dry land and plants on day 3, luminaries in the firmament on day 4, so heaven before dry earth, one work per day. Q: khalaqa l-arḍa fī yawmayni ... wa-qaddara fīhā aqwātahā fī arbaʿati ayyām ... thumma stawā ilā s-samāʾi wa-hiya dukhān ... fa-qaḍāhunna sabʿa samāwātin fī yawmayn. The earth is created first, its provisions in four days, and only then the seven heavens; the sums (2+4+2) are reckoned by the exegetes to six. There is no evening-and-morning formula, no seventh day, and the luminaries are 'lamps' of the lowest heaven.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם

matches.label: The weekly holy day, and whether it rests on God's rest
matches.note: The weekly day without the creation rest. Genesis grounds the seventh day in God's rest: wa-yišbōṯ bay-yôm haš-šəḇîʿî ... wa-yəḇāreḵ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ yôm haš-šəḇîʿî wa-yqaddēš ʾōṯô kî ḇô šāḇaṯ. The Quran's Friday (yawm al-jumuʿa, the day of assembly) has no rest and no creation basis: fa-ntashirū fī l-arḍ. This fits the Quran's denial that God rested (50:38).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Creation is completed in six days (weight 6.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 5.5). Pair score 19.5.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 25 more.

Only in Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection: Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily; Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud; A felled tree sprouts again at the scent of water, but a man dies and does not rise [contrast between the texts]; God makes the night cover the day; God sends rain on the desert where no human lives, to make grass sprout; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

matches.label: Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it
matches.note: What follows the six days. Gen: wa-ykhullû haš-šāmayim wə-hā-ʾāreṣ ... wa-yyišbōt bay-yôm haš-šəvîʿî, God rests and blesses the seventh day. Q: khalaqa l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa fī sittati ayyāmin thumma stawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi yughshī l-layla l-nahāra. The six days are kept, but in place of the rest God sits on the throne and goes on governing. There is no seventh day. cf. Q 50:38, where no weariness touches him.

leads.title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God made the great lights: the sun to rule the day, the moon and stars to rule the night (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; and 27 more.

Only in Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood: Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a fire; The people put their fingers in their ears and wrap their garments over their heads to avoid hearing the prophet; Noah's people refuse to abandon their gods Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; The flood hero prays for forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever enters his house believing, and all believers; God caused humans to grow from the earth like a plant, returns them to it and will bring them out again; Prophet summons his people night and day, openly and in secret, yet they only flee further; People are put into the earth and brought out of it again [divergence between the texts]; Destroying a people together with their offspring because of their character [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Human comes from dust and returns to dust [divergence between the texts]; Before the flood the hero tells his city that heaven will rain plenty on them [divergence between the texts]; A wish that no one be left alive by the destruction [divergence between the texts]; Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

leads.title: The Table of Nations ↔ Hud and the monument-building people of Ad
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Nimrod, first mighty man, a mighty hunter before the LORD (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in The Table of Nations: First kingdom founded in Babel and Shinar; Founding of Nineveh and the Assyrian cities; The world's nations number about seventy; All nations listed as descendants of the three sons of the flood hero; In the days of Peleg the earth was divided; Humanity created from a male and a female and made into peoples (shu'ub) and tribes to know one another; the noblest is the most pious; Nations distinguished by land, language and clan; Philistines derived from Casluhim/Caphtorim (Crete).

Only in Hud and the monument-building people of Ad: The people of ʿĀd build a monument on every height and take fortresses (maṣāniʿ) hoping to live forever; Their graves (qirbam = qivram) are their houses forever, though they named lands after themselves; The prophet Hūd is sent to the people of ʿĀd; Monuments built so that their builders may live for ever [neutral]; Men build great structures to endure, but the builders and their buildings pass [divergence between the texts]; Building with baked bricks and bitumen instead of stone and mortar; Woe to the one who builds a city (Zion) with bloodshed and injustice; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness; Builders seek to make a name for themselves and avoid dispersal; and 2 more.

matches.label: Humans build a tower whose top reaches heaven
matches.note: A tower toward heaven: Babel's builders, all humankind (hāvâ nivneh llānû ʿîr û-migdāl wə-rōʾšô vaš-šāmayim), want to make a name and not be scattered; God comes down to see, and scatters them. matches.label: A city's punishment held back for the righteous within it
matches.note: A city spared for the sake of the righteous inside it. Genesis: ha-ʾap̄ tispeh ṣaddîq ʿim rāšāʿ ... wə-lōʾ ṯiśśāʾ lam-māqôm ləmaʿan ḥămiššîm haṣ-ṣaddîqim; lōʾ ʾašḥîṯ baʿăḇûr hā-ʿăśārâ (Abraham bargains; God would spare all for ten). Quran: wa-lawlā rijālun muʾminūna wa-nisāʾun muʾminātun lam taʿlamūhum an taṭaʾūhum ... law tazayyalū la-ʿadhdhabnā lladhīna kafarū (God held back the believers' own attack on Mecca because unknown believers were inside; had they been separated, he would have punished the rest). The danger is a human army, not divine fire; no bargaining; and the righteous are to be separated out (tazayyul), not the cause of sparing everyone for ever.

Genesis: YHWH decides ha-mḵasseh ʾănî mē-ʾaḇrāhām and tells him of the outcry (zaʿăqaṯ səḏōm), and Abraham bargains for the city (18:23-32). matches.label: Who Abraham's visitors are
matches.note: Who comes: wa-la-qad jāʾat rusulunā ibrāhīma bi-l-bushrā vs wayyērāʾ ʾēlāyw YHWH ... wᵉhinnēh šᵉlōšāh ʾănāšîm. Gen has YHWH himself appear in the form of three men; Q has 'our messengers', with no number and no appearance of God.

passages.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם
וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ

matches.label: Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal he serves
matches.note: Reversed: in Gen the guests eat (wayyittēn lipnêhem wᵉhûʾ-ʿōmēd ʿălêhem taḥat hāʿēṣ wayyōʾkēlû); in Q their hands do not reach the food (fa-lammā raʾā aydiyahum lā taṣilu ilayhi nakirahum). cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14, b. Bava Metzia 86b (angels only seem to eat), outside the canon.

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ

matches.label: Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why
matches.note: Who is afraid and why: in Q Abraham is afraid because the guests will not eat (wa-awjasa minhum khīfatan qālū lā takhaf); in Gen it is Sarah who is afraid when caught laughing (wattᵉkaḥēš śārāh lēʾmōr lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾāh).

passages.text: וַתְּכַחֵ֨שׁ שָׂרָ֧ה לֵאמֹ֛ר לֹ֥א צָחַ֖קְתִּי כִּ֣י יָרֵ֑אָה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹ֖א כִּ֥י צָחָֽקְתְּ
فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ

matches.label: When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered
matches.note: The order and the answer change: in Gen Sarah overhears the promise at the tent door and then laughs inwardly (wattiṣḥaq śārāh bᵉqirbāh), and God rebukes her (lāmmāh zeh ṣāḥăqāh śārāh), she denies it (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî); in Q she is standing by and laughs first (wa-mraʾatuhu qāʾimatun fa-ḍaḥikat), then receives the tidings, with no rebuke and no denial. ṣḥq / ḍḥk are cognate.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו
וַתִּצְחַ֥ק שָׂרָ֖ה בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַחֲרֵ֤י בְלֹתִי֙ הָֽיְתָה לִּ֣י עֶדְנָ֔ה וַֽאדֹנִ֖י זָקֵֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל אַבְרָהָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי
وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ قَآئِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَٰهَا بِإِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَٰقَ يَعْقُوبَ

matches.label: A divine messenger announces a son to a barren couple
matches.note: The promise of a son: fa-basharnāhā bi-isḥāqa wa-min warāʾi isḥāqa yaʿqūb vs šôb ʾāšûb ʾēlêkā kāʿēt ḥayyāh wᵉhinnēh-bēn lᵉśārāh ʾištekā. It is said to Sarah directly in Q, to Abraham in Gen (Sarah only overhears); Q names Isaac and adds Jacob after him; Gen names no child here and adds a date (lammôʿēd ... kāʿēt ḥayyāh).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו
הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן
وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ قَآئِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَٰهَا بِإِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَٰقَ يَعْقُوبَ

matches.label: A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests
matches.note: Abraham at once brings a calf: fa-mā labitha an jāʾa bi-ʿijlin ḥanīdh (roasted) vs ʾel-habbāqār rāṣ ʾabrāhām wayyiqqaḥ ben-bāqār rak wāṭôb ... wayᵉmahēr (both stress haste). Q has no foot-washing, cakes, curds or milk.

matches.label: Who Abraham's visitors are
matches.note: Who the visitors are. Genesis: wa-yērāʾ ʾēlâw YHWH bə-ʾēlōnê mamrēʾ ... wə-hinnēh šəlōšâ ʾănāšîm (YHWH appears, as three men; YHWH himself speaks in 18:13). Quran: ḍayfu ibrāhīma l-mukramīn, addressed as ayyuhā l-mursalūn (51:31): honored guests who are 'sent ones', no number, and God is not among them.

passages.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם
וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

matches.label: Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them
matches.note: The welcome. Genesis: Abraham runs to meet them (wa-yyāroṣ liqrāʾṯām), bows to the ground and begs ʾăḏōnāy ʾim nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bə-ʿênêḵā, then wa-yəmahēr ʾaḇrāhām hā-ʾōhĕlâ ʾel śārâ. Quran: the guests speak first, fa-qālū salāman qāla salāmun qawmun munkarūn (Abraham returns the greeting and finds them strange), then fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi (he slipped off to his household). Same hurried move to the tent; the bow and the plea are absent, and Abraham's unease (munkarūn) is added.

passages.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֗י אִם נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אַל נָ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר מֵעַ֥ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ
וַיְמַהֵ֧ר אַבְרָהָ֛ם הָאֹ֖הֱלָה אֶל שָׂרָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַהֲרִ֞י שְׁלֹ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קֶ֣מַח סֹ֔לֶת ל֖וּשִׁי וַעֲשִׂ֥י עֻגֽוֹת
إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ

The refusal to eat reveals that they are angels and frightens Abraham. cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat), a solution to the same problem; not in the HB.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac: Child promised to a woman past childbearing age; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts]; The aged father asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is very old [divergence between the texts]; Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why [divergence between the texts]; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you' [divergence between the texts]; Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age [divergence between the texts]; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Darkness and light, clay and two terms, and those who would not believe: Had God sent an angel he would have made him a man; Even a book on parchment they could touch would be called magic; God destroyed earlier generations though he had established them more firmly and given them rain and rivers; Praise God who created heaven and earth and made the darknesses and the light; Earlier messengers were mocked, and what the mockers mocked surrounded them; God decreed a term (ajal) for each person, and another term named with him; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; Whether darkness is made by God or exists before creation [divergence between the texts]; 'I form light and create darkness, make peace and create evil (ra'); I YHWH do all these'; The speaker too was 'pinched off from clay' (qoratsti), like a figure nipped from a lump of clay; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.
