passages.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הַמַּלְאָכִ֤ים סְדֹ֨מָה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְל֖וֹט יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר סְדֹ֑ם וַיַּרְא לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קָם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣ם לְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין
וַיִּפְצַר בָּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ אֵלָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וּמַצּ֥וֹת אָפָ֖ה וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ

matches.label: Lot's townspeople turn on him
matches.note: The townsmen besiege Lot's house: wa-jāʾahu qawmuhu yuhraʿūna ilayhi vs nāsabbû ʿal-habbayit minnaʿar wᵉʿad-zāqēn ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wᵉnēdʿāh ʾōtām. Their answer differs: in Gen they turn on Lot as an alien who plays the judge (hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ) and try to break the door; in Q they only say la-qad ʿalimta mā lanā fī banātika min ḥaqqin wa-innaka la-taʿlamu mā nurīd.

passages.text: טֶרֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּבוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד זָקֵ֑ן כָּל הָעָ֖ם מִקָּצֶֽה
וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֶל לוֹט֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ אַיֵּ֧ה הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַלָּ֑יְלָה הוֹצִיאֵ֣ם אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְנֵדְעָ֖ה אֹתָֽם
וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ גֶּשׁ הָ֗לְאָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ הָאֶחָ֤ד בָּֽא לָגוּר֙ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֣ט שָׁפ֔וֹט עַתָּ֕ה נָרַ֥ע לְךָ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם וַיִּפְצְר֨וּ בָאִ֤ישׁ בְּלוֹט֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֖וּ לִשְׁבֹּ֥ר הַדָּֽלֶת

وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ
قَالُوا۟ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا لَنَا فِى بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ

matches.label: What Lot says to the townsmen
matches.note: Lot offers his daughters: hāʾulāʾi banātī hunna aṭharu lakum fa-ttaqū llāha wa-lā tukhzūni fī ḍayfī a-laysa minkum rajulun rashīd vs ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šᵉtê bānôt ... wᵉʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bᵉʿênêkem raq lāʾănāšîm hāʾēl ʾal-taʿăśû dābār. The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אַל נָ֥א אַחַ֖י תָּרֵֽעוּ

הִנֵּה נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אוֹצִֽיאָה נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי

وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ

matches.label: The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do
matches.note: The guests disclose their errand: yā lūṭu innā rusulu rabbika lan yaṣilū ilayka vs kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh ... wayᵉšallᵉḥēnû YHWH lᵉšaḥătāh. In Gen the angels first pull Lot inside and strike the mob with blindness (hikkû bassanwērîm); in Q, where Lot wishes for strength or a strong support (law anna lī bikum quwwatan aw āwī ilā ruknin shadīd), only their word assures him.

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת יָדָ֔ם וַיָּבִ֧יאוּ אֶת ל֛וֹט אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְאֶת הַדֶּ֖לֶת סָגָֽרוּ
וְֽאֶת הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים אֲשֶׁר פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּ֗יִת הִכּוּ֙ בַּסַּנְוֵרִ֔ים מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּלְא֖וּ לִמְצֹ֥א הַפָּֽתַח
כִּֽי מַשְׁחִתִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ אֶת הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי גָֽדְלָ֤ה צַעֲקָתָם֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ
قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِى بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ ءَاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

matches.label: When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls
matches.note: When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).

passages.text: וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר
הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ יָצָ֣א עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְל֖וֹט בָּ֥א צֹֽעֲרָה

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

matches.label: The fate of Lot's wife
matches.note: Lot's wife perishes: Gen, because she looks back and becomes a pillar of salt (wattabbēṭ ʾištô mēʾaḥărāyw wattᵉhî nᵉṣîb melaḥ); Q, excepted in advance and struck with the townsmen (illā mraʾataka innahu muṣībuhā mā aṣābahum), with no salt pillar. Whether illā mraʾataka goes with 'travel with your family' or 'let none look back' is debated by exegetes.

passages.text: וַתַּבֵּ֥ט אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מֵאַחֲרָ֑יו וַתְּהִ֖י נְצִ֥יב מֶֽלַח

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

matches.label: What falls from heaven on Sodom
matches.note: God rains destruction, with the same verb (mṭr): wa-amṭarnā ʿalayhā ḥijāratan min sijjīlin manḍūdin musawwamatan ʿinda rabbika vs waYHWH himṭîr ʿal-sᵉdōm wᵉʿal-ʿămōrāh goprît wāʾēš. What falls changes: marked stones of baked clay in Q, sulphur and fire in Gen.

passages.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה הִמְטִ֧יר עַל סְדֹ֛ם וְעַל עֲמֹרָ֖ה גָּפְרִ֣ית וָאֵ֑שׁ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה מִן הַשָּׁמָֽיִם
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا جَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِّن سِجِّيلٍ مَّنضُودٍ
مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ وَمَا هِىَ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ

matches.label: Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city
matches.note: Lot is told to take his family out: fa-asri bi-ahlika vs qûm qaḥ ʾet-ʾištᵉkā wᵉʾet-šᵉtê bᵉnōtêkā ... pen-tissāpeh baʿăwōn hāʿîr. Gen adds the sons-in-law who think he is joking (wayᵉhî kimṣaḥēq bᵉʿênê ḥătānāyw).

passages.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֶל ל֗וֹט עֹ֚ד מִֽי לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה חָתָן֙ וּבָנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֖ בָּעִ֑יר הוֹצֵ֖א מִן הַמָּקֽוֹם
וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר
וַֽיִּתְמַהְמָ֓הּ וַיַּחֲזִ֨קוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּיָד֣וֹ וּבְיַד אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּבְיַד֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתָ֔יו בְּחֶמְלַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיֹּצִאֻ֥הוּ וַיַּנִּחֻ֖הוּ מִח֥וּץ לָעִֽיר

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

matches.label: Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place
matches.note: wa-lā yaltafit minkum aḥadun vs ʾal-tabbîṭ ʾaḥărêkā wᵉʾal-taʿămōd bᵉkol-hakkikkār.

passages.text: וַיְהִי֩ כְהוֹצִיאָ֨ם אֹתָ֜ם הַח֗וּצָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הִמָּלֵ֣ט עַל נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ אַל תַּבִּ֣יט אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ וְאַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֖ד בְּכָל הַכִּכָּ֑ר הָהָ֥רָה הִמָּלֵ֖ט פֶּן תִּסָּפֶֽה

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

matches.label: Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed
matches.note: The town turned upside down: jaʿalnā ʿāliyahā sāfilahā vs wayyahăpōk ʾet-heʿārîm hāʾēl (hpk, 'overturn').

passages.text: וַֽיַּהֲפֹךְ֙ אֶת הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת כָּל הַכִּכָּ֑ר וְאֵת֙ כָּל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הֶעָרִ֔ים וְצֶ֖מַח הָאֲדָמָֽה
فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا جَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِّن سِجِّيلٍ مَّنضُودٍ

matches.label: How Lot receives the divine messengers
matches.note: Lot and the guests: Genesis has him rise, bow and press them to stay (wa-yyifṣar bām məʾōd), and he makes a feast with unleavened bread; the Quran has him distressed and helpless on their account, sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan, until they reassure him, lā takhaf wa-lā taḥzan innā munajjūka. Eager hospitality becomes dismay.

passages.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הַמַּלְאָכִ֤ים סְדֹ֨מָה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְל֖וֹט יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר סְדֹ֑ם וַיַּרְא לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קָם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣ם לְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין
וַיִּפְצַר בָּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ אֵלָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וּמַצּ֥וֹת אָפָ֖ה וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: The fate of Lot's wife

passages.text: וַתַּבֵּ֥ט אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מֵאַחֲרָ֑יו וַתְּהִ֖י נְצִ֥יב מֶֽלַח
قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطًا قَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا لَنُنَجِّيَنَّهُۥ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city
matches.note: innā muhlikū ahli hādhihi l-qaryati inna ahlahā kānū ẓālimīna ... innā munzilūna ʿalā ahli hādhihi l-qaryati rijzan mina s-samāʾi ~ kî mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet ham-māqôm haz-zeh ... wa-yšallə ḥēnû YHWH ləšaḥătāh: the messengers declare they are sent to destroy 'this place / this town'. In Genesis they say it to Lot; in the Quran first to Abraham, then to Lot.

passages.text: כִּֽי מַשְׁחִתִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ אֶת הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי גָֽדְלָ֤ה צַעֲקָתָם֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ

matches.label: Who strikes the Sodom mob's eyes
matches.note: The mob blinded at Lot's door. Genesis: ʾayyēh hā-ʾănāšîm ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēḏəʿāh ʾōṯām; the angels (hā-ʾănāšîm) strike them bas-sanwērîm and they weary themselves finding the door. The striking passes from the angel-guests to God himself, and the search for the door is dropped.

matches.note: Why Lot is saved. Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; and 21 more.

Only in Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat: God is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or something smaller; Fruits in paradise resemble those of earth: 'this is what we were given before'; A challenge to rivals to prove a divine claim [divergence between the texts]; In the hereafter the dead eat the like of what they ate on earth; God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; The people break the covenant God made with them; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); God stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain; Hell's fire has men and stones as its fuel; The blessed have purified spouses (azwaj mutahhara) in paradise; God summons the coastlands and nations (and their gods) to a court trial to argue their case; The creator made heaven and earth, light, air and food 'for their sake' (n-jb =sn), for humankind; and 4 more.

matches.label: How God made the human mate, and for what purpose
matches.note: Purpose of the mate: Gen ʿēzer kə-neḡdô (a help fit for him), and the woman built from the rib (ha-ṣṣēlāʿ) of the one man. Q khalaqa lakum min anfusikum azwājan li-taskunū ilayhā wa-jaʿala baynakum mawaddatan wa-raḥma. There is no rib, the mates come 'from yourselves' for all humans, and the purpose is rest (sakan) and love and mercy between them. Gen's ʿeṣem mē-ʿăṣāmay / dāḇaq bə-ʾištô is the closest point.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹא ט֛וֹב הֱי֥וֹת הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְבַדּ֑וֹ אֶֽעֱשֶׂהּ לּ֥וֹ עֵ֖זֶר כְּנֶגְדּֽוֹ
וַיִּבֶן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֧ים אֶֽת הַצֵּלָ֛ע אֲשֶׁר לָקַ֥ח מִן הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיְבִאֶ֖הָ אֶל הָֽאָדָֽם
וַיֹּאמֶר֮ הָֽאָדָם֒ זֹ֣את הַפַּ֗עַם עֶ֚צֶם מֵֽעֲצָמַ֔י וּבָשָׂ֖ר מִבְּשָׂרִ֑י לְזֹאת֙ יִקָּרֵ֣א אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּ֥י מֵאִ֖ישׁ לֻֽקֳחָה זֹּֽאת
وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًا لِّتَسْكُنُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

matches.note: Gen 2:21-23 wa-yyappēl ... tardēmâ ... wa-yyiqqaḥ ʾaḥat mi-ṣṣalʿōtāyw ... wa-yyiben ... ʾet ha-ṣṣēlāʿ ... lĕ-ʾiššâ ... kî mē-ʾîš luqŏḥâ zōʾt: God puts the man to sleep and builds the woman from his rib; she is named 'woman' because taken from 'man'; Q 4:1 khalaqakum min nafsin wāḥidatin wa-khalaqa minhā zawjahā wa-baththa minhumā rijālan kathīran wa-nisāʾan: created from one soul, and from it its mate. Woman from the first human is kept; sleep, rib and the wordplay are left out, the first human is a gender-neutral 'soul' (nafs, grammatically feminine), and the address is to all people (yā ayyuhā n-nās).

matches.note: The mate made out of the first human: khalaqakum min nafsin wāḥidatin wa-jaʿala minhā zawjahā li-yaskuna ilayhā vs wayyiqqaḥ ʾaḥat miṣṣalʿōtāyw ... wayyiben ... ʾet-haṣṣēlāʿ ... lᵉʾiššāh. evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Abraham's treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba: Patriarch plants a tamarisk and calls on El Olam, the Everlasting God; Seven ewe lambs given as witness to a well-ownership oath (Beersheba); Dispute over a well resolved by an oath-treaty with a local king; In a named generation people begin to call on the name of the LORD.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; Whether the deity eats (receives) the food and drink of the offerings [divergence between the texts]; The deity shows or assigns to the builder the site (old foundation) of the deity's house; and 15 more.

matches.label: Abraham settles some of his offspring in a barren valley by God's sacred House
matches.note: Expulsion becomes settlement. Gen: Sarah demands gārēš hāʾāmâ hazzōʾt wəʾet-bənāh kî lōʾ yîraš; Abraham, grieved, sends Hagar off with bread and a skin of water, and she wanders bəmidbar bəʾēr šābaʿ, then Paran. Q: Abraham himself says innī askantu min dhurriyyatī bi-wādin ghayri dhī zarʿin ʿinda baytika l-muḥarram li-yuqīmū ṣ-ṣalāh. Sarah's motive and the inheritance quarrel are gone, and a sanctuary is added.

matches.label: Abraham thanks God for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age
matches.note: Gen: the son of old age is Isaac alone (bēn lizqunāyw ... ben-məʾat šānâ), and Ishmael is set apart, kî bəyiṣḥāq yiqqārēʾ ləkā zāraʿ / gam ʾet-ben-hāʾāmâ ləgôy ʾăśîmennû. Q: Abraham thanks God for both as one gift of old age, wahaba lī ʿalā l-kibari Ismāʿīla wa-Isḥāq, Ishmael first.

matches.label: In labor the mother wishes she had died before this and been utterly forgotten
matches.note: Same sequence. A lone mother in a remote place despairs over death (ʾal-ʾerʾeh bəmôt hayyāled ... wattēbk / yā laytanī mittu qabla hādhā). A voice calls to her and says do not fear or grieve (wayyiqrāʾ malʾak ʾĕlōhîm ʾel-hāgār ... ʾal-tîrʾî / fa-nādāhā min taḥtihā allā taḥzanī). God provides water (wattēreʾ bəʾēr māyim / jaʿala rabbuki taḥtaki sariyyā). Changes: the voice comes 'from heaven' in Gen and 'from beneath her' in Q; Hagar fears for a living child, Maryam is in labor; Q adds the palm's dates.

matches.label: God tests the patriarch's obedience
matches.note: Placement of the 'test'. Gen opens with it, wə-hā-ʾĕlōhîm nissâ ʾeṯ-ʾaḇrāhām, so the reader knows from the start that it is a trial. Q names it only after the rescue: inna hādhā la-huwa l-balāʾu l-mubīn. Gen's closing reason, kî ʿattâ yāḏaʿtî kî-yərēʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾattâ (now I know, 22:12), has no counterpart: in Q God does not come to know.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְהָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים נִסָּ֖ה אֶת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי
إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ

matches.label: God commands a father to sacrifice his son
matches.note: How the command comes. Gen: direct divine speech, qaḥ-nāʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā ... wə-lek-ləḵā ʾel-ʾereṣ ha-mmōriyyâ wə-haʿălēhû šām lə-ʿōlâ (a burnt offering at a named place). Q: a dream reported by the father, innī arā fī l-manāmi annī adhbaḥuka (I see in sleep that I slaughter you), with no place, no mountain and no ʿōlâ. Q's dhabaḥa is cognate with Hebrew zāḇaḥ, while Gen uses ʿōlâ and liš-ḥōṭ (22:10).

matches.label: Who the son to be sacrificed is and how he is named
matches.note: Who the son is. Gen names him three times over: ʾeṯ-binḵā ʾeṯ-yəḥîḏəḵā ʾăšer-ʾāhaḇtā ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq. Q has only bi-ghulāmin ḥalīm (a forbearing boy) and announces Isaac only after the episode, wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn (37:112). This leaves the victim unnamed, and many exegetes read him as Ishmael. The 'only' (yāḥîḏ) son of Gen is not said.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח נָ֠א אֶת בִּנְךָ֨ אֶת יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר אָהַ֨בְתָּ֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ לְךָ֔ אֶל אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ
فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ
وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

matches.label: What the son to be sacrificed knows and says
matches.note: Who speaks, and what the son knows. Gen: Isaac does not know. He asks hinnēh hā-ʾēš wə-hā-ʿēṣîm wə-ʾayyēh ha-śśeh lə-ʿōlâ, and Abraham gives the veiled answer ʾĕlōhîm yirʾeh-lô ha-śśeh ... bənî. Q: the father tells him openly and asks his view, fa-nẓur mādhā tarā, and the son consents, yā-abati fʿal mā tuʾmaru sa-tajidunī in shāʾa llāhu mina ṣ-ṣābirīn. The address pair ʾāḇî / bənî matches yā-abati / yā-bunayya. Isaac's silence becomes the son's active submission.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִצְחָ֜ק אֶל אַבְרָהָ֤ם אָבִיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֔י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֶּ֣נִּֽי בְנִ֑י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְהָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאַיֵּ֥ה הַשֶּׂ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֱלֹהִ֞ים יִרְאֶה לּ֥וֹ הַשֶּׂ֛ה לְעֹלָ֖ה בְּנִ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: The father lays the son down for the sacrifice
matches.note: The act. Gen: wood laid on Isaac, fire and knife, an altar built, wa-yyaʿăqōḏ ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq bənô wa-yyāśem ʾōṯô ʿal-ha-mmizbēaḥ mi-mmaʿal lā-ʿēṣîm, knife raised. Q: fa-lammā aslamā wa-tallahu li-l-jabīn, both 'submitted' and he laid him on his brow. No binding (ʿăqēḏâ), no altar, no wood, no fire and no three-day journey. The decisive word is the dual aslamā (both of them submitted).

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת עֲצֵ֣י הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיָּ֨שֶׂם֙ עַל יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת הָאֵ֖שׁ וְאֶת הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו

וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶֽל הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ וַיִּ֨בֶן שָׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת הָעֵצִ֑ים וַֽיַּעֲקֹד֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֹתוֹ֙ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ מִמַּ֖עַל לָעֵצִֽים
וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת יָד֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת לִשְׁחֹ֖ט אֶת בְּנֽוֹ
فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ

matches.label: Who stops the sacrifice of the son, and why
matches.note: Who stops it, and why. Gen: wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlâw malʾaḵ YHWH min-ha-ššāmayim ... ʾaḇrāhām ʾaḇrāhām wa-yyōʾmer hinnēnî; ʾal-tišlaḥ yāḏəḵā ʾel-ha-nnaʿar, because Abraham fears God. Q: wa-nādaynāhu an yā-Ibrāhīmu qad ṣaddaqta r-ruʾyā. God calls in the first person plural, with no angel and no hinnēnî. The reason is that Abraham has already fulfilled the dream, not a prohibition.

passages.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ מִן הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל תִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר וְאַל תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָּה כִּ֣י עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי יְרֵ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אַ֔תָּה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֛כְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת יְחִידְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽנִּי
وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

matches.label: What is offered in place of the son, and who provides it
matches.note: The substitute. Gen: Abraham looks up, sees ʾayil ʾaḥar neʾĕḥaz ba-ssəḇaḵ bə-qarnâw, and offers it ʿōlâ taḥaṯ bənô; he then names the place YHWH yirʾeh. Q: wa-fadaynāhu bi-dhibḥin ʿaẓīm. God himself ransoms (fadā) with a 'great sacrifice', the animal is unnamed, Abraham does not find it, and there is no place-name or temple-mount aetiology.

passages.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּה אַ֔יִל אַחַ֕ר נֶאֱחַ֥ז בַּסְּבַ֖ךְ בְּקַרְנָ֑יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אַבְרָהָם֙ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת הָאַ֔יִל וַיַּעֲלֵ֥הוּ לְעֹלָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַבְרָהָ֛ם שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יְהוָ֣ה יִרְאֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵאָמֵ֣ר הַיּ֔וֹם בְּהַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרָאֶֽה
وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ

matches.label: The reward and blessing after the averted sacrifice
matches.note: The reward. Gen: bî nišbaʿtî nəʾum-YHWH ... bārēḵ ʾăḇāreḵḵā wə-harbâ ʾarbeh ʾeṯ-zarʿăḵā ... wə-yiraš zarʿăḵā ʾēṯ šaʿar ʾōyəḇâw wə-hiṯbārăḵû ḇə-zarʿăḵā kōl gôyê hā-ʾāreṣ, an oath and the unconditional blessing of the seed. Q: salāmun ʿalā Ibrāhīm ... wa-bāraknā ʿalayhi wa-ʿalā Isḥāqa wa-min dhurriyyatihimā muḥsinun wa-ẓālimun li-nafsihi mubīn. There is no oath and no conquest of enemy gates, and the offspring are explicitly mixed, some doing good and some wronging themselves.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֗י יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֖כְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת יְחִידֶֽךָ
כִּֽי בָרֵ֣ךְ אֲבָרֶכְךָ֗ וְהַרְבָּ֨ה אַרְבֶּ֤ה אֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכַח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל שְׂפַ֣ת הַיָּ֑ם וְיִרַ֣שׁ זַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שַׁ֥עַר אֹיְבָֽיו
וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ בְּקֹלִֽי
وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌ

وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ

leads.title: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah for Isaac ↔ Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: On entering houses greet one another with a blessed greeting from God (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Abraham's servant finds Rebekah for Isaac: God sends his angel ahead to guide the journey; The bride is asked and consents to go ('I will go'); Son brings bride into his dead mother's tent and is comforted; Patriarch goes out to meditate (or pray) in the field at evening; Hero asks God for a specific sign to identify the right person (who will offer water); Departing bride blessed to become thousands of myriads; Father insists his son's wife come from his own kin, not the local women; Bride covers herself with a veil on seeing the groom; Oath sworn by placing the hand under the thigh of the one demanding it; Descendants will possess the gate of their enemies; A trusted servant is sent abroad to find a bride for the master's son; Believing women are to draw their outer cloaks (jalabib) over themselves so they are recognized and not harmed; and 5 more.

Only in Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger: Do not address the messenger as you address one another, nor slip away without his leave; Elderly women past hope of marriage may lay aside their outer garments without displaying adornment; No blame on the blind, lame, sick or anyone eating in the houses of listed relatives or friends, together or apart; Slaves and children must ask permission at three times of undress: before dawn prayer, at noon and after the night prayer; Whether the blind and the lame may enter the house or share its table [contrast between the texts]; You may eat your fill in a neighbor's vineyard or pluck ears by hand, but not carry away or use a sickle; Creditor must wait outside for the pledge and return a poor man's cloak by sunset; Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בּ֖וֹא בְּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה לָ֤מָּה תַעֲמֹד֙ בַּח֔וּץ וְאָנֹכִי֙ פִּנִּ֣יתִי הַבַּ֔יִת וּמָק֖וֹם לַגְּמַלִּֽים

لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَن تَأْكُلُوا۟ مِنۢ بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ ءَابَآئِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ إِخْوَٰنِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخَوَٰتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَعْمَٰمِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ عَمَّٰتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخْوَٰلِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ خَٰلَٰتِكُمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُم مَّفَاتِحَهُۥٓ أَوْ صَدِيقِكُمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَأْكُلُوا۟ جَمِيعًا أَوْ أَشْتَاتًا فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُم بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ تَحِيَّةً مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُبَٰرَكَةً طَيِّبَةً كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

matches.note: Gen 3:1, 3:13 ha-nnāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... ha-nnāḥāš hiššîʾanî: a cunning serpent deceives the woman, who eats first and gives to the man (3:6); Q 2:36 fa-azallahumā sh-shayṭānu ʿanhā: Satan makes both slip (dual). No serpent, no woman eating first, no woman as channel of the sin.

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: First humans expelled from the garden
matches.note: Gen 3:23-24 wa-yšallĕḥēhû YHWH ʾĕlōhîm ... wa-ygāreš ʾet hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and a flaming sword guarding the tree of life: God drives the man out; Q 2:36 fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīhi: Satan is the subject who 'brought them out', then God's ihbiṭū 'go down' (2:36, 2:38), addressed to a plural. No cherubim, no tree of life.

passages.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם
וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן עֵ֜דֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

matches.label: Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden
matches.note: Gen 3:15 wĕ-ʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā û-bên hā-ʾiššâ û-bên zarʿăkā û-bên zarʿāh: enmity between serpent and woman and their offspring; Q 2:36 ihbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun: 'some of you enemies to others' among those sent down. The same decree of enmity (ʾêbâ / ʿaduww) at the expulsion, with the serpent gone.

passages.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: The human condition on earth after the expulsion
matches.note: Gen 3:17-19 ʾărûrâ hā-ʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā bĕ-ʿiṣṣābôn tōʾkălennâ ... ʿad šûbĕkā ʾel hā-ʾădāmâ: cursed ground, toil and death; Q 2:36 wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīn: on earth an abode and provision for a time. The curses on ground, woman and serpent are left out; the earth is a lodging and a time limit, not a curse.

passages.text: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ מִן הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ
בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance)
matches.note: The ending changes. Gen 3:12 hā-ʾiššâ ʾăšer nātattâ ʿimmādî hîʾ nātĕnâ-llî min hā-ʿēṣ wā-ʾōkēl: the man blames the woman (and God who gave her), with no repentance or pardon; Q 2:37 fa-talaqqā ādamu min rabbihi kalimātin fa-tāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa t-tawwābu r-raḥīm: Adam receives words and God turns to him in forgiveness before the descent. The Quran adds a reconciliation Genesis does not have.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה לִּ֥י מִן הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל
فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

matches.label: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden
matches.note: Q 2:35 wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi sh-shajarata 'do not come near this tree' is God's own wording; in Genesis the extension is the woman's addition: Gen 3:3 lōʾ tōʾkĕlû mimmennû wĕ-lōʾ tiggĕʿû bô 'nor touch it', which God had not said (2:17).

passages.text: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן תְּמֻתֽוּן

וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן

leads.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion ↔ Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent
leads.summary: 5 correspondences read side by side: 5 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Fig leaves sewn into coverings (weight 7.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck (weight 7.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 7.1); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.8); Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (weight 6.6); A tree whose fruit gives eternal life (weight 6.2). Pair score 79.4.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; Ground cursed; man must eat by sweat of his brow among thorns and thistles [divergence between the texts]; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts]; The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; A human is given an instruction about what not to eat and either holds fast to it or forgets it [divergence between the texts]; After the episode of the forbidden or refused food; Before the offer of a food that gives (or is said to give) eternal life [divergence between the texts]; and 1 more.

matches.label: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit
matches.note: Who tempts whom. Gen: wəhannāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... wayyōʾmer ʾel-hāʾiššâ, a clever beast addressing the woman. Q: fa-waswasa ilayhi sh-shayṭānu qāla yā Ādamu, Satan, already marked as enemy after refusing to bow (inna hādhā ʿaduwwun laka wa-li-zawjik), addressing Adam. The serpent and the woman as first addressee drop out.

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן
وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

matches.label: The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'
matches.note: What the tree offers. Gen: knowledge, wihyîtem kēʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôb wārāʿ; immortality belongs to a second tree that God guards, pen-yišlaḥ yādô wəlāqaḥ gam mēʿēṣ haḥayyîm wəʾākal wāḥay ləʿōlām. Q: the tempter names the forbidden tree itself shajarati l-khuldi wa-mulkin lā yablā. Gen's two trees merge into one, and the lure becomes eternal life and kingship, not godlike knowledge.

passages.text: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה פֶּן יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם
فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

matches.label: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked
matches.note: wattōʾkal wattittēn gam-ləʾîšāh ... wayyōʾkal wattippāqaḥnâ ʿênê šənêhem wayyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wayyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnâ; fa-akalā minhā fa-badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janna. Same sequence: eating, exposed nakedness, sewing leaves. Changes: in Gen the woman eats first and hands it on, while Q has both eat and puts the blame on Adam (wa-ʿaṣā Ādamu rabbahu fa-ghawā); fig leaves become just 'leaves of the garden'.

passages.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל
וַתִּפָּקַ֨חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת
فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ

matches.label: Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness
matches.note: Gen goes from the eating straight to curses, ʾărûrâ hāʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā ... kî-ʿāpār ʾattâ wəʾel-ʿāpār tāšûb, with no repentance and no forgiveness. Q puts election and forgiveness before the descent, thumma jtabāhu rabbuhu fa-tāba ʿalayhi wa-hadā. Adam's sin is forgiven, not cursed, and no death sentence follows.

passages.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֶֽל הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒ אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכָּל הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה עַל גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ

וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ מִן הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ
בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ

matches.label: Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck
matches.note: wəʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā ûbên hāʾiššâ ûbên zarʿăkā ûbên zarʿāh ... wayəšalləḥēhû ... waygāreš ʾet-hāʾādām; qāla hbiṭā minhā jamīʿan baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww. Enmity and expulsion. Gen's enmity is between serpent and woman and their seed, and the way back is barred by cherubim. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; In the divine realm the human is given a garment to put on [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 10 more.

leads.finding: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit

units.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion
The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall

matches.label: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit
matches.note: A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). There is no serpent and no curse to crawl on the belly (Gen 3:14).

passages.text: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן
כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

matches.label: The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals
matches.note: What the tempter promises. Gen: wi-hyîtem kē-ʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôv wā-rāʿ, and God himself confirms the danger: hēn hā-ʾādām hāyāh kə-ʾaḥad mimmennû ... wā-ḥay lə-ʿōlām. Q: mā nahākumā rabbukumā ʿan hādhihi l-shajarati illā an takūnā malakayni aw takūnā mina l-khālidīna. 'Like gods knowing good and evil' becomes 'angels or immortals', a lie (bi-ghurūrin). Q has no divine admission that the humans have become 'like one of us'.

passages.text: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה פֶּן יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

matches.label: Which of the first couple is tempted and eats first
matches.note: Who is tempted and eats first. Gen: the serpent talks to the woman (wa-yyōʾmer ʾel-hā-ʾiššāh), she eats first and gives to her husband (wat-tittēn gam-lə-ʾîšāh ʿimmāh wa-yyōʾkhal). Q uses the dual throughout: wa-zawjuka ... fa-kulā ... wa-lā taqrabā ... waswasa lahumā ... fa-lammā dhāqā l-shajarata. The couple acts together and the woman is not singled out.

passages.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל הַנָּחָ֑שׁ מִפְּרִ֥י עֵֽץ הַגָּ֖ן נֹאכֵֽל
וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל
وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?'
matches.note: God's question. Gen: the couple hide (wa-yyitḥabbēʾ hā-ʾādām wə-ʾištô), God walks in the garden and calls ʾayyekkāh, then ha-min-hā-ʿēṣ ... ʾākhāltā. Q: wa-nādāhumā rabbuhumā a-lam anhakumā ʿan tilkumā l-shajarati wa-aqul lakumā inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduwwun mubīnun. No hiding and no walking God; the question is a reminder of a warning given.

passages.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן
וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing
matches.note: The decisive reversal. Gen: hā-ʾiššāh ʾăšer nātattāh ʿimmādî hiwʾ nātənāh-llî; han-nāḥāš hiššîʾanî, the man blames the woman (and God), the woman the serpent. Q: qālā rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā wa-in lam taghfir lanā wa-tarḥamnā la-nakūnanna mina l-khāsirīna. Both confess together and ask forgiveness. Blame-shifting gives way to joint repentance, and the blame-shifter in Q is Iblis (fa-bi-mā aghwaytanī, 7:16).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה לִּ֥י מִן הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל
قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

matches.label: Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck
matches.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). There are no curses on the woman (childbirth, 3:16) or the ground (3:17-19).

passages.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Humans return to the earth they were taken from (and, in the Quran, are brought out of it again)
matches.note: Gen: ʿad šûvəkhā ʾel-hā-ʾădāmāh kî mimmennāh luqqāḥtā kî-ʿāfār ʾattāh wə-ʾel-ʿāfār tāšûv, from dust and back to dust, as a curse. Q: fīhā taḥyawna wa-fīhā tamūtūna wa-minhā tukhrajūna. Q adds the third step, resurrection from the earth.

passages.text: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב
قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ

matches.label: First humans expelled from the garden
matches.note: Gen: wa-yšalləḥēhû ... wa-ygāreš ʾet-hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and the flaming sword guarding the tree of life, lest he eat and live forever. Q: ihbiṭū ... wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīnin. A descent to a temporary home, with no guard, no tree of life and no fear of human immortality.

passages.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם
וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן עֵ֜דֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Fig leaves sewn into coverings
matches.note: Gen: wat-tippāqaḥnāh ʿênê šənêhem wa-yyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wa-yyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnāh. Q: badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-jannati. Both sew leaves, but in Q they are 'leaves of the garden' (no fig), and Q says the nakedness 'appeared' rather than 'their eyes were opened'.

passages.text: וַתִּפָּקַ֨חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

matches.label: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden
matches.note: Gen 3:3, the woman's paraphrase: wə-lōʾ tiggəʿû bô, 'nor touch it', a fence God had not said. Q, God's own command: wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi l-shajarata, 'do not come near'. The tree is unnamed in Q (no 'knowledge of good and evil').

passages.text: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן תְּמֻתֽוּן

leads.title: Jacob's flight from Laban and the theft of the teraphim ↔ Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Search proceeds through the others' bags before the youngest's (weight 6.8); Brothers pursued and accused of theft (weight 6.8). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Jacob's flight from Laban and the theft of the teraphim: In a dream an angel shows the hero the striped and speckled he-goats mounting the flock; God commands the exile to return to the land of his fathers; Idols hidden in a camel saddle on which a woman sits, claiming menstruation; Pursuer warned by God in a dream not to harm the fugitive; Hero unknowingly pronounces death on whoever stole the object, though it is his loved one; Hero flees secretly with wives, children and flocks while the father-in-law is away shearing; Shepherd made to bear the loss of animals torn by beasts; Shepherd's speech of grievance: twenty years of heat, frost, sleeplessness and bearing losses; Daughter steals her father's household idols (teraphim); Employer changed the hero's wages ten times, but God thwarted him; Daughters complain their father sold them and consumed their bride-price; A standing stone (matsevah) set up and anointed with oil; and 2 more.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 145 more.

וַיָּ֖מָת הֲדָ֑ד וַיִּהְיוּ֙ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֔וֹם אַלּ֥וּף תִּמְנָ֛ע אַלּ֥וּף עליה עַֽלְוָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף יְתֵֽת
אַלּ֧וּף אָהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה אַלּ֥וּף אֵלָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף פִּינֹֽן
אַלּ֥וּף קְנַ֛ז אַלּ֥וּף תֵּימָ֖ן אַלּ֣וּף מִבְצָֽר

וַיָּ֖מָת בָּ֑לַע וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו יוֹבָ֥ב בֶּן זֶ֖רַח מִבָּצְרָֽה
וַיָּ֖מָת יוֹבָ֑ב וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו חֻשָׁ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ הַתֵּימָנִֽי

וַיָּ֖מָת יוֹבָ֑ב וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו חוּשָׁ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ הַתֵּימָנִֽי
וַיָּ֖מָת חוּשָׁ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ תַּחְתָּ֜יו הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן בְּדַ֗ד הַמַּכֶּ֤ה אֶת מִדְיָן֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב וְשֵׁ֥ם עִיר֖וֹ עיות עֲוִֽית

leads.summary: 13 correspondences read side by side: 11 deliberately changed, 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Father loves the hero more than his brothers [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero bought by an Egyptian official [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero sold for a small sum of silver [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Father himself sends the hero to his brothers [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero cast into a pit or well [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); One brother talks the others out of killing him [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero sold for a small sum of silver (weight 7.1); Brothers bring the hero's garment with false blood (weight 7.1); One brother talks the others out of killing him (weight 7.1); A passing caravan takes the hero from the pit (weight 7.1); Father loves the hero more than his brothers (weight 6.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 6.8); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death (weight 6.8); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero (weight 6.6); Hero cast into a pit or well (weight 6.4); Dream of sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to the hero (weight 6.4). Pair score 153.3.

Only in Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt: Brothers sit down to eat bread after casting their brother into the pit; Hero's story begins when he is seventeen; Young hero brings bad reports of his brothers to their father; An anonymous man finds the wandering hero in the field and directs him; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; Father gives the hero a special garment; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Called by name, the hero answers 'Here I am' (hineni).

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 126 more.

units.title: Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt
Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)

matches.label: Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind
matches.note: Reversal of the father's response. Gen: Joseph tells father and brothers (wayəsappēr ʾel-ʾābîw wəʾel-ʾeḥāyw), and the father rebukes him (wayyigʿar-bô ʾābîw: hăbôʾ nābôʾ ʾănî wəʾimməkā ...?). Q: Joseph tells only his father, who warns 'lā taqṣuṣ ruʾyāka ʿalā ikhwatika fa-yakīdū laka kaydā' and interprets the dream as election: yajtabīka rabbuka wa-yuʿallimuka min taʾwīli l-aḥādīth.

passages.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר אֶל אָבִיו֮ וְאֶל אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּגְעַר בּ֣וֹ אָבִ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֛ה הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלָ֑מְתָּ הֲב֣וֹא נָב֗וֹא אֲנִי֙ וְאִמְּךָ֣ וְאַחֶ֔יךָ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְךָ֖ אָֽרְצָה
וַיְקַנְאוּ ב֖וֹ אֶחָ֑יו וְאָבִ֖יו שָׁמַ֥ר אֶת הַדָּבָֽר
قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ

matches.label: Father loves the hero more than his brothers
matches.note: Gen: the narrator states it, wəyiśrāʾēl ʾāhab ʾet-yôsēp mikkol-bānāyw kî ben-zəqunîm, and gives the kətōnet passîm as its sign. Q: only the brothers say it, and of two sons: la-Yūsufu wa-akhūhu aḥabbu ilā abīnā minnā ... inna abānā la-fī ḍalālin mubīn. The coat as token of favoritism is dropped; the shirt (qamīṣ) returns only as evidence.

passages.text: וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָהַ֤ב אֶת יוֹסֵף֙ מִכָּל בָּנָ֔יו כִּֽי בֶן זְקֻנִ֥ים ה֖וּא ל֑וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה ל֖וֹ כְּתֹ֥נֶת פַּסִּֽים
וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶחָ֗יו כִּֽי אֹת֞וֹ אָהַ֤ב אֲבִיהֶם֙ מִכָּל אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּשְׂנְא֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ דַּבְּר֥וֹ לְשָׁלֹֽם
إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

matches.label: Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero
matches.note: Gen: ləkû wənahargēhû wənašlikēhû bəʾaḥad habbōrôt ... wənirʾeh mah-yyihyû ḥălōmōtāyw (to defeat the dreams). Q: uqtulū Yūsufa awi ṭraḥūhu arḍan yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum wa-takūnū min baʿdihi qawman ṣāliḥīn: the motive is the father's face, and the plotters plan to become righteous afterwards.

passages.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּבְטֶ֨רֶם֙ יִקְרַ֣ב אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּֽתְנַכְּל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ
וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת וְאָמַ֕רְנוּ חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ וְנִרְאֶ֕ה מַה יִּהְי֖וּ חֲלֹמֹתָֽיו
ٱقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ قَوْمًا صَٰلِحِينَ

matches.label: One brother talks the others out of killing him
matches.note: Gen names two brothers: Reuben (ʾal-tišpəkû-dām, hašlîkû ʾōtô ʾel-habbôr hazzeh, meaning to restore him) and Judah (mah-beṣaʿ ... ləkû wənimkərennû layyišməʿēʾlîm). Q leaves one speaker unnamed, qāʾilun minhum, and merges both: throw him into ghayābati l-jubb so that baʿḍu s-sayyāra will pick him up.

passages.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיַּצִּלֵ֖הוּ מִיָּדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א נַכֶּ֖נּוּ נָֽפֶשׁ

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֣ם רְאוּבֵן֮ אַל תִּשְׁפְּכוּ דָם֒ הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְיָ֖ד אַל תִּשְׁלְחוּ ב֑וֹ לְמַ֗עַן הַצִּ֤יל אֹתוֹ֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ אֶל אָבִֽיו
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל אֶחָ֑יו מַה בֶּ֗צַע כִּ֤י נַהֲרֹג֙ אֶת אָחִ֔ינוּ וְכִסִּ֖ינוּ אֶת דָּמֽוֹ
قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ

matches.label: Father himself sends the hero to his brothers
matches.note: Reversal of initiative. Gen: Israel himself sends Joseph, ləkâ wəʾešlāḥăkā ʾălêhem ... rəʾēh ʾet-šəlôm ʾaḥêkā. Q: the brothers ask (arsilhu maʿanā ghadan yartaʿ wa-yalʿab) and the father is reluctant: innī la-yaḥzununī an tadhhabū bihi.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ רֹעִ֣ים בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם לְכָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ הִנֵּֽנִי
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לֶךְ נָ֨א רְאֵ֜ה אֶת שְׁל֤וֹם אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ וְאֶת שְׁל֣וֹם הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֵ֖נִי דָּבָ֑ר וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֨הוּ֙ מֵעֵ֣מֶק חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א שְׁכֶֽמָה
قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَنَٰصِحُونَ
أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَٰفِلُونَ

matches.label: A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death
matches.note: Gen: the brothers invent the beast, wəʾāmarnû ḥayyâ rāʿâ ʾăkālātəhû, and Jacob draws the conclusion himself, ṭārōp ṭōrap yôsēp. Q: Jacob voices the fear first, akhāfu an yaʾkulahu dh-dhiʾbu, and the brothers take up his words: fa-akalahu dh-dhiʾb. The vague ḥayyâ rāʿâ becomes the wolf.

passages.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת וְאָמַ֕רְנוּ חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ וְנִרְאֶ֕ה מַה יִּהְי֖וּ חֲלֹמֹתָֽיו
וַיַּכִּירָ֤הּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת בְּנִ֔י חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף
قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَٰفِلُونَ
قَالُوا۟ لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَٰدِقِينَ

matches.label: Hero cast into a pit or well
matches.note: Gen: wəhabbôr rēq ʾên bô māyim, a dry pit. Q: a well with water, ghayābati l-jubb, where the caravan's water-drawer lowers his bucket (fa-adlā dalwah). Q also adds a revelation to Joseph in the pit, wa-awḥaynā ilayhi la-tunabbiʾannahum bi-amrihim hādhā; God is not mentioned in Gen 37.

passages.text: וַיִּ֨קָּחֻ֔הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֥כוּ אֹת֖וֹ הַבֹּ֑רָה וְהַבּ֣וֹר רֵ֔ק אֵ֥ין בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם
فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُۥ قَالَ يَٰبُشْرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَٰعَةً وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ

matches.label: Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort
matches.note: Reversal. Gen: Jacob recognizes the coat and believes, ṭārōp ṭōrap yôsēp, rends his clothes and refuses comfort, wayəmāʾēn ləhitnaḥēm ... ʾērēd ʾel-bənî ʾābēl šəʾōlâ. Q: Jacob sees through the lie, bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amran, and answers with fa-ṣabrun jamīlun wa-llāhu l-mustaʿān.

passages.text: וַיַּכִּירָ֤הּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת בְּנִ֔י חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף
וַיִּקְרַ֤ע יַעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם שַׂ֖ק בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל בְּנ֖וֹ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים
וַיָּקֻמוּ֩ כָל בָּנָ֨יו וְכָל בְּנֹתָ֜יו לְנַחֲמ֗וֹ וַיְמָאֵן֙ לְהִתְנַחֵ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּֽי אֵרֵ֧ד אֶל בְּנִ֛י אָבֵ֖ל שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ אֹת֖וֹ אָבִֽיו
وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ

matches.label: Hero sold for a small sum of silver
matches.note: Gen: the brothers sell him, wayyimkərû ʾet-yôsēp layyišməʿēʾlîm bəʿeśrîm kāsep. Q: a passing sayyāra finds him (yā bushrā hādhā ghulām), hides him as merchandise (asarrūhu biḍāʿa) and sells him bi-thamanin bakhsin darāhima maʿdūda. The brothers are not the sellers.

passages.text: וַיֵּשְׁבוּ֮ לֶֽאֱכָל לֶחֶם֒ וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְא֔וּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֹרְחַ֣ת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים בָּאָ֖ה מִגִּלְעָ֑ד וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֣ם נֹֽשְׂאִ֗ים נְכֹאת֙ וּצְרִ֣י וָלֹ֔ט הוֹלְכִ֖ים לְהוֹרִ֥יד מִצְרָֽיְמָה

וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת יוֹסֵף֙ מִן הַבּ֔וֹר וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה
وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُۥ قَالَ يَٰبُشْرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَٰعَةً وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ
وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍۭ بَخْسٍ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ وَكَانُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ

matches.label: Hero bought by an Egyptian official
matches.note: Gen names him, pôṭîpar sərîs parʿōh śar haṭṭabbāḥîm. Q leaves him unnamed, alladhī shtarāhu min Miṣr, later al-ʿAzīz (12:30), and has him plan adoption: ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladā.

passages.text: וְהַ֨מְּדָנִ֔ים מָכְר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל מִצְרָ֑יִם לְפֽוֹטִיפַר֙ סְרִ֣יס פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׂ֖ר הַטַּבָּחִֽים

وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لِٱمْرَأَتِهِۦٓ أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُۥ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

matches.label: Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream
matches.note: Gen: Jacob's rebuke, hăbôʾ nābôʾ ʾănî wəʾimməkā wəʾaḥêkā ləhištaḥăwōt ləkā ʾārṣâ, is never literally fulfilled for the parents; only the brothers bow (Gen 42:6; 50:18). Q: wa-rafaʿa abawayhi ʿalā l-ʿarshi wa-kharrū lahu sujjadā, hādhā taʾwīlu ruʾyāya min qabl: the dream is fulfilled to the letter, with father and mother.

passages.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר אֶל אָבִיו֮ וְאֶל אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּגְעַר בּ֣וֹ אָבִ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֛ה הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלָ֑מְתָּ הֲב֣וֹא נָב֗וֹא אֲנִי֙ וְאִמְּךָ֣ וְאַחֶ֔יךָ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְךָ֖ אָֽרְצָה

وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا۟ لَهُۥ سُجَّدًا وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُءْيَٰىَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّا وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِىٓ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْبَدْوِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِىٓ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

matches.label: Dream of sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to the hero
matches.note: aḥada ʿashara kawkaban wa-sh-shamsa wa-l-qamara raʾaytuhum lī sājidīn; haššemeš wəhayyārēaḥ wəʾaḥad ʿāśār kôkābîm mištaḥăwîm lî: same eleven stars, sun and moon bowing. Q omits the first dream of the sheaves (Gen 37:7).

passages.text: וַיַּחֲלֹ֥ם עוֹד֙ חֲל֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה חָלַ֤מְתִּֽי חֲלוֹם֙ ע֔וֹד וְהִנֵּ֧ה הַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵ֗חַ וְאַחַ֤ד עָשָׂר֙ כּֽוֹכָבִ֔ים מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֖ים לִֽי
إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَٰجِدِينَ

matches.label: Brothers bring the hero's garment with false blood
matches.note: wa-jāʾū ʿalā qamīṣihi bi-damin kadhib; wayyišḥăṭû śəʿîr ʿizzîm wayyiṭbəlû ʾet-hakkuttōnet baddām: the garment in false blood brought to the father.

passages.text: וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֶת כְּתֹ֣נֶת יוֹסֵ֑ף וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ שְׂעִ֣יר עִזִּ֔ים וַיִּטְבְּל֥וּ אֶת הַכֻּתֹּ֖נֶת בַּדָּֽם
וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת כְּתֹ֣נֶת הַפַּסִּ֗ים וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶל אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ זֹ֣את מָצָ֑אנוּ הַכֶּר נָ֗א הַכְּתֹ֧נֶת בִּנְךָ֛ הִ֖וא אִם לֹֽא
وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ

leads.title: Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt ↔ Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12)
leads.summary: 10 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A passing caravan takes the hero from the pit (weight 7.1); Hero sold for a small sum of silver (weight 7.1); Brothers bring the hero's garment with false blood (weight 7.1); One brother talks the others out of killing him (weight 7.1); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death (weight 6.8); Father loves the hero more than his brothers (weight 6.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 6.8); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero (weight 6.6); Dream of sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to the hero (weight 6.4); Hero cast into a pit or well (weight 6.4). Pair score 68.1.

Only in Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt: Brothers sit down to eat bread after casting their brother into the pit; Hero's story begins when he is seventeen; Young hero brings bad reports of his brothers to their father; An anonymous man finds the wandering hero in the field and directs him; Hero bought by an Egyptian official [divergence between the texts]; Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero [divergence between the texts]; Hero cast into a pit or well [divergence between the texts]; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort [divergence between the texts]; Father loves the hero more than his brothers [divergence between the texts]; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The wife confesses the hero's innocence; A witness proposes judging by where the shirt is torn; Women of the city gossip about the wife's passion; and 47 more.

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֣ם רְאוּבֵן֮ אַל תִּשְׁפְּכוּ דָם֒ הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְיָ֖ד אַל תִּשְׁלְחוּ ב֑וֹ לְמַ֗עַן הַצִּ֤יל אֹתוֹ֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ אֶל אָבִֽיו

leads.title: Judah and Tamar ↔ Divorce before consummation; the prophet's marriages; the curtain and the cloaks
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: What a woman's veil or cloak signals to men who see her [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Judah and Tamar: Man spills his seed on the ground to avoid raising offspring for his dead brother and is struck dead; God kills a man for unspecified wickedness; A kid of the goats promised as a harlot's hire; Seal, cord and staff left as a pledge, later used as proof of paternity; Midwife ties a scarlet thread on the hand of the twin who emerges first; Man acknowledges the wronged woman: 'She is more righteous than I'; Twins contend at birth over who emerges first; A widow veils herself, sits by the road and is taken for a harlot by her father-in-law; Father-in-law withholds his youngest son from the widow, fearing he too will die; A woman accused of harlotry is sentenced to be burned; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; Sheep-shearing as an occasion for travel and festivity; and 2 more.

Only in Divorce before consummation; the prophet's marriages; the curtain and the cloaks: A wife divorced before consummation owes no waiting period ('idda); give her a gift and release her gracefully; Enter the prophet's houses only when invited to a meal and leave after; ask his wives from behind a curtain (hijab); Special marriage rules for the prophet: lawful wives, captives, named cousins who emigrated, and a woman who gives herself; afterwards no more wives; God and his angels bless (yusalluna 'ala) the prophet; believers are told to bless him and greet him with peace; How a husband sends away a divorced wife (document, gift, waiting period) [divergence between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [contrast between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [divergence between the texts]; Believing women are to draw their outer cloaks (jalabib) over themselves so they are recognized and not harmed; The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; King must not multiply horses, wives or silver and gold, nor return the people to Egypt.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 6.6); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.6); God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.6); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 6.4); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 6.1); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 5.5). Pair score 38.0.

Only in Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison: The jailer puts all the prisoners in the hero's charge; God blesses a foreigner's house for the sake of the righteous slave; The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault [divergence between the texts]; Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode [divergence between the texts]; Hero thrown into prison [divergence between the texts]; Hero nearly yields but a sign from God stops him [divergence between the texts]; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero; Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode; Hero bought by an Egyptian official; Hero thrown into prison.

Only in Tale of Two Brothers (Papyrus d'Orbiney 1,1-6,3): the household, the seduction and the false accusation: The woman makes herself look beaten (with fat and bandages), lies feigning sickness, does not pour water on her husband's hands or light the lamp, to support her accusation; In her false accusation the woman quotes her own proposal word for word as the hero's, and her own (fictive) refusal citing kinship; The false accuser tells her husband she will kill herself if he lets the accused live; The cattle speak to their herdsman and tell him where the pasture is good, and he understands them; Under the hero's care the master's cattle thrive exceedingly and multiply their calves; The hero runs away from his own brother, who pursues him to kill him; Refusing, the hero tells the woman she is like a mother to him and her husband like a father, and calls her proposal a great crime; The hero promises to tell no one of the woman's proposal and orders her never to speak of it again; The deceived husband (elder brother) sharpens his spear and waits behind the stable door to kill the hero on his return; The temptress promises the young man fine clothes as reward for lying with her; As each cow enters the stable it speaks to its herdsman, warning him that a man stands behind the door to kill him: 'flee!'; A tale opens with two brothers 'of one mother and one father', the elder a householder, the younger his helper; and 5 more.

leads.title: Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison ↔ Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)
leads.summary: 8 correspondences read side by side: 4 deliberately changed, 4 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero nearly yields but a sign from God stops him [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero thrown into prison [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode (weight 7.1); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 6.8); Hero thrown into prison (weight 6.8); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 6.6); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.6); God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.6); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 6.4); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 6.1); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 5.5). Pair score 89.7.

Only in Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison: The jailer puts all the prisoners in the hero's charge; God blesses a foreigner's house for the sake of the righteous slave; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 134 more.
