matches.label: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood
matches.note: In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna).

passages.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ

matches.label: Why God destroyed a generation or a people
matches.note: Cause of the flood: Gen 6:13 kî mālʾâ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās, the earth filled with violence, and God's own decision (hinnî mašḥîtām); Q 23:26-27: they are drowned for rejecting the messenger (bimā kadhdhabūni ... alladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), and Noah asks for it (rabbi nṣurnī).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى بِمَا كَذَّبُونِ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: When and from where the flood waters come
matches.note: Signal and source: Genesis gives a time (lə-yāmîm ʿôd šivʿâ ʾānōkhî mamṭîr) and waters from the burst springs of the deep and the windows of heaven (nivqəʿû kol maʿyənôt təhôm rabbâ wa-ʾărubbōt haš-šāmayim niftāḥû); the Quran gives a sign, 'when our command comes and the oven boils' (wa-fāra t-tannūr). cf. b. Sanh. 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the HB.

passages.text: כִּי֩ לְיָמִ֨ים ע֜וֹד שִׁבְעָ֗ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מַמְטִ֣יר עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה וּמָחִ֗יתִי אֶֽת כָּל הַיְקוּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה

בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why
matches.note: Genesis saves the whole household, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê vānāyw; the Quran excepts some: wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu minhum (the drowned son of 11:42-43), and forbids Noah to plead for the wrongdoers (wa-lā tukhāṭibnī fī lladhīna ẓalamū).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest
matches.note: End of the voyage: Genesis has the ark resting on the mountains of Ararat, an altar and burnt offerings whose odor God smells, then his promise never again to curse the ground (wa-yyiven Nōaḥ mizbēaḥ ... wa-yyāraḥ YHWH ʾet rêaḥ han-nîḥōaḥ ... lōʾ ʾōsif). The Quran has no altar, sacrifice or promise: Noah says al-ḥamdu lillāhi lladhī najjānā and prays rabbi anzilnī munzalan mubārakan, and the landing place is not named.

passages.text: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט
וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת כָּל חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי
فَإِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتَ أَنتَ وَمَن مَّعَكَ عَلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ فَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِى مُنزَلًا مُّبَارَكًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ

matches.label: Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction
matches.note: an iṣnaʿi l-fulka bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā ~ ʿăśē ləkā tēvat ʿăṣê gōfer: God commands the vessel. Genesis gives the wood, pitch and dimensions (6:14-16), the Quran only says it is built 'under our eyes and our revelation'; the ark is fulk, not tēvâ.

passages.text: עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ תֵּבַ֣ת עֲצֵי גֹ֔פֶר קִנִּ֖ים תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֶת הַתֵּבָ֑ה וְכָֽפַרְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֛הּ מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ בַּכֹּֽפֶר
וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: Animals taken aboard in pairs

لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِى ضَلَٰلَةٌ وَلَٰكِنِّى رَسُولٌ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّى وَأَنصَحُ لَكُمْ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

matches.label: Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger
matches.note: Why the flood comes. Gen: wat-timmālēʾ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô, universal violence and corruption. Q: fa-kadhdhabūhu fa-anjaynāhu ... wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā, the rejection of the messenger. The moral cause becomes a cause about revelation, and the drowned are 'a blind people' (qawman ʿamīna).

passages.text: וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס
וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֣ה נִשְׁחָ֑תָה כִּֽי הִשְׁחִ֧ית כָּל בָּשָׂ֛ר אֶת דַּרְכּ֖וֹ עַל הָאָֽרֶץ
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا عَمِينَ

matches.label: Hero's family saved with him
matches.note: Who is saved. Gen: bōʾ-ʾattāh wə-khol-bêtəkhā ʾel-hat-tēvāh; Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê-vānāyw, his household. Q: fa-anjaynāhu wa-lladhīna maʿahu fī l-fulki, 'those with him', a community of believers rather than a family (cf. Q 11:46, where a son drowns).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا عَمِينَ

leads.title: The Flood (full read) ↔ Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood
leads.summary: 6 correspondences read side by side: 6 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Seek forgiveness and repent, and God will send the sky down on you in abundant rain [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Destruction motivated by human wickedness or violence [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.5); All others perish (weight 5.9); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8). Pair score 56.1.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

Only in Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood: Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a fire; The people put their fingers in their ears and wrap their garments over their heads to avoid hearing the prophet; Noah's people refuse to abandon their gods Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; The flood hero prays for forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever enters his house believing, and all believers; God caused humans to grow from the earth like a plant, returns them to it and will bring them out again; Prophet summons his people night and day, openly and in secret, yet they only flee further; People are put into the earth and brought out of it again [divergence between the texts]; Destroying a people together with their offspring because of their character [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Human comes from dust and returns to dust [divergence between the texts]; Before the flood the hero tells his city that heaven will rain plenty on them [divergence between the texts]; A wish that no one be left alive by the destruction [divergence between the texts]; God created seven heavens in layers (sab' samawat tibaqan) or built seven strong (heavens) above humans; and 12 more.
The Flood (full read): tagged by Claude (model), reading the Hebrew.
Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

leads.finding: Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood

units.title: The Flood (full read)
Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood

matches.label: Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood
matches.note: Added role: in Genesis God speaks only to Noah (wa-yyōʾmer ʾĕlōhîm le-Nōaḥ qēṣ kol bāśār bāʾ le-fānay) and Noah never speaks to anyone; he only obeys (wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ ke-kōl ʾăšer ṣiwwāh ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm). In Q 71 Noah is a messenger and warner: yā-qawmi innī lakum nadhīrun mubīn, uʿbudū llāha wa-ttaqūhu wa-aṭīʿūn, preaching laylan wa-nahāran, jihāran, iʿlānan wa-isrāran. cf. 2 Pet 2:5, b. Sanh. 108 (Noah as preacher), not a match.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה
قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا

matches.label: Destruction motivated by human wickedness or violence
matches.note: Motive changed: Genesis gives moral corruption and violence (rabbāh rāʿat hā-ʾādām ... wa-ttimmālēʾ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās; hišḥît kol bāśār ʾet darkô). Q 71 gives rejection of the messenger and idolatry: rabbi innahum ʿaṣawnī ... wa-qālū lā tadharunna ālihatakum wa-lā tadharunna waddan wa-lā suwāʿan wa-lā yaghūtha wa-yaʿūqa wa-nasrā. Five named gods; Genesis names no god but YHWH/Elohim.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י רַבָּ֛ה רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְכָל יֵ֨צֶר֙ מַחְשְׁבֹ֣ת לִבּ֔וֹ רַ֥ק רַ֖ע כָּל הַיּֽוֹם
וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס
וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֣ה נִשְׁחָ֑תָה כִּֽי הִשְׁחִ֧ית כָּל בָּשָׂ֛ר אֶת דַּרְכּ֖וֹ עַל הָאָֽרֶץ
قَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًا

matches.label: Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents
matches.note: Who calls for destruction is reversed: in Genesis God decides alone (wa-yyōʾmer YHWH ʾemḥeh ʾet hā-ʾādām; we-hinnî mašḥîtām ʾet hā-ʾāreṣ) and even regrets creating (wa-yyinnāḥem YHWH). In Q 71:26-27 Noah asks: rabbi lā tadhar ʿalā l-arḍi mina l-kāfirīna dayyāran, innaka in tadharhum yuḍillū ʿibādaka. There is no divine regret in the Quran.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה אֶמְחֶ֨ה אֶת הָאָדָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר בָּרָ֨אתִי֙ מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה מֵֽאָדָם֙ עַד בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַד רֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַד ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֥י נִחַ֖מְתִּי כִּ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽם
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا

matches.label: Seek forgiveness and repent, and God will send the sky down on you in abundant rain
matches.note: Rain reversed: in Genesis rain from opened sky is the destruction (wa-ʾărubbōt ha-ššāmayim niftāḥû, wa-yehî ha-ggešem ʿal hā-ʾāreṣ ʾarbāʿîm yôm). Noah in Q 71:10-11 promises rain as blessing if they repent: istaghfirū rabbakum ... yursili s-samāʾa ʿalaykum midrāran, then (71:25) mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū: the sky that could have blessed them drowns them.

passages.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ
וַֽיְהִ֥י הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה
فَقُلْتُ ٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا

matches.label: Hero's family saved with him
matches.note: The saved are defined by faith, not by house: Gen 7:1 bōʾ ʾattāh we-kol bêtkā ʾel ha-ttēvāh kî ʾōtkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq. Q 71:28 rabbi ghfir lī wa-li-wālidayya wa-li-man dakhala baytiya muʾminan wa-li-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muʾmināt: whoever enters my house as a believer.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל
رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا

matches.label: Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction
matches.note: Ending changed: Genesis ends with Noah's sacrifice and God's promise lōʾ ʾōsîf leqallēl ʿôd ʾet hā-ʾădāmāh ... we-lōʾ ʾōsîf ʿôd lehakkôt ʾet kol ḥay. Q 71 ends with the drowned sent on into fire (ughriqū fa-udkhilū nāran) and Noah's prayer of forgiveness and of destruction (wa-lā tazidi ẓ-ẓālimīna illā tabārā). No sacrifice, no covenant, no 'never again'.

passages.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת כָּל חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי
مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًا
رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا

matches.label: All others perish

passages.text: וַיִּגְוַ֞ע כָּל בָּשָׂ֣ר הָרֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל הָאָ֗רֶץ בָּע֤וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבַ֣חַיָּ֔ה וּבְכָל הַשֶּׁ֖רֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵ֣ץ עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל הָאָדָֽם
כֹּ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁמַת ר֨וּחַ חַיִּ֜ים בְּאַפָּ֗יו מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֶּחָֽרָבָ֖ה מֵֽתוּ

matches.label: Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring
matches.note: Divine offspring. Gen: wa-yyirʾû ḇənê-hā-ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-bənôṯ hā-ʾāḏām ... yāḇōʾû bənê hā-ʾĕlōhîm ʾel-bənôṯ hā-ʾāḏām wə-yāləḏû lāhem. 'Sons of God' exist and beget with human women. Any begetting by God, or kinship (nasab) between God and the jinn, is denied as a lie. The Quran's target is Arab 'daughters of God', but the language of divine filiation is the point of contact.

matches.label: Noah's span of 950 years, and what it measures
matches.note: The same number with a different meaning: Genesis gives the whole lifespan, wa-yyihyû kol yəmê Nōaḥ təšaʿ mēʾôt šānâ wa-ḥămiššîm šānâ wa-yyāmōt (350 of them after the flood); the Quran gives the time Noah spent preaching among his people before the flood, fa-labitha fīhim alfa sanatin illā khamsīna ʿāman fa-akhadhahumu ṭ-ṭūfān. The Quran also writes 'a thousand less fifty' instead of 'nine hundred and fifty'.

matches.label: How the story of Noah ends
matches.note: The end of Noah's story. Gen goes from the flood straight to wa-yyāḥel nōaḥ ʾîš hā-ʾăḏāmâ wa-yyiṭṭaʿ kārem wa-yyēšt min-ha-yyayin wa-yyiškār wa-yyiṯgal, then Noah's curse ʾārûr kənāʿan. The Quran closes with a blessing: wa-taraknā ʿalayhi fī l-ākhirīna salāmun ʿalā Nūḥin fī l-ʿālamīn ... innahu min ʿibādinā l-muʾminīn. It leaves out the drunkenness, the nakedness and the curse, and preserves only praise for later generations.

matches.label: The sign the flood leaves for later generations
matches.note: What the flood leaves as a sign: Genesis has God's bow in the cloud, lə-ʾôt bərît, a covenant sign that the waters will never again destroy (wə-lōʾ yihyeh ʿôd ham-mayim lə-mabbûl); in the Quran the drowned people themselves are the sign, wa-jaʿalnāhum li-n-nāsi āyatan (āya ~ ʾôt), a warning that it can happen again to those who deny.

matches.label: The same religion (din) was enjoined on Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and the Prophet: establish it and do not divide
matches.note: A divine charge given to Noah before Abraham and Moses: Gen 9 gives Noah and his sons commands (ʾaḵ bāśār bə-nap̄šô dāmô lōʾ ṯōʾḵēlû; šōp̄ēḵ dam hā-ʾāḏām); Q 42:13 shaʿara lakum mina d-dīni mā waṣṣā bihi nūḥan ... wa-mā waṣṣaynā bihi ibrāhīma wa-mūsā wa-ʿīsā an aqīmū d-dīna wa-lā tatafarraqū fīh. In Genesis the charge to Noah is a separate, universal law under Israel's later law; in the Quran it is the same religion as that of all later prophets. cf. the rabbinic seven Noahide laws (b. Sanh 56a).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: After Zayd ends his marriage, God marries his former wife to the prophet so believers may marry the ex-wives of adopted sons (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Hosea marries Gomer; the children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi: God will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu; The prophet's children receive symbolic names announcing judgment or salvation (Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi); God commands the prophet to marry a 'woman of harlotry' as a sign of the land's unfaithfulness; 'Not my people' becomes 'my people' and 'Not pitied' becomes 'pitied'; In the latter days Israel will return and seek YHWH and David their king; Israel called sons of God; Descendants promised to be as countless as the dust, stars or sand.

Only in Zayd's wife, the seal of the prophets, and the prophet as a lamp: The greeting of the righteous in the hereafter is 'Peace' (salam); Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God and his angels bless (yusalluna 'ala) the prophet; believers are told to bless him and greet him with peace; A ruler or prophet marries the wife of a man under him [contrast between the texts]; Whether a man may marry his son's (or adopted son's) wife [divergence between the texts]; Muhammad is not the father of any of your men but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin); The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner; Glorify God in the evening, morning, afternoon and noon (set times of praise or prayer); The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; God brings believers out of darknesses into light; false gods lead others from light into darkness.

leads.title: The unfaithful wife and the new betrothal ↔ Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The faithless wife credits her lovers (the Baals) with her bread, water, wool, flax, oil and drink, not knowing God gave them (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The unfaithful wife and the new betrothal: God will allure his people into the wilderness and speak to her heart, as in the days of youth; Chain of responses: God answers the heavens, the heavens the earth, the earth grain-wine-oil, and they answer Jezreel; God betroths his people to himself forever in righteousness, justice, steadfast love, mercy and faithfulness; God will end the land's festivals, new moons and sabbaths; God hedges her way with thorns and a wall so she cannot find her lovers' paths; She will call God 'my husband (ishi)' and no longer 'my baal'; the names of the Baals removed from her mouth; The straying wife resolves 'I will go back to my first husband, for it was better then'; The unfaithful wife is threatened with being stripped naked as on the day she was born; The Valley of Achor ('trouble') becomes a door of hope; God's people portrayed as an adulterous wife who runs after lovers (the Baals); 'Not my people' becomes 'my people' and 'Not pitied' becomes 'pitied'; God makes a covenant of peace, banishing evil beasts so the flock can dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.

Only in Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend: Satan commands people to alter God's creation; Idolaters invoke only female beings besides God, and only a rebellious Satan; Salvation is not by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book: whoever does evil is requited; Cursed Satan vows to take an appointed share (naṣīb mafrūḍ) of God's servants; Satan commands people to slit the ears of cattle (a pagan dedication rite); A rebel against the high god vows, in a string of first-person 'I will' clauses, to take and to command [divergence between the texts]; Whoever does good, male or female, and believes, enters paradise; Abraham is called God's friend (ohev, 'lover'); God does not forgive associating partners with him (shirk) but forgives anything less; Not wronged by a date-stone's thread (fatīl) or groove (naqīr): proverbial minimal measures; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater; Offerings, incense and libations to the 'Queen of Heaven'.

leads.title: Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city ↔ Quraysh, small kindnesses and al-Kawthar
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God says he is sated with sacrifices and hates festivals and new moons offered by those whose hands are full of blood (weight 7.1); The deniers do not honor the orphan, push him away, and do not urge the feeding of the poor (weight 6.8). Pair score 13.9.

Only in Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city: City or people given a new name in the future age (e.g. 'City of Righteousness', 'Hephzibah'); The faithful city has become a harlot; silver turned to dross, wine diluted with water; Worshippers shamed by the sacred oaks (elim) and gardens they chose; Daughter Zion left alone like a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field, a besieged city; Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores; Sky and earth 'listen to their Lord' (adhinat) and are made to obey at the end; Israel likened to a donkey that knows, or does not understand, what it has [divergence between the texts]; Prophet addresses his own rulers and people as 'Sodom' and 'Gomorrah'; In Lot's town only one house of submitters (muslimin) was found, and the believers were brought out; Book or oracle opens with a heading naming the prophet, his father and the kings in whose days he saw the vision; God's people as sons he reared who rebelled against him; Though sins be like scarlet they shall be white as snow; though red as crimson, like wool; and 11 more.

Only in Quraysh, small kindnesses and al-Kawthar: The one who hates the prophet is the one cut off (al-abtar, without posterity); Woe to those who pray but are heedless of their prayer, make a show, and withhold small kindnesses (al-ma'un); God has given the prophet al-Kawthar (abundance; in tradition a river or pool in paradise); 'pray and sacrifice'; Quraysh's security pact (ilaf) and caravan journeys of winter and summer; they should worship the Lord of this House who fed and secured them.

وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ بَلْ مَكْرُ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذْ تَأْمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكْفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجْعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادًا وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلْأَغْلَٰلَ فِىٓ أَعْنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ

leads.title: Song of the strong city; your dead shall live ↔ The earthquake: the earth tells its news
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day the earth will tell its news, because its Lord inspired it (weight 7.3); At the end the earth is stretched out, casts out what is in it (its burdens) and empties itself (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.4.

Only in Song of the strong city; your dead shall live: Other lords ruled us; they are dead, they will not live; shades (rephaim) will not rise; their memory is wiped out; God's dew is a 'dew of lights' (tal orot) and the earth will give birth to the shades (rephaim); The earth will disclose the blood shed on it and no longer cover its slain; 'Go, my people, enter your chambers and shut the doors behind you; hide a little moment until the wrath passes'; We were pregnant, we writhed, but gave birth only to wind; we brought no salvation to the earth; God keeps the steadfast mind in perfect peace (shalom shalom) because it trusts in him; 'My soul yearns for you in the night; my spirit within me seeks you at dawn'; 'We have a strong city... Open the gates that the righteous nation that keeps faith may enter'; In Yah YHWH is an everlasting rock (tsur olamim); What the dead say when they wake from the dust [divergence between the texts]; The Gardens of Eden have their gates opened for the righteous; God lets the people discover the sleepers so they know his promise of resurrection is true; and 6 more.

Only in The earthquake: the earth tells its news: Whoever does an atom's weight (mithqal dharra) of good will see it, and an atom's weight of evil will see it; Whether the wrongs a man did on earth are counted against him at the judgment [contrast between the texts]; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people.

leads.title: Leviathan slain; the vineyard of delight; the great shofar ↔ Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day a great shofar will be blown and the lost in Assyria and outcasts in Egypt will come and worship on the holy mountain (weight 7.7); The trumpet (ṣūr) is blown and the dead are gathered (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.8.

Only in Leviathan slain; the vineyard of delight; the great shofar: Jacob's guilt is atoned by making all altar stones like crushed chalk, no Asherim or incense-stands standing; Jacob will take root, Israel blossom and bud and fill the face of the world with fruit; God threshes from the Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt and the Israelites are gathered one by one; Song of the pleasant vineyard that YHWH guards, waters every moment and keeps night and day; he has no wrath, but would burn its briars; A horn blown on the last day, and whom it gathers [divergence between the texts]; Israel is a vine brought out of Egypt and planted, whose hedges God has broken down; Leviathan, the great sea monster, named; YHWH with his hard, great, strong sword will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and slay the dragon (tannin) in the sea; Hammanim (incense altars or sun pillars) removed from the cities; God will gather the exiles even from the end of heaven and restore them; Sea, deep or sea monster subdued or defeated by God.

Only in Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales: Behind the dead is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised; The damned had taken the believers as a laughingstock; now the believers triumph; God tells the damned pleading to leave hell: 'Be driven away into it and do not speak to me'; At death the sinner begs 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do good'; it is refused; When the trumpet is blown there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask after one another; Seek refuge in God from the goadings of the devils and from their presence; The dead cannot come back to life on earth; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [divergence between the texts]; A span of many years is set against a single day [divergence between the texts]; At the judgment after death a whole lifetime is reckoned as an hour or a day; The dead cannot go back to the life they left [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

leads.title: Woe to the rebellious children going down to Egypt; returning and rest; the Teacher; Topheth prepared ↔ Sad: the chiefs marvel at one God; the confederates of old
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The chiefs marvel 'Has he made the gods one God?' and urge each other to stay patient with their gods (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Woe to the rebellious children going down to Egypt; returning and rest; the Teacher; Topheth prepared: Oracle on the beasts of the Negev: a land of lioness, viper and flying seraph through which envoys carry treasure on donkeys and camels; Egypt's help is vain and empty; God calls her 'Rahab who sits still' (rahav hem shavet); In the future God gives abundant rain, rich bread, broad pastures and fodder; streams flow on every high hill; 'We will flee on horses' - therefore you shall flee; a thousand flee at the threat of one until left like a flagpole on a hill; YHWH waits to be gracious; blessed are all who wait for him; he answers at the sound of your cry; Your Teacher will no longer hide; your eyes will see him and your ears hear a word behind you: 'This is the way, walk in it'; Silver-plated idols and gold-covered images thrown away like a menstrual cloth: 'Get out!'; The moon's light will be like the sun's and the sun's light sevenfold, like the light of seven days; The Name of YHWH comes from afar, burning with anger, lips full of wrath, tongue like devouring fire, breath like an overflowing torrent; Your song will be as on the night when a festival is hallowed, with gladness like one going with the flute to the mountain of YHWH; People tell the seers 'do not see', and the visionaries 'speak smooth things to us, prophesy illusions'; 'In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength' - but you would not; and 9 more.

Only in Sad: the chiefs marvel at one God; the confederates of old: Opponents say 'We did not hear of this in the latest religion (al-milla al-akhira); it is a fabrication'; Pharaoh 'possessor of the stakes' (dhu al-awtad); Opponents ask whether the prophet has forged a lie against God or is possessed (bihi jinna); Destroyed generations cried out when it was no longer a time for escape (lata hina manas); Scoffers ask 'Lord, hasten to us our share (qittana) before the Day of Reckoning'; If they own heaven and earth, let them ascend by the cords or ways (asbab) to heaven; Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Shuʿayb is sent to the People of the Thicket (aṣḥāb al-ayka); No host from heaven was needed: a single Shout (sayha) and they were extinguished; List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

leads.title: Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God ↔ Life like a crop, the abode of peace, darkened faces
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Parable: worldly life is like vegetation fed by rain, adorned, then cut down overnight as if it never flourished (weight 7.3); All flesh is grass and its loyalty like the flower of the field; grass withers but the word of God stands forever (weight 7.1). Pair score 14.4.

Only in Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God: 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins; God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing; God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering; A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God'; Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales?; God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; A herald of good news (mevasseret Tsiyyon) goes up on a high mountain to announce 'Behold your God!'; Satire on the making of idols: craftsman casts, goldsmith overlays, the poor choose wood that will not rot so the idol will not totter; and 17 more.

Only in Life like a crop, the abode of peace, darkened faces: The doers of good get the best reward 'and more' (ziyada); Paradise as the abode of peace (dār al-salām); The faces of evildoers are covered as with pieces of dark night; The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land; Humans are like grass that flourishes in the morning and withers by evening; At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped'.

Isaiah: kol hab-bāśār ḥāṣîr wə-ḵol ḥasdô kə-ṣîṣ haś-śāḏeh; yāḇēš ḥāṣîr nāḇēl ṣîṣ û-ḏəḇar ʾĕlōhênû yāqûm lə-ʿôlām (against the grass stands God's word). Only in Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God: 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins; God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom; God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing; God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering; A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God'; Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales?; God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; A herald of good news (mevasseret Tsiyyon) goes up on a high mountain to announce 'Behold your God!'; Satire on the making of idols: craftsman casts, goldsmith overlays, the poor choose wood that will not rot so the idol will not totter; and 18 more.

Only in The clot: recite! and the forelock: Let the opponent call his council (nadi); God will call the guards of hell (al-zabaniya); A man who forbids a servant of God to pray is threatened: he will be dragged by his lying, sinful forelock; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; A man in plenty neglects his god and calls on him only when affliction comes; Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Human created in stages: a drop of sperm (nutfa), a clinging clot ('alaq/'alaqa), then shaped and proportioned.

leads.title: Bel and Nebo carried off; God who carries Israel ↔ The hanif creed and patience

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Bel and Nebo carried off; God who carries Israel: Babylon's gods Bel and Nebo bow and stoop, their images loaded as burdens on weary beasts; God summons a bird of prey from the east, the man of his counsel (the conqueror Cyrus); God alone announces the end from the beginning and proves his deity by predictions fulfilled; Idols must be carried by their worshipers, whereas God has carried his people from the womb to old age; Satirical description of an idol being made by craftsmen from gold, silver, metal or wood, then carried and set up; Cult images are carried off by raiders or a migrating group; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped'; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in The hanif creed and patience: Set your face toward religion as a hanif (pure monotheist); Whoever is guided is guided for his own good; whoever strays strays against himself; The idol cannot speak to its worshipers or guide them; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal; there is no god beside me.

leads.title: Your sins have separated you; God arms himself ↔ The slave and the free, the mute man, the woman who unravels her yarn (Surah 16:71-100)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not be like the woman who unravels her yarn into strands after spinning it strong (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Your sins have separated you; God arms himself: God's covenant: his spirit and the words in the mouth will not depart from the mouth of the offspring forever; God puts on righteousness as a breastplate, the helmet of salvation, garments of vengeance and zeal as a cloak; Their feet run to evil and hasten to shed innocent blood; The people growl like bears and moan like doves as they wait for justice; The people's hands are defiled with blood and their fingers with iniquity; The wicked hatch vipers' eggs: whoever eats them dies, and a crushed one hatches a viper; A redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression; Not God's weakness but the people's sins separate them from God and hide his face; Truth stumbles in the public square and uprightness cannot enter; whoever turns from evil is plundered; God sees that there is no man and no intercessor, so his own arm brings salvation; The trust of the godless is a spider's house that will not stand; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?'; and 2 more.

Only in The slave and the free, the mute man, the woman who unravels her yarn (Surah 16:71-100): God brought you from your mothers' wombs knowing nothing and gave you hearing, sight and hearts; The coming of the Hour is like the blink of an eye, or nearer; God commands justice, kindness and giving to kin, and forbids indecency, wrong and oppression; Masters will not share their provision equally with their slaves (argument against partners to God); Parable: a mute, helpless man who is a burden to his master compared with one who commands justice; Parable: a slave owning nothing compared with a free man who spends secretly and openly; Before reciting scripture, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan; God made spouses for you from yourselves and from them sons and grandsons; God gave tents of hides light for travel, wool for furnishings, shade, mountain shelters and garments against heat and violence; What you have runs out; what is with God remains; Fulfill God's covenant and do not break oaths after confirming them or use them for deceit; Whoever does good, male or female, and believes, enters paradise; and 6 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.8.

Only in The throne vision and the call of Isaiah: A seraph touches the prophet's lips with a burning coal from the altar, removing his guilt; Six-winged seraphim stand above God: two wings cover the face, two the feet, two for flying; Even the tenth that remains will be burned, like a felled terebinth or oak whose stump is the holy seed; At the heavenly voice the doorposts shake and the house fills with smoke; Prophet sees the Lord seated on a high and lifted-up throne, his train filling the temple; Heavenly beings call 'Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory'; Prophet cries 'Woe is me, I am undone, a man of unclean lips' for having seen the King; The angels say: each of us has a known station; we are ranged in ranks; we glorify; God has not given the people a heart to know, eyes to see, ears to hear until today [divergence between the texts]; God is 'Lord of the mighty Throne' (rabb al-'arsh al-'azim); The prophet's word and a people deaf and blind to it [divergence between the texts]; A revealed surah increases believers in faith and the sick-hearted in filth; and 10 more.

matches.note: Same triad in the same order: Isa 6:10 hašmēn lēb hā-ʿām ... wĕ-ʾoznāyw hakbēd wĕ-ʿênāyw hāšaʿ (heart, ears, eyes); Q 2:7 khatama llāhu ʿalā qulūbihim wa-ʿalā samʿihim wa-ʿalā abṣārihim ghishāwatun (hearts, hearing, eyes). leads.title: New heavens and a new earth ↔ The day eyes stare and the earth is changed (Surah 14:42-52)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: On the last day the earth is changed into another earth, and the heavens too (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in New heavens and a new earth: Before they call God will answer; while they are still speaking he will hear; People will build houses and live in them, plant vineyards and eat their fruit, and not labor for others; In the new age no infant dies in days and one who dies at a hundred is counted a youth; God creates Jerusalem a joy; the sound of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her; God creates new heavens and a new earth; the former things will not be remembered; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; Paradise is the abode of permanence where no toil or weariness touches the blessed and grief is removed; Serpent cursed to crawl on its belly and eat dust; Wolf dwells with lamb, leopard with kid, lion eats straw like the ox, and a little child leads them.

Only in The day eyes stare and the earth is changed (Surah 14:42-52): The wrongdoers beg for a short respite to answer the call and follow the messengers; They lived in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves and saw what God did to them; On that day eyes stare fixed, heads upraised, hearts empty as air; God is not heedless; he only delays the wrongdoers to a day when eyes stare; God is swift in reckoning; The opponents' scheme was such that mountains might be moved by it; The damned wear garments of pitch (qatiran), fire covering their faces; The god is not idle (heedless) toward what the wicked do; Wrongdoers take the deity's delay to mean he does nothing; he defers, then seizes; Pitch, bitumen or naphtha as the bodily covering (ointment, garment) of the cursed or damned, with a foul drink [divergence between the texts]; God has prepared chains, iron collars and fetters (ankal) for the unbelievers.

leads.title: Idols like scarecrows in a cucumber field ↔ The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it (weight 6.5); Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.5.

Only in Idols like scarecrows in a cucumber field: Do not learn the way of the nations or be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, at which the nations are dismayed; Idols are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field: they cannot speak and must be carried because they cannot walk; God addressed as 'King of the nations' whom all must fear; The hypocrites' bodies impress and their speech is heard, but they are like propped-up timbers, thinking every cry is against them; Satirical description of an idol being made by craftsmen from gold, silver, metal or wood, then carried and set up; YHWH is the true God, the living God and everlasting King at whose wrath the earth quakes; Idols are called vain nothings (havlei shav); Worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit you; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols: A couple vow thanks for a sound child, then ascribe partners to God in what he gave; Those you call on besides God are servants like yourselves; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Parents' words to God about the child he gave them [divergence between the texts]; Taunt: do the idols have feet to walk, hands to grasp, eyes to see, ears to hear?; Likeness between the idols and those who call on them [divergence between the texts]; How God made the human mate, and for what purpose; Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; Having eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, said of idols or of people; First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps; Humankind is created from a single soul, from which its mate was made to dwell with it.

leads.title: He made the earth by his power - the Portion of Jacob ↔ The Hour, the times of praise, and the signs of God
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God shows lightning to inspire fear and hope (of rain) (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in He made the earth by his power - the Portion of Jacob: God made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom and stretched out the heavens by his understanding; Not like these is the Portion of Jacob, for he is the former of all things; Every goldsmith is shamed by his image, for his casting is a lie and there is no breath (ruah) in them; God alone stretches out the heavens; God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain.

Only in The Hour, the times of praise, and the signs of God: Everything in the heavens and the earth is devoutly obedient (qanit) to God; God created mates for humans from their own selves so they may find rest in them, with love and mercy between them; The many languages of mankind and the deity's part in them [divergence between the texts]; The diversity of human languages and colors is one of God's signs; God made human tongues different in speech and their skins (colours) distinct; God did not wrong them; they wronged themselves (refrain); Go up on (travel through) the ruins of the ancients and look: what the sight teaches [divergence between the texts]; Why humans speak many languages [divergence between the texts]; Refrain 'among his signs (ayat) is...' listing natural phenomena as evidence of God; How God made the human mate, and for what purpose [divergence between the texts]; God brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living; Nations distinguished by land, language and clan; and 7 more.

leads.title: Cursed is the man who does not hear this covenant ↔ The broken vow of charity; seventy prayers in vain
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God forbids the prophet to pray or intercede for the people, for he will not hear (weight 6.5). Pair score 6.5.

Only in Cursed is the man who does not hear this covenant: 'Cursed is the man who does not hear the words of this covenant', answered with 'Amen'; God named his people 'a green olive tree, fair with goodly fruit', but sets fire to it and its branches are broken; Judah has as many gods as cities (and altars as Jerusalem's streets); Egypt called an iron furnace (smelting furnace); A name containing Baal replaced by boshet ('shame'); God sent his servants the prophets 'rising early and sending' (hashkem), but they did not listen; Formula 'I will take you as my people and I will be your God'; Promised land described as flowing with milk and honey.

Only in The broken vow of charity; seventy prayers in vain: Hypocrites mock believers who give voluntarily and those who can give only their effort; Men vow to give alms if God enriches them, then turn miserly, and God sets hypocrisy in their hearts; Better not to vow than to vow and not pay; The vow made to the deity is not kept, the deity takes note of the breach and the vower is punished; Hero vows that if God protects and provides for him, he will worship and tithe [divergence between the texts]; Whether the prophet should intercede for a sinful people [contrast between the texts]; Even if the prophet asks forgiveness for them seventy times God will not forgive them; God is near in their mouths but far from their kidneys (hearts); Pay vows without delay; not vowing is no sin; The petitioner promises a gift if the deity grants the request: 'if you do this, I will give you ...'.

leads.title: First confession - a gentle lamb led to slaughter; the men of Anathoth ↔ Salih, the evil omen and the nine plotters of Thamud
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The men of the prophet's hometown seek his life: 'Do not prophesy in YHWH's name or you will die by our hand' (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in First confession - a gentle lamb led to slaughter; the men of Anathoth: The prophet was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter, not knowing they plotted 'Let us destroy the tree with its fruit'; Unbelievers plot to confine, kill or expel the prophet, but God plots too; The persecuted prophet asks God to let him see vengeance on his enemies; Jeremiah's 'confessions': the prophet's personal laments and complaints to God about his mission and persecutors; God tests the hearts and the kidneys (inner self).

Only in Salih, the evil omen and the nine plotters of Thamud: The people say they augur ill (iṭṭayyarnā) of the prophet; he answers that their omen (ṭāʾir) is with God; Nine men of the city swear by God to attack the prophet and his family by night and deny it to his avenger; The prophet Ṣāliḥ is sent to the people of Thamūd; King calls the prophet 'troubler of Israel' (okher Yisra'el); prophet returns the charge; They plot a plot, and God plots a plot; give the deniers respite a little; Augury: a bird's flight or alighting is an omen bound to a person [divergence between the texts]; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: I set before you life and death, blessing and curse: choose life (weight 6.5). Pair score 6.5.

Only in Zedekiah's inquiry - the way of life and the way of death: The besieged king sends to ask the prophet to inquire of God, hoping God will do a wonder and make the enemy withdraw; God himself fights against his own people with outstretched hand and mighty arm, turning their weapons back; Whoever stays in the city will die, but whoever goes out and surrenders to the besiegers will live, his life as spoil; God redeems 'with an outstretched arm' and great judgments; The city is given into the hand of the king of Babylon who will burn it with fire; Judgment by the triad sword, famine and pestilence.

Only in The city: the two highways and the steep ascent: Giving food to the hungry (water, clothing, a ferry) as the deed that justifies before the judge; The companions of the right (ashab al-yamin, al-maymana) are saved; the companions of the left (al-mash'ama) are damned; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); The steep ascent ('aqaba) is freeing a neck (slave), feeding an orphan relative or a needy man in the dust on a day of hunger; Ground cursed; man must eat by sweat of his brow among thorns and thistles [divergence between the texts]; Oath by 'this city' (Mecca), the secure city (al-balad al-amin); Whether a bound captive is released or killed; The fast God chooses is to loose bonds of injustice, free the oppressed, share bread with the hungry and clothe the naked; Ground cursed; man must eat by sweat of his brow among thorns and thistles; The evil is shut in below under a closed cover; Oath introduced by the negated formula 'No! I swear by...' (la uqsimu / fa-la uqsimu); Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Opponents nearly lure the prophet into inventing something else; God makes him firm (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Concerning the prophets - who has stood in the council of YHWH?: The prophet's heart is broken and all his bones shake; he is like a drunken man because of God's holy words; The prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and strengthen evildoers; they have become like Sodom and Gomorrah; Whether a prophet has first-hand knowledge of the heavenly council [contrast between the texts]; Whether a prophet speaks from his own heart or desire, or by revelation [contrast between the texts]; The earth mourns and the heavens above grow dark because of God's decree; God gives his people poisoned water (mei rosh) to drink and wormwood to eat; 'Have you listened in the council (sod) of God, and limited wisdom to yourself?'; Prophets and priests heal the wound lightly, saying 'Peace, peace' when there is no peace; The tree of Zaqqum grows from the bottom of hell; its spathes are like the heads of devils; the damned fill their bellies and drink boiling water; God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart; The storm of YHWH's fury goes out and whirls on the head of the wicked; in the latter days you will understand it; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Jeremiah buys his cousin's field at Anathoth during the siege: Sons and daughters passed through fire to Molech at the high places in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom; Deeds are put in an earthenware jar so they may last many days; God's eyes are open on all the ways of humanity to repay each by his deeds; Incense offered to Baal and libations to other gods on the roofs of houses; A field bought for seventeen shekels of silver; The prophet buys a family field during siege as a sign that land will again be bought; The king will see the conquering king eye to eye and speak with him mouth to mouth; God will give his people one heart and one way to fear him always; Siege ramps are raised against the city; The prophet is confined in the court of the guard in the palace; Baruch son of Neriah, the prophet's scribe; God promises an everlasting covenant (berit olam) with his people; and 5 more.

Only in Healing of the city, the Righteous Branch and the covenant with day and night: God invites the prophet to call so he will reveal great and hidden things; God has a 'covenant with day and night' that fixes their order; David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of Israel; Flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them in the towns of Judah; God promises to bring healing and cure to the ruined city; The Levitical priests will never lack a man to offer sacrifice before God; People say God has rejected the two families he chose; The voice of the bridegroom and the bride will again be heard in the ruined land; Your Lord said 'Call on me and I will answer you'; 'O David, we made you a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; judge between people with truth and do not follow desire'; God will cause a righteous Branch (tsemah) to sprout for David; The name 'YHWH is our righteousness' (YHWH tsidqenu); and 6 more.

Only in Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship: The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness; A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride; God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk; Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?'; God made the flood ship (or its survivors) a sign for all the worlds; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The moon travels across the sky as a vessel floats or swims; The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr); The sun ends its daily course at a resting place (the bedchamber where it is told 'Rest!', or its mustaqarr) [divergence between the texts]; God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning; The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; The crescent moon fixes the months and the reckoning of time; and 5 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'O David, we made you a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; judge between people with truth and do not follow desire' (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Healing of the city, the Righteous Branch and the covenant with day and night: God invites the prophet to call so he will reveal great and hidden things; God has a 'covenant with day and night' that fixes their order; David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of Israel; Flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them in the towns of Judah; God promises to bring healing and cure to the ruined city; The Levitical priests will never lack a man to offer sacrifice before God; People say God has rejected the two families he chose; The voice of the bridegroom and the bride will again be heard in the ruined land; Your Lord said 'Call on me and I will answer you'; God will cause a righteous Branch (tsemah) to sprout for David; The name 'YHWH is our righteousness' (YHWH tsidqenu); God's covenant with Israel is as sure as the fixed order of sun, moon, stars and sea; and 6 more.

Only in David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes: Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him; A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument; A case about a ewe is brought to David for judgment [divergence between the texts]; A case is put to a judge as real, and his verdict on it turns on himself [divergence between the texts]; David realizes he was being tested, asks forgiveness, falls down bowing and turns in repentance; God strengthened David's kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive judgment (fasl al-khitab); David's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts]; A named 'day of reckoning' on which accounts are settled; A man with many sheep takes another's only ewe [divergence between the texts]; Shall God treat believers like those who spread corruption, the godfearing like the wicked?; The king confesses 'I have sinned' and the prophet announces forgiveness with a remaining penalty; Sheep are divided so that one party takes nine (ninety-nine) and the other one [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

leads.title: Zedekiah's fate and the revoked release of slaves; the calf cut in two ↔ Abraham and the four birds
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Covenant ritual: animals cut in halves and a divine presence passes between them (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Zedekiah's fate and the revoked release of slaves; the calf cut in two: Owners free their Hebrew slaves under covenant oath, then take them back; Funeral cry 'Hoy, lord!' (alas, master) for a dead king; Because they revoked the slaves' release, God 'proclaims a release' for them to sword, pestilence and famine; Lachish and Azekah are the last fortified cities of Judah holding out; The king will see the conquering king eye to eye and speak with him mouth to mouth; Burnings (of spices) made at a king's funeral as for his fathers; Hebrew slaves are released in the seventh year; Your corpse food for birds and beasts with no one to frighten them away; Proclaim release (deror) throughout the land to all its inhabitants; Judgment by the triad sword, famine and pestilence.

Only in Abraham and the four birds: Abraham, asking to see how God revives the dead, takes four birds, places parts on each hill, calls them and they come flying; Abraham takes and cuts animals at God's command [divergence between the texts]; Creatures cut in pieces, the parts set apart, are made whole and alive by a spoken word [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks.

leads.title: Baruch reads the scroll; Jehoiakim cuts it with a penknife and burns it; it is rewritten ↔ The Criterion sent down; charges of forgery and the prophet who eats in markets
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Who dictated and who wrote down a prophet's book [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Baruch reads the scroll; Jehoiakim cuts it with a penknife and burns it; it is rewritten: A destroyed sacred book is rewritten from dictation with many words added; The king cuts the prophetic scroll column by column with a scribe's knife and burns it in his brazier; The king's corpse will be cast out to heat by day and frost by night; The king will have no descendant sitting on David's throne; The king and his servants hear the words of judgment and do not tear their garments; Royal officials turn in fear to one another when the scroll is read to them; Sympathetic officials tell the prophet and his scribe to hide; Some officials beg the king not to burn the scroll; The prophet dictates God's words and a scribe writes them in a scroll; A prophetic scroll is read publicly in the temple on a fast day; Perhaps the people will turn from evil and God will relent of the disaster he planned; Baruch son of Neriah, the prophet's scribe.

Only in The Criterion sent down; charges of forgery and the prophet who eats in markets: Opponents object that the messenger eats food and walks in the markets, with no angel, treasure or garden; Opponents claim the prophet had old tales written down and dictated to him morning and evening, with others helping him; God gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (al-furqān), a light and reminder; Opponents say the believers follow only a bewitched man (rajul mashur); Whether old tradition handed down from the ancients carries authority [contrast between the texts]; Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him; Worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit you; The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

matches.note: Who dictates to whom: in Jeremiah the prophet dictates and the scribe writes, wa-yyiktōv Bārûkh mip-pî Yirmyāhû ... mip-pîw yiqrāʾ ʾēlay ... wa-ʾănî kōtēv ʿal has-sēfer bad-dəyô; in the opponents' charge the prophet has old tales written down and they are dictated to him (iktatabahā fa-hiya tumlā ʿalayhi bukratan wa-aṣīlan), with helpers (aʿānahu ʿalayhi qawmun ākharūn). The Quran rejects the charge: it was sent down by the one who knows the secret (25:6).

leads.title: Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety ↔ Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers (weight 7.7); Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians (weight 7.7); The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho (weight 7.7); The captive king's sons are slaughtered before his eyes, then his eyes are put out (weight 7.3); Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken (weight 7.3). Pair score 37.9.

Only in Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety: The conquering Babylonian officers, named with their titles (Rab-saris, Rab-mag), sit in the city's Middle Gate; The foreign conqueror orders his officers to look after the prophet and do him no harm; A foreigner who helped the prophet is promised his life will be spared because he trusted God; Whoever surrenders to the enemy will live; his life shall be his booty; Captive king taken with hooks and bound in bronze fetters to Babylon.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; Seven princes or counselors who 'see the king's face' advise the king; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; The temple treasures and gold vessels of Solomon are carried off to Babylon; A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes; and 2 more.

Only in Oracle against Babylon (I): Bel and Merodach shamed, the hammer of the earth broken: Israel a scattered sheep: first Assyria devoured it, last Babylon gnawed its bones; Babylon's gods Bel and Merodach are put to shame and its idols dismayed; God opens his armory and brings out the weapons of his indignation; Babylon called the 'hammer of the whole earth' is broken; Babylon is a land of idols, mad over their terrors; God's people are lost sheep whose shepherds led them astray on the mountains; Babylon addressed by wordplay names: Merathaim ('double rebellion') and Pekod ('punishment'); Repay the city according to her deeds: do to her as she has done; Israel's iniquity will be sought and not found, for God pardons the remnant; Repeated 'A sword upon...' litany against every class of a city; A day of vengeance belonging to YHWH of hosts against his foes; Babylon taken and destroyed; and 11 more.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts]; God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city; The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); The fate of Lot's wife; God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'; and 2 more.

leads.title: Oracle against Babylon (II): golden cup, destroying mountain, Sheshach, the scroll sunk in the Euphrates ↔ The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The effects of wine and of the cup: mockery, madness, or none [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.8); God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain (weight 6.2). Pair score 13.1.

Only in Oracle against Babylon (II): golden cup, destroying mountain, Sheshach, the scroll sunk in the Euphrates: The northern kingdoms Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz are summoned against Babylon; Names hidden by the atbash letter cipher (Sheshach for Babel, Leb-qamai for Kasdim); Though Babylon should climb to heaven and fortify its height, destroyers will reach it; Ironic call to bring balm for a fallen city that cannot be healed; God punishes Bel and makes him vomit out what he swallowed; The doomed imperial city 'dwells on many waters' rich in treasures; The empire as a 'destroying mountain' to be rolled down and made a burnt mountain; God stirs up a destroying wind (or spirit) against the empire; God prepares a feast for the empire's leaders, makes them drunk, and they sleep an eternal sleep; 'The Portion of Jacob' is not like idols, but the former of all things; God dries up Babylon's 'sea' and makes her fountain dry; Babylon is a golden cup in God's hand that made all the earth drunk; and 18 more.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof; 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes'; Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth?; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Messengers go up and down between realms by a stairway or ladder of heaven (simmiltu / sullam / maʿārij) [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; and 13 more.

leads.title: Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release ↔ David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians; The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho; The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah; The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken; and 6 more.

Only in David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff: God made a spring of molten copper (or brass) flow for Solomon; The jinn did not know the unseen, else they would not have stayed in humiliating labor; Solomon dies leaning on his staff; only a creature of the earth gnawing the staff reveals his death when he falls; A superhuman craftsman casts metal vessels and furniture for a lord [divergence between the texts]; David and the coat of mail [contrast between the texts]; A king covers a journey of many stages in a single day [divergence between the texts]; How Solomon died and how his death became known [divergence between the texts]; How Solomon's great bronze works were produced [divergence between the texts]; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail; Rivers clap their hands and mountains sing together before YHWH; Who did Solomon's building and craft work [divergence between the texts]; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; and 3 more.
