leads.title: Sanctify war against her - the siege ↔ The pattern of the destroyed towns
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Divine punishment falls on a town by night or while its people take the midday rest (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

Only in Sanctify war against her - the siege: As a well keeps its water fresh, so the city keeps its wickedness fresh; The attackers 'sanctify war' (qaddeshu milhamah) against the city and plan a noon or night assault; Besiegers cut down trees and pour out a siege ramp against the city; Blow the shofar, raise the signal: gather and flee into the fortified cities before the invader; A destroying nation comes from the north.

Only in The pattern of the destroyed towns: If the towns had believed God would have opened blessings from heaven and earth; God tries towns with hardship, then with ease, then seizes them suddenly; Most of the peoples were found without fidelity to their covenant; Refrain listing plagues (famine, drought, blight, locust, pestilence, war, overthrow): 'yet you did not return to me'; God's plotting (makr / kayd) outwits the schemers; none is safe from it but the losers; Heaven is shut and no rain falls because of the people's sin; repentance brings rain; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

leads.title: Obedience not sacrifice; the Topheth becomes the Valley of Slaughter ↔ Misers, those who called God poor, and the fire-consumed offering
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God sent his servants the prophets 'rising early and sending' (hashkem), but they did not listen (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

Only in Obedience not sacrifice; the Topheth becomes the Valley of Slaughter: The bones of kings, priests, prophets and people will be taken from their graves and spread before the sun, moon and host of heaven they loved; Jerusalem told to cut off her hair (nezer) and throw it away and raise a lament on the bare heights; The surviving remnant will choose death rather than life; God sarcastically tells the people to add their burnt offerings to their sacrifices and eat the meat; God says he did not command the fathers about burnt offerings and sacrifices when he brought them out of Egypt, but obedience; God says the burning of children in the Topheth was something he never commanded nor did it enter his mind; An idol (the carved Asherah) is placed in the temple where God put his name; The Topheth and Valley of Ben-hinnom will be renamed the Valley of Slaughter, where the dead are buried for lack of room; God will silence the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; People bow down to all the host of heaven; The people's corpses will be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts with no one to frighten them away; Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods; and 1 more.

Only in Misers, those who called God poor, and the fire-consumed offering: God took the covenant of those given the Book to make it clear to people and not conceal it; Those who said 'God is poor and we are rich' are recorded and will taste the burning; Misers will have what they hoarded hung round their necks as a collar on the Day of Resurrection; Some demand that a messenger bring an offering consumed by fire as his credential; God grants the unbelievers respite only that they may increase in sin; Whether God is in need and humans rich [contrast between the texts]; An offering consumed by fire as proof of the true God or messenger [response between the texts]; Fire from heaven falls and consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust and water; God will not leave believers as they are until he separates the bad from the good; Wrongdoers take the deity's delay for indifference; the delay is not a release; What man can live and not see death, or deliver his soul from the hand of Sheol?; A writer reproaches his addressee: the oath I made you swear before the gods you have thrown behind you; and 5 more.

leads.title: Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test ↔ The parable of the two gardens; this life as rain-fed plants; the book of deeds (Surah 18:32-49)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Humans are presented before God in rows, coming as they were first created (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test: The verb 'bless' (barekh) used as a scribal euphemism for cursing God; Grown sons hold feasts in turn, each on his day, and invite their sisters; A great wind from the desert strikes the four corners of the house and it falls on the feasting children; God has set a protective hedge around the righteous man, his house and goods; 'Fire of God' falls from heaven and consumes flocks and servants; Messenger after messenger arrives while the last is still speaking, each the sole survivor of a disaster; 'Does he fear God for nothing?': piety suspected of being motivated by reward; The exemplary righteous man is a non-Israelite living in the land of Uz in the east; Father offers burnt offerings in case his children 'blessed' (cursed) God in their hearts; Mourner shaves his head and falls to the ground; A patriarch's wealth is listed in precise numbers of sheep, camels, oxen and asses; So that you do not grieve over what escapes you nor exult over what he gives you; and 20 more.

Only in The parable of the two gardens; this life as rain-fed plants; the book of deeds (Surah 18:32-49): On the last day the earth is seen laid bare and all are gathered, none left out; The proud man's garden is destroyed and he wrings his hands over what he spent on it; The ruined man says 'Would that I had associated no one with my Lord'; The rich man boasts of having more wealth and a mightier following; On entering one's garden one should say 'What God wills; there is no power except in God'; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded; If god gives you a rich harvest, do not boast of it before your neighbours; Righteous deeds endure and go with a man beyond death, when other goods do not [divergence between the texts]; Parable of two men: one owns two rich gardens and boasts to his poorer believing companion; Wealth and sons are the adornment of this life; the enduring good deeds are better with God; The wicked fade like grass and green herbs; The rich man thinks his garden will never perish and the Hour will never come; and 3 more.

Job says it himself in his lament: wə-ʾîš šāḵaḇ wə-lōʾ yāqûm ʿaḏ bilttî šāmayim ... ʾim yāmûṯ geḇer hă-yiḥyeh (and wishes for a release, ḥălîp̄āṯî). A sufferer's question in Job becomes the scoffers' claim in the Quran.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God has put collars up to their chins so their heads are forced up, and a barrier before and behind them, covering them so they do not see (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Ya-Sin; the collars and the barrier; deeds recorded: God records what people sent ahead and their traces (athar), and counts everything in a clear register (imam mubin); Oath by the Quran itself ('By the wise Quran'); Who makes the hearers deaf, blind and closed of heart to the message [divergence between the texts]; Prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

Only in Eliphaz's third speech - Job accused of social crimes: The penitent righteous will decree a thing and it will be established for him; God is in the height of heaven above the stars; the wicked think thick clouds hide him as he walks the vault (chug) of heaven; Lay your gold in the dust and Ophir gold among the stones of the wadi; Shaddai will be your gold; God delivers even the not-innocent through the cleanness of the righteous one's hands; The old way trodden by wicked men, snatched away before their time, their foundation poured out as a river (flood generation); 'Receive instruction (torah) from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart'; The wicked say to God 'Depart from us; what is Shaddai that we should serve him?'; Accusation of oppressing the poor: taking pledges, stripping the naked, denying water and bread, sending widows away empty; 'Can a man be of use to God? leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God shows lightning in fear and hope and sends thunderbolts on whom he wills (weight 7.7); God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth (weight 6.4). Pair score 14.1.

Only in God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens: Dawn seizes the edges of the earth and shakes the wicked out of it; Light and darkness each have a dwelling place and a road to it; Rhetorical question whether rain has a father and from whose womb ice and hoarfrost are born; Lightnings sent by God report back 'Here we are'; The sea bursts out of a womb at creation and is swaddled in cloud and thick darkness; God fixes a limit, bars and doors for the sea: 'Thus far you shall come and no farther'; The springs of the sea and the recesses of the deep (tehom) as unexplored regions; The clouds are the water-skins (bottles) of heaven which God tips over; God has put wisdom in the tuhot and given understanding to the sekhvi (ibis/cock); Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Only in The signs of creation, thunder and the parable of the foam (Surah 13:1-17): To every people there is a guide; God knows what every female carries and how wombs shrink or swell; Each person has angels in succession (mu'aqqibat) before and behind guarding him by God's command; Praying to idols is like stretching one's palms to water hoping it will reach one's mouth; Neighboring plots watered with one water give different fruits: a sign; Parable: torrents and smelted metal throw up foam that vanishes, while what benefits people remains; The thunder glorifies God with his praise, and the angels too in awe of him; All in heaven and earth prostrate to God, willingly or unwillingly, even their shadows morning and evening; A protector goes (stands) before and behind a man to guard him [divergence between the texts]; God raised the heavens without pillars that you can see [divergence between the texts]; Lightning, thunderbolts or hail sent from heaven at the god's command strike what he wills [divergence between the texts]; How thunder in the clouds relates to the god: his own roar or a creature praising him [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero asks the freed prisoner to mention him to the king (weight 7.1); Father revives on hearing the hero lives (weight 7.1); King dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven green ears and seven dry (weight 7.1); Brothers come for grain and do not recognize the hero (weight 7.1); Their payment is secretly returned in their bags (weight 7.1); Hero sold for a small sum of silver (weight 7.1); One prisoner is restored, the other executed and his body exposed (weight 7.1); Hero's cup is hidden in the youngest brother's bag (weight 7.1); The freed prisoner remembers the hero and recommends him (weight 7.1); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode (weight 7.1); Two fellow prisoners dream of pressing wine and carrying bread (weight 7.1); Hero demands they bring their youngest brother (weight 7.1); Brothers bring the hero's garment with false blood (weight 7.1); One brother talks the others out of killing him (weight 7.1); Birds eat bread from on top of the dreamer's head (weight 7.1); A brother offers himself or another in place of the youngest (weight 7.1); A passing caravan takes the hero from the pit (weight 7.1); Hero meets and embraces his father (weight 7.1); The brothers themselves name the thief's penalty (weight 7.1); The freed prisoner forgets the hero for years (weight 7.1); One brother stays behind in Egypt (weight 7.1); A brother or the brothers give the father a pledge for the youngest (weight 6.8); Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream (weight 6.8); Brothers pursued and accused of theft (weight 6.8); Search proceeds through the others' bags before the youngest's (weight 6.8); Hero reveals his identity to his brothers (weight 6.8); Hero thrown into prison (weight 6.8); Father loves the hero more than his brothers (weight 6.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 6.8); A wild animal is blamed for the hero's death (weight 6.8); The whole family moves to Egypt (weight 6.8); The father's eyesight fails (weight 6.8); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.6); Plan to store grain in the good years for the famine years (weight 6.6); Father refuses at first to send the youngest (weight 6.6); God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.6); Hero placed over the land's storehouses or the kingdom (weight 6.6); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 6.6); Hero declares that God turned the brothers' deed to good (weight 6.6); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero (weight 6.6); Hero forgives his brothers (weight 6.5); Hero cast into a pit or well (weight 6.4); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 6.4); Dream of sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to the hero (weight 6.4); The king's experts cannot interpret the dream (weight 6.2); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 6.1); Hero attributes his dream interpretation to God (weight 6.1); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 5.5). Pair score 326.0.

Only in Joseph in Genesis (37, 39–50): After the father's death the brothers fear revenge; Grandfather crosses his hands to bless the younger first; Hero buys the people's land for the king during the famine; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero; Father gives the hero a special garment; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Hero given an Egyptian priest's daughter as wife; Hero makes them swear to carry his bones out of Egypt; and 4 more.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 99 more.

וַתֹּאכַ֣לְנָה הַפָּר֗וֹת רָע֤וֹת הַמַּרְאֶה֙ וְדַקֹּ֣ת הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַפָּר֔וֹת יְפֹ֥ת הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְהַבְּרִיאֹ֑ת וַיִּיקַ֖ץ פַּרְעֹֽה

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ

يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

passages.text: וְיוֹסֵ֗ף ה֚וּא הַשַּׁלִּ֣יט עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ ה֥וּא הַמַּשְׁבִּ֖יר לְכָל עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֲחֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ ל֥וֹ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה
וַיַּ֥רְא יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת אֶחָ֖יו וַיַּכִּרֵ֑ם וַיִּתְנַכֵּ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר אִתָּ֣ם קָשׁ֗וֹת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ מֵאַ֣יִן בָּאתֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנַ֖עַן לִשְׁבָּר אֹֽכֶל
וַיַּכֵּ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶת אֶחָ֑יו וְהֵ֖ם לֹ֥א הִכִּרֻֽהוּ
وَجَآءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ

passages.text: וַיְצַ֣ו יוֹסֵ֗ף וַיְמַלְא֣וּ אֶת כְּלֵיהֶם֮ בָּר֒ וּלְהָשִׁ֤יב כַּסְפֵּיהֶם֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל שַׂקּ֔וֹ וְלָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם צֵדָ֖ה לַדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן
וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח הָאֶחָ֜ד אֶת שַׂקּ֗וֹ לָתֵ֥ת מִסְפּ֛וֹא לַחֲמֹר֖וֹ בַּמָּל֑וֹן וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְהִנֵּה ה֖וּא בְּפִ֥י אַמְתַּחְתּֽוֹ
וַיְהִ֗י הֵ֚ם מְרִיקִ֣ים שַׂקֵּיהֶ֔ם וְהִנֵּה אִ֥ישׁ צְרוֹר כַּסְפּ֖וֹ בְּשַׂקּ֑וֹ וַיִּרְא֞וּ אֶת צְרֹר֧וֹת כַּסְפֵּיהֶ֛ם הֵ֥מָּה וַאֲבִיהֶ֖ם וַיִּירָֽאוּ
وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَٰنِهِ ٱجْعَلُوا۟ بِضَٰعَتَهُمْ فِى رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ

وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا۟ مَتَٰعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا۟ بِضَٰعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِى هَٰذِهِۦ بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ

passages.text: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת יוֹסֵף֙ מִן הַבּ֔וֹר וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה

passages.text: وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍۭ بَخْسٍ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ وَكَانُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ

passages.text: בְּע֣וֹד שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל כַּנֶּ֑ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ כוֹס פַּרְעֹה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ
בְּע֣וֹד שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל עֵ֑ץ וְאָכַ֥ל הָע֛וֹף אֶת בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ
וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה

passages.text: يَٰصَىٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا ٱلْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِن رَّأْسِهِۦ قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ

passages.text: וְאֶת גְּבִיעִ֞י גְּבִ֣יעַ הַכֶּ֗סֶף תָּשִׂים֙ בְּפִי֙ אַמְתַּ֣חַת הַקָּטֹ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף שִׁבְר֑וֹ וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר
הֲל֣וֹא זֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁתֶּ֤ה אֲדֹנִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וְה֕וּא נַחֵ֥שׁ יְנַחֵ֖שׁ בּ֑וֹ הֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶֽם
فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَٰرِقُونَ
قَالُوا۟ نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلْمَلِكِ وَلِمَن جَآءَ بِهِۦ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا۠ بِهِۦ زَعِيمٌ

sides.note: siqāya / ṣuwāʿ al-malik

passages.text: וַיְדַבֵּר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים אֶת פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֶת חֲטָאַ֕י אֲנִ֖י מַזְכִּ֥יר הַיּֽוֹם
וְשָׁ֨ם אִתָּ֜נוּ נַ֣עַר עִבְרִ֗י עֶ֚בֶד לְשַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים וַנְּ֨סַפֶּר ל֔וֹ וַיִּפְתָּר לָ֖נוּ אֶת חֲלֹמֹתֵ֑ינוּ אִ֥ישׁ כַּחֲלֹמ֖וֹ פָּתָֽר
وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۠ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرْسِلُونِ

يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

passages.text: וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂ֧הוּ בְּבִגְד֛וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר שִׁכְבָ֣ה עִמִּ֑י וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה
וַיְהִי֙ כִּרְאוֹתָ֔הּ כִּֽי עָזַ֥ב בִּגְד֖וֹ בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַיָּ֖נָס הַחֽוּצָה
וַתַּנַּ֥ח בִּגְד֖וֹ אֶצְלָ֑הּ עַד בּ֥וֹא אֲדֹנָ֖יו אֶל בֵּיתֽוֹ

passages.text: وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُۥ مِن دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلْبَابِ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

passages.text: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן חֲלֹמ֑וֹ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר
וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי
וּבַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה שָׂרִיגִ֑ם וְהִ֤יא כְפֹרַ֨חַת֙ עָלְתָ֣ה נִצָּ֔הּ הִבְשִׁ֥ילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶ֖יהָ עֲנָבִֽים

وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ ٱلْءَاخَرُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِى خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦٓ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

passages.text: בְּזֹ֖את תִּבָּחֵ֑נוּ חֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ אִם תֵּצְא֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֧י אִם בְּב֛וֹא אֲחִיכֶ֥ם הַקָּטֹ֖ן הֵֽנָּה
וְאֶת אֲחִיכֶ֤ם הַקָּטֹן֙ תָּבִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֔י וְיֵאָמְנ֥וּ דִבְרֵיכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א תָמ֑וּתוּ וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵֽן

In Joshua God takes Abraham away (wā-ʾeqqaḥ ʾet ʾăvîkem ʾet ʾAvrāhām), and Abraham neither speaks nor argues. In the Quran Abraham argues with his father and people, who appeal to ancestral custom (wajadnā ābāʾanā), and he declares their gods his enemy (fa-innahum ʿaduwwun lī).

matches.note: A thing that cannot speak becomes a witness: hā-ʾeḇen ha-zōʾṯ tihyeh bānû lə-ʿēḏâ kî hîʾ šāməʿâ ʾēṯ kol ʾimrê YHWH ... pen təḵaḥăšûn bē-ʾlōhêḵem vs. shahida ʿalayhim ... julūduhum; anṭaqanā llāh. Joshua's stone 'heard' and will witness against denial (k-ḥ-š); the Quran's skins are made to speak against those who denied (yajḥadūn, 41:28). cf. b. Hag 16a (a man's limbs testify against him, citing Isa 43:12), not in the HB itself.

sides.note: Abraham's father served other gods. The name and the agent differ. Josh: Teraḥ ʾăvî ʾAvrāhām ... wa-yyaʿavdû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm, and God acts: wā-ʾeqqaḥ ʾet-ʾăvîkhem ʾet-ʾAvrāhām mē-ʿēver han-nāhār. Q: wa-idh qāla Ibrāhīmu li-abīhi Āzara a-tattakhidhu aṣnāman ālihatan. The father is named Āzar and confronted, and Abraham reasons his own way out (6:76-79).

sides.note: A hero of God whose father worships idols: mizbaḥ habbaʿal ʾăšer lᵉʾābîkā vs annahu ʿaduwwun li-llāh. The fathers end differently: Joash defends his son against the town (ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô); Abraham's father stays God's enemy and is disowned.

leads.title: Fall of Jericho; Rahab spared; curse on the rebuilder ↔ The people of the town, the three messengers and the man who came running

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No host from heaven was needed: a single Shout (sayha) and they were extinguished (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Fall of Jericho; Rahab spared; curse on the rebuilder: A besieged city is circled once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh; The harlot who hid the spies is spared with her family when the city falls; The army must keep total silence until the leader gives the signal to shout; Captured silver, gold, bronze and iron are holy, for the treasury of YHWH; Seven priests blow seven rams' horns before the ark; City walls collapse at a trumpet blast and a great shout; The ark goes before the army in battle or procession; Curse that whoever rebuilds the destroyed city will lose his firstborn and youngest sons; The spoils of war (anfal) belong to God and the messenger; A conquered city is burned with fire; Ban (herem): total destruction of a conquered population.

Only in The people of the town, the three messengers and the man who came running: A man comes running from the farthest part of the city urging his people to follow the messengers; The believer is told 'enter the Garden' and says 'Would that my people knew how my Lord forgave me'; Two messengers sent to a town are rejected, so God reinforces them with a third; The townsfolk say 'we augur ill of you' and threaten to stone the messengers; they reply 'your omen is with you'; Offender stoned to death by the community; Augury: a bird's flight or alighting is an omen bound to a person [divergence between the texts]; The dead cannot go back to the life they left; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied; Intercession avails only for whom God permits; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

leads.title: Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan ↔ Badr and Uhud
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) (weight 7.7); A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); The army is defeated because of one member's hidden sin (weight 7.7). Pair score 23.2.

Only in Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan: The culprit is urged to 'give glory to God' by confessing; The sinner's children, animals and property are destroyed with him; Leader complains to God after a defeat: would that we had stayed where we were; Sin described as a sequence: I saw, I coveted, I took, I hid; Spies are sent ahead to scout a land for conquest; A great heap of stones is raised over an executed man, 'to this day'; Lot or Urim-Thummim cast to identify the guilty party (tamim); Leader and elders tear their clothes, fall on their faces and put dust on their heads; A place is named after an event that happened there, 'to this day'.

Only in Badr and Uhud: God helped you at Badr when you were weak; The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter; Such days God alternates among people; Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils); Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection; After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters; Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds; Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken; The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them; Those who restrain anger and pardon people; It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me; Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled; and 23 more.

matches.note: Josh 7:21 wā-ʾēreʾ ba-ššālāl ... wā-ʾeḥmĕdēm wā-ʾeqqāḥēm: Achan saw the spoil, coveted it and took it; 7:11 ḥāṭāʾ yiśrāʾēl ... lāqĕḥû min ha-ḥērem: the whole people is guilty; Q 3:152 wa-ʿaṣaytum min baʿdi mā arākum mā tuḥibbūn: you disobeyed after God showed you what you love (the spoils), and 3:161 wa-man yaghlul yaʾti bi-mā ghalla yawma l-qiyāma: whoever embezzles will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection. Lust for spoil causes defeat in both; Joshua's culprit is found by lot and executed with his family (7:24-25), the Quran defers the embezzler's punishment to the Last Day and states that no prophet would embezzle.

passages.text: חָטָא֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְגַם֙ עָבְר֣וּ אֶת בְּרִיתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אוֹתָ֑ם וְגַ֤ם לָֽקְחוּ֙ מִן הַחֵ֔רֶם וְגַ֤ם גָּֽנְבוּ֙ וְגַ֣ם כִּֽחֲשׁ֔וּ וְגַ֖ם שָׂ֥מוּ בִכְלֵיהֶֽם

ואראה וָאֵ֣רֶא בַשָּׁלָ֡ל אַדֶּ֣רֶת שִׁנְעָר֩ אַחַ֨ת טוֹבָ֜ה וּמָאתַ֧יִם שְׁקָלִ֣ים כֶּ֗סֶף וּלְשׁ֨וֹן זָהָ֤ב אֶחָד֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים שְׁקָלִים֙ מִשְׁקָל֔וֹ וָֽאֶחְמְדֵ֖ם וָֽאֶקָּחֵ֑ם וְהִנָּ֨ם טְמוּנִ֥ים בָּאָ֛רֶץ בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאָֽהֳלִ֖י וְהַכֶּ֥סֶף תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ

وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥٓ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذْنِهِۦ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَٰزَعْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِىٍّ أَن يَغُلَّ وَمَن يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ

matches.label: The army is defeated because of one member's hidden sin
matches.note: Josh 7:7, 12 lāmâ heʿăbartā ... wĕ-lōʾ yukĕlû bĕnê yiśrāʾēl lāqûm lipnê ʾōyĕbêhem ... kî hāyû lĕ-ḥērem: Joshua asks God why they were defeated and is told it is the people's sin; Q 3:165 a-wa-lammā aṣābatkum muṣībatun ... qultum annā hādhā qul huwa min ʿindi anfusikum: when defeat struck you said 'how is this?'; say: 'it is from yourselves'. The question 'why?' after defeat, answered by the army's own guilt.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֲהָ֣הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה לָ֠מָה הֵעֲבַ֨רְתָּ הַעֲבִ֜יר אֶת הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָתֵ֥ת אֹתָ֛נוּ בְּיַ֥ד הָאֱמֹרִ֖י לְהַאֲבִידֵ֑נוּ וְלוּ֙ הוֹאַ֣לְנוּ וַנֵּ֔שֶׁב בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן

וְלֹ֨א יֻכְל֜וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לָקוּם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֔ם עֹ֗רֶף יִפְנוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י הָי֖וּ לְחֵ֑רֶם לֹ֤א אוֹסִיף֙ לִֽהְי֣וֹת עִמָּכֶ֔ם אִם לֹ֥א תַשְׁמִ֛ידוּ הַחֵ֖רֶם מִֽקִּרְבְּכֶֽם

وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥٓ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذْنِهِۦ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَٰزَعْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
أَوَلَمَّآ أَصَٰبَتْكُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أَصَبْتُم مِّثْلَيْهَا قُلْتُمْ أَنَّىٰ هَٰذَا قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ أَنفُسِكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

leads.title: Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal ↔ The man who passed a ruined town
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The fate of a destroyed town: lasting ruin or revival [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3); A destroyed city is made a perpetual ruin-mound (tel olam) (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.3.

Only in Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal: Leader holds out his javelin and does not lower his hand until victory is complete; A captured enemy king is killed and hanged on a tree until sunset, then buried under stones; Large stones plastered with lime and inscribed with the whole Torah after crossing; Column of smoke from the city is the prearranged signal of the ambush; Blessing pronounced on Mount Gerizim and curse on Mount Ebal; The whole law is read aloud before the assembly, including women, children and foreigners; A great heap of stones is raised over an executed man, 'to this day'; Altar of whole stones on which no iron tool is lifted; Feigned retreat draws defenders out while an ambush takes the city; Ban (herem): total destruction of a conquered population.

Only in The man who passed a ruined town: The sleeper is shown his donkey's bones assembled and clothed with flesh; After a century the sleeper's food and drink have not spoiled; A man passing a ruined town is made to die for a hundred years, then revived, thinking he slept a day or part of a day; The sleeper's food shows how long he slept [divergence between the texts]; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; A dead (ruined) land or town is brought back to life [divergence between the texts]; At the prophet's word there is a rattling; bones come together bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath; A man woken from a long sleep thinks he slept only a moment or a day.

matches.label: Hero smashes or burns idols
matches.note: Same sequence: the young man destroys his father's people's cult objects unseen (wayyaʿaś lāylâ / baʿda an tuwallū mudbirīn), and the townsmen ask who did it, mî ʿāśâ haddābār hazzeh ... gidʿôn ben-yôʾāš ʿāśâ / man faʿala hādhā bi-ālihatinā ... samiʿnā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu Ibrāhīm. Gideon acts on God's command (wayyōʾmer lô YHWH); Abraham on his own oath (ta-llāhi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum).

passages.text: וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת

וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה
וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי
وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ
قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: Hero blames the largest idol for the destruction
matches.note: The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָא ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ
قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ
فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ

sides.note: A hero of God whose father worships idols: mizbaḥ habbaʿal ʾăšer lᵉʾābîkā vs annahu ʿaduwwun li-llāh. The fathers end differently: Joash defends his son against the town (ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô); Abraham's father stays God's enemy and is disowned.

passages.text: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ

Lev 11 forbids many species and treats contact with nəbēlâ as defiling (hannōgēaʿ bənibəlātāh yiṭmāʾ ... wəhāʾōkēl minnibəlātāh yəkabbēs bəgādāyw). Q explains the longer Jewish list as a special burden: wa-ʿalā lladhīna hādū ḥarramnā mā qaṣaṣnā ʿalayka min qabl. Lev's carrion rule (purification, not a ban on eating) also differs from Q's maytah.

matches.note: ʾiššâ zōnâ wa-ḥălālâ lōʾ yiqqāḥû ... kî qādōš hûʾ lēʾlōhāyw ~ az-zānī lā yankiḥu illā zāniyatan aw mushrikatan ... wa-ḥurrima dhālika ʿalā l-muʾminīna: a bar on marrying a woman who has been unchaste (zônâ / zāniya). evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet's wives will receive double punishment for open indecency and double reward for obedience (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Priests' mourning and marriage limits; blemished priests: Priest with a bodily defect may not approach the altar or veil; Blemished priest still eats the holy and most holy food; High priest may not defile himself even for father or mother; Offender executed by burning; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Sacrifice called God's 'bread/food' (lahmi); Priest may defile himself only for close kin; Priests may not marry a harlot or divorcee; the high priest only a virgin of his people; Priests may not dishevel hair, tear garments, shave or gash themselves in mourning.

Only in The prophet's wives, the people of the House, and the believers men and women: The prophet's wives are given the choice between worldly adornment (with release and gift) and God and the hereafter; God wishes to remove impurity from you, people of the House (ahl al-bayt), and purify you thoroughly; Paired list of male and female believers (muslims, believers, devout, truthful, patient, humble, charitable, fasting, chaste, remembering) promised equal reward; The prophet's wives are to stay in their houses, not soften their speech, and not display themselves as in the former Jahiliyya; Each person dies for his own sin.

leads.title: The appointed times - sabbath and annual festivals ↔ The fast of Ramadan
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Length, hours and exemptions of a prescribed fast [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The appointed times - sabbath and annual festivals: A holy day is kept from evening to evening; First sheaf (omer) of the harvest waved by the priest on the morrow after the sabbath; Two leavened loaves of new grain offered as first fruits; New bread, parched grain or fresh ears may not be eaten until the first sheaf is offered; Annual Day of Atonement on the tenth of the seventh month, with self-affliction and total rest; First day of the seventh month as a 'day of blasting' (yom teru'ah); An eighth day of solemn assembly ('atseret) closes the seven-day festival; Seven full weeks (fifty days) counted from the sheaf offering to the new grain offering; Fruit of a goodly tree, palm fronds, leafy boughs and brook willows taken for the festival; Calendar of festivals with prescribed offerings (Passover, Weeks, Trumpets, Atonement, Booths); Corners of the field, gleanings and fallen grapes left for the poor and the stranger; Passover on the fourteenth of the first month at twilight; and 3 more.

Only in The fast of Ramadan: Fasting prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you; Eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn; Those able only with hardship may ransom fast days by feeding a poor person (fidya); Spouses not approached while in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques; Marital relations permitted on fast nights; spouses are garments for one another; Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down; The sick and the traveler may make up missed fast days later; A gift (bribe) from or to the powerful in court, to deprive another of his right; Making the judge take a bribe to win a case [divergence between the texts]; Marital relations during a fast [contrast between the texts]; The deity is near to the one who prays and hears (answers) him; What the annual fast is tied to [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

matches.label: Length, hours and exemptions of a prescribed fast
matches.note: Lev 23:27-32 wĕ-ʿinnîtem ʾet napšōtêkem ... kî kol ha-nnepeš ʾăšer lōʾ tĕʿunneh ... wĕ-nikrĕtâ ... mē-ʿereb ʿad ʿereb: one day of self-affliction on the tenth of the seventh month, from evening to evening, on pain of being cut off; Q 2:183-187 kutiba ʿalaykumu ṣ-ṣiyāmu ka-mā kutiba ʿalā lladhīna min qablikum ... ayyāman maʿdūdātin ... ḥattā yatabayyana lakumu l-khayṭu l-abyaḍu ... thumma atimmū ṣ-ṣiyāma ilā l-layl: a fast 'as prescribed for those before you', but for a whole month, from dawn to nightfall, with eating at night, and exemptions for the sick and traveller and ransom by feeding the poor (fidya). The day changes to a month, evening-to-evening to dawn-to-night, and karet to God 'wants ease for you' (yurīdu llāhu bikumu l-yusra).

passages.text: אַ֡ךְ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֩ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֨י הַזֶּ֜ה י֧וֹם הַכִּפֻּרִ֣ים ה֗וּא מִֽקְרָא קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְעִנִּיתֶ֖ם אֶת נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהִקְרַבְתֶּ֥ם אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָֽה
כִּ֤י כָל הַנֶּ֨פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא תְעֻנֶּ֔ה בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְנִכְרְתָ֖ה מֵֽעַמֶּֽיהָ
שַׁבַּ֨ת שַׁבָּת֥וֹן הוּא֙ לָכֶ֔ם וְעִנִּיתֶ֖ם אֶת נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם בְּתִשְׁעָ֤ה לַחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב מֵעֶ֣רֶב עַד עֶ֔רֶב תִּשְׁבְּת֖וּ שַׁבַּתְּכֶֽם
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَٰتٍ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُۥ وَأَن تَصُومُوا۟ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ

أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمْ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَّهُنَّ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنكُمْ فَٱلْـَٰٔنَ بَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَكُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلْخَيْطُ ٱلْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْطِ ٱلْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا تُبَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمْ عَٰكِفُونَ فِى ٱلْمَسَٰجِدِ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ

leads.title: Perpetual lamp, showbread, and the blasphemer stoned ↔ Retaliation and bequests
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Retaliation (talion) for killing or injury [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis) (weight 6.5). Pair score 13.5.

Only in Perpetual lamp, showbread, and the blasphemer stoned: Those who heard the blasphemy lay their hands on the offender's head before stoning; Killing a person is capital; killing an animal is compensated life for life; Offender held in custody until God's ruling is given; Pronouncing or pricking 'the Name' of God in blasphemy is a capital offense; Son of an Israelite mother and Egyptian father blasphemes the Name in a quarrel; Twelve loaves in two rows set before God each sabbath with frankincense; A perpetual lamp fed with pure beaten olive oil; Same law for the resident alien and the native; Offender stoned to death by the community.

Only in Retaliation and bequests: Kin of the slain may pardon and accept compensation (diya) instead of retaliation, a lightening from God; 'In retaliation there is life for you'; Retaliation (qisas) for the slain: free for free, slave for slave, female for female; What person is matched to a man who was killed [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Clause on whoever alters a sealed grant or a bequest [divergence between the texts]; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; Whoever alters the wording of a fixed text (tablet, bequest) after it is set bears the penalty; A negligent owner may pay a ransom for his life; In a homicide, the 'lord of the blood' decides: if he says 'let him die' the killer dies, if 'let him pay' he pays; the king has no part; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; Whether payment may substitute for a life.

matches.label: The fat tail of the sheep is offered
matches.note: What fat is exempt. Lev puts on the altar ha-ḥēlev ha-məkhasseh ʾet-haq-qerev wə-ʾēt kol-ha-ḥēlev ʾăšer ʿal-haq-qerev (the fat on the entrails) and ha-ʾalyāh təmîmāh lə-ʿummat he-ʿāṣeh (the fat tail by the backbone). Q exempts mā ḥamalat ẓuhūruhumā awi l-ḥawāyā (what the backs carry, or the entrails) from the ban. cf. (not a match) the rabbinic ḥelev / shuman distinction (b. Ḥullin 49b).

Only in Priests who despise God's name with blemished offerings: The altar is called 'the table of YHWH' and the offering 'bread' (lehem); God wishes someone would shut the temple doors rather than kindle the altar in vain; A son honors his father and a servant his master: 'If I am a father, where is my honor?'; God calls himself 'a great king' (melekh gadol) whose name is feared among the nations; 'Offer that to your governor; would he accept you?': sarcastic comparison of God and a human ruler; Disputation form: God states a claim, the people object 'How have you...?', and God answers; Blemished animal (lame, blind) may not be sacrificed.

Only in Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God: Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews; Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God; Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna'; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); God swears by himself: to me every knee shall bow and every tongue swear; Whether God has or begets a son [contrast between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; A good deed done for one's land is laid up in the god's basket (credited by the god); The god's whereabouts named as the sunrise and the sunset (east and west) [divergence between the texts]; East and west belong to God; wherever you turn, there is the face of God; 'He spoke and it came to be; he commanded and it stood firm'; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Cluster of divine epithets in sequence (e.g. the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, doer of what he wills; or Lord, King, God of mankind) (weight 5.7). Pair score 5.7.

Only in The jealous and avenging God against Nineveh: One who plots evil against YHWH comes out of the enemy city, a counselor of Belial (beliyya'al); God's way is in whirlwind and storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet; YHWH is an avenging God (noqem), 'lord of wrath' (ba'al hemah), keeping anger for his enemies; 'Who can stand before his indignation?': rhetorical question on the unendurable divine wrath; God rebukes the sea and dries it up and makes all rivers fail; Bashan, Carmel and Lebanon wither; Command to destroy figured stones, molten images and high places of the land; God broke the bars of the yoke and made the people walk upright; God is a jealous God; God called rock, fortress, refuge, stronghold or tower of strength; Formula of divine attributes: slow to anger, abundant in mercy, visits iniquity to fourth generation; Brief oracles against neighboring nations (Amalek, Kenite, Asshur, Kittim); At God's coming the earth quakes, heavens drip and mountains flow; and 1 more.

Only in The constellations: the people of the ditch and the preserved tablet: The scripture is a glorious recitation inscribed on a preserved tablet (lawh mahfuz) in heaven; Oath by the sky possessing the constellations or towers (dhat al-buruj); The people of the ditch (ashab al-ukhdud) sit by a fire pit, watching what they do to believers, whose only offense was faith in God; The deity calls himself or herself the doer (of what he says, of what he wills); The scripture is a glorious recitation inscribed on a preserved tablet (lawh mahfuz) in heaven [divergence between the texts]; A single heavenly tablet holding supreme decrees, and whether it is guarded or can be stolen [divergence between the texts]; Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people [divergence between the texts]; The epithet 'he does what he wills' (Eg. Mrr=f-jrr=f, Ar. faʿʿālun li-mā yurīd) [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation); List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people; A series of oaths by natural phenomena (dawn, night, day, sun, moon, sky, earth, stars, winds) opens or punctuates a passage.

passages.text: אַ֗ף כִּֽי עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֶלְךָ֖ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת

וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לִשְׁמֹ֗עַ וְלֹא זָכְר֤וּ נִפְלְאֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּהֶ֔ם וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת עָרְפָּ֔ם וַיִּתְּנוּ רֹ֛אשׁ לָשׁ֥וּב לְעַבְדֻתָ֖ם בְּמִרְיָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֩ אֱל֨וֹהַּ סְלִיח֜וֹת חַנּ֧וּן וְרַח֛וּם אֶֽרֶךְ אַפַּ֥יִם וְרַב וחסד חֶ֖סֶד וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּֽם

וְאַתָּה֙ בְּרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים לֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר אֶת עַמּ֣וּד הֶ֠עָנָן לֹא סָ֨ר מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֤ם בְּיוֹמָם֙ לְהַנְחֹתָ֣ם בְּהַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת עַמּ֨וּד הָאֵ֤שׁ בְּלַ֨יְלָה֙ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ בָֽהּ
وَلَقَدْ جَآءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذْتُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱسْمَعُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

leads.title: Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession ↔ Al-Talaq: divorce and the waiting period, two witnesses, nursing wages, and the seven heavens and earths
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to God (weight 6.5). Pair score 6.5.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 17 more.

Only in Al-Talaq: divorce and the waiting period, two witnesses, nursing wages, and the seven heavens and earths: Divorce women at (the start of) their waiting period ('idda), count it, and do not expel them from their homes during it unless for flagrant indecency; House divorced wives as you live, support them while pregnant, and pay them if they nurse your child; otherwise another woman may nurse; At the end of the term, retain or part with them honorably, and call two just witnesses; God created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, the command descending between them; Waiting period of three months for women past menses or not yet menstruating; for the pregnant, until delivery; Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away [contrast between the texts]; Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away [divergence between the texts]; What one gives is graded by one's means: the rich much, the poor little; At the end of the term, retain or part with them honorably, and call two just witnesses [divergence between the texts]; The offering is reduced for those who cannot afford it; How many heavens there are [divergence between the texts]; Husband writes a bill of divorcement for 'some indecency' and sends her away; and 3 more.

leads.title: Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail ↔ Exodus, the calf and the wilderness
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt (weight 7.7); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people (weight 6.8); The people grumble against their leaders about food or water (weight 6.1). Pair score 36.2.

Only in Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail: Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint; A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin; Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets'; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' [divergence between the texts]; Spirit rests on people and they prophesy (ecstatically); Craved food granted, then plague strikes while meat is still in their mouths; Leader protests he did not conceive or bear the people to carry them like a nurse; Exhausted leader asks God to kill him; Manna described: like coriander seed, look of bdellium, taste of oil cakes, falls with the dew; Seventy elders of Israel accompany or assist the prophet [divergence between the texts]; Some of the spirit on the leader is taken and placed on others; and 4 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; Ruler orders the killing of male infants [divergence between the texts]; Moses strikes the rock for water [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

matches.note: Num 11:5 zākarnû ʾet ha-ddāgâ ... ʾēt ha-qqiššuʾîm wĕ-ʾēt hā-ʾăbaṭṭiḥîm wĕ-ʾet he-ḥāṣîr wĕ-ʾet ha-bbĕṣālîm wĕ-ʾet ha-ššûmîm; Q 2:61 baqlihā wa-qiththāʾihā wa-fūmihā wa-ʿadasihā wa-baṣalihā. Three cognates (qiššuʾîm / qiththāʾ, bĕṣālîm / baṣal, šûmîm / fūm). Changed: in Numbers the craving is for meat (mî yaʾăkilēnû bāśār, 11:4) and the food is remembered from Egypt; in the Quran the complaint is 'one food' (lan naṣbira ʿalā ṭaʿāmin wāḥidin), fish and meat are absent, lentils are added. The outcome changes too: plague in Num 11:33; in Q ihbiṭū miṣran fa-inna lakum mā saʾaltum, and humiliation.

matches.label: Two faithful spies dissent from the majority
matches.note: Num names Yəhôšuaʿ bin-Nûn wə-Khālēv ben-Yəfunneh, who tear their garments and say YHWH ʾittānû ʾal-tîrāʾum. Q has only rajulāni mina lladhīna yakhāfūna (unnamed). passages.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן נ֗וּן וְכָלֵב֙ בֶּן יְפֻנֶּ֔ה מִן הַתָּרִ֖ים אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ קָרְע֖וּ בִּגְדֵיהֶֽם
וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֶל כָּל עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֤רְנוּ בָהּ֙ לָת֣וּר אֹתָ֔הּ טוֹבָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹֽד

قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا ٱدْخُلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غَٰلِبُونَ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓا۟ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

matches.label: After the people's rebellion the prophet intercedes for them or asks to be separated from them
matches.note: A reversal. In Num God offers to destroy the people (ʾakkennû vad-dever ... wə-ʾeʿĕśeh ʾōtəkhā lə-gôy gādôl), and Moses intercedes (səlaḥ-nāʾ la-ʿăwōn hā-ʿām ha-zzeh). וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁמְע֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּֽי הֶעֱלִ֧יתָ בְכֹחֲךָ֛ אֶת הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה מִקִּרְבּֽוֹ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لَآ أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِى وَأَخِى فَٱفْرُقْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

matches.label: Forty years of wandering, a year for each day of scouting
matches.note: Num: arbāʿîm šānāh, a year for each day of scouting (yôm laš-šānāh), until the corpses fall (ʿad-tōm pigrêkhem bam-midbār). matches.label: What Korah's sin was, and why the earth swallowed him
matches.note: Korah's offence: Numbers has a religious revolt against Moses and Aaron, rav lākhem kî khol hā-ʿēdâ kullām qədōšîm ... û-maddûaʿ titnaśśəʾû ʿal qəhal YHWH, with Dathan, Abiram and 250 chieftains. The Quran has the wealth and arrogance of a single man of Moses' people: Qārūna kāna min qawmi Mūsā fa-baghā ʿalayhim wa-ātaynāhu mina l-kunūzi mā inna mafātiḥahu la-tanūʾu bi-l-ʿuṣbati, who boasts innamā ūtītuhu ʿalā ʿilmin ʿindī and parades in his finery. The Quran has no priesthood dispute, incense test or fellow rebels. cf. b. Sanh. 110a and b. Pes. 119a (Korah's wealth), outside the HB.

matches.note: Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. A sequence of exclusive heirs becomes a set of simultaneous shares. The Quran begins yūṣīkumu llāhu 'God charges you' (cf. ḥuqqat mišpāṭ, 27:11).

matches.label: A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally
matches.note: The same legal category: Q khaṭaʾan = Num bi-šəgāgāh (unintentional killing). The remedy differs. Num: asylum in a city of refuge (wə-nās šāmmāh rōṣēaḥ makkēh-nefeš bi-šəgāgāh). matches.label: The marriage of fatherless girls is tied to their inheritance
matches.note: In both, a female orphan's inheritance is tied to her marriage. Num makes marriage within the father's clan a duty, so the naḥălāh does not pass to another tribe: ʾakh lə-mišpaḥat maṭṭēh ʾăvîhem tihyênāh lə-nāšîm. leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed, 1 opposite ruling, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How the case of a wife suspected of adultery is decided [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Adultery done in secret with no witness and not caught in the act (weight 7.7); Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7); Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal (weight 7.7); Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 38.7.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven.

Only in Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath: The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers; A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers; A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath; The adulterer is excluded from the company of the just [divergence between the texts]; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Judges told to let no pity hold them back from carrying out a fixed punishment; How many lashes a flogging may have [contrast between the texts]; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; The penalty for adultery or fornication [contrast between the texts]; The penalty for falsely accusing a woman of unchastity [divergence between the texts]; Husband who falsely accuses his bride is flogged, fined 100 silver, and may never divorce her; and 4 more.

matches.label: Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses
matches.note: Who swears: in Num 5 only the woman, made to swear by the priest (wə-hišbîaʿ ʾōtāh hak-kōhēn bi-švuʿat hā-ʾālâ), answering ʾāmēn ʾāmēn; in Q 24 the husband swears first, four times by God (arbaʿu shahādātin bi-llāh) and a fifth time that God's curse (laʿnat Allāh) be on him if he lies, then the wife swears four counter-oaths and a fifth calling God's wrath (ghaḍab Allāh) on herself. The curse falls on both parties, no priest is involved and there is no sanctuary rite.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts]; Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven; and 3 more.

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Something (a reed) born without father or mother, out of the storm [divergence between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; To prove the truth, the parties call down destruction or curse on the liar together with wives and children; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity; By whose power a healer revives the dead and heals the sick [divergence between the texts]; Parties to a dispute call down divine punishment on the liar, with their wives and children; and 14 more.

matches.note: Num 6:5, 18 taʿar lōʾ yaʿăbōr ʿal rōʾšô ... wĕ-gillaḥ ha-nnāzîr petaḥ ʾōhel môʿēd ... wĕ-nātan ʿal hā-ʾēš ʾăšer taḥat zebaḥ ha-ššĕlāmîm: hair uncut during the vow, shaved at the sanctuary at its end and burned under the offering; Q 2:196 wa-lā taḥliqū ruʾūsakum ḥattā yablugha l-hadyu maḥillahu: no shaving in the pilgrim state until the offering reaches its place. leads.title: The Nazirite vow ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
leads.summary: 1 shared motif, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The Nazirite vow: Priest places the boiled shoulder and cakes in the hands of the shaved Nazirite and waves them; Nazirite may not become unclean even for the corpse of father, mother, brother or sister; A man or a woman may take the vow of a Nazirite; Sudden death of someone beside a Nazirite voids his vow and he must start again; After the vow's completion rite the Nazirite may drink wine; Abstinence from wine, by vow or by general law [divergence between the texts]; One with an ailment of the head pays ransom by fasting, alms or sacrifice; Nazirite abstains from wine, vinegar, grapes and everything from the vine down to seeds and skins; Nazirite's shaved hair is put on the fire under the well-being offering; When a consecrated person shaves the head [divergence between the texts]; The consecrated person lets his hair grow uncut as the sign of his vow; Two turtledoves or two young pigeons offered (in place of a lamb if one cannot afford it).

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; Whether the deity eats (receives) the food and drink of the offerings [divergence between the texts]; The deity shows or assigns to the builder the site (old foundation) of the deity's house; and 15 more.

matches.label: Abstinence from wine, by vow or by general law
matches.note: Abstention from wine. Num: by vow, as a mark of holiness (mi-yyayin wə-šēkhār yazzîr), and the Nazirite brings a ḥaṭṭāʾt, wə-khipper ʿālāyw mēʾăšer ḥāṭāʾ ʿal-ha-nnāfeš. Q forbids self-imposed abstinence (lā tuḥarrimū ṭayyibāti mā aḥalla llāhu lakum, 5:87), yet makes wine itself rijsun min ʿamali l-shayṭāni for all (5:90). cf. (not a match) b. Taʿanit 11a, which reads Num 6:11 as the sin of self-denial.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Measure for measure: as you have done, so it shall be done to you; your deed returns on your head (weight 7.1); The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness (weight 6.0). Pair score 13.1.

Only in Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH: Edom condemned for violence against its brother Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's fall; Exiles of Jerusalem in Sepharad and of Israel as far as Zarephath will repossess the land; The enemy stands at the crossroads to cut off and hand over the fleeing survivors; Prohibition of gloating over, looting or handing over one's brother on the day of his calamity; The house of Jacob will be fire and the house of Esau stubble consumed without survivor; On Mount Zion there will be escape (peletah) and holiness in the coming judgment; Saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingship shall be YHWH's; Conquerors cast lots over a captured city or its nobles; The wicked should drink of the wrath (cup) of Shaddai.

Only in The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen: The people of paradise ask the damned what brought them to hell; they answer: we did not pray, feed the poor, and we denied the day; Those who turn from the reminder are like startled wild asses fleeing from a lion (qaswara); Every soul is held in pledge (rahina) for what it has earned; Each of the deniers wants to be given scrolls unrolled (personally revealed) to him; Over hell are nineteen; its keepers are angels whose number is made a test; God created a man alone, gave him extended wealth and sons present at his side; yet he wants more and stubbornly opposes the signs; The companions of the right (ashab al-yamin, al-maymana) are saved; the companions of the left (al-mash'ama) are damned; The intercession of intercessors will not benefit the damned; no soul has power to help another; How many wardens or demons are set over the underworld or hell [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; The people wash their garments to prepare for God's appearance; You will not will unless God wills; At the judgment the dead state whether they fed the hungry [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

leads.title: YHWH sayings and royal sayings (man plans, God disposes) ↔ Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Grey hair is a crown of glory, found in the way of righteousness (weight 7.1); The throne is established by righteousness (and loyalty) (weight 7.1); Getting wisdom is better than gold, understanding than silver or jewels (weight 6.8); The heart of man plans his way but YHWH directs his steps; only YHWH's counsel stands (weight 6.6); Saying of the type 'X is an abomination (to'evah) to YHWH but Y is his delight' (weight 6.4); Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded (weight 5.3). Only in YHWH sayings and royal sayings (man plans, God disposes): By loyalty and faithfulness (hesed we-emet) iniquity is atoned for; When a man's ways please YHWH he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him; YHWH has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of evil; The worker's appetite works for him, for his mouth urges him on; The wrath of a king is messengers of death, but a wise man will pacify it; The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from YHWH; Divination (qesem) is on the lips of the king; his mouth does not err in judgment; Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones; Roll (commit) your works to YHWH and your plans will be established; The worthless man (ish beliyya'al) digs up evil and on his lips is a scorching fire; A whisperer separates close friends; In the light of the king's face is life; his favor is like a cloud of the latter rain; and 8 more.

leads.title: 'These also are of the wise': judgment, retaliation and the sluggard's field ↔ Provision in measure, rain, ships like mountains and the ethics of consultation and pardon
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether one may pay back a wrong in kind [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Do not say 'I will do to him as he has done to me; I will pay the man back for his deed' (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in 'These also are of the wise': judgment, retaliation and the sluggard's field: He who gives an honest answer kisses the lips; Prepare your work outside and get your field ready; afterwards build your house; The wise man passes the field of the sluggard, overgrown with thorns and nettles, its stone wall broken down, and draws a lesson; Showing partiality in judgment is not good; he who tells the wicked 'you are righteous' is cursed by peoples; 'A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands', and poverty comes like a vagabond, want like an armed man; A collection introduced as 'words of (or sayings belonging to) the wise'; A faithful witness does not lie; a false witness breathes out lies and will not go unpunished.

Only in Provision in measure, rain, ships like mountains and the ethics of consultation and pardon: The believers conduct their affairs by mutual consultation (shura); God has dispersed living creatures (dabba) in both the heavens and the earth and can gather them; God accepts repentance from his servants and pardons evil deeds; Retaliation in kind is permitted, but whoever pardons and makes peace has his reward with God; A blow is repaid with its like: every deed is interlocked with its consequence; God's control of the wind over ships at sea: raising a storm or stilling it [divergence between the texts]; Whatever misfortune strikes people is for what their own hands have earned, though God pardons much; What is given in this life is passing enjoyment (mata'); what is with God is better and more lasting; God sends down rain after people have despaired and spreads out his mercy; Ships running on the sea like landmarks/mountains are a sign; God could still the wind and leave them motionless or wreck them; If God gave his servants unlimited provision they would transgress on earth, so he sends down in measure; Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis) [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

matches.label: Whether one may pay back a wrong in kind
matches.note: ʾal tōʾmar ka-ʾăšer ʿāśâ lî kēn ʾeʿĕśeh lô ʾāšîḇ lā-ʾîš kə-p̄āʿŏlô forbids repaying in kind. A ban in Proverbs, a preference in the Quran.

leads.title: End of the Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel section) ↔ Not two gods; daughters ascribed to God and buried alive; milk, wine and the bee (Surah 16:51-70)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: From the bee's belly comes a drink of many colors in which is healing for people (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in End of the Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel section): Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, lest YHWH see it, be displeased and turn his anger from him; By wisdom a house is built and by knowledge its rooms are filled with precious riches; Rescue those being taken to death; do not say 'we did not know', for the weigher of hearts knows; The righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble in calamity; He who plans evil will be called a master of schemes (ba'al mezimmot); Eat honey, my son, for it is good; so is wisdom sweet to your soul; Wisdom is too high (like corals, ra'mot) for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the gate; Do not envy sinners or evildoers, for there is a future (aharit) and your hope will not be cut off; Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and heart will be questioned; Fear YHWH and the king, and do not mix with those who seek change; Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them; A section of sayings closely paralleling the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope; and 4 more.

Only in Not two gods; daughters ascribed to God and buried alive; milk, wine and the bee (Surah 16:51-70): The polytheists assign daughters to God while wishing sons for themselves; God says: do not take two gods; he is only one God; When told of a daughter's birth the father's face darkens and he hides from people in shame; Burying a newborn daughter in the dust is condemned; Pure milk issues from cattle's bellies from between dung and blood: a sign; Some are returned to the feeblest age (ardhal al-'umur), knowing nothing after knowledge; God reveals (awha) to the bee to build in mountains, trees and trellises and follow his paths; The bee, sent or inspired by the deity, goes through the mountains [divergence between the texts]; At the judgment the girl buried alive (al-maw'uda) is asked for what sin she was killed; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; A deity gives the bee an order: where to go and what to do [divergence between the texts]; A drink said to contain healing for the sick: wine or honey [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

Only in Proverbs 3:13-35, wisdom a tree of life; creation by wisdom; neighbor ethics: By God's knowledge the deeps were split open and the clouds drip dew; Do not withhold good from its owner or tell your neighbor 'Go and come back tomorrow' when you have it; Wisdom 'is a tree of life to those who grasp her'; Wisdom holds length of days in her right hand, riches and honor in her left; The one who keeps wisdom lies down without fear; his sleep is sweet; he need not fear sudden terror; Wisdom cannot be bought with gold of Ophir, onyx, sapphire, glass, coral, crystal, pearls or topaz of Cush; God made all his works in wisdom; Getting wisdom is better than gold, understanding than silver or jewels; Wisdom (hokhmah) personified as a woman who speaks in the first person.
