leads.title: Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures) ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The ant, a people without strength, prepares its food in summer (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures): The adulteress eats, wipes her mouth and says 'I have done no wrong'; Pressing milk produces butter, pressing the nose produces blood, pressing anger produces strife (pun on af 'nose/anger'); Do not slander a slave to his master lest he curse you; Four small but wise creatures: ants storing food in summer, rock-badgers housed in rock, locusts with no king marching in ranks, the lizard in kings' palaces; Four stately in stride: the lion mightiest of beasts, the strutting rooster (zarzir), the he-goat, and a king with his army; Catalogue of a corrupt 'generation' (dor): cursing parents, self-righteous yet unwashed, haughty, with sword-teeth devouring the poor; If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, put your hand on your mouth; The leech ('aluqah) has two daughters: 'Give, give!'; The locusts have no king yet all go out in ranks; The eye that mocks a father and scorns a mother will be pecked out by ravens of the valley and eaten by young vultures; Four wonders: the way of an eagle in the sky, a serpent on a rock, a ship in the sea, and a man with a young woman ('almah); Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and the eyes of man are never satisfied; and 4 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 42 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Man created from ringing clay like pottery, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire (marij min nar) (weight 7.7); The sun and the moon run by exact reckoning (husban) (weight 7.7); All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n) (weight 7.7); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 5.5). Pair score 28.7.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; God built the sky, raised its canopy, darkened its night and brought out its forenoon; after that he spread out the earth; and 37 more.

Only in Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier: God raised the sky and set the Balance: do not transgress in the balance; weigh with justice and do not skimp; Lord of the two easts and the two wests (the solstitial sunrises and sunsets); The Merciful (al-Rahman) taught the Quran, created man and taught him clear speech (bayan); From the two seas come pearls and coral (marjan); The divine balance does not tilt, therefore a human judge may not tilt it [divergence between the texts]; A creation litany with a refrain after every line [divergence between the texts]; The text addresses jinn and humans together in the dual ('you two', al-thaqalan, 'the two weighty ones'); The deity made or presides over the balance; do not tamper with it or make it short; A god sets up or holds the scales so that weighing in trade is just; Earth and heavens will perish and wear out like a garment, changed like clothing, but God remains the same; Just weights and measures, and the ground given for them [divergence between the texts]; Refrain repeated 31 times: 'Which then of the bounties of your Lord will you two (jinn and humans) deny?'; and 11 more.

leads.title: Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus ↔ Abraham preaches against idols, is saved from the fire, and Lot believes
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 6.6). Pair score 6.6.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 32 more.

Only in Abraham preaches against idols, is saved from the fire, and Lot believes: Idols are taken only as a bond of affection among people in this life; on the Day they will disown and curse one another; The idols own no provision (rizq) for their worshippers; seek provision from God; How God brings Abraham out of his homeland's danger (Ur, or the fire) [divergence between the texts]; Can any of the nations' vanities bring rain, or can the heavens give showers? Only YHWH; Lot believes in Abraham, who declares 'I am emigrating to my Lord'; Family migrates from Ur of the Chaldeans to Harran on the way to Canaan; God placed prophecy and the Book among the descendants of Noah and Abraham; Who leads Abraham's departure from his homeland, with Lot, and why [divergence between the texts]; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation); Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied.

matches.label: A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus
matches.note: A short plague list. Q: fa-arsalnā ʿalayhimu l-ṭūfāna wa-l-jarāda wa-l-qummala wa-l-ḍafādiʿa wa-l-dama āyātin mufaṣṣalātin, five plagues. Ps 105: hāfakh ʾet-mêmêhem lə-dām ... šāraṣ ʾarṣām ṣəfardəʿîm ... ʿārōv kinnîm ... ʾarbeh. Q's last three, qummal, ḍafādiʿ, dam (lice, frogs, blood), are Exodus's first three (dām, ṣəfardəʿîm, kinnîm) in reverse order. Q adds ṭūfān, which is in no HB list, and leaves out the death of the firstborn (Ps 105:36).

leads.title: Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile ↔ Legends of the ancients, the fallen roof, the angels who take souls (Surah 16:24-50)
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol (weight 5.9). Pair score 5.9.

Only in Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile: Israel ate 'sacrifices of the dead' (zivhei metim) at Baal-peor; God caused the exiles to be pitied by all their captors; God grants the people's wilderness craving but sends wasting (razon) into their souls; Provoked at Meribah, Moses spoke rashly with his lips and suffered because of the people; Phinehas's intervention 'was reckoned to him as righteousness for all generations'; Israel 'yokes itself' to Baal of Peor; List of punishment types for the nations: stone-storm, the Shout, swallowing by the earth, drowning; The people exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass; Moses 'stood in the breach' (pérets) before God to turn back his wrath from destroying the people; God turned the sea into dry land and they crossed the river on foot; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; A closing doxology and the divine title it uses [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Legends of the ancients, the fallen roof, the angels who take souls (Surah 16:24-50): The angels are not arrogant; they fear their Lord above them and do as commanded; God came at the plotters' building from its foundations and the roof fell on them; Those who emigrate for God after being wronged will be settled well in this world and rewarded more in the next; Polytheists excuse themselves: had God willed we would not have worshipped others nor forbidden anything; The arrogant are told to enter the gates of hell to abide in it; Those who mislead bear their own full burdens and some of the burdens of those they misled; Deniers swear their strongest oaths that God will not raise the dead; All in heaven and earth prostrate to God, willingly or unwillingly, even their shadows morning and evening; Those who receive the dead greet him with 'peace' on his arrival [divergence between the texts]; Every nation has a messenger, and it is judged justly when he comes; Travel in the land and see the end of those before you; 'Ask the people of the Reminder (ahl al-dhikr) if you do not know': appeal to earlier scripture-holders; and 6 more.

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Young servers go round with a variety of vessels serving a mixed drink [divergence between the texts]; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; and 12 more.

leads.title: Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany ↔ The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God is called the speaker's lamp who lights his darkness (weight 7.1); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 6.4). Pair score 13.4.

Only in Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany: God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy; The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22); At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare; 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?'; God reaches from on high and draws the sufferer out of many waters; Foreigners come cringing and trembling to submit to the king; God answers the distressed when he calls and removes the evil; God hears the cry from his (heavenly) temple; God shows himself loyal to the loyal and crooked to the crooked; God trains the king's hands for war so his arms bend a bow of bronze; God shows steadfast love to his anointed and his seed forever; 'By my God I leap over a wall'; and 13 more.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds in flight, wings spread, praise the deity; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The god titled 'light of heaven(s) and earth' (nūr šamāmī u qaqqari / nūru l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ), and those deprived of light walk in darkness; and 11 more.

leads.summary: 14 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Egypt is called 'the tents of Ham' or 'the land of Ham' (weight 7.3); Swarms (arov) of insects or wild beasts fill the houses of Egypt (weight 7.3); Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); God kills every firstborn of the land, from the king's heir to the lowest servant and cattle (weight 7.1); Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp (weight 7.1); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 7.1); Water brought out of a rock by the leader's rod (weight 7.1); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 7.1); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 6.6); God rains bread from heaven to feed the people in the desert (weight 6.6); Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 6.6); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 6.5); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 6.4); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 6.1). Pair score 96.2.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 27 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 19 more.

leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111)

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 5.5). Pair score 12.9.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 39 more.

Only in Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111): Call on God as Allah or as al-Rahman: to him belong the most beautiful names; After Pharaoh's drowning Israel is told to dwell in the land; at the last promise they are gathered in a mixed crowd; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between; The prophet answers the accusing king: 'I think you are doomed'; Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited; Moses was given nine clear signs; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between [contrast between the texts]; The scripture is sent down in portions so the prophet recites it to people at intervals; Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited [divergence between the texts]; Whatever name is pronounced, it belongs to the one god: 'he is our god' / 'his are the beautiful names'; Whatever name is pronounced, it belongs to the one god: 'he is our god' / 'his are the beautiful names' [divergence between the texts]; Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse); and 5 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Cycle: God punishes, the people seek him and repent, then flatter him and sin again (weight 7.3); Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.2.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 39 more.

Only in 'God's hand is fettered'; the blessings of observing the Torah: Believers, Jews, Sabians and Christians who believe in God and the last day and do good need not fear; Whenever they kindle the fire of war, God extinguishes it; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' Ps: wa-ynassû-ʾēl bi-lvāvām ... ha-yûkhal ʾēl laʿărōkh šulḥān bam-midbār, the rebels' test, answered by wrath (wa-yyitʿabbār) and then manna rained down (wa-yyamṭēr ʿălêhem mān ... dəgan-šāmayim). Q: hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka an yunazzila ʿalaynā māʾidatan mina l-samāʾi, asked by the disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn), not rebels. Jesus warns (ittaqū llāh), then prays; God grants it, and the threat comes afterwards: fa-man yakfur baʿdu ... ʿadhāban lā uʿadhdhibuhu aḥadan. The table becomes an ʿīd. In Ps the punishment is for asking; in Q for disbelief after the sign.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Enemies roar in the sanctuary, hack its carved work with axes and burn it to the ground [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Enemies roar in the sanctuary, hack its carved work with axes and burn it to the ground (weight 6.4). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Psalm 79, the nations have come into your inheritance: Prayer that God not remember against us the iniquities of former generations; Bodies of God's servants left as food for birds and beasts; blood poured like water around Jerusalem with none to bury; Vengeance multiplied sevenfold (or seventy-sevenfold); Prayer 'Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you'; Nations taunt 'Where is their God?'; Israel called the flock of God's pasture; Communal lament over national disaster, asking why God has rejected his people; Heading assigns the psalm to a Levitical singer or guild (Jeduthun, Asaph, sons of Korah, Heman, Ethan); Lament question 'How long, O God?' / 'Why have you rejected us forever?'.

Only in The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8): Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant; Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)'; It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice; God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs; The storm or enemy destroys the city a second time; The enemy sent against the city enters its sanctuary and wrecks what it finds; The god himself rouses a mighty foreign enemy against his own land or people; The god himself sends a fierce foreign people against his own city or people; God sends against Israel servants of his of great might who range through their homes; Because of his people's offence their own god lets a foreign power oppress them for a time, and later gives the land (or the upper hand) back; A swift journey by night ends at a distant sanctuary; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; and 5 more.

The Quran puts the heavens too under man's use, and the sea as a road for ships rather than the fish's 'paths of the seas'. The psalm ends in wonder at the Name; the Quran in a call to reflect and give thanks (tashkurūn, yatafakkarūn).

leads.title: A cleansing fountain, the end of prophecy, and the struck shepherd ↔ Abraham's line of eighteen prophets; Torah in sheets; the false claimant
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: False prophet put to death (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God executes justice for orphan and widow and loves the stranger (weight 5.9). Pair score 5.9.

Only in The Bethel delegation's question about fasting: 'When you fasted and mourned these seventy years, was it for me that you fasted?'; The people made their hearts like shamir (adamant or flint) so as not to hear the Torah; A delegation asks the priests whether to keep weeping and abstaining in the fifth month now the temple is rebuilt; As God called and they would not hear, so they will call and he will not hear; Months are dated by their Babylonian names (Shevat, Kislev); The 'former prophets' called the fathers to repent and they did not listen; A prophecy is dated by day, month and year of the Persian king Darius; The exile lasts seventy years as Jeremiah prophesied; Curse: God will scatter the people among the nations.

Only in Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay': The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world; God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr); Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave; Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts; Vines or palms of a hostile neighbour are cut down [divergence between the texts]; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; How spoil taken from the enemy is distributed [divergence between the texts]; Fay' (booty gained without cavalry or camels) goes to God, the messenger, kin, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, so wealth does not circulate only among the rich; They thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; The wealth of a ruined or expelled people passes to others who did not have it [divergence between the texts]; The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; and 8 more.

Only in Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah: Men thickened on their lees who say in their hearts 'YHWH will do neither good nor evil'; The Day of YHWH is a sacrifice he has prepared, with invited guests consecrated; Litany of the Day: day of wrath, distress, ruin, darkness, cloud and thick darkness, shofar and alarm; God will search Jerusalem with lamps to find the complacent; Named districts of Jerusalem (Fish Gate, Mishneh/Second Quarter, Maktesh/Mortar) wail; A prophet's genealogy is traced several generations back to a king (Hezekiah); God will punish officials and princes who wear foreign garments; People bow and swear both by YHWH and by Malkam (their king or Milcom); God will sweep away humans, beasts, birds of the air and fish of the sea from the face of the ground (creation reversed); Idolatrous priests (kemarim) who burned incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations are put down; Priests do not tread on a temple threshold, explained by an event; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; and 7 more.

Only in Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius: The three goddesses al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, 'the third, the other', named and rejected; They follow only conjecture (zann), and conjecture avails nothing against the truth; God created the pairs, male and female, from a drop of sperm (nutfa) when it is emitted; A surah ends with the command to prostrate (sajda verse); God destroyed 'Ad 'the first' (implying a second 'Ad); God knew you when he produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' bellies; do not claim purity; The idols are only names you and your fathers have named, for which God sent down no authority; God is 'the Lord of Sirius' (al-shi'ra), a star worshipped by some Arabs; Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, except minor slips (al-lamam), find God's forgiveness wide; To your Lord is the final end (al-muntaha); 'Is the male for you and the female for him? That is an unfair division'; 'Which of your Lord's bounties (ala') will you dispute/deny?'; and 19 more.

leads.title: Noah's challenge to his people ↔ Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Why God destroyed a generation or a people (weight 7.3); Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood (weight 6.8); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 6.2); Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger (weight 5.9); The Prophet asks no wage for the message (weight 5.7); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 37.4.

Only in Noah's challenge to his people: Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; Leader protests he never took so much as a donkey from anyone; A seer faced with payment or worldly gain [contrast between the texts]; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; The flood hero is blessed after the flood; the content of the blessing [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero receives when he leaves the vessel [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his father's teaching is to be driven away: 'he is not your son, he was not born to you' [divergence between the texts]; The earth is addressed in the vocative and bidden to open, receive or swallow something [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; and 36 more.

matches.label: Why God destroyed a generation or a people

passages.text: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ خَلَٰٓئِفَ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

sides.note: Why the generation drowns: in Q because they rejected the messenger (wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā); in Gen because the earth was full of violence and corruption (wattimmālēʾ hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô). Moral corruption becomes rejection of a prophet.

passages.text: فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

sides.note: Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'.

matches.label: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood

passages.text: وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُم مَّقَامِى وَتَذْكِيرِى بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ فَأَجْمِعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ ٱقْضُوٓا۟ إِلَىَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ
فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

sides.note: Noah before the flood: in Gen he says nothing to anyone and simply obeys (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer ṣiwwāh ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm kēn ʿāśāh); in Q he preaches and challenges his people: yā qawmi in kāna kabura ʿalaykum maqāmī wa-tadhkīrī bi-āyāti llāhi ... fa-ajmiʿū amrakum wa-shurakāʾakum. Q adds the speech.

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ

sides.note: Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu).

وَيَٰقَوْمِ لَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مَالًا إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُوا۟ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَٰكِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكُمْ قَوْمًا تَجْهَلُونَ

فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ
فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ

sides.note: The guest does not sit, does not go to the table, does not put his lip to the cup (§3:15-20); Abraham's guests' hands do not reach the calf (lā taṣilu ilayhi), and he mistrusts them.

passages.text: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ

sides.note: The host's question to the guest who will not eat: 'why do you not eat ... why do you not drink, my lord?' against fa-qarrabahu ilayhim qāla a-lā taʾkulūn. Who the refusing guest is, is broken in the Hittite. 51:24-27 is not in the list of candidates: I add it here.

leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The flood waters are hot or boiling (weight 7.1); A specific sign marks the moment to board (weight 6.8); A member of the hero's family is lost (weight 6.8); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 6.5); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 6.2); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 6.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 45.1.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; The flood hero is blessed after the flood; the content of the blessing [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero receives when he leaves the vessel [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his father's teaching is to be driven away: 'he is not your son, he was not born to you' [divergence between the texts]; The earth is addressed in the vocative and bidden to open, receive or swallow something [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; The flood hero is told he is only a man like the speaker(s) [divergence between the texts]; When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts]; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

leads.title: Salih, the she-camel and the Shout ↔ Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A people is destroyed by the Shout / Blast (al-sayha) (weight 7.7); Refrain 'away with...' (bu'dan li-) the destroyed people (weight 7.1); The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land (weight 6.8); Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings (weight 6.6); Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him' (weight 6.2). Pair score 34.5.

Only in Salih, the she-camel and the Shout: The people tell their prophet he had been their hope before this; After the crime the people are given three days' enjoyment in their homes before destruction; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan: The people mock: 'Does your prayer command you that we abandon our fathers' gods or our way with our wealth?'; The prophet does not wish to do himself what he forbids them; he wants only reform; What God leaves you (baqiyyat Allah) is better than dishonest gain; Only the prophet's clan keeps the people from stoning him; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; Roll call of destroyed peoples: Noah's, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned cities; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 7.3); Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him (weight 7.3); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 6.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 6.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 6.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). evidence.text: No longer produced by the current pipeline (2026-10-31): its statistics or cognate checks no longer meet the thresholds after a method change. Kept for review.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness (weight 6.7); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 24.3.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: The first man names the animals; God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man; God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; Formula 'no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve'; A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked; Fig leaves sewn into coverings; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

Only in Lawful food and true piety: Those who conceal scripture for gain eat only fire into their bellies; Eating an animal that died or was torn requires washing and makes unclean until evening; Refusal of revelation in favor of what was found with the fathers is rebuked; Wealth given for (freeing) necks, i.e. ransoming slaves and captives; Unbelievers are like beasts shouted at by a herdsman, hearing only a call and a cry; Piety (birr) is not turning faces east or west but faith, giving wealth to kin, orphans, poor, travelers, beggars and captives.

Only in Abrogation, the foreign teacher, coerced unbelief, food law, Abraham the hanif and the Sabbath (Surah 16:101-128): Abraham was a hanif, neither Jew nor Christian nor polytheist; God abrogates or causes to be forgotten a verse and brings a better or similar one (naskh); Opponents claim a foreign-tongued man teaches the prophet; answer: this is clear Arabic; Call to God's way with wisdom and good counsel and argue in the best way; One forced to disbelieve while his heart is firm in faith is excused; Only four foods are forbidden: carrion, blood, swine and what is offered to other than God; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; Good foods once lawful were forbidden to the Jews as punishment for their wrongdoing; The Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus) brings the revelation down from God; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater; If you retaliate, do so in kind; but patience is better; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it; An opponent dismisses the revelation as inherited sorcery (sihr yu'thar) or 'only the word of a mortal'; Parable of a secure town supplied from everywhere which was ungrateful and was made to taste the garment of hunger and fear; Making some of God's provision unlawful and some lawful on your own authority is condemned.

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةً مَّا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ

sides.note: In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna).

passages.text: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ
فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ

sides.note: Genesis' Noah obeys in silence (wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm) and is never sent to anyone; the Quran's Noah is 'their brother' and 'a trustworthy messenger' (akhūhum ... rasūlun amīn) who asks no wage, and his people 'denied the messengers' (kadhdhabat qawmu Nūḥin al-mursalīn).

matches.label: Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why

passages.text: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

sides.note: Genesis saves the whole household, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê vānāyw; the Quran excepts some: wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu minhum (the drowned son of 11:42-43), and forbids Noah to plead for the wrongdoers (wa-lā tukhāṭibnī fī lladhīna ẓalamū).

passages.text: فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ

sides.note: Who is saved with Noah: Genesis, his household for his own righteousness, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... kî ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq (Noah, his sons, his wife, his sons' wives); Quran, najjinī wa-man maʿiya mina l-muʾminīna ... fa-anjaynāhu wa-man maʿahu fī l-fulki l-mashḥūn, the believers who followed him, the 'lowliest' (al-ardhalūn, 26:111). The saved group is defined by faith, not by kinship.

units.title: The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations

matches.label: A god's act sets fresh (sweet) water against salt (bitter) water

passages.text: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا

sides.note: Sumerian a sis (bitter/salt water) against a dug3 (sweet water); Arabic milḥ ujāj against ʿadhb furāt. In Dilmun the god abolishes the salt water; in 25:53 God keeps both and sets a barzakh and ḥijr maḥjūr between them.

passages.text: وَمَا يَسْتَوِى ٱلْبَحْرَانِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ سَآئِغٌ شَرَابُهُۥ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَمِن كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَوَاخِرَ لِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

sides.note: The same pair, sweet against bitter water, with ships of wealth in both: Enki makes Dilmun's salt pools sweet and has ships (ma2 gal-gal) bring gold, cornelian and wood; 35:12 keeps the two seas apart (mā yastawī l-baḥrān), with fresh meat and ornaments (ḥilya) from both and ships (al-fulk mawākhir) seeking God's bounty.

matches.label: God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them

passages.text: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا

وَمَا يَسْتَوِى ٱلْبَحْرَانِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ سَآئِغٌ شَرَابُهُۥ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَمِن كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَوَاخِرَ لِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

sides.note: no barrier mentioned here; fresh meat and ornaments from both

matches.label: God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers

passages.text: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُورًا

sides.note: arsala r-riyāḥa bushran bayna yaday raḥmatihi ~ ʿōśeh malʾākhāyw rûḥôt: winds sent as messengers (arsala / malʾākh); in the Quran they bring news of the coming rain.

passages.text: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ جَاعِلِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُو۟لِىٓ أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَ يَزِيدُ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ مَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
وَٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا فَسُقْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ

sides.note: ʿōśeh malʾāḵâw rûḥôṯ məšārəṯâw ʾēš lōhēṭ vs. jāʿili l-malāʾikati rusulan (35:1) and arsala r-riyāḥa (35:9). Both make (ʿōśeh / jāʿil) heavenly envoys: malʾāḵ and malak are the same word and both mean 'one sent', which the Quran repeats with rusulan.

matches.label: God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky

passages.text: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُورًا
لِّنُحْۦِىَ بِهِۦ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا وَنُسْقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَٰمًا وَأَنَاسِىَّ كَثِيرًا
وَٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا فَسُقْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ

matches.label: Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection

passages.text: لِّنُحْۦِىَ بِهِۦ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا وَنُسْقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَٰمًا وَأَنَاسِىَّ كَثِيرًا
وَٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا فَسُقْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ

sides.note: 'thus is the resurrection (al-nushur)'

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A god's act sets fresh (sweet) water against salt (bitter) water [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them (weight 6.8); God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers (weight 6.6); God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 6.5); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 5.5). Pair score 32.8.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; Night covers the sleepers as a garment, the land as in death; the day is a rising (waking); Two waters, the sweet and the salt sea, meet or mingle [divergence between the texts]; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; What sets the daily sleeping and rising of people [divergence between the texts]; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; The wind carries good news (Akk. bussurtu, Ar. bushr, mubashshirāt) [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

Only in The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas: God made the angels messengers with wings in twos, threes and fours, adding to creation what he wills; To God ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up; Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy; he calls his party to the blaze; The false gods do not own even the thin skin of a date-stone (qitmir); they cannot hear prayer and will disown it at the Resurrection; The form, faces and number of wings of heavenly beings [divergence between the texts]; Each cherub or living creature has four faces (human, lion, ox/cherub, eagle), four wings and human hands under the wings; What God opens no one can shut, and what he withholds no one can release; What happens where fresh and salt water meet [divergence between the texts]; If God willed he could remove you and bring a new creation; God began man's creation from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of a despised fluid, then shaped him and breathed of his spirit; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; No one is granted long life or has his life shortened except it is in a Book; and 3 more.

leads.title: Lot and his people ↔ Lot and the people who expel the pure
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Lot condemns his people for approaching males and leaving the wives God created for them (weight 7.7); The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers (weight 7.3); Lot's people threaten to expel him (weight 7.3); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 6.8); Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt (weight 6.6); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 5.9); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 47.2.

Only in Lot and his people: Lot's family is saved except an old woman among those who stayed behind; What the sin of Lot's townsmen was [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'; The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked.

Only in Lot and the people who expel the pure: Lot's people mock his family as 'people who keep themselves pure' and order their expulsion; What Lot says to the townsmen [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him [divergence between the texts].

passages.text: أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ
وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةً مِّن دُونِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ

matches.label: The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers

passages.text: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

matches.label: Lot's people threaten to expel him

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ
فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ

matches.label: The fate of Lot's wife

passages.text: إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

sides.note: illā ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the one family member lost. Genesis names her Lot's wife and says why (she looked back) and how (pillar of salt); the Quran says only 'an old woman among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.

passages.text: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

sides.note: Who decides the wife's fate: Genesis gives her own act, the warning ʾal tabbîṭ ʾaḥărêkā and wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ; the Quran gives God's decree, illā mraʾatahu qaddarnāhā mina l-ghābirīna, 'we decreed her among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.

leads.title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains ↔ Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 6.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 6.5); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 6.0). Pair score 33.2.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; The king of Egypt as a god who has no second / no other god [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; and 46 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people; and 2 more.

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

sides.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. The Quran's 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ) excludes exactly what Exodus says, that the hand was leprous (məṣōraʿat), and needs no second step of restoring it (4:7).

matches.label: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs

passages.text: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

sides.note: Pharaoh's response to the sign: Exod 7:13 wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿ ʾălēhem ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart hardened as God foretold (God hardens it himself at 14:4, 14:8); Q 26:49 has no hardening and no divine agency, only Pharaoh's rage: āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu la-kabīrukumu lladhī ʿallamakumu s-siḥra, with a threat of amputation and crucifixion.

passages.text: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

sides.note: Why Egypt refuses: Exod 8:15 the magicians admit ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, yet wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh ... ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart is hardened as God foretold; Q 27:14 wa-jaḥadū bihā wa-staiqanathā anfusuhum ẓulman wa-ʿuluwwan, they rejected the signs though inwardly convinced, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. Refusal by God's design becomes knowing, self-chosen denial.

وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: into his bosom (jayb), white without evil

matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest

passages.text: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ

sides.note: fa-lammā jāʾathum āyātunā mubṣiratan qālū hādhā siḥrun mubīnun ~ wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm wa-yyaʿăśû gam hēm ... bə-lahăṭêhem kēn: Pharaoh's side treats the signs as magic; Exodus shows it by having the magicians copy them, the Quran by having Pharaoh's people call them 'clear sorcery'.

passages.text: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

sides.note: Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.

passages.text: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ

sides.note: rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

sides.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

passages.text: ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'.

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed

passages.text: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

sides.note: God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual).

passages.text: وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

sides.note: Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

sides.note: fa-lammā raʾāhā tahtazzu ka-annahā jānnun wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib ~ wa-yhî lə-nāḥāš wa-yyānās Mōše mippānāyw: Moses flees from his transformed staff in both. Exodus then has God order him to grasp the snake by the tail (šəlaḥ yādəkā wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô); the Quran has God reassure him: yā Mūsā lā takhaf innī lā yakhāfu ladayya l-mursalūna.

passages.text: وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْءَامِنِينَ

sides.note: As at Q 27:10: wa-yyānās Mōše mip-pānāyw ~ wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib; Exodus' command to seize the snake's tail (wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô) becomes yā Mūsā aqbil wa-lā takhaf innaka mina l-āminīn, 'come forward and do not fear, you are safe'.

sides.note: jadhwa min al-nār, 'a firebrand', that you may warm yourselves

matches.label: Moses' hand turned white as a sign

passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. The Quran's 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ) excludes exactly what Exodus says, that the hand was leprous (məṣōraʿat), and needs no second step of restoring it (4:7).

passages.text: ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'.

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils; Child makes birds from clay that come alive; Jesus asks 'Who are my helpers to God?' and the disciples (hawariyyun) answer 'We are God's helpers'; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil; Jesus heals the born-blind and the leper and raises the dead by God's leave; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; Prophet is taken up alive to heaven in a whirlwind; God sent down the Torah (al-Tawrat) and the Gospel (al-Injil) before as guidance.

Only in Mary, the spirit in human form, the birth under the palm, the speaking infant (Surah 19:16-40): A divine messenger announces a son to a virgin untouched by any man; Mother gives birth alone in a remote place; The Day of Regret (yawm al-hasra) when the matter is decided; God's spirit appears to a woman in the form of a well-proportioned man; The prophet child is dutiful to his parent(s), not an arrogant tyrant; God answers doubt: 'It is easy for me; I created you before when you were nothing'; God gives life and death and is the inheritor of the earth and all on it; Denial that God has taken a son (walad); God does not beget and was not begotten; Jesus says 'worship God, my Lord and your Lord'; The infant Jesus declares himself God's servant, given the Book and made a prophet; 'That is Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute'; Labor pains drive the mother to the trunk of a palm tree; Mary is addressed as 'sister of Aaron'; Mary withdraws from her family to an eastern place behind a screen; A spring or stream appears for the mother; The mother returns with the child and her people accuse her of an enormity; In labor the mother wishes she had died before this and been utterly forgotten; A palm tree provides food to the mother; 'Peace on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive'; The factions differ among themselves about Jesus; God breathed of his spirit into the woman who guarded her chastity; A voice from beneath her consoles the mother: 'do not grieve'; Mother keeps a vow of silence; Refrain 'And mention in the Book ...' introducing a series of prophet portraits; The woman seeks refuge in God from the mysterious visitor.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The blessed recline on couches set in rows (or face to face) (weight 7.7); Youths (ghilman) like hidden pearls go round serving them (weight 7.7); Abundant fruit in paradise from which the blessed eat (weight 7.1); The blessed are paired with wide-eyed maidens (hur 'in) (weight 7.1); The effects of wine and of the cup: mockery, madness, or none [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.8). Pair score 36.4.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof; 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes'; Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth?; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Messengers go up and down between realms by a stairway or ladder of heaven (simmiltu / sullam / maʿārij) [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; and 10 more.

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Young servers go round with a variety of vessels serving a mixed drink [divergence between the texts]; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; and 8 more.

leads.title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 7.3); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 6.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 6.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 6.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). Pair score 33.0.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; In the divine realm the human is given a garment to put on [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; A hostile spirit is commanded 'go out' of the dwelling; Heavenly beings do obeisance when the first human has been made: to the maker or to the man [divergence between the texts]; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; The underworld or hell has seven doors or gates; The underworld has seven gates, bolted and opened one at a time [divergence between the texts]; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; What divine element is put into the clay of the first human: a slain god's flesh, blood and spirit, or God's breath [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.
